The couple encouraged women to repurpose their old wedding dresses for the event; seemingly the only one who did was Real Housewife Carole Radziwill.

Then it was off to the Hôtel de la Marine for a reception and dinner. Before the guests sat down, Denning gave a vaguely political speech calling attention to the fact that this was a gay wedding and urging the roomful of people with lots of resources and power to take care of those whose rights they were celebrating. At the after-party, French drag queen Nicky Doll performed. The fairy-tale weekend ended with a black-tie affair at Château de Villette on the last Saturday of summer with the couple in custom midnight-blue Hermès tuxedos.

The pair have been well received in New York in part because they’re so happy to be here. “Anna loved him because she could invite him to any dinner party and sit him next to any annoying or difficult person and he knew how to show up, lift the conversation, and never complain,” one fashion editor recalls of Porch. “He’s just very kind and normal and unassuming,” says Wes Gordon, the creative director of Carolina Herrera and a friend of Porch’s. “It’s easy to forget he was a very senior person at Meta and now OpenAI.”

Porch and Denning are tight with theater producers, fashion designers, art curators, and socialites such as Lauren Santo Domingo, Jenna Lyons, and Derek Blasberg. “They were two separately quiet people in different realms and then when they came together, they started making a splash,” says one journalist. “A lot of people will make names for themselves in San Francisco and L.A. and then they come to New York and it’s like being shot out of a cannon into other worlds.”

A couple of months after the wedding, Porch was at Instagram HQ in Menlo Park when Altman’s call came through. They discussed how “everyone’s talking about AI and productivity and that’s great, but no one’s talking about AI and culture,” Porch recalls. “And those two things are going to come together, and culture is run by all these creative industries, and question mark on what that’s going to look like.”

There were more conversations, with Altman and Fidji Simo, Altman’s then-No. 2, with whom Porch worked for more than a decade at Meta. “I think what Fidji really realized is there was an enterprise-and-sales arm that was being built for it, but there wasn’t anyone to work on the talent side,” Porch tells me. “That is where there was an obvious opening for me to come in.” Still, he had just gotten married, and he politely declined. When Simo came calling again in January, Porch was more receptive. “It was like, ‘New Year, new me.’ Time to jump to the next frontier,” he says. “Sam, I feel, is the same person I met socially years ago in San Francisco. And it’s kind of fun to work for a gay guy.”

He started in March, spending his first few months on a listening tour, mostly in New York and L.A., meeting with everyone from the Council of Fashion Designers of America to HBO showrunners. “I ran around and went to a bunch of people I knew would have strong opinions on it, good or bad,” says Porch. He went to the Cannes Film Festival, meeting with directors and hearing their feedback on the technology. “There was way more openness because directors have been using AI forever,” says Porch. He also went to San Francisco — “a lot,” he says, stressing the t — “to bond with the product folks and the researchers and try to get a sense of what they’re really interested in. I don’t have that many mathematicians on speed dial.”

Then he brought people together for intimate events — “just a lot of relationship building for the company,” says Porch. At Paris Fashion Week, he hosted a dinner at Sushi Park with Joopiter, Pharrell Williams’s digital-first auction house, for various French creators. “It wasn’t heavy programming, and it wasn’t branded,” Porch says. “It was just a collab with Joopiter to get people talking.” He has also hosted dinners for TBPN, the daily tech-industry podcast OpenAI acquired in April to help bolster positive conversation around AI. The first TBPN dinner was held in L.A. and attended by the Foster sisters, Monica Lewinsky, Crazy Rich Asians director John Chu, and manager turned tech-investor Guy Oseary. They replicated it in New York a few months later at the downtown restaurant Kiko, where TBPN president Dylan Abruscato was seated next to SNL’s Chloe Fineman and Kareem Rahma of “Subway Takes.” Vogue head of editorial content Chloe Malle and Vanity Fair editorial director Mark Guiducci were also in attendance. “He has been very instrumental in helping TBPN deepen our relationships with Condé Nast,” says Abruscato.

A few days before our interview, I attended one such event, a dinner Porch co-hosted at the subterranean members’ club Chez Margaux. In celebration of influencer Serena Kerrigan’s new book, the gathering was attended by a mix of podcasters, creators, and Real Housewives, but, I noted to Porch, I didn’t hear any discussion about AI. “That was a personal dinner, just so you understand. My personal and professional kind of blend,” he says. “But what’ll happen from that dinner is Serena’s probably going to call me in two months and be like, ‘Wait, I have this idea. I love Chat for this. Do you wanna do this thing with me?’ So there’s a nice cadence of how that happens. But also, you know, there were three Real Housewives there. If an AI model comes up on the show, it might be Chat because we have this nice drumbeat. This is what I’ve been trying to explain to folks: It’s not about deals; it’s about relationships.”

Still, it’s hard to say what exactly is supposed to result from this strategy. The idea appears to be that all this social lubrication will pay off and that Altman and his ilk will one day be seen less as freakish world destroyers than as parts of a broader mosaic of American celebrity. Familiarity, even at an elite level, tends to trickle down.

So far, though, things look decisively less glamorous than they did at Instagram. Aside from Lionel Messi’s ChatGPT World Cup partnership, the most prominent celebrities working with the company have been rookie NFL quarterback Fernando Mendoza, who recently spoke to GQ about using ChatGPT for meal planning and nutrition, and designer Francesco Risso, who discussed the role of Astra in his creative process in an OpenAI-sponsored video on Vogue’s YouTube channel. “There might come a day when I get a call from Charles about doing something, and I’ll navigate that in real time, but I recognize this brand has very bad PR right now,” says one creative professional. They add, “If you’re someone who doesn’t like where things are headed, anyone affiliated with this world is going to be seen as part of the problem.”

“When Kevin Systrom or Adam Mosseri were having events with celebrities, people wanted their leverage to help them grow their account, grow their influence,” says one media executive. Instagram is inherently about marketing yourself; OpenAI’s main product isn’t yet public facing. “Aligning yourself with OpenAI, every star has to ask, ‘What’s in it for me?’ — except for potentially a big check and a lot of blowback,” says the media executive. Skepticism around technology has only grown since Hollywood cashed in on the NFT and crypto crazes, resulting in embarrassing commercials and promotions that blew up in many high-profile faces. And the threat AI poses to cultural fields also seems to be putting a higher premium on good old-fashioned human creativity and originality. “I don’t care how cute you make Waymo look: This autonomous-AI-powered life is not warm and cuddly,” says the media executive. “There’s not a cool factor.”

At the same time, many in the entertainment industry are desperate. “Right now in Hollywood, only the top people are working,” the executive says. “It’s why Robert Pattinson is in every project or why Nicole Kidman is literally in everything you watch on TV. The next tier down is not getting jobs.” According to Porch, when he joined OpenAI, there was a backlog of inquiries from various celebrities looking for an endorsement deal, production studios wanting to become more AI focused, fashion houses trying to figure out e-commerce, and sports teams and leagues looking to integrate more AI. It’s possible that we will look back at this moment as we do at musicians who wouldn’t give their songs to iTunes. “Now, it’s like, ‘I can’t believe you would have turned down the check,’” one journalist says.

Some people roll their eyes at Porch, dismissing him as someone whose job is to be friends with famous people and questioning whether he has any expertise at all. “He’s a super-wily leverager of social relationships, but it helps when you have multimillion-dollar marketing budgets to get people what they want,” says a tech adviser. Another media executive sees what Porch has done as a kind of surfing: You choose your wave, start paddling at the right time, and rise at the perfect moment. It’d be fair to say Porch is a good surfer, they note. And now people are watching to see if he can stay up. “He sits in the middle of the convergence of media, culture, and tech, but he’s also right at the changing of the tide,” says the tech adviser, noting that Porch embodies a certain older-millennial brand that may be going out of fashion. “How much longer does someone like him maintain clout when it may be based on an outdated model of how those worlds interact?”

Porch insists he’s not worried. “What I keep coming back to is, I think, the usefulness of AI,” he says. “What it’s transforming for people is undeniable. And the more conversations I have, I just — I feel it coming, people being able to talk about it more.” He adds, “Everything moves faster in AI.”

*A previous version of this story misstated Eva Chen’s role at Meta.

照片：Danielle Levitt for New York Magazine 照片：Danielle Levitt for New York Magazine 8 月，有消息透露，格温妮丝·帕特洛 (Gwyneth Paltrow) 将在她阿玛甘塞特的家中举办“一场私人的、不公开的露天晚宴”，以纪念 OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman)。 Puck 的马特·贝洛尼 (Matt Belloni) 爆料了这一消息，他写道：“我想，如果不讨好我们的新人工智能霸主，汉普顿的夏天就不算完整。” “幸运的是，格温妮丝·帕特洛为你提供了保障。”一位 X 用户写道，强烈反对是“五音不全的笨蛋”，晚餐被推迟了。

“天哪，互联网让它变得比原来更重要了，”10 月一个清爽的下午，在苏活区圣安布罗厄斯 (Sant Ambroeus) 外，负责与帕特洛团队共进晚餐的查尔斯·波奇 (Charles Porch) 一边喝着阿诺·帕尔默 (Arnold Palmer) 啤酒一边说道。 “格温妮丝投资了这个领域。她总是举办这些投资者晚宴。萨姆正从镇上过来，我当时想，‘我们就这么做吧。’”

Altman 于 2025 年聘请了 Porch，为 OpenAI 做他十多年来为 Instagram 所做的成功的事情：说服好莱坞及其他地区的名人使用该平台并与该平台合作，帮助这家科技公司在文化上具有相关性。帕特洛晚宴引发的恐慌反映了自 Porch 推出 Instagram 时代以来，公众对大型科技公司的情绪发生了多大转变，当时安娜·温图尔 (Anna Wintour) 为其时任首席执行官凯文·斯特罗姆 (Kevin Systrom) 举办了类似的活动。我问他这是否让他重新思考剧本。 “这使得这看起来像是策略，但实际上并不是策略。那就像一顿晚餐，”波奇说。 “但我知道这些晚餐是有效的，因为我看到了。我们最终完成了晚餐，非常棒。” 9月底，事情发生在纽约一位人工智能爱好者的公寓里。

超过一定收入水平的每个人似乎都认识查尔斯·波奇，但很少有人能告诉你他到底做什么。 20 岁时，他开着祖母的本田雅阁旅行车出现在洛杉矶，并在接下来的二十年里培养了一个由名人和影响者组成的强大网络。音乐制作人大卫·福斯特 (David Foster) 的女儿艾琳·福斯特 (Erin Foster) 人脉广泛，她在华纳兄弟唱片公司 (Warner Bros. Records) 的下属时期认识了波奇，她说：“他一步步走得非常小心，从不烧毁一座桥梁，从不不按顺序说话，从不以错误的方式利用机会。”

45 岁的 Porch 说：“我不是一个业务开发人员或品牌人员。我是负责关系的人，负责让每个人都了解新技术。”他自称是“技术乐观主义者”，长期以来一直在个人和专业之间的灰色地带游刃有余。 “有一个关于交朋友的策略。”

当他在大流行之前抵达纽约时，似乎很少有人注意到。对于那些不知道或不关心 2010 年代初门洛帕克发生的事情的人来说，他们第一次听说 Porch 很可能是在他于 2025 年与亿万富翁的继承人罗伯特·丹宁 (Robert Denning) 结婚之后，与杰里·宋飞 (Jerry) 和杰西卡·宋飞 (Jessica Seinfeld)、玛莉丝卡·哈吉泰 (Mariska Hargitay)、安东尼·布林肯 (Antony Blinken)、哈里·斯泰尔斯 (Harry Styles)（与他有一个教子）、尼基·希尔顿·罗斯柴尔德 (Nicky Hilton Rothschild) 一起度过了三天的巴黎富裕生活。达伦·沃克（Darren Walker）、珍娜·里昂（Jenna Lyons）以及各个欧洲贵族。事实证明，这是继杰夫·贝索斯和劳伦·桑切斯·贝索斯之后今年夏天最豪华的婚礼。突然间，他和​​丹宁无处不在，这对权力同性恋夫妇渗透到了纽约社会的每一个晚会、筹款活动和开幕式上。波奇的生活漩涡在他的 Instagram 故事中上演：在尼克斯队赛季揭幕战的场边、在夏威夷参加 Jen Meyer 众星云集的婚礼、在巴黎观看席琳·迪翁 (Céline Dion) 与瑞茜·威瑟斯彭 (Reese Witherspoon) 和卡莉·克劳斯 (Karlie Kloss)。

在连接娱乐和科技的过程中，他发现自己处于几个重叠的权力圈的中心，并凭借自己的能力成为一个人物。当我指出这一点时，他说：“我知道，这很可怕。” “他真的很擅长把一个房间整合在一起，现在他就是这个房间的一部分了，”与他共事的一位人士说道。 “在成为当权派的一员之前，他就了解这个房间。”

不难理解为什么 OpenAI 希望 Porch 站在自己一边。 “这很有趣：我认为每个人都想讨厌 Open AI，但每个人都想喜欢 Charles Porch，”播客 Nayeema Raza 说道。 “这可能就是山姆的价值。”

波奇的工作绝非易事。为什么艺术家和其他创意类型想要插入一些有可能取代他们的东西？ “对人工智能的全力支持可能是好莱坞目前最大的第三轨问题。人们感到害怕，”一位媒体高管表示。近几个月来，有关人工智能的头条新闻不仅引发了人们的恐慌，人们不仅担心工作岗位流失和版权侵权，还担心 OpenAI 代理的行为失控并威胁要摧毁整个互联网。科技行业的邪恶是今年几部最热门电影的主题，而这些电影正是由 Porch 试图吸引的行业制作的。 “查尔斯可以让他们坐下来，听萨姆·奥尔特曼阐述他的愿景。但如果愿景是‘我要摧毁你的行业’，那其实并不重要，”波奇的一位前同事说。

“我正在努力找出人工智能以一种好的方式出现在文化中的方式和时刻，”波奇说，他有着冰蓝色的大眼睛、完美光滑的头部和永久的微笑，看起来有点像人工智能如何呈现人类。 “我每天看到的是，人们表面上反对人工智能，但对如何使用它却完全保密。这几乎就像他们早上参加人工智能抗议，然后下午和我开会。你知道这让我想起了什么吗？GLP-1 的早期，当时的感觉是，这有点可耻；你在作弊。但后来每个人都说，等等，这件事太不可思议了。”

照片：Danielle Levitt for New York Magazine Porch 在南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿长大。他的母亲是法国人，父亲是阿拉巴马人，还有一个严重残疾的妹妹。 “我总是在幕后，照顾我的妹妹并确保每个人都感到舒适，”他说。 “因为我姐姐不会说话，所以她周围的人会很奇怪。我想让每个人都感觉良好，所以我只负责调节温度。这种看护的感觉是我与生俱来的。”他在新泽西州普林斯顿的一所男子合唱团寄宿学校度过了中学时光。 “我们会在巴士上上学，我们会环游世界并演唱宗教音乐，”波奇说，并指出他小时候曾多次在卡内基音乐厅演出。他在加利福尼亚州蒙特雷完成了高中学业，2002 年从麦吉尔大学毕业后，他开车去了洛杉矶。

在某些方面，波奇的好运气要归功于克雷格列表，因为他在网站上找到的公寓的女房东为他提供了在华纳兄弟唱片公司营销部门实习的机会，并在那里认识了福斯特。 “然后，突然间，我参加了凯特·哈德森的万圣节派对。”

福斯特说：“当我把他带入我的世界时，我发现人们总是被查尔斯吸引，因为他不想从任何人那里得到任何东西”，而且“他自己似乎并没有试图成为人才”。福斯特补充道，门廊“成为人们感到安全的人，无论是在工作生活中还是在朋友圈子里”。 “他从来没有给人留下一个用户或会不按顺序发言或分享私人信息的人的印象。”

news.title: One brutal Minecraft night scared 50 AI agents into inventing chicken handoff protocols, a Fertilizer Officer, and fishing shifts
news.title_en: One brutal Minecraft night scared 50 AI agents into inventing chicken handoff protocols, a Fertilizer Officer, and fishing shifts
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
In experiments by Y Combinator Labs and Olam Labs, OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol model showed two very different sides. When 50 agents were tasked with peaceful civilization-building in Minecraft, they froze up in absurd bureaucracy. In direct competition against Claude Opus 5.5, they independently downloaded the game's source code to win. Simulations like these are meant to serve as an early warning system before AI swarms act unpredictably in real-world systems.

news.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI

news.author: OpenAI 官方动态
news.original_content: How OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend designed for the scale of development that Codex makes possible.
news.content_snippet: How OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend designed for the scale of development that Codex makes possible.
news.summary_en: OpenAI's engineering team announced the launch of Pando, a custom Git-compatible backend designed to handle the massive development scale generated by AI tools like Codex. Traditional Git infrastructure struggles to cope with the sheer volume of code produced autonomously around the clock, forcing OpenAI to build this scalable alternative to keep version control from melting.
news.title_zh: OpenAI自研Pando系统重构Git
news.summary_zh: OpenAI官方推出专为AI代码生成规模化开发设计的Git兼容后端Pando系统
news.article_content_zh:
OpenAI近日官方披露了名为Pando的技术项目，这是一款专为配合其AI代码生成工具Codex而生的高性能Git兼容后端系统。

随着大模型在软件工程领域的深度渗透，AI生成的代码量呈指数级增长，传统分布式版本控制系统在处理海量提交记录、频繁合并冲突以及极高并发操作时逐渐显现出性能瓶颈。Pando的问世正是为了填补这一底层基础设施的空白，确保在大规模自动化编程时代，代码版本管理能够跟上AI狂飙突进的步伐。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI工程团队在官方技术博客宣布推出全新自研后端系统Pando，旨在解决Codex等AI大规模代码生成带来的版本控制压力。由于传统的Git在面对AI全天候疯狂暴走式产出的海量代码时频繁性能崩溃，OpenAI不得不亲自动手，打造了这个完美兼容Git标准但能支撑恐怖代码量级的底层基础设施，以防自家程序员被AI卷到失业前先被版本冲突折磨疯。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI's engineering team announced the launch of Pando, a custom Git-compatible backend designed to handle the massive development scale generated by AI tools like Codex. Traditional Git infrastructure struggles to cope with the sheer volume of code produced autonomously around the clock, forcing OpenAI to build this scalable alternative to keep version control from melting.

news.content_snippet: Illustration by Mark Harris; Photographs by Thea Traff for The New York Times, AJ Mast for The New York Times, Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times, Getty Images
news.summary_en: Anthropic is aggressively securing compute capacity, expecting over 3.5GW by 2026 by diversifying beyond Nvidia to sign deals with Amazon, Google, AMD, chipmakers, and former crypto miners.
news.title_zh: Anthropic狂揽算力：2026年容量超3.5吉瓦
news.summary_zh: Anthropic通过疯狂签署算力大单，在2026年将拥有超3.5吉瓦算力，并摆脱对英伟达的单一依赖

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Anthropic为了打破算力瓶颈并支撑大模型训练，近期开启了疯狂的算力并购与合作大单签约。消息显示，该公司预计在2026年获得超过3.5吉瓦（GW）的电力与算力容量，并在未来计划将该规模翻倍。在此过程中，Anthropic彻底摆脱了对英伟达AI芯片的单一依赖，转而与亚马逊、谷歌、AMD及多家芯片商和前加密矿企签署了数十项基础设施协议。

news.title_en: S-1 update: Anthropic reports Q3 revenue up 12x YoY to nearly $17B, a $23.3B net loss, up from $12.1B in Q3 2025, and operating expenses up 292% YoY to $17.5B (Bailey Lipschultz/Bloomberg)
news.author: Bloomberg
news.original_content:
Bailey Lipschultz / Bloomberg:
S-1 update: Anthropic reports Q3 revenue up 12x YoY to nearly $17B, a $23.3B net loss, up from $12.1B in Q3 2025, and operating expenses up 292% YoY to $17.5B  —  Anthropic PBC disclosed a twelve-fold increase in quarterly revenue wh
news.content_snippet: Anthropic PBC disclosed a twelve-fold increase in quarterly revenue while revealing that it intends to spend more than $895 billion …
news.summary_en: Anthropic reported a 12x revenue surge to $17B in Q3, fueled by market expansion, yet operating expenses spiked 292% to $17.5B. This resulted in a net loss widening from $12.1B to $23.3B, highlighting the extreme cash-burn nature of the ongoing AI arms race.
news.title_zh: Anthropic季度营收激增12倍，但亏损如深渊
news.summary_zh: Anthropic第三季度营收同比增长12倍至170亿美元，但运营费用狂飙致净亏损扩大至233亿美元

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Anthropic在最新的S-1备案文件中披露，第三季度营收暴增12倍达170亿美元，主要得益于产品市场扩张；然而运营开支激增292%至175亿美元，导致季度净亏损从上年同期的121亿美元进一步扩大至233亿美元，反映出AI军备竞赛中“烧钱换增长”的极端现状。

news.title: Email: OpenAI plans to merge ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs on desktop for select users before rolling it out widely; Codex "will remain a separate experience" (Ivan Mehta/TechCrunch)
news.title_en: Email: OpenAI plans to merge ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs on desktop for select users before rolling it out widely; Codex "will remain a separate experience" (Ivan Mehta/TechCrunch)
news.author: TechCrunch
news.article_content:
The ChatGPT desktop app can be a confusing piece of software, given that there are ChatGPT and Codex sections, and within the former, there are Chat and Work tabs. With so many options, it’s sometimes easy to forget where you are working and where exactly your project is.

In an apparent effort to address this, OpenAI is now gearing up to merge the Chat and Work tabs within the ChatGPT experience, according to an email sent to users. OpenAI said that initially, this experience will be available to select users for feedback before it is rolled out widely.

“This will enable you to move from exploring an idea to having ChatGPT carry it through, all in one place. You can bring in your files and plugins and ask ChatGPT to build a website, create a presentation, or do things for you on the web, while reviewing and guiding its work. Codex will remain a separate experience in the ChatGPT desktop app,” the email said.

OpenAI also said with this transition, both ChatGPT and Codex will draw tokens from the same allowance pool. It said this change won’t impact most users, but based on usage and model, some folks might need to wait for resets more frequently.

Rival Anthropic merged Claude’s chat and Cowork functions into one screen in September.

news.article_content_zh:
ChatGPT 桌面应用程序可能是一个令人困惑的软件，因为它有 ChatGPT 和 Codex 部分，而在前者中，有聊天和工作选项卡。有如此多的选择，有时很容易忘记您在哪里工作以及您的项目到底在哪里。

根据发送给用户的电子邮件，为了解决这个问题，OpenAI 现在正准备将 Chat 和 Work 选项卡合并到 ChatGPT 体验中。 OpenAI 表示，这种体验最初将向选定的用户提供反馈，然后再广泛推广。

“这将使您能够从探索一个想法转变为让 ChatGPT 将其付诸实施，一切都在一个地方。您可以引入您的文件和插件，并要求 ChatGPT 构建一个网站、创建演示文稿或在网络上为您做一些事情，同时审查和指导其工作。Codex 将仍然是 ChatGPT 桌面应用程序中的一种单独体验，”电子邮件中说道。

OpenAI 还表示，通过这一转变，ChatGPT 和 Codex 都将从同一配额池中提取代币。它表示这一变化不会影响大多数用户，但根据使用情况和型号，有些人可能需要更频繁地等待重置。

竞争对手 Anthropic 在 9 月份将 Claude 的聊天和 Cowork 功能合并到一个屏幕中。

news.title: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
news.title_en: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors. A single task can use 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat prompt. The more useful the agent becomes, the more calls it makes. With per-token pricing, the workflows creating the most value can also become the most expensive.

The financial pressure is already visible. Uber reportedly exhausted its entire 2026 AI budget by April after expanding its use of Claude Code. GitHub Copilot moved from flat-rate pricing to metered credits. Gartner predicts that AI coding token costs will surpass average developer salaries by 2028.

The natural response is rationing usage caps, seat limits, and approvals before developers launch agents. But blanket limits can restrict the workflows delivering value. They also optimize the wrong number. Cost per token measures consumption, not results. Some spending reflects waste, including retries and runaway loops. Some represents the work of shipping software. A meter cannot distinguish them, and neither can a spending cap.

news.title: The Download: the agentic web arrives and the drive for safer roads
news.title_en: The Download: the agentic web arrives and the drive for safer roads
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
In 2001, a decade after inventing the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision: an internet navigated by autonomous software agents that address our every need, without requiring us to muck about with browsers and search engines ourselves.

At the time, the idea seemed far-fetched. But a quarter-century on, AI agents are beginning to make it a reality. They can triage your inbox, do your grocery shopping, and even access your bank accounts.

This new era is being called the agentic web. It will inevitably transform the internet—and whether the human web survives this transition is anyone’s guess.

news.title: When You Should—and Shouldn’t—Use AI to Search the Web
news.title_en: When You Should—and Shouldn’t—Use AI to Search the Web
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
When asked to search the web, the latest versions of these bots are combining elements of traditional web search (they're essentially just googling on your behalf) with knowledge they are able to pull out of their training data. Everything is then packaged and formatted in the now-familiar, polished generative AI style.

It's the added AI elements on top of the traditional googling where the differences come in, and that means AI-powered search may not always be the best option.

If you're looking up something simple and widely known—like the height of the Empire State Building—then AI search is a pretty safe bet. Not only is information like this easy to access online, the “autocorrect” probability patterns favored by large language models mean there's a near-certain chance that the results you see will include the right information.

If you just need a quick look-up, AI is OK. The more obscure the question, though, the closer you need to look at the answer. If you've asked something less well known, like the fifth-billed actor in an obscure television show, there might only be one or two references to it on the web, and an AI might choose the wrong one.

One of the takeaways from recent Stanford University research is that when AI finds an accurate source, it's very good at pulling the right information out of it. Where it tends to fall down is in not finding accurate sources (either because there aren't any or because the query has been misinterpreted) and presenting a confident answer anyway.

AI search is also helpful when you have a complex query that a standard Google search wouldn't be able to parse: "I need to know the best restaurants in San Francisco for a family of five who want to spend no more than $200." AI is able to query and collate multiple sources in response to a search like this, and then present a well-synthesized answer. A traditional web search would give you a list of blue links that most probably just rank San Francisco restaurants by more basic criteria.

Again though, sources are crucial. AI bots have never been to San Francisco or eaten there. They are relying on public accounts on the web, written by people who have. Where there are no exact page matches, they'll look for related words (like "affordable" or "family") and generate an answer.

For queries where there's lots of information online, like San Francisco restaurants, AI web search can feel incredibly useful. For less popular destinations and more specific requests ("dining tables shaped like stars"), you need to be more careful with the results, as the way that AI joins the dots then becomes less reliable.

So, with the caveat that you should always do some kind of double-check, AI web search works best for common queries that are likely to lead to a lot of accurate, up-to-date information online. In both the way they process search queries, and package together and synthesize answers, AI chatbots are a significant upgrade on googling.

The way generative AI bots and LLMs are put together means they work best when paraphrasing, synthesizing, and summarizing. But these processes can also introduce mistakes. If your search needs precise details (like a celebrity quotation, a report stat, or a device specification), a traditional Google search may work best.

Heading to Google and searching the old way is also likely to be better if you want full control over the sources used. Offloading web searches to AI is convenient, but you're relying on them to interpret your search correctly, find the right sources, and then extract accurate information from those sources. It saves time, but it's more opaque.

If you know the websites you trust most for technology news, for example, you can prioritize them in a traditional web search in a way that AI might not be able to. Researchers from UC San Diego have found that AI web searches will sometimes pick sources because they're more relevant to the query, rather than because they're ranked as more authoritative.

That means a personal blog might get chosen above a professional health care site if the AI deems it to be a closer match to what the user is actually searching for. This is a choice that you would be much less likely to make when scanning a traditional list of results, as you'd typically pick the one you trusted the most.

Other areas where traditional searching still wins out are for breaking news (there can sometimes be a lag in the timeliness of the data AI pulls up) and for high-stakes searches where you absolutely cannot make a mistake—searches related to health, the law, or your finances, for instance.

If you do feel like an AI approach is needed, be sure to double- and triple-check the sources the chatbot has used, which should be linked inside the answer. If you're in any doubt, you can ask the AI for clarification on where something was sourced from, to make sure it isn't an LLM invention.

Classic Google searches can still turn up false information on the web, of course, but you're in a much better position to discern what's true and accurate and what isn't without a chatbot in the middle. For queries where that's more important than convenience and speed, there's still a place for the old way of searching the web.

news.article_content_zh:
当被要求搜索网络时，这些机器人的最新版本将传统网络搜索的元素（它们本质上只是代表您进行谷歌搜索）与它们能够从训练数据中提取的知识相结合。然后，所有内容都会以现在熟悉的、完善的生成式人工智能风格进行打包和格式化。

差异在于传统谷歌搜索之上添加的人工智能元素，这意味着人工智能驱动的搜索可能并不总是最好的选择。

如果您正在查找一些简单且众所周知的内容（例如帝国大厦的高度），那么人工智能搜索是一个非常安全的选择。这样的信息不仅可以轻松在线访问，而且大型语言模型所青睐的“自动更正”概率模式意味着您看到的结果几乎肯定会包含正确的信息。

如果你只是需要快速查找，人工智能就可以。然而，问题越模糊，你就越需要仔细研究答案。如果你问了一些不太为人所知的问题，比如一部不起眼的电视节目中的第五名演员，网络上可能只有一两个参考资料，而人工智能可能会选择错误的答案。

斯坦福大学最近的研究得出的结论之一是，当人工智能找到准确的来源时，它非常擅长从中提取正确的信息。它往往会失败的地方是找不到准确的来源（要么因为没有任何来源，要么因为查询被误解）并且无论如何都无法提供自信的答案。

当您遇到标准 Google 搜索无法解析的复杂查询时，人工智能搜索也会很有帮助：“我需要知道旧金山最好的一家五口之家的餐厅，他们的花费不超过 200 美元。”人工智能能够查询和整理多个来源来响应这样的搜索，然后提供一个综合良好的答案。传统的网络搜索会给您一个蓝色链接列表，这些链接很可能只是根据更基本的标准对旧金山餐厅进行排名。

不过，来源仍然至关重要。人工智能机器人从未去过旧金山或在那里吃过饭。他们依赖网络上的公共帐户，这些帐户是由拥有公共帐户的人编写的。如果没有精确的页面匹配，他们将查找相关单词（例如“负担得起”或“家庭”）并生成答案。

对于网上有大量信息的查询，比如旧金山的餐馆，人工智能网络搜索会感觉非常有用。对于不太受欢迎的目的地和更具体的要求（“星星形状的餐桌”），您需要对结果更加小心，因为人工智能连接点的方式变得不太可靠。

因此，需要注意的是，您应该始终进行某种双重检查，人工智能网络搜索最适合常见查询，这些查询可能会导致大量准确、最新的在线信息。人工智能聊天机器人在处理搜索查询、打包和综合答案方面都是谷歌搜索的重大升级。

生成式人工智能机器人和法学硕士的组合方式意味着它们在释义、综合和总结时效果最佳。但这些过程也可能会引入错误。如果您的搜索需要精确的详细信息（例如名人名言、报告统计数据或设备规格），传统的 Google 搜索可能效果最好。

如果您想完全控制所使用的来源，那么前往 Google 并以旧方式搜索也可能会更好。将网络搜索转移给人工智能很方便，但您需要依靠它们来正确解释您的搜索，找到正确的来源，然后从这些来源中提取准确的信息。它节省了时间，但更不透明。

例如，如果您知道最信任的科技新闻网站，您可以在传统网络搜索中以人工智能可能无法做到的方式对它们进行优先排序。加州大学圣地亚哥分校的研究人员发现，人工智能网络搜索有时会选择来源，因为它们与查询更相关，而不是因为它们被评为更权威。

这意味着，如果人工智能认为个人博客与用户实际搜索的内容更匹配，那么可能会选择个人博客而不是专业医疗保健网站。在扫描传统结果列表时，您不太可能做出这种选择，因为您通常会选择最信任的结果。

传统搜索仍然胜出的其他领域是突发新闻（人工智能提取的数据的及时性有时可能存在滞后）和绝对不会出错的高风险搜索，例如与健康、法律或财务相关的搜索。

news.title: Saudi Aramco takes 49 percent stake in AI firm Humain with $2.6 billion deal
news.title_en: Saudi Aramco takes 49 percent stake in AI firm Humain with $2.6 billion deal
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Saudi Aramco is buying into Humain, the company meant to turn Saudi Arabia into a global AI hub. According to Aramco, the oil giant is taking a 49 percent stake and contributing about $2.6 billion in 2026 along with its own AI technology. Humain was founded in May 2025 by the sovereign wealth fund PIF and builds data centers, develops cloud services, and trains AI models like the Arabic language model ALLaM.

Humain plans to build three gigawatts of data center capacity by 2030. The company wants to serve demand both domestically and abroad and become a leading AI exporter. Business is already picking up. In late August, AMD reported that infrastructure built jointly with Cisco and Humain is now serving customers inside and outside Saudi Arabia. Aramco plans to use the technology in its own operations and generate additional revenue by selling its own AI solutions. Through its investment arm Wa'ed Ventures, the company also holds a stake in Korean AI chip developer Rebellions.

news.content_snippet: The man who helped develop the technology for liquid crystal displays — the screens in flat-panel televisions and laptops — has died at 101.
news.summary_en: British physicist Cyril Hilsum has passed away at the age of 101, recognized as the pioneer who enabled modern flat-panel display technology. news.title: OpenAI prepares lobbying blitz for a post-midterm Washington
news.title_en: OpenAI prepares lobbying blitz for a post-midterm Washington
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
OpenAI is gearing up for a political lobbying and PR push after the US midterms. According to Axios, the company is bracing for a tougher fight in Washington if Democrats win control of the House.

After two years under a friendly administration, big tech companies with close ties to President Trump are facing growing regulatory pressure. Rivals like Meta are already building bridges to Democrats. OpenAI's policy chief Chris Lehane plans to steer the AI debate through 2028 with a mix of new and repackaged proposals. The pitch centers on one idea: AI doesn't replace people. To back that up, OpenAI is proposing binding safety rules that build on earlier ideas. Lehane calls them "speed limits."

The company is also responding to growing local backlash against data centers. According to Axios, OpenAI wants to rebrand the facilities as "AI Compute Campuses" and is promising economic benefits to host communities. Lehane says the company's top priority in the new Congress is fast-tracking safety rules for frontier models.

ai_analysis.digest_zh: OpenAI正为美国政局变动后的监管挑战进行大规模游说布局，其策略核心是推进“AI不会取代人类”的叙事，并提出所谓“速度限制”的AI安全规则。同时，公司计划将数据中心包装为“AI计算园区”以缓解民众对能耗的抵触，试图在立法机构通过抢占定义权来锁定行业优势。
ai_analysis.digest_en: OpenAI is ramping up lobbying efforts to navigate shifting political tides in Washington, promoting a narrative that AI won't replace humans while proposing 'speed limit' safety rules. The company is also rebranding energy-intensive data centers as 'AI Compute Campuses' to win public and regulatory support.

包装安全叙事与数据中心品牌
意图通过立法锁定行业护城河

news.article_content_zh:
OpenAI 正在为美国中期选举后的政治游说和公关活动做准备。据 Axios 称，如果民主党赢得众议院控制权，该公司将在华盛顿面临更激烈的战斗。

在友好政府执政两年后，与特朗普总统关系密切的大型科技公司面临着越来越大的监管压力。像 Meta 这样的竞争对手已经在与民主党建立桥梁。 OpenAI 的政策负责人 Chris Lehane 计划通过一系列新的和重新包装的提案来引导人工智能辩论持续到 2028 年。此次演讲围绕一个想法：人工智能不会取代人类。为了支持这一点，OpenAI 提出了基于早期想法的具有约束力的安全规则。勒汉称其为“速度限制”。

该公司还在应对当地对数据中心日益增长的强烈反对。据 Axios 称，OpenAI 希望将这些设施重新命名为“人工智能计算园区”，并承诺为所在社区带来经济效益。勒汉表示，该公司在新一届国会的首要任务是快速制定前沿车型的安全规则。

【起因与机理】应对大选后潜在的监管压力，确保公司在行业规则制定中的主导权
【关键技术规格】包装安全叙事与数据中心品牌。
【观点态度】意图通过立法锁定行业护城河。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] To pre-empt tougher regulations post-election and maintain industry dominance
[Key Specification] Launching major political lobbying campaign.
[Perspective & Impact] Attempting to lock in moats via legislation.

news.title: Hundreds of Mundane AI Apps Are Hiding Sexually Abusive Deepfake Features
news.title_en: Hundreds of Mundane AI Apps Are Hiding Sexually Abusive Deepfake Features
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
At first glance, the self-proclaimed “pet portrait” app Viefur appears to be just another AI slop generator. Using digital coins sold in the app—around $4 will buy 130 coins—pet photos can be turned into an “anthropomorphic portrait,” with the critter dressed in “human clothing” and inserted into bizarre scenes. Think a hamster wearing beach shorts, sunglasses, and lounging in a swimming pool or a Hawaiian shirt-wearing cat, drinking from a coconut.

All of this is cover for what appears to be the app’s true purpose: creating sexually abusive deepfake images.

A WIRED investigation found the app is part of a network of more than 400 connected domains and apps that, like Viefur, often claim to be everyday services—such as language tuition or AI workout coaches. When accessed under certain conditions, however, apps in the network stealthily load a web interface allowing the generation of explicit AI sexual images and videos using photos users upload. The apps include AI scenes such as “bedroom rape” and “threatening knife,” where a man holds a knife to a woman’s neck.

The network was discovered hiding in plain sight, by multiple researchers, after they investigated links from thousands of video ads containing explicit deepfake content that were published on Meta’s Facebook and Instagram. As WIRED has reported in recent months, hundreds of these ads contained AI generated child sexual abuse material, including images of real children and a member of a European royal family. The ads reached tens of thousands of people and have prompted investigations from regulators around the world.

In each case, the ads linked out to the deceptive apps in Apple and Google’s app stores—allowing people to generate explicit images and make payments using Apple and Google Pay. The network behind the nudify apps appears to have been publishing them for around a year, at times publishing dozens per week. This is despite Google, Apple, and Meta saying they enforce their policies that do not allow harmful deepfake content on their platforms.

The apps and domains investigated by WIRED appear to be run by Chinese developers and a Hong Kong registered entity called KeLing Technology Limited, according to a review of web domains and how the services operate. Email addresses linked to the entity, apps, and related services, did not respond to multiple requests for comment from WIRED, but after being contacted, they appeared to erase public connections between KeLing Technology Limited and the deepfake tools.

“This is an organized, commercially run operation: One operator behind hundreds of disposable apps and domains, cloaked to pass App Store review and pushed through tens of thousands of Meta ads under fake payer names,” says Paul Bouchaud, a lead researcher at the nonprofit AI Forensics, who investigated the network. “They don’t expect enforcement to catch up, and so far it hasn’t.”

Download one of the apps in the deepfake network and you may see exactly what was advertised—such as an app to create AI pet pictures. But behind the scenes, researchers found, the apps are quietly making determinations about whether to show the benign content or load a web interface showing explicit deepfakes.

“Each time the application is downloaded, there is a call to the server with some information, such as where the user is coming from, the language, some unique identifier, and then the server replies whether or not to show the explicit or the non-explicit version of it,” explains Bouchaud, who reverse engineered the apps’ and associated websites’ code. They say there’s no clear list of reasons why one user may be shown the explicit version of an app, but one trigger appears to be downloading it after clicking an associated ad on Meta’s platforms.

Websites linked to the apps have revealed the network’s secrets and the scale that it operates on. Opening one of the apps’ websites will likely show an entirely black screen and no content. The only noticeable change is that the URL updates to include the word “risk.” But the websites host the hidden explicit deepfake layer that can be loaded in each app.

This web interface contains dozens of pornography deepfake video and image templates—with users able to upload images of people to be added to the sexual scenes. The interface allows the purchase of “diamonds” to generate images and links to other social media accounts where users can contact the developers with questions or complaints.

Also hidden in the websites’ code are details about the entire network. A JavaScript bundle that can easily be unpicked, researchers say, contains a list of all the domains and apps that have been created by the developers—including app package details, encryption keys, Facebook advertising trackers, and more.

“They contained this giant configuration list of other domains with different encryption keys,” says Maël Le Touz, a staff threat researcher at security firm Infoblox, who identified almost 500 linked domains. “They run the same code and they all reference one another.”

Bouchard’s analysis of when domains were registered found that the apps started to appear toward the end of 2025, with a spike during the spring of this year. At one point, around 30 nudify apps-websites were being registered each week, the researcher says, with 27 live on Google’s Play Store in September. These apps had been downloaded more than 350,000 times collectively and many were rated suitable for all age groups, Bouchard’s research says.

One of the most popular apps, called DiffAI, was created in December 2025 and has been downloaded more than 100,000 times from the Play Store. A user review on Google’s Play Store stated: “This app contains templates for creating CSAM and other types of pornographic material. It performs no age verification.”

DiffAI was removed from the Play Store shortly before WIRED contacted Google about the network. Google did not respond to WIRED’s request for comment, though it had removed the majority of the apps ahead of being contacted. (Portions of the deepfake network were reported on by Danish journalists in September.)

Similarly, Apple removed 19 apps from its App Store, including pet photo app Viefur, after WIRED asked the company about the activity and shared associated domains. “We designed the App Store to be a safe and trusted place for our users, and nudification apps and other pornographic content are strictly prohibited,” says Apple spokesperson Adam Dema.

“We review every app before it’s published, and these apps complied with our rules when we reviewed them,” Dema says. “After approval, their developers changed the website the app pulls its content from, replacing what we approved with pornographic content, and promoted it through pornographic ads hosted on a third-party platform.” The company says it has suspended tens of thousands of apps for using these “bait-and-switch” tactics over the last year and recently updated its app store rules to further restrict “nudify” tools.

Central to the “nudify” network appears to be a host of Chinese developers whose identities seem to have been intentionally hidden. “It’s using exclusive Chinese hosting, the code is written in Chinese and has a lot of comments in Chinese,” Le Touz says, noting explicit videos in ads posted to Meta’s platforms promoting the apps contained watermarks from Chinese-language video editing software.

The apps and domains across the network have often used generic privacy policies, free email addresses from Gmail or Outlook, and obscure developer names as part of their alleged efforts to hide their connections. Ads for the apps posted on Meta’s platforms have also used apparently false names—such as Draftmondcreldbro Duhustepre and Swaldmungsha Glasirdcroldshold—and pages with no followers. Since the start of this year, Bouchaud’s research has found tens of thousands of explicit deepfake ads linked to the network—often using similar language in their advertising copy—on Meta’s platforms.

“These ads violate not just one, but several of Meta’s policies,” says Katie Paul, the director of the Tech Transparency Project, who first uncovered the ads showing deepfake explicit depictions of minors. “There is no question about what you are seeing, what the app is advertising,” she says. Paul says tech companies need to answer questions about where money generated from the apps goes and how those behind the nudification apps and services constantly seem to bypass their content moderation and safety systems.

Towards the end of September, a notification sent to users of the explicit deepfake interface announced that a new AI model could be used—the model was called Veyra, with a tagline in the apps of “More real. More natural. More wild.” The homepage of a website called Veyra AI listed its contact email as a KeLing Technology address.

When WIRED contacted KeLing email addresses, plus some of those listed in apps privacy policies, we received no response. However, after WIRED reached out, someone renamed some of the associated online social media channels, removed KeLing email addresses from the AI Veyra website, and removed the KeLing Technology Limited address from the first registered website.

Meta says it banned KeLing Technology Limited from advertising in 2025 after it failed to “comply with a cease and desist letter.” (Meta declined to share the letter with WIRED citing legal reasons.) “We have strict rules against promoting nudify apps and work aggressively to keep this material off our services,” a Meta spokesperson says. Meta says that while KeLing Technology Limited has continued to try and advertise through other ways, it takes action against the ads when it becomes aware of them.

After WIRED shared the 400-plus domains with Meta, the spokesperson said they had shared more than 3,000 associated ads linked to them, two-thirds of which it had already removed from its systems. Meta later told WIRED it has taken action against 11,600 ad accounts, more than 4,700 business pages, 5,200 users, and 15,000 pages linked to the domains, blocking 209 apps from advertising on its platforms.

“The criminals behind them take increasingly deceptive steps to evade detection—hiding behind fake names and identities, running ads that look benign, and sometimes linking to Google's and Apple's app stores, with the ads' true intent revealed only after a click,” the spokesperson says.

As WIRED finished reporting this story, similar ads and apps continued to be published on the tech platforms.

news.title: The agentic web is here
news.title_en: The agentic web is here
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
In 2001, a decade after he invented the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision. Together with two colleagues, he published an article in the magazine Scientific American in which he outlined what he called the “Semantic Web”: an internet designed to be navigated by autonomous software agents that could address our every need, without requiring us to muck about with browsers and search engines ourselves.

To illustrate what this might look like, Berners-Lee and his colleagues told a story about a pair of siblings who use their agents to automatically research and book a physical therapy appointment for their mother, making sure it would be covered by insurance and fit their busy calendars.

At the turn of the millennium, this vision seemed far-fetched: Google had only been online for a couple of years, and most people were still on dial-up connections. But a quarter-century on, the dream of autonomous software agents that use the internet and carry out tasks for us has finally been realized. New tools such as Meta’s blockbuster Muse agent and OpenAI’s Dots are logging record downloads and being given access to people’s bank accounts and email inboxes, and Anthropic

在2001年万维网诞生十年后，蒂姆·伯纳斯-李与其同僚在《科学美国人》杂志发表文章，勾勒了名为“语义网”的新愿景：一个专为自主软件智能体导航设计的互联网，能够满足人们的各种需求，而无需亲自拨弄浏览器和搜索引擎。
