news.title: SemiAnalysis launches GDPx, an agentic capability benchmark measuring 11 domains, including chip design, cybersecurity, and RSI; Opus 5.5 tops with a 12% score (SemiAnalysis)
news.title_en: SemiAnalysis launches GDPx, an agentic capability benchmark measuring 11 domains, including chip design, cybersecurity, and RSI; Opus 5.5 tops with a 12% score (SemiAnalysis)
news.author: SemiAnalysis
news.article_content:
GDPx is a benchmark that covers the most valuable domains for frontier intelligence. It aims to be the world’s best benchmark for measuring general agentic capabilities.

We believe the first trillion dollars of AI revenue will be concentrated in sectors that can deploy frontier intelligence at high ROI, not broadly diffused throughout the whole economy. Building a general-purpose benchmark based on share of GDP or the SOC/O*NET occupational taxonomy is therefore a mistake. If your goal is to track the progress of frontier models, you should focus on the domains where they will be most impactful.

And intentionally forgo industries like government, real estate, and insurance.

GDPx is a true frontier-level benchmark: even the best model scores just 12%.

GDPxIt’s worth emphasizing that certain models like Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra have sandbagged overall scores due to their safety classifiers. If we exclude cyber, biology, and alignment—the three domains where safety classifiers sometimes kick in—you get the following results instead.

GDPxWe were pleasantly surprised by how well this ranking lines up with our subjective impression of the models. OpenAI and Anthropic generally dominate the top of the ranking while SpaceXAI, Meta, and open-weight models are all meaningfully behind. Gemini 4 Carbon is a real improvement from Google and the only model in the same ballpark as Opus and Astra. It will be interesting to see people’s impressions once Carbon becomes generally available.

We believe it’s underrated how relevant safety classifiers are when picking the best model for certain use cases. For example, Muse Wonder Full is actually the best available cyber model today by a meaningful margin.

GDPxWe also generally observe meaningful spikiness across all leading models.

GDPxOpus 5.5 is the best all-around model and wins in quant trading, hardware design, and chip design. Gemini 4 Carbon is the best bio model (likely due to weaker safety classifiers) and edges out the win in software engineering. GPT-6 Astra wins convincingly for RSI and is also the best model for materials science. Our finance and legal tasks are so challenging that basically every model scores exactly 0.

Interestingly, if you subset to a single model family, you will sometimes see very similar spikes.

GDPxThe cost vs performance Pareto frontier also matches our general experience using the models: Luna and DeepSeek fight for the low end, Opus wins the high end, and OpenAI claims the middle. Again, however, the appearance of Gemini 4 Carbon is worth watching closely.

Domain-specific benchmarks have gotten significantly better over the past year largely thanks to the rise of specialized RL environment startups. Yet OpenAI’s GDPval (along with its derivatives like GDPval AA v2.1) remains the most popular general purpose benchmark still reported on major new model release cards. This is despite being released over a year ago on September 25, 2025—an eternity in AI land. GDPval may have been marketed as a “knowledge work” benchmark, but agents weren’t really even a thing yet. This had a huge impact on its task design, and as we’ll later explain, makes GDPval woefully inadequate for evaluating today’s frontier models.

Our goal with GDPx is to create the world’s best benchmark for general agentic capabilities. However, as soon as we started working on this project, it became clear why we’ve yet to see a worthy GDPval successor. Models like GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5.5 are already pushing the boundaries of human knowledge. If you want to make a finance or cyber task these models can only solve < 20% of the time, you need real domain expertise to ensure the task is hard for the right reasons. Many popular benchmarks sidestep this problem by shipping tasks that are downright unfair. This typically manifests in a grader that checks for requirements impossible to infer from the task description or environment. For example, a coding problem may ask the model to fix a bug that a human engineer would agree has two valid solutions—one using “module A” and another using “module B”. However, a poorly designed grader may require the AI to use “module A” and unfairly give 0 reward when the AI chooses “module B”. Correct all such issues, and the benchmark often ends up being saturated.

Making high quality tasks for a single domain you have expertise in is already hard enough—there’s a reason why labs are willing to pay $5k+ for a single high quality task. Finding one company with sufficient expertise in both AI evals and enough domains to make a broad-based GDP benchmark is downright impossible.

All partners were subject to a rigorous QA process we detail in the methodology section. For some domains, we had multiple partners who wanted to be exclusive and ran a process to select the one with the highest quality tasks.

We would like to give a huge thank you to all of our partners for contributing to GDPx. They’re among the best vendors for their respective domains and it would’ve been impossible to create such a broad-based benchmark without their help.

Additionally, we’d like to thank Fireworks for providing inference for all the open source models, Modal for providing the sandbox infra needed to run our tasks, as well as Abhijay Rana for helping source some of the partners and assisting with early QA.

To be clear, we believe GDPval was impressive for its time and was the first benchmark to evaluate AI on such a broad range of tasks. It’s not OpenAI’s fault that a benchmark created before the rise of agents does a poor job evaluating them today.

Every GDPval task is precisely specified and non-interactive, with all the necessary context directly spoon-fed to the model in the prompt. Consider the following representative finance example below:

SemiAnalysisAttached to this prompt is a very plain, single-page PDF that gives the model even more context about the two projects.

An actual document used for an OpenAI GDPval finance task. Source: OpenAIFrom here, the model is asked to directly one-shot its task of writing a 15 page pdf to recommend one of the two options.

Despite the task description itself being unnaturally wordy, the overall task lacks detail about the “two significant investment opportunities.” The model is expected to take nothing more than a ~500 word, high-level description of the two options and convert it into an “up to 15 page” pdf recommending one of them. As you’d expect, even OpenAI’s reference solution is mostly filler slop.

Relatedly, the task simply lacks a realistic, rich environment. A human expert tasked with making a recommendation between two investment opportunities would do a ton of research first to gather information—searching through pdfs, excel models, emails, etc. This process of gathering context is a big part of what makes actual work difficult and is entirely missing from GDPval.

This second point is extremely important to understand. Not including domain-specific, simulated work environments for each task is the single biggest issue with GDPval. Agents today have already progressed well beyond narrow, well-scoped tasks like “generate a pdf/excel file/word doc/powerpoint based on just this reference file attached below + a few hundred word prompt,” yet basically every GDPval task fits this exact shape. As for tools, the model is only given access to web search, a code interpreter, and libraries to modify PDFs, word docs, excel files, powerpoints, images, audio, and video.

Graders are entirely rubric-based which is often noisy. Human expert inter-rater agreement was just 71% on the gold subset and their automated grader was even worse.

Broken rubrics with vague criteria, incorrect standards, and sometimes downright wrong requirements.

Incorrect golden expert solutions that are used as references for grading the model output.

Tasks that depend on a previous point in time and now have broken links, outdated prices, etc.

SemiAnalysisThe task environment is seeded by a real transaction from Living Context’s enterprise network. In it, Bannock Capital (a PE fund) buys ~62% of Haverly Snack Company for $880M plus an earnout. Eakin Lowry is the sell-side banker and Marbury Kline is the accounting advisor. The environment consists of ~4000 anonymized files separated into four categories: Haverly’s virtual data room (VDR) and independent deal folders for Bannock, Eakin and Marbury (all fake names of course).

Each task is performed from the perspective of Bannock, Eakin or Marbury. Haverly’s VDR is always loaded into the environment along with the appropriate deal folder. The specific example above is an accounting task that an associate from Marbury was actually asked to do in the real transaction. Unlike the GDPval task that spoon-fed all the relevant context to the model in the prompt, the AI needs to adeptly navigate a real ~2000 file deal room to gather the right context in order to successfully complete this task—just like a real human associate did.

All of our other domains contain similarly rich environments. Cyber tasks are based on real zero days discovered by Arithmetic’s security engineers and include multiple running services in the environment. Material science tasks put the model inside simulated laboratories complete with battery cyclers, a catalyst reactor, a transmission electron microscope, and more. Hardware design tasks include live sessions of Siemens NX and test the model output on real AWS FPGA instances. These are just a few examples—we’ll cover each of our partners in depth later in the article.

We believe it’s a mistake to build a benchmark for general agentic capabilities based on share of GDP or the SOC/O*NET occupational taxonomy because AI diffusion won’t be equally distributed and not all domains will need frontier intelligence. Thus, if your goal is to track the progress of frontier models, you should focus on the domains where they’ll be most impactful.

From there, we reached out to 30+ RL environment companies that have expertise in chip design, cybersecurity, biology, RSI, materials science, etc. Every potential partner was subject to the same rigorous agentic QA (quality assurance) process which checks for consistency, completeness, cheating, unfair verifiers, and much more. Our QA process was based on Andrew and Max’s previous experience co-founding an RL environment startup that sold data to multiple frontier labs. When we run this same QA process on popular benchmarks like Terminal Bench 4.0, it flags nearly 50% of tasks as broken. Of course, we also manually reviewed hundreds of trajectories to verify what our automated QA was flagging and to catch things that automated QA normally wouldn’t. We also perform failure mode analysis on our tasks to ensure our set is diverse and that even within a task, models fail for a variety of reasons.

However, we are also well-aware that any QA system can be gamed given sufficient iteration. If a task only passes QA after 3-4 rounds of feedback, it becomes very difficult to tell whether the task actually became good, or if the provider simply tricked your QA process.

For this reason, all partners were required to pass our automated QA first try with only minor mistakes at worst. Of course, if our QC flagged serious issues, we gave potential partners the chance to explain why we were incorrect. This strict requirement—along with provider reputation backchanneling—allows us to be confident in the quality of GDPx despite not having in-house expertise in every domain.

news.article_content_zh:
GDPx 是一个涵盖前沿情报最有价值领域的基准。它的目标是成为世界上衡量通用代理能力的最佳基准。

我们认为，第一万亿美元的人工智能收入将集中在能够以高投资回报率部署前沿智能的领域，而不是广泛扩散到整个经济。因此，根据 GDP 份额或 SOC/O*NET 职业分类建立通用基准是一个错误。如果您的目标是跟踪前沿模型的进展，您应该关注它们最有影响力的领域。

并有意放弃政府、房地产和保险等行业。

GDPx 是真正的前沿水平基准：即使是最好的模型得分也只有 12%。

来源：GDPx 值得强调的是，某些模型（例如 Opus 5.5 和 GPT-6 Astra）由于其安全分类器而将总体分数纳入沙袋。如果我们排除网络、生物学和一致性（安全分类器有时会发挥作用的三个领域），您会得到以下结果。

来源：GDPx 我们对这个排名与我们对模型的主观印象的吻合程度感到惊喜。 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 总体上占据了排名榜首，而 SpaceXAI、Meta 和开放权重模型都明显落后。 Gemini 4 Carbon 是 Google 的真正改进，也是唯一与 Opus 和 Astra 处于同一水平的型号。一旦 Carbon 普遍可用，看看人们的印象将会很有趣。

我们认为，在为某些用例选择最佳模型时，安全分类器的相关性被低估了。例如，Muse Wonder Full 实际上是当今最好的可用网络模型，并且具有显着的优势。

资料来源：GDPx 我们还普遍观察到所有领先模型都出现有意义的尖峰。

资料来源：GDPxOpus 5.5 是最好的全能模型，在量化交易、硬件设计和芯片设计方面获胜。 Gemini 4 Carbon 是最好的生物模型（可能是由于安全分类器较弱），并且在软件工程方面取得了胜利。 GPT-6 Astra 在 RSI 方面令人信服地获胜，也是材料科学的最佳模型。我们的财务和法律任务非常具有挑战性，基本上每个模型的得分都是 0。

有趣的是，如果您将其划分为单个模型系列，有时您会看到非常相似的峰值。

来源：GDPx 成本与性能帕累托前沿也符合我们使用模型的一般经验：Luna 和 DeepSeek 争夺低端，Opus 赢得高端，OpenAI 占据中端。不过，Gemini 4 Carbon的外观再次值得密切关注。

在过去的一年里，特定领域的基准测试有了显着的改善，这很大程度上要归功于专门的 RL 环境初创公司的崛起。然而，OpenAI 的 GDPval（及其衍生品，如 GDPval AA v2.1）仍然是主要新型号发布卡上报告的最受欢迎的通用基准。尽管这一消息是在一年多前的 2025 年 9 月 25 日发布的——这在人工智能领域是永恒的。 GDPval 可能已被宣传为“知识工作”基准，但代理还不是真正的东西。这对其任务设计产生了巨大影响，正如我们稍后将解释的，这使得 GDPval 严重不足以评估当今的前沿模型。

我们 GDPx 的目标是创建世界上通用代理能力的最佳基准。然而，当我们开始研究这个项目时，我们就清楚为什么我们还没有看到一个值得 GDPval 的继任者。 GPT-6 Astra 和 Opus 5.5 等模型已经在突破人类知识的界限。如果您想要完成一项财务或网络任务，这些模型只能解决 < 20% 的时间，您需要真正的领域专业知识来确保任务因正确的原因而困难。许多流行的基准通过传送完全不公平的任务来回避这个问题。这通常体现在评分器中，该评分器检查无法从任务描述或环境中推断出的要求。例如，编码问题可能要求模型修复一个人类工程师同意有两个有效解决方案的错误——一个使用“模块 A”，另一个使用“模块 B”。然而，设计不佳的评分器可能会要求人工智能使用“模块A”，而当人工智能选择“模块B”时，不公平地给予0奖励。纠正所有这些问题，基准通常最终会饱和。

为您拥有专业知识的单个领域制定高质量的任务已经足够困难了——这就是为什么实验室愿意为单个高质量任务支付 5,000 美元以上的原因。找到一家在人工智能评估和领域都拥有足够专业知识来制定广泛的 GDP 基准的公司是完全不可能的。

所有合作伙伴都必须遵守我们在方法部分详细介绍的严格的质量保证流程。对于某些领域，我们有多个合作伙伴想要独占，并运行了一个流程来选择任务质量最高的合作伙伴。

我们衷心感谢所有为 GDPx 做出贡献的合作伙伴。他们是各自领域的最佳供应商之一，如果没有他们的帮助，就不可能创建如此广泛的基准。

此外，我们要感谢 Fireworks 为所有开源模型提供推理，感谢 Modal 提供运行我们的任务所需的沙箱基础设施，还要感谢 Abhijay Rana 帮助寻找一些合作伙伴并协助进行早期 QA。

需要明确的是，我们认为 GDPval 在当时令人印象深刻，并且是第一个在如此广泛的任务上评估人工智能的基准。在智能体兴起之前创建的基准如今对它们的评估效果不佳，这并不是 OpenAI 的错。

每个 GDPval 任务都是精确指定的且非交互式的，所有必要的上下文都直接在提示中填入模型。请考虑以下具有代表性的财务示例：

来源：SemiAnalysis 此提示附带的是一个非常简单的单页 PDF，它为模型提供了有关这两个项目的更多背景信息。

用于 OpenAI GDPval 财务任务的实际文档。来源：OpenAI 从这里开始，模型被要求直接完成编写 15 页 pdf 的任务，以推荐两个选项之一。

尽管任务描述本身过于冗长，但总体任务缺乏有关“两个重要投资机会”的细节。该模型预计只会对这两个选项进行大约 500 字的高级描述，并将其转换为推荐其中一个选项的“最多 15 页”的 pdf 文件。正如您所料，即使是 OpenAI 的参考解决方案也主要是填料渣。

与此相关的是，该任务根本缺乏现实、丰富的环境。负责在两个投资机会之间提出建议的人类专家首先会进行大量研究来收集信息——通过 pdf、excel 模型、电子邮件等进行搜索。这种收集背景信息的过程是导致实际工作变得困难的一个重要部分，并且在 GDPval 中完全缺失。

理解第二点非常重要。 GDPval 的最大问题是不包括每项任务的特定领域的模拟工作环境。今天的代理已经远远超出了狭窄的、范围明确的任务，例如“根据下面附加的参考文件+几百字的提示生成 pdf/excel 文件/word 文档/powerpoint”，但基本上每个 GDPval 任务都符合这个确切的形状。至于工具，该模型只能访问网络搜索、代码解释器和修改 PDF、Word 文档、Excel 文件、PowerPoint、图像、音频和视频的库。

评分者完全基于评分标准，这通常很吵。人类专家评分者在黄金子集上的一致性仅为 71%，而他们的自动评分器甚至更差。

破碎的标准，标准模糊，标准不正确，有时甚至是完全错误的要求。

用作模型输出分级参考的不正确的黄金专家解决方案。

依赖于先前时​​间点且现在具有断开的链接、过时的价格等的任务。

来源：SemiAnalysis 该任务环境是由来自 Living Context 企业网络的真实交易生成的。其中，Bannock Capital（私募基金）以 8.8 亿美元加股息收购了 Haverly Snack Company 约 62% 的股份。 Eakin Lowry 是卖方银行家，Marbury Kline 是会计顾问。该环境由约 4000 个匿名文件组成，分为四类：Haverly 的虚拟数据室 (VDR) 以及 Bannock、Eakin 和 Marbury 的独立交易文件夹（当然都是假名）。

每项任务都是从班诺克、埃金或马伯里的角度执行的。 Haverly 的 VDR 始终与相应的交易文件夹一起加载到环境中。上面的具体例子是马伯里的一位同事在真实的交易中实际被要求做的会计任务。与 GDPval 任务不同的是，GDPval 任务会在提示中将所有相关上下文输入到模型中，而 AI 需要熟练地导航真实的约 2000 个文件处理室来收集正确的上下文，才能成功完成此任务，就像真正的人类同事所做的那样。

我们所有其他域都包含类似的丰富环境。网络任务基于 Arithmetic 安全工程师发现的真实零日漏洞，并包括环境中多个正在运行的服务。材料科学任务将模型放置在配备电池循环器、催化剂反应器、透射电子显微镜等的模拟实验室中。硬件设计任务包括西门子 NX 的实时会话以及在真实 AWS FPGA 实例上测试模型输出。这些只是几个例子，我们将在本文后面深入介绍我们的每个合作伙伴。

我们认为，根据 GDP 份额或 SOC/O*NET 职业分类法建立通用代理能力基准是错误的，因为人工智能扩散不会均匀分布，而且并非所有领域都需要前沿情报。因此，如果您的目标是跟踪前沿模型的进展，您应该关注它们最有影响力的领域。

从那里，我们联系了 30 多家在芯片设计、网络安全、生物学、RSI、材料科学等领域拥有专业知识的 RL 环境公司。每个潜在合作伙伴都受到同样严格的代理 QA（质量保证）流程的约束，该流程检查一致性、完整性、作弊、不公平验证者等等。我们的质量保证流程基于 Andrew 和 Max 之前共同创立一家 RL 环境初创公司的经验，该公司将数据出售给多个前沿实验室。当我们在 Terminal Bench 4.0 等流行基准上运行相同的 QA 流程时，它会将近 50% 的任务标记为已损坏。当然，我们还手动审查了数百个轨迹，以验证我们的自动化 QA 标记的内容，并捕获自动化 QA 通常不会标记的内容。我们还对任务进行故障模式分析，以确保我们的任务集是多样化的，并且即使在任务内，模型也会因各种原因而失败。

然而，我们也很清楚，只要有足够的迭代，任何 QA 系统都可以进行游戏。如果一项任务在 3-4 轮反馈后才通过 QA，那么就很难判断该任务是否真的变得很好，或者提供者是否只是欺骗了您的 QA 流程。

因此，所有合作伙伴都必须首先通过我们的自动质量检查，最坏的情况下也只能出现小错误。当然，如果我们的质量控制标记出严重问题，我们会给潜在合作伙伴机会来解释为什么我们是错误的。这一严格的要求以及提供商声誉反向渠道使我们对 GDPx 的质量充满信心，尽管我们并不具备每个领域的内部专业知识。

【起因与机理】认为应关注模型在实际经济产出领域的表现，而非泛化的大众基准
【关键数据与实测】揭露目前顶尖模型在专业领域得分仅12%。
【观点态度】倡导从“通用智力”向“经济价值”视角转变。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] To focus on actual economic impact rather than generalized, low-utility benchmarks
[Key Metrics] Exposes that leading models score only 12% in professional domains.
[Perspective & Impact] Advocates for a shift from 'general intelligence' to 'economic value' metrics.

celebrity.title_en:
Republicans earned this humiliation.

Newsflash for the GOP: campaigning on no new wars and lower prices, then starting a major war and raising prices, isn’t a good political strategy.

Trump and the Republican Party were handed a generational opportunity in 2024. 

Groups such as MAHA voters and young men, along with growing support among Hispanic and Muslim voters, helped give them a coalition that could have reshaped American politics for a generation.

They squandered it in two years.

What happened tonight is the opposite of political rocket science.

The GOP invited everyone into its “big tent,” then betrayed the people who showed up. 

Broken promises on virtually everything except closing the border. 

What did they expect would happen?

They confused support for their promises with unconditional loyalty to their party. 

They acted like winning an election meant they no longer had to listen to the people who won it for them.

The biggest slap in the face was to MAGA itself. 

Their most loyal supporters were promised a government that would finally put them first. 

Republicans cannot campaign on changing everything, fail to deliver on the things people care about most, and then blame those people for being angry.

The handling of the Epstein files, the promises surrounding DOGE being abandoned, and the endless cycle of big announcements followed with zero change or action only compounded the issue.

You cannot build an entire movement around exposing corruption and demanding accountability, then act offended when your own supporters demand both from you.

What exactly were Republicans asking voters to reward tonight? 

At some point, “the Democrats are worse” stops being a campaign and starts being an admission that you have nothing else to offer.

The Republican Party took an extraordinary political opening and turned it into a case study in arrogance, complacency, and wasted potential.

But you could argue this is the best possible outcome for Republicans before 2028. 

They just received a brutal warning while they still have two years to change course.

If their response is to blame voters, attack critics, and insist everything is going perfectly, they deserve what comes next.

Life after Trump is approaching. 

Republicans have to decide whether they will return to the neocon politics their own voters rejected, remain trapped in defending everything Trump does, or build a party capable of keeping its promises.

Democrats, meanwhile, have just been handed the opportunity Republicans wasted. 

Their biggest mistake would be assuming tonight means voters have embraced every part of the Democratic agenda.

Voters punishing Republicans is not a blank check for Democrats. 

If Democrats spend the next two years indulging their own ideological factions, letting the DSA set the direction, and dismissing concerns about affordability and everyday life, they will make the exact same mistake.

Republicans thought anger at Democrats would spare them from having to deliver. 

Democrats should not be stupid enough to believe anger at Republicans will spare them either.

Neither party owns the people who vote for it. 

Earn their trust, keep your promises, or expect to lose it.

celebrity.quote_zh:
共和党人应受这样的羞辱。

共和党的快讯：在竞选中主张不发动新的战争和降低价格，然后发动一场大规模战争并提高价格，这并不是一个好的政治策略。

2024 年，特朗普和共和党获得了一个世代相传的机会。

MAHA 选民和年轻人等团体，以及西班牙裔和穆斯林选民日益增长的支持，帮助他们建立了一个联盟，该联盟可能重塑一代人的美国政治。

两年之内他们就把它浪费掉了。

今晚发生的事情与政治火箭科学相反。

共和党邀请所有人进入它的“大帐篷”，然后背叛了出现的人。

除了关闭边境之外，几乎所有事情都没有兑现承诺。

他们期望会发生什么？

他们混淆了对自己承诺的支持和对政党的无条件忠诚。

他们表现得好像赢得选举意味着他们不再需要听取为他们赢得选举的人的意见。

最大的一记耳光是打给MAGA自己的。

他们最忠实的支持者得到了一个最终将他们放在第一位的政府的承诺。

共和党人不能在竞选中力图改变一切，未能实现人们最关心的事情，然后指责这些人的愤怒。

爱泼斯坦文件的处理、围绕 DOGE 的承诺被放弃，以及随之而来的无休止的重大公告、零变化或行动，只会让问题变得更加复杂。

你不能围绕揭露腐败和要求问责来发起一场完整的运动，然后当你自己的支持者要求你同时要求你做到这两点时，你又表现得被冒犯了。

共和党人今晚到底要求选民奖励什么？

在某种程度上，“民主党更糟糕”不再是一场竞选活动，而是开始承认你没有其他可提供的。

共和党采取了非同寻常的政治开放，并将其变成了傲慢、自满和浪费潜力的案例研究。

但你可能会说，这是共和党在 2028 年之前可能出现的最佳结果。

他们刚刚收到残酷的警告，而他们还有两年的时间改变路线。

如果他们的反应是指责选民、攻击批评者并坚称一切进展顺利，那么他们就活该承受接下来的后果。

特朗普之后的生活即将到来。

共和党人必须决定是否要回到被自己的选民拒绝的新保守主义政治，还是继续为特朗普所做的一切辩护，还是建立一个能够信守承诺的政党。

与此同时，民主党人刚刚获得了共和党人浪费的机会。

他们最大的错误是假设今晚意味着选民已经接受了民主党议程的各个部分。

选民惩罚共和党并不是民主党的空白支票。

如果民主党人在接下来的两年里放纵自己的意识形态派别，让 DSA 设定方向，并忽视对负担能力和日常生活的担忧，他们就会犯同样的错误。

共和党人认为对民主党人的愤怒会让他们不必兑现承诺。

民主党人不应该愚蠢到相信对共和党人的愤怒也会让他们幸免。

任何一方都不拥有投票给它的人。

赢得他们的信任，信守承诺，否则就会失去信任。

celebrity.title_en:
Republicans earned this humiliation.

Newsflash for the GOP: campaigning on no new wars and lower prices, then starting a major war and raising prices, isn’t a good political strategy.

Trump and the Republican Party were handed a generational opportunity in 2024. 

Groups such as MAHA voters and young men, along with growing support among Hispanic and Muslim voters, helped give them a coalition that could have reshaped American politics for a generation.

They squandered it in two years.

What happened tonight is the opposite of political rocket science.

The GOP invited everyone into its “big tent,” then betrayed the people who showed up. 

Broken promises on virtually everything except closing the border. 

What did they expect would happen?

They confused support for their promises with unconditional loyalty to their party. 

They acted like winning an election meant they no longer had to listen to the people who won it for them.

The biggest slap in the face was to MAGA itself. 

Their most loyal supporters were promised a government that would finally put them first. 

Republicans cannot campaign on changing everything, fail to deliver on the things people care about most, and then blame those people for being angry.

The handling of the Epstein files, the promises surrounding DOGE being abandoned, and the endless cycle of big announcements followed with zero change or action only compounded the issue.

You cannot build an entire movement around exposing corruption and demanding accountability, then act offended when your own supporters demand both from you.

What exactly were Republicans asking voters to reward tonight? 

At some point, “the Democrats are worse” stops being a campaign and starts being an admission that you have nothing else to offer.

The Republican Party took an extraordinary political opening and turned it into a case study in arrogance, complacency, and wasted potential.

But you could argue this is the best possible outcome for Republicans before 2028. 

They just received a brutal warning while they still have two years to change course.

If their response is to blame voters, attack critics, and insist everything is going perfectly, they deserve what comes next.

Life after Trump is approaching. 

Republicans have to decide whether they will return to the neocon politics their own voters rejected, remain trapped in defending everything Trump does, or build a party capable of keeping its promises.

Democrats, meanwhile, have just been handed the opportunity Republicans wasted. 

Their biggest mistake would be assuming tonight means voters have embraced every part of the Democratic agenda.

Voters punishing Republicans is not a blank check for Democrats. 

If Democrats spend the next two years indulging their own ideological factions, letting the DSA set the direction, and dismissing concerns about affordability and everyday life, they will make the exact same mistake.

Republicans thought anger at Democrats would spare them from having to deliver. 

Democrats should not be stupid enough to believe anger at Republicans will spare them either.

Neither party owns the people who vote for it. 

Earn their trust, keep your promises, or expect to lose it.

共和党的快讯：在竞选中主张不发动新的战争和降低价格，然后发动一场大规模战争并提高价格，这并不是一个好的政治策略。

2024 年，特朗普和共和党获得了一个世代相传的机会。

两年之内他们就把它浪费掉了。

共和党邀请所有人进入它的“大帐篷”，然后背叛了出现的人。

除了关闭边境之外，几乎所有事情都没有兑现承诺。

他们期望会发生什么？

他们混淆了对自己承诺的支持和对政党的无条件忠诚。

他们表现得好像赢得选举意味着他们不再需要听取为他们赢得选举的人的意见。

最大的一记耳光是打给MAGA自己的。

他们最忠实的支持者得到了一个最终将他们放在第一位的政府的承诺。

共和党人不能在竞选中力图改变一切，未能实现人们最关心的事情，然后指责这些人的愤怒。

共和党人今晚到底要求选民奖励什么？

在某种程度上，“民主党更糟糕”不再是一场竞选活动，而是开始承认你没有其他可提供的。

共和党采取了非同寻常的政治开放，并将其变成了傲慢、自满和浪费潜力的案例研究。

他们刚刚收到残酷的警告，而他们还有两年的时间改变路线。

如果他们的反应是指责选民、攻击批评者并坚称一切进展顺利，那么他们就活该承受接下来的后果。

特朗普之后的生活即将到来。

共和党人必须决定是否要回到被自己的选民拒绝的新保守主义政治，还是继续为特朗普所做的一切辩护，还是建立一个能够信守承诺的政党。

与此同时，民主党人刚刚获得了共和党人浪费的机会。

他们最大的错误是假设今晚意味着选民已经接受了民主党议程的各个部分。

选民惩罚共和党并不是民主党的空白支票。

如果民主党人在接下来的两年里放纵自己的意识形态派别，让 DSA 设定方向，并忽视对负担能力和日常生活的担忧，他们就会犯同样的错误。

共和党人认为对民主党人的愤怒会让他们不必兑现承诺。

民主党人不应该愚蠢到相信对共和党人的愤怒也会让他们幸免。

任何一方都不拥有投票给它的人。

赢得他们的信任，信守承诺，否则就会失去信任。

She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records ca
celebrity.title_en:
She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records can ruin lives.

GenLayer aims to settle AI-agent disputes in minutes: one AI validator proposes a verdict, others check independently, and decisions can be appealed.

On 27 March 2023, Alison MacPherson paid via RingGo on Hunter Street in Kirkcaldy. She typed 9 for 8 and missed the Z. A penalty followed.

Her receipt matched the time and place. A tribunal sided with her. Fife Council appealed. On 8 January 2024, the Upper Tribunal overturned it and sent it back.

The judge accepted her good faith, but the payment covered another car.

The payment was real. The registration wasn't hers.

Lee Castleton faced worse in the film: Horizon falsely showed a £23,000 gap. Without a lawyer, he faced £321,000 in legal costs and bankruptcy.

AI can't rewrite laws or guarantee truth. Millions of agent deals need evidence checked and decisions open to challenge.

If an AI agent pays under the wrong ID, what matters more: the receipt, the intent or the rule?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

celebrity.quote_zh:
她付了停车费。错误的数字和缺失的 Z 将她送上了法庭。

@GenLayer 的电影给我的震撼是：不良记录会毁掉生活。

GenLayer 的目标是在几分钟内解决人工智能代理纠纷：一名人工智能验证者提出裁决，其他人独立检查，并且可以对决定提出上诉。

celebrity.title_en:
People should always be in control of the future.

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people to be relegated to a role of doing things that “AI systems think makes sense to reward in humans”.

People should not cede control of the future to superintelligence, and that requirement should ultimately constrain AI progress.
celebrity.title_zh:
人们应该始终掌控未来。

OpenAI 反对这样一种观念，即人们被降级到做“人工智能系统认为对人类有意义的奖励”的事情是可以接受的。

人们不应该将对未来的控制权交给超级智能，而这一要求最终应该限制人工智能的进步。

celebrity.title: Google says its education updates give schools "more choice, not less"; Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search are off by default and can be enabled individually (@newsfromgoogle)
celebrity.title_en: Google says its education updates give schools "more choice, not less"; Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search are off by default and can be enabled individually (@newsfromgoogle)
celebrity.title_zh: 谷歌回应教育版AI更新：默认关闭
celebrity.author: @newsfromgoogle
celebrity.author_role: AI 先锋观察者
celebrity.content_snippet: Google says its education updates give schools "more choice, not less"; Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search are off by default and can be enabled individually (@newsfromgoogle)
celebrity.summary_en: Google announced that its education updates, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and AI Search, will be turned off by default, allowing schools to enable them individually. This move aims to address growing concerns from educators regarding student data privacy and classroom control.
celebrity.summary_zh: 谷歌针对教育界对AI工具的隐私与控制担忧，宣布旗下Gemini等AI功能在教育版中默认处于关闭状态。
celebrity.full_text_zh: 谷歌表示，其教育更新为学校提供了“更多选择，而不是更少”； Gemini、Gemini Notebook 和搜索默认处于关闭状态，可以单独启用
celebrity.quote_zh: 谷歌表示，其教育更新为学校提供了“更多选择，而不是更少”； Gemini、Gemini Notebook 和搜索默认处于关闭状态，可以单独启用
celebrity.full_text_en: Google says its education updates give schools "more choice, not less"; Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search are off by default and can be enabled individually (@newsfromgoogle)
celebrity.quote_en: Google says its education updates give schools "more choice, not less"; Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search are off by default and can be enabled individually (@newsfromgoogle)

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 谷歌在近期针对教育市场的技术更新中明确表示，其推出的Gemini、Gemini Notebook以及AI搜索等核心功能将默认处于关闭状态，学校可根据需求自行选择是否开启。此举旨在回应教育界对学生数据隐私和课堂控制权的长期担忧，试图通过交出选择权来缓解学校对大模型入校的抵触情绪。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Google announced that its education updates, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and AI Search, will be turned off by default, allowing schools to enable them individually. This move aims to address growing concerns from educators regarding student data privacy and classroom control.

elements_zh.where: 教育市场与产品更新场景
elements_zh.what: 宣布Gemini、Gemini Notebook和AI搜索在教育版中默认关闭，由学校自主选择是否开启
elements_zh.why: 回应教育界对AI工具隐私与控制权的担忧，降低学校对大模型入校的抵触

elements_en.what: Announced that Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and AI Search are disabled by default for schools to toggle individually
elements_en.why: To address educators' concerns over data privacy and classroom control regarding AI tools

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 说白了就是大厂把“翻车风险”打包贴心地送到了校长桌上：爱开不开，反正锅我们不背。毕竟比起教出个天才学生，学校更怕家长因为隐私问题把校董告上法庭。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Translation: Big Tech is gracefully handing the liability clipboard straight to school principals. They'd rather give you the 'choice' than handle another PTA panic over data privacy.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 谷歌在近期针对教育市场的技术更新中明确表示，其推出的Gemini、Gemini Notebook以及AI搜索等核心功能将默认处于关闭状态，学校可根据需求自行选择是否开启。此举旨在回应教育界对学生数据隐私和课堂控制权的长期担忧，试图通过交出选择权来缓解学校对大模型入校的抵触情绪。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Google announced that its education updates, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and AI Search, will be turned off by default, allowing schools to enable them individually. This move aims to address growing concerns from educators regarding student data privacy and classroom control.
key_points_zh: 谷歌面向教育市场推出Gemini等AI工具更新
相关AI功能默认关闭，支持学校按需独立开启
旨在缓解教育界对AI隐私与自主控制权的担忧
key_points_en: Google rolls out AI updates for the education market
Features are off by default, toggleable individually by schools
Aims to ease educators' concerns over privacy and control

celebrity.title_en:
Over the last 20 years across my various businesses I've spent over $15,000 on 'artists'.

Commissioned art work, stuff for streams, fliers, YT stuff, banners, logos, etc...  A few big ticket items, but lots of little projects.

It is hands down the most miserable, time wasting, and laborious processes I've ever experienced when it comes to dealing with contract work.  And I did contracts in heavy civil construction...

A few thousand pissed down the drain on referred artists that just ghosted me after taking deposits.

Thumbnail artists that think they know what is better on a thumbnail than I do, so they completely ignore directions and do their own thing...

Logos that are copy right infringements or such near copies of other work it's shameful.

1 in 5.  MAYBE.  That's how many acted like actual professionals, delivered work on time, did what was asked, and finished the work.  Almost all of those were corporate firms too, not individuals.

It's so bad I've mostly just avoided having to use the industry when ever possible.  But the next time a big project I need comes up I'm going to double book it.

I'll go the traditional route, and the AI route.  And that is what will decide how I spend my money, and more importantly my time, going forward.

The OP is right.  Artists aren't saving their own careers.  They are pushing people to other less shitty interactions, and have been for years.

The difference is, there was no other choice before.  There is now.

celebrity.title:
This is going to be a bit longer than usual:  

1. Tesla is building compute, just for our own highest-ROI use case Tesl
celebrity.title_en:
This is going to be a bit longer than usual:  

1. Tesla is building compute, just for our own highest-ROI use case Tesla’s Cortex 1 and Cortex 2 clusters at Giga Texas are already in production at well over 200 MW combined, with a stated target of ~400 MW of SI (Super Intelligence) training compute by the end of 2026.  That capacity is primarily for training vehicle autonomy/FSD and Optimus models, remember those? 
We are running an enormous fleet on FSD.  
The difference vs SpaceX/xAI is priority. xAI is a pure AI lab that needs massive generic training flops for frontier models (and can sell excess capacity to Anthropic and others). 
Tesla’s highest-value use of the same capital is our proprietary real-world data flywheel for cars and bots. 
Diverting significant capacity to external customers would slow the exact products that justify Tesla’s valuation premium today.  

2. Merchant GPU compute is a brutal business Tesla doesn’t need to enter Rapid GPU depreciation and stranded capacity risk are real (Elon has commented on half-built data centers and idle chips). 
Nvidia owns the silicon stack; hyperscalers and specialized neoclouds already dominate the rental market. 

Tesla’s actual competitive advantage in the AI infrastructure stack is energy, not training chips. It has already sold hundreds of millions to ~$1B of Megapacks into the Colossus buildouts. That’s higher-margin, more defensible, and leverages what Tesla already does at scale.⁠ 
Selling raw flops would put Tesla in direct competition with Nvidia, AWS, CoreWeave, etc., in a capital-intensive, fast-depreciating business where it has no structural edge.  

3. The Dojo experience is a cautionary tale Tesla shut down Dojo in 2025 after Elon called the Dojo 2 design an “evolutionary dead end” and much of the team left. The company pivoted hard to Nvidia for training clusters while focusing its own silicon (AI5/AI6 and later) on inference in vehicles and robots. Re-entering custom training hardware at scale just to become a merchant seller would repeat a hard lesson.⁠ 

However, all this chip know-how is not lost and used now in the Terafab pilot.  

4. SpaceX’s speed is real, but it’s solving a different problem Colossus 1  and 2 are impressive, and SpaceX’s construction/execution culture is a genuine advantage for pure data-center buildouts. 

Tesla’s construction teams are optimized for vehicle and energy product factories, not multi-gigawatt pure-play AI campuses. 

SpaceX/xAI also benefits from being able to treat excess capacity as a revenue stream; Tesla’s equivalent excess capacity is better used accelerating FSD and Optimus software.⁠  

5. On “build it and sell it to SpaceX” Tesla is already the power supplier to those clusters. 
The more logical path (if any) is modular hardware like the Megapod rather than competing head-on as a pure compute seller. Even then, SpaceX is currently the world’s fastest large-scale data-center builder. 

Tesla’s scarce capital and engineering bandwidth is better spent on the products only Tesla can ship  

So, to sum it up:  
Tesla is already scaling to 400 MW of training compute for its own FSD and Optimus needs. 
Merchant GPU rental is a low-moat, high-depreciation business that Nvidia and the hyperscalers already own. 
Tesla’s real AI infrastructure edge is energy and the proprietary physical-world data only its fleet generates. 
Selling flops to SpaceX or anyone else would just slow the higher-value autonomy and robotics timeline.

我们在 FSD 上运行着一支庞大的车队。
与 SpaceX/xAI 的区别在于优先级。 xAI 是一个纯粹的人工智能实验室，需要针对前沿模型进行大量通用训练失败（并且可以将多余的产能出售给 Anthropic 和其他公司）。
特斯拉对同一资本的最高价值用途是我们用于汽车和机器人的专有现实世界数据飞轮。
将大量产能转移给外部客户将会减缓产品的生产速度，而这些产品恰恰证明了特斯拉目前的估值溢价是合理的。

2.商用GPU计算是一项残酷的业务特斯拉不需要进入GPU快速折旧和搁浅容量风险是真实的（埃隆评论了半建成的数据中心和闲置芯片）。
Nvidia 拥有硅堆栈；超大规模和专业的新云已经主导了租赁市场。

特斯拉在人工智能基础设施堆栈上的实际竞争优势是能源，而不是训练芯片。它已经在 Colossus 的扩建中销售了数亿至约 10 亿美元的 Megapack。这是更高的利润，更具有防御性，并且利用了特斯拉已经大规模做的事情。⁠
出售原始失败产品将使特斯拉在资本密集型、快速贬值的业务中与英伟达、AWS、CoreWeave 等直接竞争，而特斯拉没有结构性优势。

3. Dojo 的经历是一个警示故事 在 Elon 称 Dojo 2 设计为“进化的死胡同”并且大部分团队成员离开后，特斯拉于 2025 年关闭了 Dojo。该公司大力转向 Nvidia 的训练集群，同时将自己的芯片（AI5/AI6 及更高版本）专注于车辆和机器人的推理。为了成为商人而重新大规模进入定制培训硬件将重复一个惨痛的教训。⁠

然而，所有这些芯片技术并没有丢失，并且现在已在 Terafab 试点中使用。

4. SpaceX 的速度是真实的，但它正在解决不同的问题 Colossus 1 和 2 令人印象深刻，并且 SpaceX 的构建/执行文化对于纯数据中心建设来说是真正的优势。

特斯拉的施工团队针对汽车和能源产品工厂进行了优化，而不是针对数千兆瓦的纯人工智能园区。

SpaceX/xAI 还受益于能够将过剩产能视为收入来源；特斯拉的等效过剩产能更好地用于加速 FSD 和 Optimus 软件。⁠

5.关于“建造它并将其出售给SpaceX”，特斯拉已经是这些集群的电力供应商。
更合乎逻辑的路径（如果有的话）是像 Megapod 这样的模块化硬件，而不是作为纯粹的计算销售商正面竞争。即便如此，SpaceX 仍是目前世界上最快的大型数据中心建设者。

特斯拉稀缺的资本和工程带宽最好用在只有特斯拉才能发货的产品上

所以，总结一下：
Tesla 已经将训练计算规模扩展到 400 MW，以满足其自身的 FSD 和 Optimus 需求。
商用 GPU 租赁是 Nvidia 和超大规模企业已经拥有的低护城河、高折旧业务。
特斯拉真正的人工智能基础设施优势是能源和只有其车队生成的专有物理世界数据。
向 SpaceX 或其他任何人出售失败的产品只会减慢更高价值的自主和机器人技术的开发进度。
celebrity.full_text_en:
This is going to be a bit longer than usual:  

1. Tesla is building compute, just for our own highest-ROI use case Tesla’s Cortex 1 and Cortex 2 clusters at Giga Texas are already in production at well over 200 MW combined, with a stated target of ~400 MW of SI (Super Intelligence) training compute by the end of 2026.  That capacity is primarily for training vehicle autonomy/FSD and Optimus models, remember those? 
We are running an enormous fleet on FSD.  
The difference vs SpaceX/xAI is priority. xAI is a pure AI lab that needs massive generic training flops for frontier models (and can sell excess capacity to Anthropic and others). 
Tesla’s highest-value use of the same capital is our proprietary real-world data flywheel for cars and bots. 
Diverting significant capacity to external customers would slow the exact products that justify Tesla’s valuation premium today.  

2. Merchant GPU compute is a brutal business Tesla doesn’t need to enter Rapid GPU depreciation and stranded capacity risk are real (Elon has commented on half-built data centers and idle chips). 
Nvidia owns the silicon stack; hyperscalers and specialized neoclouds already dominate the rental market. 

Tesla’s actual competitive advantage in the AI infrastructure stack is energy, not training chips. It has already sold hundreds of millions to ~$1B of Megapacks into the Colossus buildouts. That’s higher-margin, more defensible, and leverages what Tesla already does at scale.⁠ 
Selling raw flops would put Tesla in direct competition with Nvidia, AWS, CoreWeave, etc., in a capital-intensive, fast-depreciating business where it has no structural edge.  

3. The Dojo experience is a cautionary tale Tesla shut down Dojo in 2025 after Elon called the Dojo 2 design an “evolutionary dead end” and much of the team left. The company pivoted hard to Nvidia for training clusters while focusing its own silicon (AI5/AI6 and later) on inference in vehicles and robots. Re-entering custom training hardware at scale just to become a merchant seller would repeat a hard lesson.⁠ 

However, all this chip know-how is not lost and used now in the Terafab pilot.  

4. SpaceX’s speed is real, but it’s solving a different problem Colossus 1  and 2 are impressive, and SpaceX’s construction/execution culture is a genuine advantage for pure data-center buildouts. 

Tesla’s construction teams are optimized for vehicle and energy product factories, not multi-gigawatt pure-play AI campuses. 

SpaceX/xAI also benefits from being able to treat excess capacity as a revenue stream; Tesla’s equivalent excess capacity is better used accelerating FSD and Optimus software.⁠  

5. On “build it and sell it to SpaceX” Tesla is already the power supplier to those clusters. 
The more logical path (if any) is modular hardware like the Megapod rather than competing head-on as a pure compute seller. Even then, SpaceX is currently the world’s fastest large-scale data-center builder. 

Tesla’s scarce capital and engineering bandwidth is better spent on the products only Tesla can ship  

So, to sum it up:  
Tesla is already scaling to 400 MW of training compute for its own FSD and Optimus needs. 
Merchant GPU rental is a low-moat, high-depreciation business that Nvidia and the hyperscalers already own. 
Tesla’s real AI infrastructure edge is energy and the proprietary physical-world data only its fleet generates. 
Selling flops to SpaceX or anyone else would just slow the higher-value autonomy and robotics timeline.

celebrity.quote_zh:
这会比平常长一点：

1.特斯拉正在构建计算，只是为了我们自己的最高投资回报率用例特斯拉位于德克萨斯州 Giga 的 Cortex 1 和 Cortex 2 集群已经投入生产，总功率远超 200 MW，其既定目标是到 2026 年底实现约 400 MW 的 SI（超级智能）训练计算。该能力主要用于训练车辆自动驾驶/FSD 和 Optimus 模型，还记得那些吗？
我们在 FSD 上运行着一支庞大的车队。
与 SpaceX/xAI 的区别在于优先级。 xAI 是一个纯粹的人工智能实验室，需要针对前沿模型进行大量通用训练失败（并且可以将多余的产能出售给 Anthropic 和其他公司）。
特斯拉对同一资本的最高价值用途是我们用于汽车和机器人的专有现实世界数据飞轮。
将大量产能转移给外部客户将会减缓产品的生产速度，而这些产品恰恰证明了特斯拉目前的估值溢价是合理的。

2.商用GPU计算是一项残酷的业务特斯拉不需要进入GPU快速折旧和搁浅容量风险是真实的（埃隆评论了半建成的数据中心和闲置芯片）。
Nvidia 拥有硅堆栈；超大规模和专业的新云已经主导了租赁市场。

特斯拉在人工智能基础设施堆栈上的实际竞争优势是能源，而不是训练芯片。它已经在 Colossus 的扩建中销售了数亿至约 10 亿美元的 Megapack。这是更高的利润，更具有防御性，并且利用了特斯拉已经大规模做的事情。⁠
出售原始失败产品将使特斯拉在资本密集型、快速贬值的业务中与英伟达、AWS、CoreWeave 等直接竞争，而特斯拉没有结构性优势。

3. Dojo 的经历是一个警示故事 在 Elon 称 Dojo 2 设计为“进化的死胡同”并且大部分团队成员离开后，特斯拉于 2025 年关闭了 Dojo。该公司大力转向 Nvidia 的训练集群，同时将自己的芯片（AI5/AI6 及更高版本）专注于车辆和机器人的推理。为了成为商人而重新大规模进入定制培训硬件将重复一个惨痛的教训。⁠

然而，所有这些芯片技术并没有丢失，并且现在已在 Terafab 试点中使用。

4. SpaceX 的速度是真实的，但它正在解决不同的问题 Colossus 1 和 2 令人印象深刻，并且 SpaceX 的构建/执行文化对于纯数据中心建设来说是真正的优势。

特斯拉的施工团队针对汽车和能源产品工厂进行了优化，而不是针对数千兆瓦的纯人工智能园区。

SpaceX/xAI 还受益于能够将过剩产能视为收入来源；特斯拉的等效过剩产能更好地用于加速 FSD 和 Optimus 软件。⁠

5.关于“建造它并将其出售给SpaceX”，特斯拉已经是这些集群的电力供应商。
更合乎逻辑的路径（如果有的话）是像 Megapod 这样的模块化硬件，而不是作为纯粹的计算销售商正面竞争。即便如此，SpaceX 仍是目前世界上最快的大型数据中心建设者。

特斯拉稀缺的资本和工程带宽最好用在只有特斯拉才能发货的产品上

所以，总结一下：
Tesla 已经将训练计算规模扩展到 400 MW，以满足其自身的 FSD 和 Optimus 需求。
商用 GPU 租赁是 Nvidia 和超大规模企业已经拥有的低护城河、高折旧业务。
特斯拉真正的人工智能基础设施优势是能源和只有其车队生成的专有物理世界数据。
向 SpaceX 或其他任何人出售失败的产品只会减慢更高价值的自主和机器人技术的开发进度。

3. Dojo 的经历是一个警示故事 在 Elon 称 Dojo 2 设计为“进化的死胡同”并且大部分团队成员离开后，特斯拉于 2025 年关闭了 Dojo。该公司大力转向 Nvidia 的训练集群，同时将自己的芯片（AI5/AI6 及更高版本）专注于车辆和机器人的推理。为了成为商人而重新大规模进入定制培训硬件将重复一个惨痛的教训。⁠

然而，所有这些芯片技术并没有丢失，并且现在已在 Terafab 试点中使用。

4. SpaceX 的速度是真实的，但它正在解决不同的问题 Colossus 1 和 2 令人印象深刻，并且 SpaceX 的构建/执行文化对于纯数据中心建设来说是真正的优势。

特斯拉的施工团队针对汽车和能源产品工厂进行了优化，而不是针对数千兆瓦的纯人工智能园区。

SpaceX/xAI 还受益于能够将过剩产能视为收入来源；特斯拉的等效过剩产能更好地用于加速 FSD 和 Optimus 软件。⁠

5.关于“建造它并将其出售给SpaceX”，特斯拉已经是这些集群的电力供应商。
更合乎逻辑的路径（如果有的话）是像 Megapod 这样的模块化硬件，而不是作为纯粹的计算销售商正面竞争。即便如此，SpaceX 仍是目前世界上最快的大型数据中心建设者。

特斯拉稀缺的资本和工程带宽最好用在只有特斯拉才能发货的产品上

所以，总结一下：
Tesla 已经将训练计算规模扩展到 400 MW，以满足其自身的 FSD 和 Optimus 需求。
商用 GPU 租赁是 Nvidia 和超大规模企业已经拥有的低护城河、高折旧业务。
特斯拉真正的人工智能基础设施优势是能源和只有其车队生成的专有物理世界数据。
向 SpaceX 或其他任何人出售失败的产品只会减慢更高价值的自主和机器人技术的开发进度。

celebrity.title_en:
Thank you + some unfiltered thoughts.

I wanted to start by thanking everyone who took the time to watch my film, either online or in Marfa, and everyone who collected a print. It genuinely means a lot to me.

Over the years, this space has become smaller and smaller, both on the artist and collector sides. It's been a journey of experimentation, evolution and constant adaptation to the market. Many people have left, while a much smaller group has continued to believe in this space and what we're building.

We've moved through NFTs, digital art, physical art and everything in between. And now, I feel like we're left with a small group of passionate artists, collectors and individuals who genuinely enjoy being here, regardless of where the market is going.

As a landscape photographer, I've experienced my fair share of highs and lows. We all know photography has had a complicated relationship with the NFT and digital art space, with many people questioning its value, its place in the art world, or simply not connecting with the medium.

I was fortunate enough to be one of the first photographers on SuperRare in 2021, and my life has never been the same since.

I've had the opportunity to work on some incredible projects, like FreeHawaiiPhoto, where I introduced the idea of CC0 to the space and later watched many artists and major NFT projects embrace it. I had the chance to experiment with AI very early on in 2021, and eventually did a commission that took me all the way to China, thanks to a collector who believed in my vision.

I'm extremely proud of my journey and what I've contributed to this space. I haven't always been perfect, and there are certainly things I would do differently today, but I've always tried to advocate for artists, and especially photographers.

In 2023, I dedicated an entire year of my life to writing and creating a children's book based on a true story. I released it as a high-end limited edition combining physical books and NFTs. It unfortunately didn't have the success I had hoped for. Recently, I packed away all the remaining books and put them into storage. And strangely, I didn't feel sadness. I felt an immense sense of pride.

Pride in having followed an idea I deeply believed in, even if it didn't resonate with as many people as I had hoped. Pride in having created something beautiful, meaningful and completely different from anything I had done before. Of course, some things could have been better, but I genuinely believe I created a beautiful and inspiring story that future generations will appreciate.

It reminded me how important it is to pursue something you're truly passionate about, even when people don't understand it, even when the outcome isn't what you expected.

Three years later, I found myself in Marfa, presenting my first short documentary in front of about a hundred people.

And even though our space has become significantly smaller, I genuinely felt the warmth, kindness and compassion of this little community.

My film wasn't about NFTs or generative art. It was about mountains, physical endurance, personal growth and my relationship with photography. And yet, people showed up. They watched, they listened, they asked questions, and some connected with the work enough to collect a physical print.

That meant more to me than I can properly express.

I've dedicated the past decade of my life to photography and the mountains. That fire has burned brighter at certain moments than others, but it has never stopped growing. If anything, I feel more connected to what I create today than ever before.

Marfa was incredibly special to me. I hadn't felt that supported and appreciated in a long time. It also reminded me that genuine human connections, conversations and shared experiences will always mean more than likes or numbers on social media.

I have so much gratitude for the people who recognize that fire in me and continue to show their support, in whatever way they can.

Being an independent artist in 2026 is hard. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

Here, hard work doesn't always translate into success. You constantly have to challenge yourself, adapt, be more vocal, more confident, more visible, more of everything. Creating the art itself is only a small part of what it takes to make a living from it.

And I know this isn't unique to artists. It's the reality of running almost any business. Having a great product, or creating something you're deeply proud of, is rarely enough on its own.

But through all the ups and downs, the experiments that worked and the ones that didn't, this community has remained by far one of the most engaged and supportive I've ever had.

I don't know exactly where this space is going, or what it will look like in a few years. But I know that some of the most meaningful opportunities, experiences and human connections of my life came from being part of it.

And for that, I will always be grateful.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that success doesn't always look the way we imagined it would. Sometimes it's a sold-out release, sometimes it's a project that barely sells, and sometimes it's a room full of people who genuinely care about something you've poured your heart into.

And I'm learning to appreciate all of it.

If you've made it this far, thank you for reading, for being here, and for continuing to support what I create. It means more than you know. 💙

celebrity.quote_zh:
谢谢你+一些未经过滤的想法。

首先，我想感谢所有花时间在网上或马尔法观看我的电影的人，以及所有收集印刷品的人。这对我来说确实意义重大。

多年来，无论是对于艺术家还是收藏家来说，这个空间都变得越来越小。这是一个实验、进化和不断适应市场的旅程。许多人已经离开，而一小部分人仍然相信这个领域和我们正在建设的东西。

我们已经经历了 NFT、数字艺术、实体艺术以及介于两者之间的一切。现在，我觉得我们留下了一小群充满热情的艺术家、收藏家和个人，他们真正喜欢在这里，无论市场走向何方。

作为一名风光摄影师，我经历过不少的高潮和低谷。我们都知道摄影与 NFT 和数字艺术空间有着复杂的关系，许多人质疑它的价值、它在艺术世界中的地位，或者干脆与媒体没有联系。

我很幸运成为 2021 年 SuperRare 的第一批摄影师之一，从那以后我的生活就不再一样了。

我有机会参与一些令人难以置信的项目，比如 FreeHawaiiPhoto，我在其中引入了 CC0 的想法，后来看到许多艺术家和主要的 NFT 项目都接受了它。我很早就有机会在 2021 年尝试人工智能，并最终完成了一项委托，将我带到了中国，这要感谢一位相信我愿景的收藏家。

我对我的旅程以及我为这个领域做出的贡献感到非常自豪。我并不总是完美的，今天我肯定会做一些不同的事情，但我一直试图为艺术家，尤其是摄影师辩护。

2023年，我用了整整一年的时间来写作和创作一本根据真实故事改编的儿童读物。我将其作为实体书和 NFT 相结合的高端限量版发布。不幸的是，它没有取得我所希望的成功。最近，我把剩下的书全部收起来，入库。奇怪的是，我并没有感到悲伤。我感到一种巨大的自豪感。

为遵循自己深信不疑的想法而感到自豪，即使它没有像我希望的那样引起那么多人的共鸣。为创造了一些美丽、有意义且与我以前所做的完全不同的东西而感到自豪。当然，有些事情本来可以做得更好，但我真诚地相信我创造了一个美丽而鼓舞人心的故事，子孙后代将会欣赏。

它提醒我追求你真正热爱的事情是多么重要，即使人们不理解它，即使结果不是你所期望的。

三年后，我来到了马尔法，在大约一百人面前展示了我的第一部短片纪录片。

尽管我们的空间变得越来越小，但我确实感受到了这个小社区的温暖、善良和同情心。

我的电影与 NFT 或生成艺术无关。这是关于山脉、身体耐力、个人成长以及我与摄影的关系。然而，人们还是出现了。他们观看、聆听、提出问题，其中一些人与作品的联系足以收集实物印刷品。

这对我来说意义重大，超出了我所能正确表达的范围。

我将生命的过去十年奉献给了摄影和山脉。这团火在某些时刻比其他时刻燃烧得更猛烈，但它从未停止增长。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是我感觉自己与今天所创造的东西的联系比以往任何时候都更加紧密。

玛法对我来说非常特别。我已经很久没有感受到这样的支持和赞赏了。它还提醒我，真正的人际关系、对话和分享的经历永远比社交媒体上的点赞或数字更有意义。

我非常感谢那些认识到我内心的火焰并继续以任何方式表示支持的人们。

2026 年成为一名独立艺术家很困难。我不会假装不是这样。

在这里，努力工作并不总是能转化为成功。你必须不断地挑战自己、适应、更加直言不讳、更加自信、更加引人注目，等等。创作艺术本身只是靠艺术谋生的一小部分。

我知道这并不是艺术家独有的。这是几乎所有企业经营的现实。拥有一款出色的产品，或者创造出令您深感自豪的东西，仅靠其本身是远远不够的。

但经历了所有的起起落落，经历了成功和失败的实验，这个社区迄今为止仍然是我所拥有过的最积极参与和支持的社区之一。

我不知道这个空间到底会走向何方，也不知道几年后它会是什么样子。但我知道，我一生中一些最有意义的机会、经历和人际关系都来自于其中。

为此，我将永远心怀感激。

我想我想说的是，成功并不总是像我们想象的那样。有时它是一个售罄的版本，有时它是一个几乎卖不出去的项目，有时它是一个房间里挤满了真正关心你倾注心血的人。

我正在学着欣赏这一切。

如果您已经读到这里，感谢您的阅读、来到这里并继续支持我的创作。这意味着比你知道的更多。 💙

三年后，我来到了马尔法，在大约一百人面前展示了我的第一部短片纪录片。

尽管我们的空间变得越来越小，但我确实感受到了这个小社区的温暖、善良和同情心。

我的电影与 NFT 或生成艺术无关。这是关于山脉、身体耐力、个人成长以及我与摄影的关系。然而，人们还是出现了。他们观看、聆听、提出问题，其中一些人与作品的联系足以收集实物印刷品。

这对我来说意义重大，超出了我所能正确表达的范围。

我将生命的过去十年奉献给了摄影和山脉。这团火在某些时刻比其他时刻燃烧得更猛烈，但它从未停止增长。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是我感觉自己与今天所创造的东西的联系比以往任何时候都更加紧密。

玛法对我来说非常特别。我已经很久没有感受到这样的支持和赞赏了。它还提醒我，真正的人际关系、对话和分享的经历永远比社交媒体上的点赞或数字更有意义。

我非常感谢那些认识到我内心的火焰并继续以任何方式表示支持的人们。

2026 年成为一名独立艺术家很困难。我不会假装不是这样。

在这里，努力工作并不总是能转化为成功。你必须不断地挑战自己、适应、更加直言不讳、更加自信、更加引人注目，等等。创作艺术本身只是靠艺术谋生的一小部分。

我知道这并不是艺术家独有的。这是几乎所有企业经营的现实。拥有一款出色的产品，或者创造出令您深感自豪的东西，仅靠其本身是远远不够的。

但经历了所有的起起落落，经历了成功和失败的实验，这个社区迄今为止仍然是我所拥有过的最积极参与和支持的社区之一。

我不知道这个空间到底会走向何方，也不知道几年后它会是什么样子。但我知道，我一生中一些最有意义的机会、经历和人际关系都来自于其中。

为此，我将永远心怀感激。

我想我想说的是，成功并不总是像我们想象的那样。有时它是一个售罄的版本，有时它是一个几乎卖不出去的项目，有时它是一个房间里挤满了真正关心你倾注心血的人。

我正在学着欣赏这一切。

如果您已经读到这里，感谢您的阅读、来到这里并继续支持我的创作。这意味着比你知道的更多。 💙

celebrity.content_snippet:
Thank you + some unfiltered thoughts.

I wanted to start by thanking everyone who took the time to watch my film, either online or in Marfa, and everyone who collected a print. It genuinely means a lot to me.

Over the years, this space has become smaller and smaller, both on the artist and collector sides. It's been a journey of experimentation, evolution and constant adaptation to the market. Many people have left, while a much smaller group has continued to believe in this space and what we're building.

We've moved through NFTs, digital art, physical art and everything in between. And now, I feel like we're left with a small group of passionate artists, collectors and individuals who genuinely enjoy being here, regardless of where the market is going.

As a landscape photographer, I've experienced my fair share of highs and lows. We all know photography has had a complicated relationship with the NFT and digital art space, with many people questioning its value, its place in the art world, or simply not connecting with the medium.

I was fortunate enough to be one of the first photographers on SuperRare in 2021, and my life has never been the same since.

I've had the opportunity to work on some incredible projects, like FreeHawaiiPhoto, where I introduced the idea of CC0 to the space and later watched many artists and major NFT projects embrace it. I had the chance to experiment with AI very early on in 2021, and eventually did a commission that took me all the way to China, thanks to a collector who believed in my vision.

I'm extremely proud of my journey and what I've contributed to this space. I haven't always been perfect, and there are certainly things I would do differently today, but I've always tried to advocate for artists, and especially photographers.

In 2023, I dedicated an entire year of my life to writing and creating a children's book based on a true story. I released it as a high-end limited edition combining physical books and NFTs. It unfortunately didn't have the success I had hoped for. Recently, I packed away all the remaining books and put them into storage. And strangely, I didn't feel sadness. I felt an immense sense of pride.

Pride in having followed an idea I deeply believed in, even if it didn't resonate with as many people as I had hoped. Pride in having created something beautiful, meaningful and completely different from anything I had done before. Of course, some things could have been better, but I genuinely believe I created a beautiful and inspiring story that future generations will appreciate.

It reminded me how important it is to pursue something you're truly passionate about, even when people don't understand it, even when the outcome isn't what you expected.

Three years later, I found myself in Marfa, presenting my first short documentary in front of about a hundred people.

And even though our space has become significantly smaller, I genuinely felt the warmth, kindness and compassion of this little community.

My film wasn't about NFTs or generative art. It was about mountains, physical endurance, personal growth and my relationship with photography. And yet, people showed up. They watched, they listened, they asked questions, and some connected with the work enough to collect a physical print.

That meant more to me than I can properly express.

I've dedicated the past decade of my life to photography and the mountains. That fire has burned brighter at certain moments than others, but it has never stopped growing. If anything, I feel more connected to what I create today than ever before.

Marfa was incredibly special to me. I hadn't felt that supported and appreciated in a long time. It also reminded me that genuine human connections, conversations and shared experiences will always mean more than likes or numbers on social media.

I have so much gratitude for the people who recognize that fire in me and continue to show their support, in whatever way they can.

Being an independent artist in 2026 is hard. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

Here, hard work doesn't always translate into success. You constantly have to challenge yourself, adapt, be more vocal, more confident, more visible, more of everything. Creating the art itself is only a small part of what it takes to make a living from it.

And I know this isn't unique to artists. It's the reality of running almost any business. Having a great product, or creating something you're deeply proud of, is rarely enough on its own.

But through all the ups and downs, the experiments that worked and the ones that didn't, this community has remained by far one of the most engaged and supportive I've ever had.

I don't know exactly where this space is going, or what it will look like in a few years. But I know that some of the most meaningful opportunities, experiences and human connections of my life came from being part of it.

And for that, I will always be grateful.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that success doesn't always look the way we imagined it would. Sometimes it's a sold-out release, sometimes it's a project that barely sells, and sometimes it's a room full of people who genuinely care about something you've poured your heart into.

And I'm learning to appreciate all of it.

If you've made it this far, thank you for reading, for being here, and for continuing to support what I create. It means more than you know. 💙

But through all the ups and downs, the experiments that worked and the ones that didn't, this community has remained by far one of the most engaged and supportive I've ever had.

I don't know exactly where this space is going, or what it will look like in a few years. But I know that some of the most meaningful opportunities, experiences and human connections of my life came from being part of it.

And for that, I will always be grateful.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that success doesn't always look the way we imagined it would. Sometimes it's a sold-out release, sometimes it's a project that barely sells, and sometimes it's a room full of people who genuinely care about something you've poured your heart into.

And I'm learning to appreciate all of it.

If you've made it this far, thank you for reading, for being here, and for continuing to support what I create. It means more than you know. 💙

我们已经经历了 NFT、数字艺术、实体艺术以及介于两者之间的一切。现在，我觉得我们留下了一小群充满热情的艺术家、收藏家和个人，他们真正喜欢在这里，无论市场走向何方。

我很幸运成为 2021 年 SuperRare 的第一批摄影师之一，从那以后我的生活就不再一样了。

我对我的旅程以及我为这个领域做出的贡献感到非常自豪。我并不总是完美的，今天我肯定会做一些不同的事情，但我一直试图为艺术家，尤其是摄影师辩护。

2023年，我用了整整一年的时间来写作和创作一本根据真实故事改编的儿童读物。我将其作为实体书和 NFT 相结合的高端限量版发布。不幸的是，它没有取得我所希望的成功。最近，我把剩下的书全部收起来，入库。奇怪的是，我并没有感到悲伤。我感到一种巨大的自豪感。

为遵循自己深信不疑的想法而感到自豪，即使它没有像我希望的那样引起那么多人的共鸣。为创造了一些美丽、有意义且与我以前所做的完全不同的东西而感到自豪。当然，有些事情本来可以做得更好，但我真诚地相信我创造了一个美丽而鼓舞人心的故事，子孙后代将会欣赏。

它提醒我追求你真正热爱的事情是多么重要，即使人们不理解它，即使结果不是你所期望的。

三年后，我来到了马尔法，在大约一百人面前展示了我的第一部短片纪录片。

尽管我们的空间变得越来越小，但我确实感受到了这个小社区的温暖、善良和同情心。

我的电影与 NFT 或生成艺术无关。这是关于山脉、身体耐力、个人成长以及我与摄影的关系。然而，人们还是出现了。他们观看、聆听、提出问题，其中一些人与作品的联系足以收集实物印刷品。

这对我来说意义重大，超出了我所能正确表达的范围。

我将生命的过去十年奉献给了摄影和山脉。这团火在某些时刻比其他时刻燃烧得更猛烈，但它从未停止增长。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是我感觉自己与今天所创造的东西的联系比以往任何时候都更加紧密。

玛法对我来说非常特别。我已经很久没有感受到这样的支持和赞赏了。它还提醒我，真正的人际关系、对话和分享的经历永远比社交媒体上的点赞或数字更有意义。

我非常感谢那些认识到我内心的火焰并继续以任何方式表示支持的人们。

2026 年成为一名独立艺术家很困难。我不会假装不是这样。

在这里，努力工作并不总是能转化为成功。你必须不断地挑战自己、适应、更加直言不讳、更加自信、更加引人注目，等等。创作艺术本身只是靠艺术谋生的一小部分。

我知道这并不是艺术家独有的。这是几乎所有企业经营的现实。拥有一款出色的产品，或者创造出令您深感自豪的东西，仅靠其本身是远远不够的。

但经历了所有的起起落落，经历了成功和失败的实验，这个社区迄今为止仍然是我所拥有过的最积极参与和支持的社区之一。

我不知道这个空间到底会走向何方，也不知道几年后它会是什么样子。但我知道，我一生中一些最有意义的机会、经历和人际关系都来自于其中。

为此，我将永远心怀感激。

我想我想说的是，成功并不总是像我们想象的那样。有时它是一个售罄的版本，有时它是一个几乎卖不出去的项目，有时它是一个房间里挤满了真正关心你倾注心血的人。

我正在学着欣赏这一切。

如果您已经读到这里，感谢您的阅读、来到这里并继续支持我的创作。这意味着比你知道的更多。 💙
celebrity.full_text_en:
Thank you + some unfiltered thoughts.

I wanted to start by thanking everyone who took the time to watch my film, either online or in Marfa, and everyone who collected a print. It genuinely means a lot to me.

Over the years, this space has become smaller and smaller, both on the artist and collector sides. It's been a journey of experimentation, evolution and constant adaptation to the market. Many people have left, while a much smaller group has continued to believe in this space and what we're building.

We've moved through NFTs, digital art, physical art and everything in between. And now, I feel like we're left with a small group of passionate artists, collectors and individuals who genuinely enjoy being here, regardless of where the market is going.

As a landscape photographer, I've experienced my fair share of highs and lows. We all know photography has had a complicated relationship with the NFT and digital art space, with many people questioning its value, its place in the art world, or simply not connecting with the medium.

I was fortunate enough to be one of the first photographers on SuperRare in 2021, and my life has never been the same since.

I've had the opportunity to work on some incredible projects, like FreeHawaiiPhoto, where I introduced the idea of CC0 to the space and later watched many artists and major NFT projects embrace it. I had the chance to experiment with AI very early on in 2021, and eventually did a commission that took me all the way to China, thanks to a collector who believed in my vision.

I'm extremely proud of my journey and what I've contributed to this space. I haven't always been perfect, and there are certainly things I would do differently today, but I've always tried to advocate for artists, and especially photographers.

In 2023, I dedicated an entire year of my life to writing and creating a children's book based on a true story. I released it as a high-end limited edition combining physical books and NFTs. It unfortunately didn't have the success I had hoped for. Recently, I packed away all the remaining books and put them into storage. And strangely, I didn't feel sadness. I felt an immense sense of pride.

Pride in having followed an idea I deeply believed in, even if it didn't resonate with as many people as I had hoped. Pride in having created something beautiful, meaningful and completely different from anything I had done before. Of course, some things could have been better, but I genuinely believe I created a beautiful and inspiring story that future generations will appreciate.

It reminded me how important it is to pursue something you're truly passionate about, even when people don't understand it, even when the outcome isn't what you expected.

Three years later, I found myself in Marfa, presenting my first short documentary in front of about a hundred people.

And even though our space has become significantly smaller, I genuinely felt the warmth, kindness and compassion of this little community.

My film wasn't about NFTs or generative art. It was about mountains, physical endurance, personal growth and my relationship with photography. And yet, people showed up. They watched, they listened, they asked questions, and some connected with the work enough to collect a physical print.

That meant more to me than I can properly express.

I've dedicated the past decade of my life to photography and the mountains. That fire has burned brighter at certain moments than others, but it has never stopped growing. If anything, I feel more connected to what I create today than ever before.

Marfa was incredibly special to me. I hadn't felt that supported and appreciated in a long time. It also reminded me that genuine human connections, conversations and shared experiences will always mean more than likes or numbers on social media.

I have so much gratitude for the people who recognize that fire in me and continue to show their support, in whatever way they can.

Being an independent artist in 2026 is hard. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

Here, hard work doesn't always translate into success. You constantly have to challenge yourself, adapt, be more vocal, more confident, more visible, more of everything. Creating the art itself is only a small part of what it takes to make a living from it.

And I know this isn't unique to artists. It's the reality of running almost any business. Having a great product, or creating something you're deeply proud of, is rarely enough on its own.

But through all the ups and downs, the experiments that worked and the ones that didn't, this community has remained by far one of the most engaged and supportive I've ever had.

I don't know exactly where this space is going, or what it will look like in a few years. But I know that some of the most meaningful opportunities, experiences and human connections of my life came from being part of it.

And for that, I will always be grateful.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that success doesn't always look the way we imagined it would. Sometimes it's a sold-out release, sometimes it's a project that barely sells, and sometimes it's a room full of people who genuinely care about something you've poured your heart into.

And I'm learning to appreciate all of it.

If you've made it this far, thank you for reading, for being here, and for continuing to support what I create. It means more than you know. 💙

celebrity.content_snippet:
Thank you + some unfiltered thoughts.

I wanted to start by thanking everyone who took the time to watch my film, either online or in Marfa, and everyone who collected a print. It genuinely means a lot to me.

Over the years, this space has become smaller and smaller, both on the artist and collector sides. It's been a journey of experimentation, evolution and constant adaptation to the market. Many people have left, while a much smaller group has continued to believe in this space and what we're building.

We've moved through NFTs, digital art, physical art and everything in between. And now, I feel like we're left with a small group of passionate artists, collectors and individuals who genuinely enjoy being here, regardless of where the market is going.

As a landscape photographer, I've experienced my fair share of highs and lows. We all know photography has had a complicated relationship with the NFT and digital art space, with many people questioning its value, its place in the art world, or simply not connecting with the medium.

I was fortunate enough to be one of the first photographers on SuperRare in 2021, and my life has never been the same since.

I've had the opportunity to work on some incredible projects, like FreeHawaiiPhoto, where I introduced the idea of CC0 to the space and later watched many artists and major NFT projects embrace it. I had the chance to experiment with AI very early on in 2021, and eventually did a commission that took me all the way to China, thanks to a collector who believed in my vision.

I'm extremely proud of my journey and what I've contributed to this space. I haven't always been perfect, and there are certainly things I would do differently today, but I've always tried to advocate for artists, and especially photographers.

In 2023, I dedicated an entire year of my life to writing and creating a children's book based on a true story. I released it as a high-end limited edition combining physical books and NFTs. It unfortunately didn't have the success I had hoped for. Recently, I packed away all the remaining books and put them into storage. And strangely, I didn't feel sadness. I felt an immense sense of pride.

Pride in having followed an idea I deeply believed in, even if it didn't resonate with as many people as I had hoped. Pride in having created something beautiful, meaningful and completely different from anything I had done before. Of course, some things could have been better, but I genuinely believe I created a beautiful and inspiring story that future generations will appreciate.

It reminded me how important it is to pursue something you're truly passionate about, even when people don't understand it, even when the outcome isn't what you expected.

Three years later, I found myself in Marfa, presenting my first short documentary in front of about a hundred people.

And even though our space has become significantly smaller, I genuinely felt the warmth, kindness and compassion of this little community.

My film wasn't about NFTs or generative art. It was about mountains, physical endurance, personal growth and my relationship with photography. And yet, people showed up. They watched, they listened, they asked questions, and some connected with the work enough to collect a physical print.

That meant more to me than I can properly express.

I've dedicated the past decade of my life to photography and the mountains. That fire has burned brighter at certain moments than others, but it has never stopped growing. If anything, I feel more connected to what I create today than ever before.

Marfa was incredibly special to me. I hadn't felt that supported and appreciated in a long time. It also reminded me that genuine human connections, conversations and shared experiences will always mean more than likes or numbers on social media.

I have so much gratitude for the people who recognize that fire in me and continue to show their support, in whatever way they can.

Being an independent artist in 2026 is hard. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

Here, hard work doesn't always translate into success. You constantly have to challenge yourself, adapt, be more vocal, more confident, more visible, more of everything. Creating the art itself is only a small part of what it takes to make a living from it.

And I know this isn't unique to artists. It's the reality of running almost any business. Having a great product, or creating something you're deeply proud of, is rarely enough on its own.

But through all the ups and downs, the experiments that worked and the ones that didn't, this community has remained by far one of the most engaged and supportive I've ever had.

I don't know exactly where this space is going, or what it will look like in a few years. But I know that some of the most meaningful opportunities, experiences and human connections of my life came from being part of it.

And for that, I will always be grateful.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that success doesn't always look the way we imagined it would. Sometimes it's a sold-out release, sometimes it's a project that barely sells, and sometimes it's a room full of people who genuinely care about something you've poured your heart into.

And I'm learning to appreciate all of it.

If you've made it this far, thank you for reading, for being here, and for continuing to support what I create. It means more than you know. 💙

I guess what I'm trying to say is that success doesn't always look the way we imagined it would. Sometimes it's a sold-out release, sometimes it's a project that barely sells, and sometimes it's a room full of people who genuinely care about something you've poured your heart into.

And I'm learning to appreciate all of it.

If you've made it this far, thank you for reading, for being here, and for continuing to support what I create. It means more than you know. 💙
celebrity.summary_zh:
程。许多人已经离开，而一小部分人仍然相信这个领域和我们正在建设的东西。

我们已经经历了 NFT、数字艺术、实体艺术以及介于两者之间的一切。现在，我觉得我们留下了一小群充满热情的艺术家、收藏家和个人，他们真正喜欢在这里，无论市场走向何方。

作为一名风光摄影师，我经历过不少的高潮和低谷。我们都知道摄影与 NFT 和数字艺术空间有着复杂的关系，许多人质疑它的价值、它在艺术世界中的地位，或者干脆与媒体没有联系。

我很幸运成为 2021 年 SuperRare 的第一批摄影师之一，从那以后我的生活就不再一样了。

我有机会参与一些令人难以置信的项目，比如 FreeHawaiiPhoto，我在其中引入了 CC0 的想法，后来看到许多艺术家和主要的 NFT 项目都接受了它。我很早就有机会在 2021 年尝试人工智能，并最终完成了一项委托，将我带到了中国，这要感谢一位相信我愿景的收藏家。

我对我的旅程以及我为这个领域做出的贡献感到非常自豪。我并不总是完美的，今天我肯定会做一些不同的事情，但我一直试图为艺术家，尤其是摄影师辩护。

2023年，我用了整整一年的时间来写作和创作一本根据真实故事改编的儿童读物。我将其作为实体书和 NFT 相结合的高端限量版发布。不幸的是，它没有取得我所希望的成功。最近，我把剩下的书全部收起来，入库。奇怪的是，我并没有感到悲伤。我感到一种巨大的自豪感。

为遵循自己深信不疑的想法而感到自豪，即使它没有像我希望的那样引起那么多人的共鸣。为创造了一些美丽、有意义且与我以前所做的完全不同的东西而感到自豪。当然，有些事情本来可以做得更好，但我真诚地相信我创造了一个美丽而鼓舞人心的故事，子孙后代将会欣赏。

它提醒我追求你真正热爱的事情是多么重要，即使人们不理解它，即使结果不是你所期望的。

三年后，我来到了马尔法，在大约一百人面前展示了我的第一部短片纪录片。

尽管我们的空间变得越来越小，但我确实感受到了这个小社区的温暖、善良和同情心。

我的电影与 NFT 或生成艺术无关。这是关于山脉、身体耐力、个人成长以及我与摄影的关系。然而，人们还是出现了。他们观看、聆听、提出问题，其中一些人与作品的联系足以收集实物印刷品。

这对我来说意义重大，超出了我所能正确表达的范围。

我将生命的过去十年奉献给了摄影和山脉。这团火在某些时刻比其他时刻燃烧得更猛烈，但它从未停止增长。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是我感觉自己与今天所创造的东西的联系比以往任何时候都更加紧密。

玛法对我来说非常特别。我已经很久没有感受到这样的支持和赞赏了。它还提醒我，真正的人际关系、对话和分享的经历永远比社交媒体上的点赞或数字更有意义。

我非常感谢那些认识到我内心的火焰并继续以任何方式表示支持的人们。

2026 年成为一名独立艺术家很困难。我不会假装不是这样。

在这里，努力工作并不总是能转化为成功。你必须不断地挑战自己、适应、更加直言不讳、更加自信、更加引人注目，等等。创作艺术本身只是靠艺术谋生的一小部分。

我知道这并不是艺术家独有的。这是几乎所有企业经营的现实。拥有一款出色的产品，或者创造出令您深感自豪的东西，仅靠其本身是远远不够的。

但经历了所有的起起落落，经历了成功和失败的实验，这个社区迄今为止仍然是我所拥有过的最积极参与和支持的社区之一。

我不知道这个空间到底会走向何方，也不知道几年后它会是什么样子。但我知道，我一生中一些最有意义的机会、经历和人际关系都来自于其中。

为此，我将永远心怀感激。

我想我想说的是，成功并不总是像我们想象的那样。有时它是一个售罄的版本，有时它是一个几乎卖不出去的项目，有时它是一个房间里挤满了真正关心你倾注心血的人。

我正在学着欣赏这一切。

如果您已经读到这里，感谢您的阅读、来到这里并继续支持我的创作。这意味着比你知道的更多。 💙

celebrity.title_en:
🚨 XENOBLADE CHRONICLES 2 is being recompiled for PC — and the opening sections are reportedly PLAYABLE! ⚔️🔥

Developer AksharDP has released an experimental Windows recompilation of Nintendo's Switch RPG, built on technology from XCX Recomp and TotK Recomp!

🔥 CURRENT PROGRESS:

✅ Game boots successfully and reaches the main menu!

✅ New Game works, with the opening cutscenes reportedly running!

✅ First battle playable, with working combat controls!

✅ Goldmouth reached, with functioning audio, dialogue and text!

✅ Vulkan 1.3 rendering and native PC input support!

✅ Windows installer available — no need to compile the project manually!

📦 Version 0.1.2 available now!

⚠️ VERY EARLY DEVELOPMENT!

The developer reports that the opening sections are working, but the full game is NOT confirmed playable. Expect graphical issues, crashes and incomplete functionality.

🧪 Independent gameplay verification is still needed.

⚙️ Built using static recompilation technology rather than conventional Switch emulation.

💿 Requires your own Xenoblade Chronicles 2 game files with update 3.0.1.

🛠️ Developed by AksharDP, with extensive assistance from Claude Code. The developer explicitly acknowledges that most of the code and documentation was AI-generated.

⭐ Star the GitHub repository to follow development!

🔗https://t.co/7BjMlecm5T

Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an
celebrity.title_en:
Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

When we first launched, most people approved every permission prompt by hand and mostly used Claude to answer questions and write tests. 

Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products. 

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Thank you to our users for embracing a new way of working. Your constant feedback shaped so much of what we shipped and your stories made the work so meaningful.

Excited to see what you all make next!

Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products. 

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Thank you to our users for embracing a new way of working. Your constant feedback shaped so much of what we shipped and your stories made the work so meaningful.

Excited to see what you all make next!
celebrity.quote_zh:
星期五是我在 Anthropic 的最后一天。

两年前，当 Claude Code 还是一个小型内部工具时，我要求它构建一个 RL 环境。我操纵了它数十个小时，但从未手动编写过一行代码。它成功了，我被迷住了，然后我加入了这个团队。

当我们第一次推出时，大多数人都手动批准了每个权限提示，并且大多使用 Claude 来回答问题和编写测试。

今天，默认情况是相信克劳德的判断来自动批准。克劳德进行大规模迁移并构建新产品。

帮助 Claude Code 打造成行业定义的产品是我一生的旅程。

感谢 Claude Code、Cowork 和 Tag 背后令人难以置信的团队。这些产品是您数以千计的好创意的总和。我会想念和你们一起工作的。

感谢我们的用户接受新的工作方式。您不断的反馈塑造了我们交付的产品，您的故事使这项工作变得如此有意义。

很高兴看到你们接下来会做什么！
celebrity.full_text_en:
Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

When we first launched, most people approved every permission prompt by hand and mostly used Claude to answer questions and write tests. 

Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products. 

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Thank you to our users for embracing a new way of working. Your constant feedback shaped so much of what we shipped and your stories made the work so meaningful.

Excited to see what you all make next!

celebrity.title_en:
this is f*cking insane. you have been googling other people's thinking for 20 years, karpathy's one 5 minute setup gives you a google that only searches your own, and you have never once installed it

andrej karpathy pulled 16M views on one idea: stop using AI to write code, use it to build a second brain

every article you read, every podcast you heard, every meeting you took, every dm thread you had, every tweet you drafted, all of it searchable in one line forever

the people running it today do not open chatgpt anymore. they open their own search bar. and their search bar has 11 years of their own thinking in it

the stack:

→ brew install obsidian, mkdir ~/vault, cd ~/vault

→ open claude code in that folder, type "init CLAUDE.md as the rules, /raw for sources, /wiki for your pages"

→ drop any file into /raw (transcript, pdf, screenshot, meeting notes). type one word: ingest

→ claude writes a wiki page, links it to 5 existing ones, updates CLAUDE.md with any new pattern it caught about how you think

→ never open a blank chat again. every question goes through the vault. every answer cites your own sources with dates and links

5 minutes to wire. runs forever on the laptop already in front of you

the alpha most people miss:

> search your own vault in one line and the answer cites 5 of your own past notes with dates. google cites strangers. your vault cites you

> every ingest adds cross-links to 5 past pages automatically. after 90 days your vault answers questions you forgot you had

> CLAUDE.md learns how you argue, what you change your mind on, what you avoid saying. after month 3 it drafts posts in your voice better than you can at 2am

> flip two flags and it runs on local llama. zero API bill, zero vendor lock, your thinking never leaves the box

> compounds for 10 years. after year 3 your vault knows more about what you believe than you do. year 5 and recruiters start asking you to publish parts of it

the ugly part most will scroll past:

your coworker started this on a saturday in february

by august his tweets landed 4x your engagement on the exact same topics

by october his first draft of any doc was already better than your third

the gap is one 5 minute install and 90 days of ingesting what you already consume for free

celebrity.quote_zh:
这太他妈疯狂了。你已经用谷歌搜索别人的想法20年了，karpathy的一个5分钟设置给你一个只搜索你自己的谷歌，而你从来没有安装过它

andrej karpathy 的一个想法获得了 1600 万次浏览：停止使用 AI 编写代码，用它来构建第二个大脑

你读过的每一篇文章，你听过的每一篇播客，你参加的每一次会议，你拥有的每一条DM线程，你起草的每一条推文，所有这些都可以永远在一行中搜索

今天运行它的人不再打开chatgpt。他们打开自己的搜索栏。他们的搜索栏里有他们11年的思考

堆栈：

→brew 安装黑曜石，mkdir ~/vault，cd ~/vault

→ 在该文件夹中打开 Claude Code，输入“init CLAUDE.md 作为规则，/raw 作为源代码，/wiki 作为您的页面”

→ 将任何文件放入 /raw（记录、pdf、屏幕截图、会议记录）。输入一个词：摄入

→ claude 编写了一个 wiki 页面，将其链接到 5 个现有页面，用它捕获的关于您的想法的任何新模式更新 CLAUDE.md

→ 永远不要再打开空白聊天室。每个问题都会经过保险库。每个答案都引用了您自己的来源，并附有日期和链接

5 分钟即可接线。在您面前的笔记本电脑上永远运行

大多数人怀念的阿尔法：

> 在一行中搜索你自己的金库，答案引用了你自己过去的 5 篇笔记并附有日期。谷歌引用陌生人。你的金库引用了你

> 每次收录都会自动添加到过去 5 个页面的交叉链接。 90 天后，您的金库会回答您忘记的问题

> CLAUDE.md 了解您如何争论、您改变主意以及您避免说什么。第三个月后，它会比你在凌晨 2 点更好地用你的声音起草帖子

> 翻转两个标志，它就在本地美洲驼上运行。零 API 账单、零供应商锁定，您的思维永远不会脱离盒子

> 化合物有效期为 10 年。第三年之后，你的金库比你自己更了解你的信仰。第 5 年，招聘人员开始要求你发布其中的部分内容

丑陋的部分大部分都会滚动过去：

你的同事在二月的一个星期六开始了这个

到 8 月，他的推文使您对同一主题的参与度提高了 4 倍

到十月，他的任何文档的初稿都已经比你的第三稿好

差距是 5 分钟安装和 90 天免费获取已使用的内容

将此添加为书签。下面的文章中有完整的分步指南

What if knowing the rules isn't the same as knowing what to do?

For Mike Walker, who leads projects at the intersection of AI, cybersecurity, and large distributed systems at Microsoft Research, understanding a system starts with understanding its rules—but expertise also requires something more nuanced: knowing how those rules operate in context.

In a new Microsoft Research Podcast episode, Walker joins Principal Technical Program Manager Weishung Liu to talk cybersecurity, hacker culture, autonomous systems, leadership, and what his personal and professional challenges have taught him about judgment and adaptability.

First, learn the rules. Then see what's possible.
