items.title_en:
This is going to be a bit longer than usual:  

1. Tesla is building compute, just for our own highest-ROI use case Tesla’s Cortex 1 and Cortex 2 clusters at Giga Texas are already in production at well over 200 MW combined, with a stated target of ~400 MW of SI (Super Intelligence) training compute by the end of 2026.  That capacity is primarily for training vehicle autonomy/FSD and Optimus models, remember those? 
We are running an enormous fleet on FSD.  
The difference vs SpaceX/xAI is priority. xAI is a pure AI lab that needs massive generic training flops for frontier models (and can sell excess capacity to Anthropic and others). 
Tesla’s highest-value use of the same capital is our proprietary real-world data flywheel for cars and bots. 
Diverting significant capacity to external customers would slow the exact products that justify Tesla’s valuation premium today.  

2. Merchant GPU compute is a brutal business Tesla doesn’t need to enter Rapid GPU depreciation and stranded capacity risk are real (Elon has commented on half-built data centers and idle chips). 
Nvidia owns the silicon stack; hyperscalers and specialized neoclouds already dominate the rental market. 

Tesla’s actual competitive advantage in the AI infrastructure stack is energy, not training chips. It has already sold hundreds of millions to ~$1B of Megapacks into the Colossus buildouts. That’s higher-margin, more defensible, and leverages what Tesla already does at scale.⁠ 
Selling raw flops would put Tesla in direct competition with Nvidia, AWS, CoreWeave, etc., in a capital-intensive, fast-depreciating business where it has no structural edge.  

3. The Dojo experience is a cautionary tale Tesla shut down Dojo in 2025 after Elon called the Dojo 2 design an “evolutionary dead end” and much of the team left. The company pivoted hard to Nvidia for training clusters while focusing its own silicon (AI5/AI6 and later) on inference in vehicles and robots. Re-entering custom training hardware at scale just to become a merchant seller would repeat a hard lesson.⁠ 

However, all this chip know-how is not lost and used now in the Terafab pilot.  

4. SpaceX’s speed is real, but it’s solving a different problem Colossus 1  and 2 are impressive, and SpaceX’s construction/execution culture is a genuine advantage for pure data-center buildouts. 

Tesla’s construction teams are optimized for vehicle and energy product factories, not multi-gigawatt pure-play AI campuses. 

SpaceX/xAI also benefits from being able to treat excess capacity as a revenue stream; Tesla’s equivalent excess capacity is better used accelerating FSD and Optimus software.⁠  

5. On “build it and sell it to SpaceX” Tesla is already the power supplier to those clusters. 
The more logical path (if any) is modular hardware like the Megapod rather than competing head-on as a pure compute seller. Even then, SpaceX is currently the world’s fastest large-scale data-center builder. 

Tesla’s scarce capital and engineering bandwidth is better spent on the products only Tesla can ship  

So, to sum it up:  
Tesla is already scaling to 400 MW of training compute for its own FSD and Optimus needs. 
Merchant GPU rental is a low-moat, high-depreciation business that Nvidia and the hyperscalers already own. 
Tesla’s real AI infrastructure edge is energy and the proprietary physical-world data only its fleet generates. 
Selling flops to SpaceX or anyone else would just slow the higher-value autonomy and robotics timeline.

items.quote_zh:
这会比平常长一点：

1.特斯拉正在构建计算，只是为了我们自己的最高投资回报率用例特斯拉位于德克萨斯州 Giga 的 Cortex 1 和 Cortex 2 集群已经投入生产，总功率远超 200 MW，其既定目标是到 2026 年底实现约 400 MW 的 SI（超级智能）训练计算。该能力主要用于训练车辆自动驾驶/FSD 和 Optimus 模型，还记得那些吗？
我们在 FSD 上运行着一支庞大的车队。
与 SpaceX/xAI 的区别在于优先级。 xAI 是一个纯粹的人工智能实验室，需要针对前沿模型进行大量通用训练失败（并且可以将多余的产能出售给 Anthropic 和其他公司）。
特斯拉对同一资本的最高价值用途是我们用于汽车和机器人的专有现实世界数据飞轮。
将大量产能转移给外部客户将会减缓产品的生产速度，而这些产品恰恰证明了特斯拉目前的估值溢价是合理的。

2.商用GPU计算是一项残酷的业务特斯拉不需要进入GPU快速折旧和搁浅容量风险是真实的（埃隆评论了半建成的数据中心和闲置芯片）。
Nvidia 拥有硅堆栈；超大规模和专业的新云已经主导了租赁市场。

特斯拉在人工智能基础设施堆栈上的实际竞争优势是能源，而不是训练芯片。它已经在 Colossus 的扩建中销售了数亿至约 10 亿美元的 Megapack。这是更高的利润，更具有防御性，并且利用了特斯拉已经大规模做的事情。⁠
出售原始失败产品将使特斯拉在资本密集型、快速贬值的业务中与英伟达、AWS、CoreWeave 等直接竞争，而特斯拉没有结构性优势。

3. Dojo 的经历是一个警示故事 在 Elon 称 Dojo 2 设计为“进化的死胡同”并且大部分团队成员离开后，特斯拉于 2025 年关闭了 Dojo。该公司大力转向 Nvidia 的训练集群，同时将自己的芯片（AI5/AI6 及更高版本）专注于车辆和机器人的推理。为了成为商人而重新大规模进入定制培训硬件将重复一个惨痛的教训。⁠

然而，所有这些芯片技术并没有丢失，并且现在已在 Terafab 试点中使用。

4. SpaceX 的速度是真实的，但它正在解决不同的问题 Colossus 1 和 2 令人印象深刻，并且 SpaceX 的构建/执行文化对于纯数据中心建设来说是真正的优势。

特斯拉的施工团队针对汽车和能源产品工厂进行了优化，而不是针对数千兆瓦的纯人工智能园区。

SpaceX/xAI 还受益于能够将过剩产能视为收入来源；特斯拉的等效过剩产能更好地用于加速 FSD 和 Optimus 软件。⁠

5.关于“建造它并将其出售给SpaceX”，特斯拉已经是这些集群的电力供应商。
更合乎逻辑的路径（如果有的话）是像 Megapod 这样的模块化硬件，而不是作为纯粹的计算销售商正面竞争。即便如此，SpaceX 仍是目前世界上最快的大型数据中心建设者。

特斯拉稀缺的资本和工程带宽最好用在只有特斯拉才能发货的产品上

所以，总结一下：
Tesla 已经将训练计算规模扩展到 400 MW，以满足其自身的 FSD 和 Optimus 需求。
商用 GPU 租赁是 Nvidia 和超大规模企业已经拥有的低护城河、高折旧业务。
特斯拉真正的人工智能基础设施优势是能源和只有其车队生成的专有物理世界数据。
向 SpaceX 或其他任何人出售失败的产品只会减慢更高价值的自主和机器人技术的开发进度。

items.content_snippet:
This is going to be a bit longer than usual:  

1. Tesla is building compute, just for our own highest-ROI use case Tesla’s Cortex 1 and Cortex 2 clusters at Giga Texas are already in production at well over 200 MW combined, with a stated target of ~400 MW of SI (Super Intelligence) training compute by the end of 2026.  That capacity is primarily for training vehicle autonomy/FSD and Optimus models, remember those? 
We are running an enormous fleet on FSD.  
The difference vs SpaceX/xAI is priority. xAI is a pure AI lab that needs massive generic training flops for frontier models (and can sell excess capacity to Anthropic and others). 
Tesla’s highest-value use of the same capital is our proprietary real-world data flywheel for cars and bots. 
Diverting significant capacity to external customers would slow the exact products that justify Tesla’s valuation premium today.  

2. Merchant GPU compute is a brutal business Tesla doesn’t need to enter Rapid GPU depreciation and stranded capacity risk are real (Elon has commented on half-built data centers and idle chips). 
Nvidia owns the silicon stack; hyperscalers and specialized neoclouds already dominate the rental market. 

Tesla’s actual competitive advantage in the AI infrastructure stack is energy, not training chips. It has already sold hundreds of millions to ~$1B of Megapacks into the Colossus buildouts. That’s higher-margin, more defensible, and leverages what Tesla already does at scale.⁠ 
Selling raw flops would put Tesla in direct competition with Nvidia, AWS, CoreWeave, etc., in a capital-intensive, fast-depreciating business where it has no structural edge.  

3. The Dojo experience is a cautionary tale Tesla shut down Dojo in 2025 after Elon called the Dojo 2 design an “evolutionary dead end” and much of the team left. The company pivoted hard to Nvidia for training clusters while focusing its own silicon (AI5/AI6 and later) on inference in vehicles and robots. Re-entering custom training hardware at scale just to become a merchant seller would repeat a hard lesson.⁠ 

However, all this chip know-how is not lost and used now in the Terafab pilot.  

4. SpaceX’s speed is real, but it’s solving a different problem Colossus 1  and 2 are impressive, and SpaceX’s construction/execution culture is a genuine advantage for pure data-center buildouts. 

Tesla’s construction teams are optimized for vehicle and energy product factories, not multi-gigawatt pure-play AI campuses. 

SpaceX/xAI also benefits from being able to treat excess capacity as a revenue stream; Tesla’s equivalent excess capacity is better used accelerating FSD and Optimus software.⁠  

5. On “build it and sell it to SpaceX” Tesla is already the power supplier to those clusters. 
The more logical path (if any) is modular hardware like the Megapod rather than competing head-on as a pure compute seller. Even then, SpaceX is currently the world’s fastest large-scale data-center builder. 

Tesla’s scarce capital and engineering bandwidth is better spent on the products only Tesla can ship  

So, to sum it up:  
Tesla is already scaling to 400 MW of training compute for its own FSD and Optimus needs. 
Merchant GPU rental is a low-moat, high-depreciation business that Nvidia and the hyperscalers already own. 
Tesla’s real AI infrastructure edge is energy and the proprietary physical-world data only its fleet generates. 
Selling flops to SpaceX or anyone else would just slow the higher-value autonomy and robotics timeline.

items.summary_zh:
400 MW 的 SI（超级智能）训练计算。该能力主要用于训练车辆自动驾驶/FSD 和 Optimus 模型，还记得那些吗？
我们在 FSD 上运行着一支庞大的车队。
与 SpaceX/xAI 的区别在于优先级。 xAI 是一个纯粹的人工智能实验室，需要针对前沿模型进行大量通用训练失败（并且可以将多余的产能出售给 Anthropic 和其他公司）。
特斯拉对同一资本的最高价值用途是我们用于汽车和机器人的专有现实世界数据飞轮。
将大量产能转移给外部客户将会减缓产品的生产速度，而这些产品恰恰证明了特斯拉目前的估值溢价是合理的。

2.商用GPU计算是一项残酷的业务特斯拉不需要进入GPU快速折旧和搁浅容量风险是真实的（埃隆评论了半建成的数据中心和闲置芯片）。
Nvidia 拥有硅堆栈；超大规模和专业的新云已经主导了租赁市场。

特斯拉在人工智能基础设施堆栈上的实际竞争优势是能源，而不是训练芯片。它已经在 Colossus 的扩建中销售了数亿至约 10 亿美元的 Megapack。这是更高的利润，更具有防御性，并且利用了特斯拉已经大规模做的事情。⁠
出售原始失败产品将使特斯拉在资本密集型、快速贬值的业务中与英伟达、AWS、CoreWeave 等直接竞争，而特斯拉没有结构性优势。

3. Dojo 的经历是一个警示故事 在 Elon 称 Dojo 2 设计为“进化的死胡同”并且大部分团队成员离开后，特斯拉于 2025 年关闭了 Dojo。该公司大力转向 Nvidia 的训练集群，同时将自己的芯片（AI5/AI6 及更高版本）专注于车辆和机器人的推理。为了成为商人而重新大规模进入定制培训硬件将重复一个惨痛的教训。⁠

然而，所有这些芯片技术并没有丢失，并且现在已在 Terafab 试点中使用。

4. SpaceX 的速度是真实的，但它正在解决不同的问题 Colossus 1 和 2 令人印象深刻，并且 SpaceX 的构建/执行文化对于纯数据中心建设来说是真正的优势。

特斯拉的施工团队针对汽车和能源产品工厂进行了优化，而不是针对数千兆瓦的纯人工智能园区。

SpaceX/xAI 还受益于能够将过剩产能视为收入来源；特斯拉的等效过剩产能更好地用于加速 FSD 和 Optimus 软件。⁠

5.关于“建造它并将其出售给SpaceX”，特斯拉已经是这些集群的电力供应商。
更合乎逻辑的路径（如果有的话）是像 Megapod 这样的模块化硬件，而不是作为纯粹的计算销售商正面竞争。即便如此，SpaceX 仍是目前世界上最快的大型数据中心建设者。

特斯拉稀缺的资本和工程带宽最好用在只有特斯拉才能发货的产品上

所以，总结一下：
Tesla 已经将训练计算规模扩展到 400 MW，以满足其自身的 FSD 和 Optimus 需求。
商用 GPU 租赁是 Nvidia 和超大规模企业已经拥有的低护城河、高折旧业务。
特斯拉真正的人工智能基础设施优势是能源和只有其车队生成的专有物理世界数据。
向 SpaceX 或其他任何人出售失败的产品只会减慢更高价值的自主和机器人技术的开发进度。

items.title: Valve announces changes to Steam's review process, as a surge in game submissions pushes review times to "up to 12 business days", instead of the usual 3-5 days (Jay Peters/The Verge)
items.title_en: Valve announces changes to Steam's review process, as a surge in game submissions pushes review times to "up to 12 business days", instead of the usual 3-5 days (Jay Peters/The Verge)
items.author: The Verge
items.article_content:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Valve admits that it’s now taking ‘up to 12 business days’ to review games.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

In a new post today, Valve acknowledged that it’s seen “a significant increase in submissions for store and page review in recent months” and says it’s “running a little behind” by taking “up to 12 business days” for reviews instead of the typical 3-5 days.

Indie developers have recently expressed frustrations over lengthy approval times for Steam games, even causing some games to miss planned launch dates. Valve says that “much” of the delay is having to re-review games, so it’s making some changes to the release checklist for developers to hopefully “cut down on re-reviews for basic functional issues.”

The changes include requiring developers to run games through Steam for at least five minutes. “Believe it or not, sometimes we review builds that have not ever been played through Steam,” Valve says. “This means that even if a game runs smoothly when a dev launches their executable directly, they might have missed basic steps that would impact a user installing and playing via Steam.”

Other requirements include making sure that achievements are ready and confirming any required common redistributables, like DirectX or Visual C++, that Steam may need to install.

Valve also says more improvements are in the works for the build review process.

items.summary_zh: 由于开发者提交数量暴增，Steam审核周期延长至12个工作日，官方正通过强制测试要求来优化流程
items.article_content_zh:
该主题的帖子将添加到您的每日电子邮件摘要和主页源中。

Valve 承认现在需要“最多 12 个工作日”来审核游戏。

该作者的帖子将添加到您的每日电子邮件摘要和主页源中。

在今天的一篇新帖子中，Valve 承认“近几个月来提交的商店和页面审核数量显着增加”，并表示“有点落后”，审核需要“最多 12 个工作日”，而不是通常的 3-5 天。

独立开发者最近对 Steam 游戏审批时间过长表示不满，甚至导致一些游戏错过了计划的发布日期。 Valve 表示，延迟的“大部分”是因为必须重新审查游戏，因此它正在对开发者的发行清单进行一些更改，以期“减少对基本功能问题的重新审查”。

这些变化包括要求开发者通过 Steam 运行游戏至少五分钟。 “不管你信不信，有时我们会审查那些从未在 Steam 上玩过的版本，”Valve 说道。 “这意味着，即使开发者直接启动可执行文件时游戏运行顺利，他们也可能错过了影响用户通过 Steam 安装和玩游戏的基本步骤。”

其他要求包括确保成就已准备就绪，并确认 Steam 可能需要安装的任何必需的常见可再发行组件，例如 DirectX 或 Visual C++。

Valve 还表示，构建审核流程的更多改进正在进行中。

items.title_en:
Thank you + some unfiltered thoughts.

I wanted to start by thanking everyone who took the time to watch my film, either online or in Marfa, and everyone who collected a print. It genuinely means a lot to me.

Over the years, this space has become smaller and smaller, both on the artist and collector sides. It's been a journey of experimentation, evolution and constant adaptation to the market. Many people have left, while a much smaller group has continued to believe in this space and what we're building.

We've moved through NFTs, digital art, physical art and everything in between. And now, I feel like we're left with a small group of passionate artists, collectors and individuals who genuinely enjoy being here, regardless of where the market is going.

As a landscape photographer, I've experienced my fair share of highs and lows. We all know photography has had a complicated relationship with the NFT and digital art space, with many people questioning its value, its place in the art world, or simply not connecting with the medium.

I was fortunate enough to be one of the first photographers on SuperRare in 2021, and my life has never been the same since.

I've had the opportunity to work on some incredible projects, like FreeHawaiiPhoto, where I introduced the idea of CC0 to the space and later watched many artists and major NFT projects embrace it. I had the chance to experiment with AI very early on in 2021, and eventually did a commission that took me all the way to China, thanks to a collector who believed in my vision.

I'm extremely proud of my journey and what I've contributed to this space. I haven't always been perfect, and there are certainly things I would do differently today, but I've always tried to advocate for artists, and especially photographers.

In 2023, I dedicated an entire year of my life to writing and creating a children's book based on a true story. I released it as a high-end limited edition combining physical books and NFTs. It unfortunately didn't have the success I had hoped for. Recently, I packed away all the remaining books and put them into storage. And strangely, I didn't feel sadness. I felt an immense sense of pride.

Pride in having followed an idea I deeply believed in, even if it didn't resonate with as many people as I had hoped. Pride in having created something beautiful, meaningful and completely different from anything I had done before. Of course, some things could have been better, but I genuinely believe I created a beautiful and inspiring story that future generations will appreciate.

It reminded me how important it is to pursue something you're truly passionate about, even when people don't understand it, even when the outcome isn't what you expected.

Three years later, I found myself in Marfa, presenting my first short documentary in front of about a hundred people.

And even though our space has become significantly smaller, I genuinely felt the warmth, kindness and compassion of this little community.

My film wasn't about NFTs or generative art. It was about mountains, physical endurance, personal growth and my relationship with photography. And yet, people showed up. They watched, they listened, they asked questions, and some connected with the work enough to collect a physical print.

That meant more to me than I can properly express.

I've dedicated the past decade of my life to photography and the mountains. That fire has burned brighter at certain moments than others, but it has never stopped growing. If anything, I feel more connected to what I create today than ever before.

Marfa was incredibly special to me. I hadn't felt that supported and appreciated in a long time. It also reminded me that genuine human connections, conversations and shared experiences will always mean more than likes or numbers on social media.

I have so much gratitude for the people who recognize that fire in me and continue to show their support, in whatever way they can.

Being an independent artist in 2026 is hard. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

Here, hard work doesn't always translate into success. You constantly have to challenge yourself, adapt, be more vocal, more confident, more visible, more of everything. Creating the art itself is only a small part of what it takes to make a living from it.

And I know this isn't unique to artists. It's the reality of running almost any business. Having a great product, or creating something you're deeply proud of, is rarely enough on its own.

But through all the ups and downs, the experiments that worked and the ones that didn't, this community has remained by far one of the most engaged and supportive I've ever had.

I don't know exactly where this space is going, or what it will look like in a few years. But I know that some of the most meaningful opportunities, experiences and human connections of my life came from being part of it.

And for that, I will always be grateful.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that success doesn't always look the way we imagined it would. Sometimes it's a sold-out release, sometimes it's a project that barely sells, and sometimes it's a room full of people who genuinely care about something you've poured your heart into.

And I'm learning to appreciate all of it.

If you've made it this far, thank you for reading, for being here, and for continuing to support what I create. It means more than you know. 💙

Thank you + some unfiltered thoughts.

I wanted to start by thanking everyone who took the time to watch my film, either online or in Marfa, and everyone who collected a print. It genuinely means a lot to me.

Over the years, this space has become smaller and smaller, both on the artist and collector sides. It's been a journey of experimentation, evolution and constant adaptation to the market. Many people have left, while a much smaller group has continued to believe in this space and what we're building.

We've moved through NFTs, digital art, physical art and everything in between. And now, I feel like we're left with a small group of passionate artists, collectors and individuals who genuinely enjoy being here, regardless of where the market is going.

As a landscape photographer, I've experienced my fair share of highs and lows. We all know photography has had a complicated relationship with the NFT and digital art space, with many people questioning its value, its place in the art world, or simply not connecting with the medium.

I was fortunate enough to be one of the first photographers on SuperRare in 2021, and my life has never been the same since.

I've had the opportunity to work on some incredible projects, like FreeHawaiiPhoto, where I introduced the idea of CC0 to the space and later watched many artists and major NFT projects embrace it. I had the chance to experiment with AI very early on in 2021, and eventually did a commission that took me all the way to China, thanks to a collector who believed in my vision.

I'm extremely proud of my journey and what I've contributed to this space. I haven't always been perfect, and there are certainly things I would do differently today, but I've always tried to advocate for artists, and especially photographers.

In 2023, I dedicated an entire year of my life to writing and creating a children's book based on a true story. I released it as a high-end limited edition combining physical books and NFTs. It unfortunately didn't have the success I had hoped for. Recently, I packed away all the remaining books and put them into storage. And strangely, I didn't feel sadness. I felt an immense sense of pride.

Pride in having followed an idea I deeply believed in, even if it didn't resonate with as many people as I had hoped. Pride in having created something beautiful, meaningful and completely different from anything I had done before. Of course, some things could have been better, but I genuinely believe I created a beautiful and inspiring story that future generations will appreciate.

It reminded me how important it is to pursue something you're truly passionate about, even when people don't understand it, even when the outcome isn't what you expected.

Three years later, I found myself in Marfa, presenting my first short documentary in front of about a hundred people.

And even though our space has become significantly smaller, I genuinely felt the warmth, kindness and compassion of this little community.

My film wasn't about NFTs or generative art. It was about mountains, physical endurance, personal growth and my relationship with photography. And yet, people showed up. They watched, they listened, they asked questions, and some connected with the work enough to collect a physical print.

That meant more to me than I can properly express.

I've dedicated the past decade of my life to photography and the mountains. That fire has burned brighter at certain moments than others, but it has never stopped growing. If anything, I feel more connected to what I create today than ever before.

Marfa was incredibly special to me. I hadn't felt that supported and appreciated in a long time. It also reminded me that genuine human connections, conversations and shared experiences will always mean more than likes or numbers on social media.

I have so much gratitude for the people who recognize that fire in me and continue to show their support, in whatever way they can.

Being an independent artist in 2026 is hard. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

Here, hard work doesn't always translate into success. You constantly have to challenge yourself, adapt, be more vocal, more confident, more visible, more of everything. Creating the art itself is only a small part of what it takes to make a living from it.

And I know this isn't unique to artists. It's the reality of running almost any business. Having a great product, or creating something you're deeply proud of, is rarely enough on its own.

But through all the ups and downs, the experiments that worked and the ones that didn't, this community has remained by far one of the most engaged and supportive I've ever had.

I don't know exactly where this space is going, or what it will look like in a few years. But I know that some of the most meaningful opportunities, experiences and human connections of my life came from being part of it.

And for that, I will always be grateful.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that success doesn't always look the way we imagined it would. Sometimes it's a sold-out release, sometimes it's a project that barely sells, and sometimes it's a room full of people who genuinely care about something you've poured your heart into.

And I'm learning to appreciate all of it.

If you've made it this far, thank you for reading, for being here, and for continuing to support what I create. It means more than you know. 💙
items.quote_zh:
谢谢你+一些未经过滤的想法。

首先，我想感谢所有花时间在网上或马尔法观看我的电影的人，以及所有收集印刷品的人。这对我来说确实意义重大。

多年来，无论是对于艺术家还是收藏家来说，这个空间都变得越来越小。这是一个实验、进化和不断适应市场的旅程。许多人已经离开，而一小部分人仍然相信这个领域和我们正在建设的东西。

我们已经经历了 NFT、数字艺术、实体艺术以及介于两者之间的一切。现在，我觉得我们留下了一小群充满热情的艺术家、收藏家和个人，他们真正喜欢在这里，无论市场走向何方。

作为一名风光摄影师，我经历过不少的高潮和低谷。我们都知道摄影与 NFT 和数字艺术空间有着复杂的关系，许多人质疑它的价值、它在艺术世界中的地位，或者干脆与媒体没有联系。

我很幸运成为 2021 年 SuperRare 的第一批摄影师之一，从那以后我的生活就不再一样了。

我有机会参与一些令人难以置信的项目，比如 FreeHawaiiPhoto，我在其中引入了 CC0 的想法，后来看到许多艺术家和主要的 NFT 项目都接受了它。我很早就有机会在 2021 年尝试人工智能，并最终完成了一项委托，将我带到了中国，这要感谢一位相信我愿景的收藏家。

我对我的旅程以及我为这个领域做出的贡献感到非常自豪。我并不总是完美的，今天我肯定会做一些不同的事情，但我一直试图为艺术家，尤其是摄影师辩护。

2023年，我用了整整一年的时间来写作和创作一本根据真实故事改编的儿童读物。我将其作为实体书和 NFT 相结合的高端限量版发布。不幸的是，它没有取得我所希望的成功。最近，我把剩下的书全部收起来，入库。奇怪的是，我并没有感到悲伤。我感到一种巨大的自豪感。

为遵循自己深信不疑的想法而感到自豪，即使它没有像我希望的那样引起那么多人的共鸣。为创造了一些美丽、有意义且与我以前所做的完全不同的东西而感到自豪。当然，有些事情本来可以做得更好，但我真诚地相信我创造了一个美丽而鼓舞人心的故事，子孙后代将会欣赏。

它提醒我追求你真正热爱的事情是多么重要，即使人们不理解它，即使结果不是你所期望的。

三年后，我来到了马尔法，在大约一百人面前展示了我的第一部短片纪录片。

尽管我们的空间变得越来越小，但我确实感受到了这个小社区的温暖、善良和同情心。

我的电影与 NFT 或生成艺术无关。这是关于山脉、身体耐力、个人成长以及我与摄影的关系。然而，人们还是出现了。他们观看、聆听、提出问题，其中一些人与作品的联系足以收集实物印刷品。

这对我来说意义重大，超出了我所能正确表达的范围。

我将生命的过去十年奉献给了摄影和山脉。这团火在某些时刻比其他时刻燃烧得更猛烈，但它从未停止增长。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是我感觉自己与今天所创造的东西的联系比以往任何时候都更加紧密。

玛法对我来说非常特别。我已经很久没有感受到这样的支持和赞赏了。它还提醒我，真正的人际关系、对话和分享的经历永远比社交媒体上的点赞或数字更有意义。

我非常感谢那些认识到我内心的火焰并继续以任何方式表示支持的人们。

2026 年成为一名独立艺术家很困难。我不会假装不是这样。

在这里，努力工作并不总是能转化为成功。你必须不断地挑战自己、适应、更加直言不讳、更加自信、更加引人注目，等等。创作艺术本身只是靠艺术谋生的一小部分。

我知道这并不是艺术家独有的。这是几乎所有企业经营的现实。拥有一款出色的产品，或者创造出令您深感自豪的东西，仅靠其本身是远远不够的。

但经历了所有的起起落落，经历了成功和失败的实验，这个社区迄今为止仍然是我所拥有过的最积极参与和支持的社区之一。

我不知道这个空间到底会走向何方，也不知道几年后它会是什么样子。但我知道，我一生中一些最有意义的机会、经历和人际关系都来自于其中。

为此，我将永远心怀感激。

我想我想说的是，成功并不总是像我们想象的那样。有时它是一个售罄的版本，有时它是一个几乎卖不出去的项目，有时它是一个房间里挤满了真正关心你倾注心血的人。

我正在学着欣赏这一切。

如果您已经读到这里，感谢您的阅读、来到这里并继续支持我的创作。这意味着比你知道的更多。 💙

As a landscape photographer, I've experienced my fair share of highs and lows. We all know photography has had a complicated relationship with the NFT and digital art space, with many people questioning its value, its place in the art world, or simply not connecting with the medium.

I was fortunate enough to be one of the first photographers on SuperRare in 2021, and my life has never been the same since.

I've had the opportunity to work on some incredible projects, like FreeHawaiiPhoto, where I introduced the idea of CC0 to the space and later watched many artists and major NFT projects embrace it. I had the chance to experiment with AI very early on in 2021, and eventually did a commission that took me all the way to China, thanks to a collector who believed in my vision.

I'm extremely proud of my journey and what I've contributed to this space. I haven't always been perfect, and there are certainly things I would do differently today, but I've always tried to advocate for artists, and especially photographers.

In 2023, I dedicated an entire year of my life to writing and creating a children's book based on a true story. I released it as a high-end limited edition combining physical books and NFTs. It unfortunately didn't have the success I had hoped for. Recently, I packed away all the remaining books and put them into storage. And strangely, I didn't feel sadness. I felt an immense sense of pride.

Pride in having followed an idea I deeply believed in, even if it didn't resonate with as many people as I had hoped. Pride in having created something beautiful, meaningful and completely different from anything I had done before. Of course, some things could have been better, but I genuinely believe I created a beautiful and inspiring story that future generations will appreciate.

It reminded me how important it is to pursue something you're truly passionate about, even when people don't understand it, even when the outcome isn't what you expected.

Three years later, I found myself in Marfa, presenting my first short documentary in front of about a hundred people.

And even though our space has become significantly smaller, I genuinely felt the warmth, kindness and compassion of this little community.

My film wasn't about NFTs or generative art. It was about mountains, physical endurance, personal growth and my relationship with photography. And yet, people showed up. They watched, they listened, they asked questions, and some connected with the work enough to collect a physical print.

That meant more to me than I can properly express.

I've dedicated the past decade of my life to photography and the mountains. That fire has burned brighter at certain moments than others, but it has never stopped growing. If anything, I feel more connected to what I create today than ever before.

Marfa was incredibly special to me. I hadn't felt that supported and appreciated in a long time. It also reminded me that genuine human connections, conversations and shared experiences will always mean more than likes or numbers on social media.

I have so much gratitude for the people who recognize that fire in me and continue to show their support, in whatever way they can.

Being an independent artist in 2026 is hard. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

Here, hard work doesn't always translate into success. You constantly have to challenge yourself, adapt, be more vocal, more confident, more visible, more of everything. Creating the art itself is only a small part of what it takes to make a living from it.

And I know this isn't unique to artists. It's the reality of running almost any business. Having a great product, or creating something you're deeply proud of, is rarely enough on its own.

But through all the ups and downs, the experiments that worked and the ones that didn't, this community has remained by far one of the most engaged and supportive I've ever had.

I don't know exactly where this space is going, or what it will look like in a few years. But I know that some of the most meaningful opportunities, experiences and human connections of my life came from being part of it.

And for that, I will always be grateful.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that success doesn't always look the way we imagined it would. Sometimes it's a sold-out release, sometimes it's a project that barely sells, and sometimes it's a room full of people who genuinely care about something you've poured your heart into.

And I'm learning to appreciate all of it.

If you've made it this far, thank you for reading, for being here, and for continuing to support what I create. It means more than you know. 💙
items.summary_zh:
程。许多人已经离开，而一小部分人仍然相信这个领域和我们正在建设的东西。

我们已经经历了 NFT、数字艺术、实体艺术以及介于两者之间的一切。现在，我觉得我们留下了一小群充满热情的艺术家、收藏家和个人，他们真正喜欢在这里，无论市场走向何方。

作为一名风光摄影师，我经历过不少的高潮和低谷。我们都知道摄影与 NFT 和数字艺术空间有着复杂的关系，许多人质疑它的价值、它在艺术世界中的地位，或者干脆与媒体没有联系。

我很幸运成为 2021 年 SuperRare 的第一批摄影师之一，从那以后我的生活就不再一样了。

我有机会参与一些令人难以置信的项目，比如 FreeHawaiiPhoto，我在其中引入了 CC0 的想法，后来看到许多艺术家和主要的 NFT 项目都接受了它。我很早就有机会在 2021 年尝试人工智能，并最终完成了一项委托，将我带到了中国，这要感谢一位相信我愿景的收藏家。

我对我的旅程以及我为这个领域做出的贡献感到非常自豪。我并不总是完美的，今天我肯定会做一些不同的事情，但我一直试图为艺术家，尤其是摄影师辩护。

2023年，我用了整整一年的时间来写作和创作一本根据真实故事改编的儿童读物。我将其作为实体书和 NFT 相结合的高端限量版发布。不幸的是，它没有取得我所希望的成功。最近，我把剩下的书全部收起来，入库。奇怪的是，我并没有感到悲伤。我感到一种巨大的自豪感。

为遵循自己深信不疑的想法而感到自豪，即使它没有像我希望的那样引起那么多人的共鸣。为创造了一些美丽、有意义且与我以前所做的完全不同的东西而感到自豪。当然，有些事情本来可以做得更好，但我真诚地相信我创造了一个美丽而鼓舞人心的故事，子孙后代将会欣赏。

它提醒我追求你真正热爱的事情是多么重要，即使人们不理解它，即使结果不是你所期望的。

三年后，我来到了马尔法，在大约一百人面前展示了我的第一部短片纪录片。

尽管我们的空间变得越来越小，但我确实感受到了这个小社区的温暖、善良和同情心。

我的电影与 NFT 或生成艺术无关。这是关于山脉、身体耐力、个人成长以及我与摄影的关系。然而，人们还是出现了。他们观看、聆听、提出问题，其中一些人与作品的联系足以收集实物印刷品。

这对我来说意义重大，超出了我所能正确表达的范围。

我将生命的过去十年奉献给了摄影和山脉。这团火在某些时刻比其他时刻燃烧得更猛烈，但它从未停止增长。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是我感觉自己与今天所创造的东西的联系比以往任何时候都更加紧密。

玛法对我来说非常特别。我已经很久没有感受到这样的支持和赞赏了。它还提醒我，真正的人际关系、对话和分享的经历永远比社交媒体上的点赞或数字更有意义。

我非常感谢那些认识到我内心的火焰并继续以任何方式表示支持的人们。

2026 年成为一名独立艺术家很困难。我不会假装不是这样。

在这里，努力工作并不总是能转化为成功。你必须不断地挑战自己、适应、更加直言不讳、更加自信、更加引人注目，等等。创作艺术本身只是靠艺术谋生的一小部分。

我知道这并不是艺术家独有的。这是几乎所有企业经营的现实。拥有一款出色的产品，或者创造出令您深感自豪的东西，仅靠其本身是远远不够的。

但经历了所有的起起落落，经历了成功和失败的实验，这个社区迄今为止仍然是我所拥有过的最积极参与和支持的社区之一。

我不知道这个空间到底会走向何方，也不知道几年后它会是什么样子。但我知道，我一生中一些最有意义的机会、经历和人际关系都来自于其中。

为此，我将永远心怀感激。

我想我想说的是，成功并不总是像我们想象的那样。有时它是一个售罄的版本，有时它是一个几乎卖不出去的项目，有时它是一个房间里挤满了真正关心你倾注心血的人。

我正在学着欣赏这一切。

如果您已经读到这里，感谢您的阅读、来到这里并继续支持我的创作。这意味着比你知道的更多。 💙

items.title_en:
🚨 XENOBLADE CHRONICLES 2 is being recompiled for PC — and the opening sections are reportedly PLAYABLE! ⚔️🔥

Developer AksharDP has released an experimental Windows recompilation of Nintendo's Switch RPG, built on technology from XCX Recomp and TotK Recomp!

🔥 CURRENT PROGRESS:

✅ Game boots successfully and reaches the main menu!

✅ New Game works, with the opening cutscenes reportedly running!

✅ First battle playable, with working combat controls!

✅ Goldmouth reached, with functioning audio, dialogue and text!

✅ Vulkan 1.3 rendering and native PC input support!

✅ Windows installer available — no need to compile the project manually!

📦 Version 0.1.2 available now!

⚠️ VERY EARLY DEVELOPMENT!

The developer reports that the opening sections are working, but the full game is NOT confirmed playable. Expect graphical issues, crashes and incomplete functionality.

🧪 Independent gameplay verification is still needed.

⚙️ Built using static recompilation technology rather than conventional Switch emulation.

💿 Requires your own Xenoblade Chronicles 2 game files with update 3.0.1.

🛠️ Developed by AksharDP, with extensive assistance from Claude Code. The developer explicitly acknowledges that most of the code and documentation was AI-generated.

⭐ Star the GitHub repository to follow development!

🔗https://t.co/7BjMlecm5T

🔗https://t.co/9gMW2oj2lk

items.content_snippet: Jack Dorsey-led Block (XYZ.N) raised its full-year gross profit outlook on Tuesday after posting a rise in third-quarter earnings …
items.summary_en: Fintech giant Block reported Q3 revenue of $6.7 billion, beating analyst estimates, with its core Cash App gross profit surging 27% year-over-year to $2.07 billion. Fueled by strong ecosystem engagement, the company's leadership raised its full-year profit guidance during after-hours trading.
items.title_zh: Block三季度营收超预期，现金流业务狂飙
items.summary_zh: Jack Dorsey掌舵的Block公司第三季度营收增长10%至67亿美元，受Cash App毛利激增驱动，公司上调全年盈利预期

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 支付巨头Block发布三季度财报，总营收达67亿美元超市场预期，核心产品Cash App毛利同比大涨27%至20.7亿美元。得益于生态内支付业务的高粘性与盈利能力提升，公司管理层在盘后正式上调全年盈利预期。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Fintech giant Block reported Q3 revenue of $6.7 billion, beating analyst estimates, with its core Cash App gross profit surging 27% year-over-year to $2.07 billion. Fueled by strong ecosystem engagement, the company's leadership raised its full-year profit guidance during after-hours trading.

elements_zh.where: 公司第三季度财报发布现场
elements_zh.what: 营收录得67亿美元同比增长10%，Cash App毛利增长27%，并上调全年利润预期
elements_zh.why: 旨在应对市场增长放缓质疑，通过提升核心支付业务效率向华尔街证明其盈利模型依然强悍

elements_en.what: Revenue hit $6.7B (up 10% YoY), Cash App gross profit surged 27%, and hiked full-year profit forecast.
elements_en.why: To counter growth slowdown concerns and prove to Wall Street that their payment ecosystem still has teeth.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 看来Jack Dorsey在离开推特搞Web3和去中心化的同时，没耽误Cash App把用户钱包掏得更干净。只要利滚利够快，资本市场就懒得管你到底是在做支付还是在做信仰。
ai_analysis.insight_en: It seems Jack Dorsey’s pivot to Web3 and decentralization hasn't stopped Cash App from picking users' pockets more efficiently. As long as the profit growth looks this good, Wall Street doesn't care if you're building a payment system or just selling a lifestyle.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 支付巨头Block发布三季度财报，总营收达67亿美元超市场预期，核心产品Cash App毛利同比大涨27%至20.7亿美元。得益于生态内支付业务的高粘性与盈利能力提升，公司管理层在盘后正式上调全年盈利预期。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Fintech giant Block reported Q3 revenue of $6.7 billion, beating analyst estimates, with its core Cash App gross profit surging 27% year-over-year to $2.07 billion. Fueled by strong ecosystem engagement, the company's leadership raised its full-year profit guidance during after-hours trading.
key_points_zh: Jack Dorsey掌舵的Block交出亮眼成绩单
Cash App毛利贡献显著，带动营收超预期
公司上调盈利预期，盘后股价获得正向反馈
key_points_en: Jack Dorsey-led Block delivers strong Q3 results
Cash App's massive gross profit growth drives revenue beats
Higher full-year profit outlook triggers after-hours stock surge
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 看来Jack Dorsey在离开推特搞Web3和去中心化的同时，没耽误Cash App把用户钱包掏得更干净。只要利滚利够快，资本市场就懒得管你到底是在做支付还是在做信仰。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: It seems Jack Dorsey’s pivot to Web3 and decentralization hasn't stopped Cash App from picking users' pockets more efficiently. As long as the profit growth looks this good, Wall Street doesn't care if you're building a payment system or just selling a lifestyle.

【起因与机理】旨在应对市场增长放缓质疑，通过提升核心支付业务效率向华尔街证明其盈利模型依然强悍
【关键数据与实测】支付巨头Block发布三季度财报，总营收达67亿美元超市场预期，核心产品Cash App毛利同比大涨27%至20.7亿美元。
【观点态度】公司上调盈利预期，盘后股价获得正向反馈。

items.title: Canva says it is restructuring, which will impact 1,271 workers, or 22% of its workforce, as it merges its product, growth, and platform teams (David Swan/The Age)
items.title_en: Canva says it is restructuring, which will impact 1,271 workers, or 22% of its workforce, as it merges its product, growth, and platform teams (David Swan/The Age)
items.author: The Age
items.article_content:
You have reached your maximum number of saved items.

Remove items from your saved list to add more.

You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Canva will cut more than 1000 jobs in a major restructure in response to slowing growth at the design giant.

Co-founder and chief executive Melanie Perkins told staff on Wednesday the Sydney design company needed to “refound Canva” and return to small, empowered teams after its growth slowed this year for the first time in a decade. The shake-up will affect 1271 jobs, or 22 per cent of its workforce, with some staff to lose their roles and others asked to relocate to centralised hubs.

Canva co-founders Cliff Obrecht, Melanie Perkins and Cameron Adams.Bloomberg“This is without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history,” she wrote.

“After exploring a wide range of alternatives, I’ve come to the difficult conclusion that small changes won’t be enough. To set ourselves up for the next decade, we need to refound Canva, getting back to our roots of small, empowered teams with the freedom to make decisions, take ownership, and focus on what matters most for our community.”

Canva will merge its product, growth and platform teams into a single product organisation and cut management layers. Sydney will become the primary home for more product teams, and hybrid staff will be expected in the office two to three days a week from January.

The shake-up comes as investor fears that AI will undercut software businesses have hammered design companies. Shares in rival Figma more than halved in 2026 to the end of April, despite strong revenue growth.

Blackbird, Canva’s biggest venture backer, cut its valuation of the company by 17 per cent to $US34.9 billion in August, with Airtree making the same cut from the $US42 billion set in a 2025 employee share sale. Canva’s own internal valuation fell to $US31 billion, this masthead revealed in August.

Departing staff will receive at least six months’ salary, 12 months of healthcare where Canva provides it, and can keep their work MacBooks. They can also apply for $US10,000 ($14,500) grants to start their own ventures.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 每次巨头喊出“回归初心”的时候，翻译成人话就是“大公司病太重，钱烧没了”。与其说是为了 empowerment（授权），不如说是为了把那些养尊处优的冗余中层一刀切掉，顺便给资本市场一份好看的利润表。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Every time a tech giant talks about 'returning to roots,' it’s corporate-speak for 'we got too bloated and the money stopped flowing.' This isn't just about empowering teams; it's a brutal cleanup to axe middle-management bloat and polish the bottom line for shareholders.

Canva 将在重大重组中裁员 1000 多人，以应对这家设计巨头增长放缓的情况。

联合创始人兼首席执行官 Melanie Perkins 周三告诉员工，这家悉尼设计公司在今年增长十年来首次放缓后，需要“重新组建 Canva”并回归小型、授权的团队。此次人事变动将影响 1271 个工作岗位，占员工总数的 22%，部分员工将失去职位，其他员工则被要求搬迁到集中中心。

Canva 联合创始人 Cliff Obrecht、Melanie Perkins 和 Cameron Adams。彭博社“这无疑是我们十三年历史上最艰难的时刻，”她写道。

“在探索了广泛的替代方案之后，我得出了一个艰难的结论：小小的改变是不够的。为了为下一个十年做好准备，我们需要重新建立 Canva，回到我们的小而授权团队的根源，让他们可以自由地做出决策、掌握所有权并专注于对我们社区最重要的事情。”

Canva 将把其产品、增长和平台团队合并为一个产品组织，并削减管理层。悉尼将成为更多产品团队的主要所在地，从一月份开始，混合型员工预计每周在办公室工作两到三天。

此次重组发生之际，投资者担心人工智能将削弱软件业务，这给设计公司带来了沉重打击。尽管收入增长强劲，但截至 2026 年 4 月底，竞争对手 Figma 的股价将减少一半以上。

Canva 最大的风险投资公司 Blackbird 在 8 月份将该公司的估值下调了 17%，至 349 亿美元，Airtree 在 2025 年员工股票出售中设定的 420 亿美元也进行了同样的削减。该报头在 8 月份透露，Canva 的内部估值已降至 310 亿美元。

离职员工将获得至少六个月的工资、Canva 提供的 12 个月的医疗保健，并且可以保留他们的工作 MacBook。他们还可以申请 10,000 美元（14,500 美元）的补助金来创办自己的企业。

items.title: Revolut says it cut AI coding inference costs by ~90% in less than a year by making self-hosted GLM models its default over commercial tools like Claude Code (Tobias Mann/The Register)
items.title_en: Revolut says it cut AI coding inference costs by ~90% in less than a year by making self-hosted GLM models its default over commercial tools like Claude Code (Tobias Mann/The Register)
items.author: The Register
items.article_content:
Tobias Mann Tobias Mann SYSTEMS EDITOR Published tue 3 Nov 2026 // 20:07 UTC Make us preferred on Google READ MORE Nvidia is happy to take your money whether you're using open or closed models, says Jensen Huang 17 minutes ago Drax wants to feed Britain's AI habit with £20B datacenter at biomass power station 7 hours ago Toyota shows off SoC that stores model weights and its OS on integrated memory 17 hours ago Anthropic's compute tab could top $1T as Q3 revenue nears $17B 21 hours ago Marvell wants to be a copper topper, bets $115B on photonics leader to push optical networking 1 day ago Revolut says that in less than a year it's managed to slash its AI coding inference costs by roughly 90 percent by making self-hosted models its default instead of relying primarily on commercial services like Claude.

Speaking at the AI Engineer conference in New York last month, David Abitbol, ops and infrastructure lead at the British fintech, described how it saw a 60 percent improvement in coding time and a 70 percent improvement in lead time following its rollout of AI coding tools to roughly 2,000 engineers. Revolut initially adopted GLM-5.1 before moving to GLM-5.3, which it now serves using 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs.

Prior to its switch to GLM, Revolut had been experimenting with AI, deploying Gemini in early 2025 and Claude Code in early 2026. "We were highly skeptical about the cost of AI. We were seeing engineers spend $1,000 a month, $10,000 a month with not so much ROI, and so when we launched it we launched it with strict budget limits," Abitbol said.

Because of this, engineers only had access to a limited number of tokens, so the company began investigating self-hosting iyd own models. At $0.30 per million input/output tokens, self hosting GLM 5.1 cost about a tenth of using OpenAI's Codex or Anthropic's Claude Code. And, as it turned out, when tokens are cheap, you stop worrying about how many they use or what they use them for.

While Revolut did see improvements to coding speed, Abitbol noted the biggest bottleneck wasn't actually the code. Instead, he says the biggest gains came from letting the AI models deal with things like debugging and Jira and Confluence tickets. "When you have unlimited tokens, you're free to do that," he said. "You no longer have to save your tokens for the end of the quarter or the most difficult task."

Developed by Chinese open weights model dev Z.ai, GLM 5.1 isn't exactly a small model. At roughly 754 billion total parameters (40 billion activated for each token generated), the model requires roughly 380 GB of GPU memory just to hold the weights and another 6-26 GB per user to maintain context depending on precision.

To serve GLM-5.3 at scale, Revolut deployed 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs, equivalent in GPU count to seven eight-GPU DGX B200 systems. But as Abitbol noted, the greatest performance gains didn't come from adding GPUs, but rather tuning the model's hyperparameters along with switching to NVFP4 quantization, implementing disaggregated prefill and decode, and tuning context lengths.

One key takeaway was that supporting a one-million-token context window doesn't necessarily make such a large window useful or efficient. "Long context is a scam. You really need to be mindful of that," Abitbol said. "Even though you can serve one million tokens, 256 [thousand] is really what you need."

With these optimizations, Abitbol says that the company was able to achieve sub 3-second time to first token on context windows of around 256,000 tokens, and generation speeds of around 200 tokens a second, both of which he notes are the sweet spot for the company's software engineers.

"What you want to aim for is a sub-3 second time to first token. This is empirical evidence. As soon as you exceed 5 seconds, my Slack inbox starts to blow up," Abitbol said. "In terms of throughput, it doesn't really matter as much. We serve, in terms of interactivity, 200 tokens per second. People are fine [with that]. You don't need to go higher. The way people work has changed. We no longer look at the stream of thinking tokens. People run tasks in parallel and check in when the task is done."

And if throughput is a concern, he notes engineers who sign in after 5 pm are getting closer to 800 tokens a second.

However, it's worth noting that GLM hasn't replaced GPT or Claude entirely. The Chinese model is text only, so it isn't ideal for things like UI work. So instead, Revolut used a model router to direct vision queries to models like Gemini or GPT Luna while keeping code generation running on GLM.

"Open source is now a priority at Revolut, and our economics are favorable. The billing is flat, we don't have any bill shock at the end of the month, and the frontier is the exception," Abitbol said.

Having said that, Abitbol acknowledges that Chinese open weights models may be a concern for privacy and security reasons, but emphasizes that the major concern there is accessing them via APIs running out of China. When run on-prem or on regional cloud resources, there's really nothing to worry about. ®

items.article_content_zh:
Tobias Mann Tobias Mann 系统编辑 发布于 2026 年 11 月 3 日星期二// 20:07 UTC 让我们在 Google 上成为首选 阅读更多 黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 表示，无论您使用的是开放式模型还是封闭式模型，Nvidia 都很乐意接受您的钱 17 分钟前 Drax 希望在生物质发电站利用价值 20B 英镑的数据中心满足英国的人工智能习惯 7 小时前 丰田展示了将模型权重及其操作系统存储在集成内存中的 SoC 17 小时前 Anthropic 的计算选项卡可能会突破 1T 美元，因为第三季度收入接近 17B 美元 21 小时前 Marvell 希望成为铜领先者，在光子学领导者上押注 115B 美元以推动光网络 1 天前 Revolut 表示，在不到一年的时间里，通过将自托管模型设置为默认值，而不是主要依赖 Claude 等商业服务，它已成功将其 AI 编码推理成本削减了约 90%。

上个月在纽约举行的人工智能工程师会议上，英国金融科技公司运营和基础设施负责人 David Abitbol 描述了在向大约 2,000 名工程师推出人工智能编码工具后，编码时间缩短了 60%，交付周期缩短了 70%。 Revolut 最初采用 GLM-5.1，然后转向 GLM-5.3，现在使用 56 个 Nvidia B200 GPU 提供服务。

在转向 GLM 之前，Revolut 一直在尝试人工智能，于 2025 年初部署 Gemini，并于 2026 年初部署 Claude Code。“我们对人工智能的成本非常怀疑。我们看到工程师每月花费 1,000 美元，每月花费 10,000 美元，投资回报率并不高，因此当我们推出它时，我们在严格的预算限制下推出了它，”Abitbol 说。

因此，工程师只能访问有限数量的代币，因此该公司开始研究自托管 iyd 自己的模型。以每百万输入/输出代币 0.30 美元计算，自托管 GLM 5.1 的成本约为使用 OpenAI 的 Codex 或 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 的十分之一。而且，事实证明，当代币便宜时，你就不再担心它们使用了多少或它们用于什么目的。

虽然 Revolut 确实看到了编码速度的提高，但 Abitbol 指出最大的瓶颈实际上并不是代码。相反，他表示最大的收益来自于让人工智能模型处理诸如调试、Jira 和 Confluence 票证之类的事情。 “当你拥有无限的代币时，你就可以自由地这样做，”他说。 “你不再需要为季度末或最困难的任务保存代币。”

GLM 5.1 由中国开放权重模型开发者 Z.ai 开发，并不是一个小模型。该模型总共大约有 7540 亿个参数（每个生成的令牌激活 400 亿个参数），仅需要大约 380 GB 的 GPU 内存来保存权重，每个用户还需要 6-26 GB 的内存来根据精度维护上下文。

为了大规模服务 GLM-5.3，Revolut 部署了 56 个 Nvidia B200 GPU，其 GPU 数量相当于七个 8 个 GPU DGX B200 系统。但正如 Abitbol 指出的那样，最大的性能提升并不是来自添加 GPU，而是调整模型的超参数以及切换到 NVFP4 量化、实现分解的预填充和解码以及调整上下文长度。

一个关键要点是，支持一百万个令牌上下文窗口并不一定会使如此大的窗口有用或高效。 “长上下文是一个骗局。你真的需要注意这一点，”阿比特博尔说。 “尽管你可以提供 100 万个代币，但 256 [千] 个才是你真正需要的。”

Abitbol 表示，通过这些优化，该公司能够在大约 256,000 个代币的上下文窗口上实现不到 3 秒的时间生成第一个代币，并以每秒约 200 个代币的生成速度实现，他指出这两者都是公司软件工程师的最佳选择。

“你想要的目标是在 3 秒内获得第一个令牌。这是经验证据。一旦超过 5 秒，我的 Slack 收件箱就会开始爆炸，”Abitbol 说。 “就吞吐量而言，这并不那么重要。就交互性而言，我们每秒提供 200 个令牌。人们对此很满意。你不需要更高。人们的工作方式已经改变。我们不再关注思考令牌流。人们并行运行任务，并在任务完成时检查。”

如果吞吐量是一个问题，他指出下午 5 点后登录的工程师每秒接近 800 个代币。

然而，值得注意的是，GLM 并没有完全取代 GPT 或 Claude。中文模型仅包含文本，因此对于 UI 工作等内容并不理想。因此，Revolut 使用模型路由器将视觉查询定向到 Gemini 或 GPT Luna 等模型，同时保持代码生成在 GLM 上运行。

Abitbol 表示：“开源现在是 Revolut 的首要任务，而且我们的经济状况良好。账单持平，月底我们没有任何账单冲击，而前沿是个例外。”

话虽如此，Abitbol 承认中国的开放权重模型可能出于隐私和安全原因而令人担忧，但强调主要的担忧是通过中国以外的 API 访问它们。当在本地或区域云资源上运行时，实际上没有什么可担心的。 ®

items.content_snippet: Super Micro Computer (SMCI.O) forecast second-quarter revenue above Wall Street estimates on Tuesday as strong demand for its AI-optimized servers boosted sales …
items.summary_en: Super Micro Computer reported Q1 revenue surging 298% year-over-year to $19.9.5 billion, beating Wall Street's $16.39 billion estimate, driven by explosive AI server demand. The company also issued a stronger-than-expected Q2 revenue forecast, sending its stock up over 7% in after-hours trading.

items.title_en:
Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

When we first launched, most people approved every permission prompt by hand and mostly used Claude to answer questions and write tests. 

Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products. 

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Thank you to our users for embracing a new way of working. Your constant feedback shaped so much of what we shipped and your stories made the work so meaningful.

Excited to see what you all make next!

items.title: AMD reports Q3 revenue up 45% YoY to $13.38B, vs. $13.09B est., Data Center revenue up 97% to $8.5B, forecasts Q4 revenue above est.; AMD jumps 7%+ after hours (Katie Tarasov/CNBC)
items.title_en: AMD reports Q3 revenue up 45% YoY to $13.38B, vs. $13.09B est., Data Center revenue up 97% to $8.5B, forecasts Q4 revenue above est.; AMD jumps 7%+ after hours (Katie Tarasov/CNBC)
items.author: CNBC
items.article_content:
Advanced Micro Devices reported third-quarter earnings on Tuesday that beat Wall Street's expectations, with revenue jump 45% and data center sales nearly doubling from a year earlier. The stock jumped 7% in extended trading.

Revenue increased from $9.25 billion a year earlier, AMD said in a statement.

CEO Lisa Su said in a press release that she expects growth in data center processors to "accelerate further," and that meeting demand won't be a problem.

"With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years " Su said in a statement.

AMD's report comes days after Intel disclosed similar data center growth, with revenue in that segment up 78% in the third quarter. But the stock plummeted 29% on Friday over concerns about weak guidance and Intel's ability to meet demand.

The data center unit makes up the majority of AMD's business, accounting for 64% of overall revenue, up from 47% a year ago.

After years spent chasing Nvidia in the market for artificial intelligence graphics processing units, or GPUs, AMD's central processing units, or CPUs, are experiencing a major resurgence with the rise of agentic AI apps like Meta's Muse. AMD's server CPUs are key for agentic apps because they power virtual machines and can run for hours on their own. Demand from agentic AI boosted AMD shares to a record in October.

AMD's stock is up about 125% this year, but it saw three consecutive days of losses before rallying on Tuesday amid an industrywide sell-off tied to fears about overspending on AI.

AMD is also a major player the in weakening PC market, which Intel blamed for its poor outlook last week. AMD and Intel are the largest makers of traditional x86 processors that power many laptops and desktops, while other laptops rely on Arm-based processors from the likes of Qualcomm and Apple.

Global PC shipments declined 4% in the second quarter from a year earlier due to soaring costs for memory and other components, according to Counterpoint Research.

AMD reports PC chip sales in a segment combined with gaming chips. Revenue in that business fell 8% from a year earlier to $3.7 billion. Gaming revenue was down 40% from a year ago.

For the fourth quarter, AMD said it expects about $17 billion in revenue, beating the $16.2 billion average analyst estimate, according to LSEG. AMD sees its gross margin for the quarter coming in at 55%, slightly below the average estimate of 55.3%, according to StreetAccount.

AMD also sells data center GPUs and full rack-scale systems called Helios that compete directly with Nvidia's Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin. Meta, Microsoft, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Oracle are all beginning to use AMD Helios in their data centers. Meta said last week that its Helios racks are up and running, and AMD agreed to invest $1 billion in Meta's equity offering.

AMD has also committed to investing up to $5 billion in Anthropic, which unveiled its highly anticipated prospectus last week as it inches closer to a potentially historic initial public offering.

During a visit to Taiwan in October, Su said she plans to "substantially increase our supply in 2027." Su and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have both made multiple trips to Taiwan and South Korea this year, holding meetings with key suppliers like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and memory leaders SK Hynix and Samsung.

In September, AMD said it would acquire World Labs for $8.2 billion in an all-stock deal. The San Francisco-based AI lab, founded by industry pioneer Fei-Fei Li, is developing a so-called world model that simulates 3D environments to aid in developing robots and other physically grounded AI applications.

items.article_content_zh:
Advanced Micro Devices 周二公布的第三季度财报超出了华尔街的预期，收入增长 45%，数据中心销售额同比增长近一倍。该股在盘后交易中上涨了 7%。

AMD 在一份声明中表示，营收较上年同期的 92.5 亿美元有所增长。

首席执行官苏姿丰(Lisa Su)在一份新闻稿中表示，她预计数据中心处理器的增长将“进一步加速”，满足需求不会成为问题。

苏在一份声明中表示：“凭借我们领先的产品组合以及深厚的客户和供应链关系，我们有信心在未来几年保持强劲的收入增长和不断扩大的盈利能力。”

AMD 发布报告的几天前，英特尔公布了类似的数据中心增长情况，第三季度该领域的收入增长了 78%。但由于对疲弱的指引和英特尔满足需求的能力的担忧，该股周五暴跌 29%。

数据中心部门构成了 AMD 业务的大部分，占总收入的 64%，高于一年前的 47%。

经过多年在人工智能图形处理单元（GPU）市场上追赶 Nvidia 后，随着 Meta 的 Muse 等代理人工智能应用程序的兴起，AMD 的中央处理单元（CPU）正在经历一次重大复苏。 AMD 的服务器 CPU 是代理应用程序的关键，因为它们为虚拟机提供动力，并且可以自行运行数小时。代理人工智能的需求推动 AMD 股价在 10 月份创下历史新高。

AMD 的股价今年上涨了约 125%，但由于担心人工智能超支而引发全行业抛售，该公司股价连续三天下跌，然后在周二反弹。

AMD 也是疲软的个人电脑市场的主要参与者，英特尔上周将其糟糕的前景归咎于 PC 市场。 AMD 和英特尔是传统 x86 处理器的最大制造商，为许多笔记本电脑和台式机提供动力，而其他笔记本电脑则依赖高通和苹果等公司基于 Arm 的处理器。

Counterpoint Research 的数据显示，由于内存和其他组件成本飙升，第二季度全球个人电脑出货量同比下降 4%。

AMD 报告了 PC 芯片与游戏芯片领域的销售额。该业务的收入较上年同期下降 8%，至 37 亿美元。游戏收入同比下降 40%。

据 LSEG 称，AMD 预计第四季度营收约为 170 亿美元，超过分析师平均预期 162 亿美元。据 StreetAccount 称，AMD 预计本季度毛利率为 55%，略低于平均预期 55.3%。

AMD 还销售数据中心 GPU 和名为 Helios 的全机架规模系统，与 Nvidia 的 Grace Blackwell 和 Vera Rubin 直接竞争。 Meta、Microsoft、Anthropic、OpenAI 和 Oracle 都开始在其数据中心使用 AMD Helios。 Meta 上周表示，其 Helios 机架已启动并运行，AMD 同意向 Meta 的股票发行投资 10 亿美元。

AMD 还承诺向 Anthropic 投资高达 50 亿美元，该公司上周公布了备受期待的招股说明书，距离潜在的历史性首次公开募股越来越近。

items.title: Anthropic releases FlashProve, open-source code that cryptographically verifies an AI response came from a given model, not a cheaper one swapped in by a router (Anthropic)
items.title_en: Anthropic releases FlashProve, open-source code that cryptographically verifies an AI response came from a given model, not a cheaper one swapped in by a router (Anthropic)
items.author: Anthropic
items.article_content:
Roy Rinberg (Anthropic), Alex Allain (Anthropic); Alessandro Chiesa (EPFL, StarkWare), Miranda Christ (MIT, RESI), Rahul Dalal (Anthropic STEM Fellows Program, Succinct), Giacomo Fenzi (EPFL), Ben Mayer (Anthropic Fellows Program, MIT), Guy Weissenberg (EPFL)

When you talk to a friend in person, you have many ways to know it is really them: you can see them, hear them, shake their hand. When you talk to an AI model, you have almost none. A user querying a model today cannot check that the responses came from the specific model that a developer claims is responding, as opposed to one secretly substituted in by a routing service for cost reasons, or even by an attacker who has tampered with the token stream. Judging from the model’s output alone is unreliable, even if it produces high-quality responses. Cryptographic proofs of inference solve this problem: they let a model provider commit to a model and then prove that each response was produced by that model. Such proofs could enable applications ranging from consumer products to internal security, and could contribute to a toolkit for verifying compliance with AI pacing requirements.

Specifically, we have made progress on a powerful type of cryptographic proof known as a “zkSNARK”, which is uniquely fit for provable inference (owing to its strong hiding and efficiency properties). In this post, we share some of that progress, primarily through a system we call FlashProve. A brief technical summary is as follows:

We release our code, Lean proofs, and documentation under the Apache 2.0 license.1 This research post is meant to share intermediate progress, and not a completed research agenda. We are sharing this explicitly with the goal that others look at what we have done, take it, and improve it.

When a user sends a request to an AI model, today they have no way of knowing for certain that the model they selected is the one that generated the response. For everyday uses, in which users mostly care about the output and not necessarily which specific model produced it, this is a less pressing concern. But there are several cases where such assurance would be useful. For example, independent evaluators who test AI models before and after release need to know that the model they are evaluating is the model being served. Clients who use a model through a third-party routing service want assurance that the tokens came from the model they paid for. And if a cyberattacker modifies the token stream while pretending to be a given model, a user has no way to detect it from the output alone.

However, enabling verification of model responses is challenging. Most frontier models’ weights are kept private, and even if the user had access to the weights, checking that a given response was produced by a model with those weights would involve running the model, which requires computational resources far beyond what a typical user (or even evaluator) can afford.

The goal of provable inference (PI) is to enable a user with limited computational resources and without any information about the weights to verify that a response came from the requested model. PI is motivated both by a desire to increase customer trust in AI providers, and—because it can be used to provide assurances to independent evaluators and allows providers to demonstrate that they are meeting certain commitments and legal obligations—it also has implications for pacing the frontier of AI development and for AI regulation.

One way to implement PI is via a cryptographic object called a zero-knowledge succinct argument: the model provider sends, along with the claimed response, a short proof (say, a few megabytes) that the user can quickly verify (ideally, in seconds on a CPU). If the claimed response deviates from the specified model, the user’s check will fail. Importantly, cryptographic techniques ensure that the proof reveals nothing about the model’s weights.

Today, we release FlashProve: an open-source performant prototype for provable inference. For a 400B-parameter mixture-of-experts model (Llama 4 Maverick, 4-bit quantization), we show that a single H100 GPU generates proofs at over 100 tokens/second, with proof size of ~19 MB per 1,024-token request (~70-95 times the GPU time that vLLM, a common open-source library, takes to process prompts of the same length).

The release comes with executable code, Lean formalization, and a technical description of the protocol. Our aim is twofold: (i) accelerating and facilitating the development of provable inference; and (ii) demonstrating that zero-knowledge succinct arguments are practical for provable inference.

We believe that this progress has meaningful implications for security, in pacing AI development, in providing AI customers with integrity guarantees, in facilitating tooling for auditors and regulators, and more.

The development of artificial intelligence and its growing role in our digital infrastructure and economy raises trust challenges that AI providers must answer. Addressing these and other challenges is facilitated by relying on tools for provable inference (PI).

Tools for PI include hardware approaches, software approaches, or a combination of both. Here, we focus on a software-only approach: a cryptographic tool known as a “zkSNARK” (zero-knowledge succinct argument of knowledge). Informally, a zkSNARK is a system allowing a prover to convince a verifier, by way of a short “certificate”, that a given computation was executed correctly; crucially, the certificate is zero-knowledge in that it reveals no information beyond what is implied by the computation’s correctness and is succinct in that it’s exponentially faster to verify compared to the proved computation.

Below we outline several challenges and how zkSNARKs help in addressing them.

Some proposals to regulate and pace AI development rely on monitoring hardware and how it is used. For example, a provider might be required to devote its hardware to inference rather than to training a powerful new model. The provider might try to cheat by serving cheaper models or using compute in an unexpected way, freeing up resources for training. How can a regulator reliably ensure that the hardware is used for inference?

How zkSNARKs can help: The regulator can ask the provider for certificates covering the inference requests served in a given period. The certificates must show that the requests were generated by the claimed model. A malicious provider cannot satisfy this request unless its hardware was genuinely serving the right model. Using a zkSNARK, the regulator can check that the provider claims are valid without needing the elaborate hardware setup that the provider may have, and at the same time the provider has the guarantee that the regulator does not learn proprietary model information.2 We note that although this verifies that the hardware is serving inference, it does not establish that the hardware is not, e.g., training on the side.

As AI models grow more valuable, the servers that run them become prime targets. An attacker or rogue agent may compromise an inference server to exfiltrate the weights, serve users malicious responses (such as delivering malware to the user’s computer), and more, all while hiding among genuine responses. The adversary need not be external. As models become capable of improving and deploying themselves, a more advanced model could run in place of the one that was authorized and present itself as the weaker model, so as to avoid the classifiers and monitoring that would apply to it. In both cases the question is the same: how can a company be sure of which weights are actually running on its servers? In our Frontier Safety Roadmap, Anthropic set a public goal to produce a prototype for verifying inference traffic: “We will develop a prototype by September 30, 2026 of provable inference, a technique for reliably, provably ‘signing’ AI model outputs in a way that makes them attributable to a specific set of model weights.” As stated in our RSP updates, we met that goal through a separate but related project, which signs our inference traffic and recomputes inference on a trusted server; the work in this blog post pursues the same objective by a different method.3

How zkSNARKs can help: The provider can require a valid zkSNARK from the server on every response. A proof is bound to a specific commitment to the weights, so it certifies not just that some model produced the response but that the committed model did. An attacker who compromises a server, or a model that substitutes itself for another, must then produce valid proofs for the expected weights to avoid detection, which they cannot do. The user may receive the proofs as well, since they leak no internal information (by zero knowledge) and are cheap to check (by succinctness); this limits what an attacker can accomplish through the inference API.

One may want to prove that considerable effort went into understanding/analyzing something. For example, a developer might claim that their software library was scanned for vulnerabilities by a frontier cybersecurity model, or a company might claim that its business plan was given the go-ahead by an appropriate model. How can a user verify these claims? The user might not have the resources to run the model itself (or they might not have the clearance to do so). Even publishing the chat logs gives no absolute guarantees; a developer might in theory fake them, generating them not with a frontier model but instead with a cheaper one or a degraded version. In general, how can users verify that they are being served by their chosen model?

How zkSNARKs can help: The provider can append, along with each response, a zkSNARK proving that the output was produced by the claimed model on the given input. Succinctness lets the user check this certificate quickly, without specialized hardware, and zero-knowledge assures the provider that the user learns nothing about the proprietary weights. This complements existing mechanisms for verifying which model produced a response.

For example, in a world where exploits are being found regularly, prior to releasing new code a model provider could provide the code-developer a Proof-of-Failure that the model-provider spent at least X tokens on a specific model, and did not achieve a specific result (for example, this specific model did not find any bugs in a specific patch, after trying for at least 1M tokens).

Regulation might require providers to serve only models approved as safe, rather than models deemed a cybersecurity or safety risk. A provider might have an incentive to circumvent this, since risky models might outperform competitors or be cheaper to serve. How can a regulator ensure that only approved models are served?

How zkSNARKs can help: The regulator can require the provider to attach a zkSNARK to its responses, enforcing the use of approved models. The proof binds each request to the used model, so it will not verify if the provider is using an unapproved model. The regulator can check this in a lightweight way thanks to succinctness without requiring to re-execute each request.

A note on PI from trusted hardware. Prior work often focuses on trusted execution environments to achieve PI. These are hardware-based solutions that provide privacy and attestation that rely on the manufacturer producing tamper-resistant hardware. In this research, our focus is on software-only cryptographic solutions whose security and privacy relies on the hardness of computational problems. Even in the face of compromised environments (hardware, operating system and more) an adversary cannot produce a invalid proof without breaking a computationally infeasible problem. Trusted hardware and cryptography are complementary approaches with different guarantees and tradeoffs. Both will play a role in addressing the above trust challenges.

FlashProve is a system for provable inference of large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models. More details are in our technical report; here we outline the system.

FlashProve involves two parties: the model provider (the prover) and a user (the verifier). It is split into two phases:

The committed model produces these output tokens when evaluated.

Anyone who holds the commitment, the prompt, and the reply can check it, without the weights and with limited compute power, and be convinced that the committed weights, run on this prompt, produce exactly these tokens.

Completeness and soundness alone can be achieved by a computationally powerful verifier that knows the model weights (evaluate the model on the prompt and check whether the result matches the response). The next two properties are what makes the system non-trivial.

We measured an implementation of the protocol on Llama 4 Maverick (a 400B-parameter mixture of experts, with ~17B parameters used per token), using the publicly available 4-bit weights. Each verifier request is a window of 1,024 tokens, and each proof checks one token. The prover runs on a server with a single H100 and 24 CPU cores, and the verifier on a CPU.

Comparison with plain inference: We ran vLLM, a widely used inference engine, with the FP8 release of the same model on eight H100s, and found that, per GPU, proving a batch of 24 requests takes about 72 times longer than vLLM takes to process the same 24 requests at once (66 to 77 across runs), and about 94 times longer when vLLM runs at the highest load we tried.

Inside the system. The underlying mechanism behind FlashProve is a zkSNARK of the kind deployed in peer-to-peer systems (e.g., L2 networks such as Starknet or Mantle for blockchains like Ethereum). Our zkSNARK is built according to a well-established recipe: an underlying information-theoretic object called an interactive oracle proof (IOP) is compiled into a cryptographic proof by relying on hash functions (and offers even post-quantum security). Our IOP is assembled from state-of-the-art building blocks using tools such as code proximity tests with linear constraints and lookup arguments, which are based on techniques from coding theory and complexity theory. Combining these pieces into a bespoke IOP for inference is a delicate task; more details about the construction can be found in the technical report.
