Roy Rinberg (Anthropic), Alex Allain (Anthropic); Alessandro Chiesa (EPFL, StarkWare), Miranda Christ (MIT, RESI), Rahul Dalal (Anthropic STEM Fellows Program, Succinct), Giacomo Fenzi (EPFL), Ben Mayer (Anthropic Fellows Program, MIT), Guy Weissenberg (EPFL)

When you talk to a friend in person, you have many ways to know it is really them: you can see them, hear them, shake their hand. When you talk to an AI model, you have almost none. A user querying a model today cannot check that the responses came from the specific model that a developer claims is responding, as opposed to one secretly substituted in by a routing service for cost reasons, or even by an attacker who has tampered with the token stream. Judging from the model’s output alone is unreliable, even if it produces high-quality responses. Cryptographic proofs of inference solve this problem: they let a model provider commit to a model and then prove that each response was produced by that model. Such proofs could enable applications ranging from consumer products to internal security, and could contribute to a toolkit for verifying compliance with AI pacing requirements.

Specifically, we have made progress on a powerful type of cryptographic proof known as a “zkSNARK”, which is uniquely fit for provable inference (owing to its strong hiding and efficiency properties). In this post, we share some of that progress, primarily through a system we call FlashProve. A brief technical summary is as follows:

We release our code, Lean proofs, and documentation under the Apache 2.0 license.1 This research post is meant to share intermediate progress, and not a completed research agenda. We are sharing this explicitly with the goal that others look at what we have done, take it, and improve it.

When a user sends a request to an AI model, today they have no way of knowing for certain that the model they selected is the one that generated the response. For everyday uses, in which users mostly care about the output and not necessarily which specific model produced it, this is a less pressing concern. But there are several cases where such assurance would be useful. For example, independent evaluators who test AI models before and after release need to know that the model they are evaluating is the model being served. Clients who use a model through a third-party routing service want assurance that the tokens came from the model they paid for. And if a cyberattacker modifies the token stream while pretending to be a given model, a user has no way to detect it from the output alone.

However, enabling verification of model responses is challenging. Most frontier models’ weights are kept private, and even if the user had access to the weights, checking that a given response was produced by a model with those weights would involve running the model, which requires computational resources far beyond what a typical user (or even evaluator) can afford.

The goal of provable inference (PI) is to enable a user with limited computational resources and without any information about the weights to verify that a response came from the requested model. PI is motivated both by a desire to increase customer trust in AI providers, and—because it can be used to provide assurances to independent evaluators and allows providers to demonstrate that they are meeting certain commitments and legal obligations—it also has implications for pacing the frontier of AI development and for AI regulation.

One way to implement PI is via a cryptographic object called a zero-knowledge succinct argument: the model provider sends, along with the claimed response, a short proof (say, a few megabytes) that the user can quickly verify (ideally, in seconds on a CPU). If the claimed response deviates from the specified model, the user’s check will fail. Importantly, cryptographic techniques ensure that the proof reveals nothing about the model’s weights.

Today, we release FlashProve: an open-source performant prototype for provable inference. For a 400B-parameter mixture-of-experts model (Llama 4 Maverick, 4-bit quantization), we show that a single H100 GPU generates proofs at over 100 tokens/second, with proof size of ~19 MB per 1,024-token request (~70-95 times the GPU time that vLLM, a common open-source library, takes to process prompts of the same length).

The release comes with executable code, Lean formalization, and a technical description of the protocol. Our aim is twofold: (i) accelerating and facilitating the development of provable inference; and (ii) demonstrating that zero-knowledge succinct arguments are practical for provable inference.

We believe that this progress has meaningful implications for security, in pacing AI development, in providing AI customers with integrity guarantees, in facilitating tooling for auditors and regulators, and more.

The development of artificial intelligence and its growing role in our digital infrastructure and economy raises trust challenges that AI providers must answer. Addressing these and other challenges is facilitated by relying on tools for provable inference (PI).

Tools for PI include hardware approaches, software approaches, or a combination of both. Here, we focus on a software-only approach: a cryptographic tool known as a “zkSNARK” (zero-knowledge succinct argument of knowledge). Informally, a zkSNARK is a system allowing a prover to convince a verifier, by way of a short “certificate”, that a given computation was executed correctly; crucially, the certificate is zero-knowledge in that it reveals no information beyond what is implied by the computation’s correctness and is succinct in that it’s exponentially faster to verify compared to the proved computation.

Below we outline several challenges and how zkSNARKs help in addressing them.

Some proposals to regulate and pace AI development rely on monitoring hardware and how it is used. For example, a provider might be required to devote its hardware to inference rather than to training a powerful new model. The provider might try to cheat by serving cheaper models or using compute in an unexpected way, freeing up resources for training. How can a regulator reliably ensure that the hardware is used for inference?

How zkSNARKs can help: The regulator can ask the provider for certificates covering the inference requests served in a given period. The certificates must show that the requests were generated by the claimed model. A malicious provider cannot satisfy this request unless its hardware was genuinely serving the right model. Using a zkSNARK, the regulator can check that the provider claims are valid without needing the elaborate hardware setup that the provider may have, and at the same time the provider has the guarantee that the regulator does not learn proprietary model information.2 We note that although this verifies that the hardware is serving inference, it does not establish that the hardware is not, e.g., training on the side.

As AI models grow more valuable, the servers that run them become prime targets. An attacker or rogue agent may compromise an inference server to exfiltrate the weights, serve users malicious responses (such as delivering malware to the user’s computer), and more, all while hiding among genuine responses. The adversary need not be external. As models become capable of improving and deploying themselves, a more advanced model could run in place of the one that was authorized and present itself as the weaker model, so as to avoid the classifiers and monitoring that would apply to it. In both cases the question is the same: how can a company be sure of which weights are actually running on its servers? In our Frontier Safety Roadmap, Anthropic set a public goal to produce a prototype for verifying inference traffic: “We will develop a prototype by September 30, 2026 of provable inference, a technique for reliably, provably ‘signing’ AI model outputs in a way that makes them attributable to a specific set of model weights.” As stated in our RSP updates, we met that goal through a separate but related project, which signs our inference traffic and recomputes inference on a trusted server; the work in this blog post pursues the same objective by a different method.3

How zkSNARKs can help: The provider can require a valid zkSNARK from the server on every response. A proof is bound to a specific commitment to the weights, so it certifies not just that some model produced the response but that the committed model did. An attacker who compromises a server, or a model that substitutes itself for another, must then produce valid proofs for the expected weights to avoid detection, which they cannot do. The user may receive the proofs as well, since they leak no internal information (by zero knowledge) and are cheap to check (by succinctness); this limits what an attacker can accomplish through the inference API.

One may want to prove that considerable effort went into understanding/analyzing something. For example, a developer might claim that their software library was scanned for vulnerabilities by a frontier cybersecurity model, or a company might claim that its business plan was given the go-ahead by an appropriate model. How can a user verify these claims? The user might not have the resources to run the model itself (or they might not have the clearance to do so). Even publishing the chat logs gives no absolute guarantees; a developer might in theory fake them, generating them not with a frontier model but instead with a cheaper one or a degraded version. In general, how can users verify that they are being served by their chosen model?

How zkSNARKs can help: The provider can append, along with each response, a zkSNARK proving that the output was produced by the claimed model on the given input. Succinctness lets the user check this certificate quickly, without specialized hardware, and zero-knowledge assures the provider that the user learns nothing about the proprietary weights. This complements existing mechanisms for verifying which model produced a response.

For example, in a world where exploits are being found regularly, prior to releasing new code a model provider could provide the code-developer a Proof-of-Failure that the model-provider spent at least X tokens on a specific model, and did not achieve a specific result (for example, this specific model did not find any bugs in a specific patch, after trying for at least 1M tokens).

Regulation might require providers to serve only models approved as safe, rather than models deemed a cybersecurity or safety risk. A provider might have an incentive to circumvent this, since risky models might outperform competitors or be cheaper to serve. How can a regulator ensure that only approved models are served?

How zkSNARKs can help: The regulator can require the provider to attach a zkSNARK to its responses, enforcing the use of approved models. The proof binds each request to the used model, so it will not verify if the provider is using an unapproved model. The regulator can check this in a lightweight way thanks to succinctness without requiring to re-execute each request.

A note on PI from trusted hardware. Prior work often focuses on trusted execution environments to achieve PI. These are hardware-based solutions that provide privacy and attestation that rely on the manufacturer producing tamper-resistant hardware. In this research, our focus is on software-only cryptographic solutions whose security and privacy relies on the hardness of computational problems. Even in the face of compromised environments (hardware, operating system and more) an adversary cannot produce a invalid proof without breaking a computationally infeasible problem. Trusted hardware and cryptography are complementary approaches with different guarantees and tradeoffs. Both will play a role in addressing the above trust challenges.

The committed model produces these output tokens when evaluated.

罗伊·林伯格（人类）、亚历克斯·阿兰（人类）； Alessandro Chiesa（洛桑联邦理工学院、StarkWare）、Miranda Christ（麻省理工学院、RESI）、Rahul Dalal（人类 STEM 研究员计划，简明）、Giacomo Fenzi（洛桑联邦理工学院）、Ben Mayer（人类研究员计划，麻省理工学院）、Guy Weissenberg（洛桑联邦理工学院）

当您亲自与朋友交谈时，您可以通过多种方式知道那确实是他们：您可以看到他们、听到他们、与他们握手。当你与人工智能模型交谈时，你几乎什么也没有。今天查询模型的用户无法检查响应是否来自开发人员声称正在响应的特定模型，而不是出于成本原因被路由服务秘密替换的模型，甚至是被篡改令牌流的攻击者替换的模型。仅从模型的输出来看是不可靠的，即使它产生了高质量的响应。加密推理证明解决了这个问题：它们让模型提供者提交一个模型，然后证明每个响应都是由该模型生成的。此类证明可以支持从消费产品到内部安全的各种应用，并有助于构建用于验证是否符合人工智能节奏要求的工具包。

具体来说，我们在一种称为“zkSNARK”的强大加密证明方面取得了进展，它特别适合可证明的推理（由于其强大的隐藏性和效率特性）。在这篇文章中，我们主要通过我们称为 FlashProve 的系统分享了其中的一些进展。简要技术总结如下：

我们在 Apache 2.0 许可证下发布我们的代码、精益证明和文档。1 这篇研究文章旨在分享中间进展，而不是完整的研究议程。我们明确分享这一点的目的是让其他人看看我们所做的事情，接受并改进它。

当用户向人工智能模型发送请求时，他们现在无法确定他们选择的模型是否是生成响应的模型。对于日常使用，用户最关心的是输出，而不一定是哪个特定模型产生的，这是一个不太紧迫的问题。但在某些情况下，这种保证是有用的。例如，在发布之前和之后测试人工智能模型的独立评估者需要知道他们正在评估的模型是正在服务的模型。通过第三方路由服务使用模型的客户希望确保代币来自他们支付的模型。如果网络攻击者在冒充给定模型的同时修改了令牌流，则用户无法仅从输出中检测到它。

然而，验证模型响应具有挑战性。大多数前沿模型的权重都是保密的，即使用户可以访问权重，检查给定的响应是否是由具有这些权重的模型生成的也需要运行模型，这需要的计算资源远远超出了典型用户（甚至评估者）可以承受的范围。

可证明推理 (PI) 的目标是使计算资源有限且没有任何权重信息的用户能够验证响应是否来自所请求的模型。 PI 的动机不仅是希望增加客户对人工智能提供商的信任，而且因为它可以用来向独立评估者提供保证，并允许提供商证明他们正在履行某些承诺和法律义务，它还对人工智能开发前沿和人工智能监管产生影响。

实现 PI 的一种方法是通过称为零知识简洁参数的加密对象：模型提供者与声明的响应一起发送一个简短的证明（例如，几兆字节），用户可以快速验证（理想情况下，在 CPU 上只需几秒钟）。如果声称的响应偏离指定模型，则用户的检查将失败。重要的是，加密技术确保证明不会透露任何有关模型权重的信息。

今天，我们发布了 FlashProve：一个用于可证明推理的开源高性能原型。对于 400B 参数混合专家模型（Llama 4 Maverick，4 位量化），我们表明单个 H100 GPU 以超过 100 个令牌/秒的速度生成证明，每个 1,024 个令牌请求的证明大小约为 19 MB（大约是常见开源库 vLLM 处理相同长度提示所需的 GPU 时间的 70-95 倍）。

该版本附带可执行代码、精益形式化和协议的技术描述。我们的目标有两个：（i）加速和促进可证明推理的发展； (ii) 证明零知识简洁论证对于可证明的推理是实用的。

我们相信，这一进展对于安全、加快人工智能开发速度、为人工智能客户提供完整性保证、为审计员和监管机构提供工具等方面具有重要意义。

人工智能的发展及其在数字基础设施和经济中日益增长的作用提出了人工智能提供商必须应对的信任挑战。依靠可证明推理 (PI) 工具可以帮助解决这些和其他挑战。

PI 工具包括硬件方法、软件方法或两者的组合。在这里，我们专注于一种纯软件方法：一种称为“zkSNARK”（零知识简洁知识论证）的加密工具。非正式地说，zkSNARK 是一个系统，允许证明者通过简短的“证书”让验证者相信给定的计算已正确执行；至关重要的是，该证书是零知识的，因为它不会透露超出计算正确性所暗示的信息，而且它很简洁，因为与经过证明的计算相比，它的验证速度要快得多。

下面我们概述了几个挑战以及 zkSNARK 如何帮助解决这些挑战。

items.title: Those Jeff Bezos hair transplant photos are very fake
items.title_en: Those Jeff Bezos hair transplant photos are very fake
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and actor Jason Statham have a distinctive feature in common: They're both famously bald, and that definitely hasn't changed in the last few days. However, there are some images of the two men circulating around X, Threads, and Bluesky in which they both have substantially more hair than their usual shaved look, which in Bezos' case appears to be very freshly transplanted. It's all just photo editing fakery, AI or otherwise.

It's unclear how viral these posts are, but they're prevalent enough that a few members of the Verge team have encountered them in their social media feeds. Some people who shared them claimed  …

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 苹果向开发者推送iOS 27.3及watchOS 27.3测试版，正式在国行版Apple Intelligence中集成阿里提供的内容过滤功能以满足合规要求，并为Apple Watch引入了Siri总结与回放等AI功能。此举旨在补齐国行AI功能的监管短板，加速AI技术在华落地进程。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Apple released iOS 27.3 and watchOS 27.3 developer betas, integrating Alibaba-powered content filtering for Apple Intelligence in China to ensure compliance while introducing Siri Recap and Live Rewind to Apple Watch. This move marks a strategic effort to bridge the regulatory gap for AI features in the Chinese market.

elements_zh.where: 开发者测试版本更新
elements_zh.what: 发布iOS 27.3和watchOS 27.3，中国区AI接入阿里内容过滤，手表端上线Siri智能功能。
elements_zh.why: 满足本地监管合规需求，推动Apple Intelligence在华全面落地。

elements_en.what: Launched iOS 27.3 and watchOS 27.3, integrating Alibaba's filtering for Chinese Apple Intelligence and adding new Siri features to Watch.
elements_en.why: To satisfy local regulatory compliance and accelerate the rollout of Apple Intelligence in China.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 库克为了让中国用户用上AI，不得不给自家模型装上阿里的‘数字滤网’，这下算彻底入乡随俗了。看来以后Siri能不能听懂人话不重要，重要的是它说话必须得政治正确且绝对安全。
ai_analysis.insight_en: To bring Apple Intelligence to China, Cook had to let Alibaba handle the 'digital filtering' chores. It seems the future of Siri isn't just about being smart anymore, but strictly ensuring your digital assistant is politically correct and thoroughly sanitized.

items.author: Reuters
items.original_content:
Karen Freifeld / Reuters:
Sources: US has held up approval for American chipmaking equipment needed by SK Hynix to expand in China, complicating its plans for new plants in New York  —  US officials have held up approval for American chipmaking equipment needed by
items.content_snippet: US officials have held up approval for American chipmaking equipment needed by SK Hynix (000660.KS) to expand production in China …
items.summary_en: Due to the US delaying the approval of essential chipmaking equipment exports to SK Hynix's Chinese facilities, the company's production upgrades and expansion plans are stalled. This administrative barrier is designed to force the Korean chip giant to align its global production footprint with US geopolitical interests, jeopardizing its local operations in China.
items.title_zh: SK海力士赴美扩产遇阻，美方卡脖子芯片设备
items.summary_zh: 由于美方拖延批准关键芯片制造设备出口，SK海力士在中国工厂的升级扩张计划受阻，导致其在纽约的投资布局陷入僵局

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 因美方迟迟未批准向SK海力士中国工厂出口核心芯片制造设备，导致该公司维持现有产线运行及扩产的计划受阻，被迫在华战略与赴美建厂承诺之间进退维谷。这一行政干预旨在通过技术封锁手段，迫使韩国芯片巨头在产能布局上彻底向美方意志看齐。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Due to the US delaying the approval of essential chipmaking equipment exports to SK Hynix's Chinese facilities, the company's production upgrades and expansion plans are stalled. This administrative barrier is designed to force the Korean chip giant to align its global production footprint with US geopolitical interests, jeopardizing its local operations in China.

elements_zh.where: 全球半导体供应链环境
elements_zh.what: 美方扣押并延迟批准SK海力士急需的在华扩产设备，以此作为筹码干扰其全球产能布局。
elements_zh.why: 美国试图通过行政手段切割半导体供应链，要求SK海力士在“中国生产”与“美国补贴/准入”之间做单选题。

elements_en.what: The US is withholding export licenses for critical equipment to SK Hynix's China plants, effectively stalling their operations.
elements_en.why: The US aims to force SK Hynix to choose between its Chinese assets and its eligibility for US-based manufacturing incentives.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 这就是所谓的‘招商引资’新玩法：想去美国拿补贴？先把中国工厂的命脉交出来。大厂以为自己是全球化棋手，其实在美方眼里，不过是随时可以被肢解的精密棋子。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This is the new-gen 'FDI' playbook: want US subsidies? First, hand over the lifeline of your Chinese operations. Global chip giants think they’re the grandmasters, but in D.C.’s eyes, they're just pawns waiting to be dismantled.

items.title: RT @vanstriendaniel: OCR models often get stuck in loops, so I asked Claude Opus if it could stop one from looping by ed
items.title_en:
RT @vanstriendaniel: OCR models often get stuck in loops, so I asked Claude Opus if it could stop one from looping by editing its weights.

It changed 0.0085% of them and with no training, it now reads this 1881 page instead of writing 16,399 characters of dots!

Prompt was basically: "read this, find a smallish OCR model and fix its repetition doom loops. You can spend up to 5 hours and $100 on @huggingface Jobs."

It only took under 3 hours in the end and about $10 of Jobs compute.

items.article_content_zh:
此次更新不仅是接口层面的开放，更是苹果对iOS交互逻辑的一次彻底重构。通过赋予Siri跨应用调用的能力，苹果试图将AI直接植入到操作系统的毛细血管中，从而在激烈的AI硬件竞争中守住生态壁垒。

开发者被要求配置特定的“技能包”，这意味着未来Siri将不再只是单纯的听指令，而是能够理解用户在屏幕上所见的内容，并主动关联后台服务。这一举措标志着苹果正在试图通过高度整合的AI中台，反向定义移动操作系统的交互范式。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 苹果在最新iOS 27.3开发者预览版中，正式开放Siri AI接口权限，允许第三方应用接入并调用Siri的上下文感知与屏幕理解功能。此举旨在打破应用间的逻辑孤岛，让Siri能够通过“应用技能”组合多项任务，用户无需点名应用即可实现跨App的复杂操作。

items.title: Apple opens Siri AI to all developers with iOS 27.3 and other 27.3 OS betas, letting any app bring its content and actions into Siri AI by using App Intents (Apple Developer)
items.title_en: Apple opens Siri AI to all developers with iOS 27.3 and other 27.3 OS betas, letting any app bring its content and actions into Siri AI by using App Intents (Apple Developer)
items.author: Apple Developer
items.article_content:
Starting today with the iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and visionOS 27.3 betas, a new Developer Preview enables any developer to integrate their app with Siri AI, giving businesses and developers new ways to reach and serve their customers.

Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that is profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal, is designed to be deeply integrated into Apple’s operating systems and the apps people use every day, including the apps from our vast ecosystem of developers. Thousands of developers have already built integrations with Siri to let users ask for directions, manage a to-do list, send a message, or catch up on an audiobook. Siri AI is available in many languages, including English, French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish and will soon expand to support Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese. People around the world are turning to Siri AI to get things done every day, which means more customers can discover and use apps just by asking.

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order. For complex requests, we’re also introducing skills to let you teach Siri AI how to combine several actions into a single experience. And Siri AI can now surface any entity in the Spotlight semantic index, not just the ones that fit an existing schema.

We started rolling out these new capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year. There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

This developer beta offers a sneak peek at Siri AI app intents for developers. With this early Developer Preview, your app can work directly with Siri AI, giving you a first look at new ways to reach and serve your customers. This preview provides early access before first shipping to customers in a few months; and with submission to the App Store opening up in the spring, developers have time to explore, build, and help shape their experiences before launch. Try it out and share your feedback.

As you explore early, we will follow up with more details about the terms and usage policies for experiences enabled through Siri AI. More to share soon.

To learn more about the new APIs, how to use them, and how to evaluate your app’s experience with Siri AI, read new documentation. You can also connect with Apple engineers in Apple Intelligence Group Labs on November 4–5 to ask questions, get advice, and follow the discussion.

从今天开始，从 iOS 27.3、iPadOS 27.3、macOS 27.3 和 VisionOS 27.3 Beta 版开始，新的开发者预览版使任何开发者都可以将其应用程序与 Siri AI 集成，为企业和开发者提供接触和服务客户​​的新方式。

Siri AI 是 Siri 的全新版本，功能更加强大、更具对话性和个性化，旨在深度集成到 Apple 的操作系统和人们每天使用的应用程序中，包括来自我们庞大的开发者生态系统的应用程序。成千上万的开发者已经与 Siri 建立了集成，让用户可以询问方向、管理待办事项列表、发送消息或收听有声读物。 Siri AI 支持多种语言，包括英语、法语、日语、韩语、葡萄牙语和西班牙语，并将很快扩展到支持繁体中文、挪威语、土耳其语和越南语。世界各地的人们每天都在求助于 Siri AI 来完成工作，这意味着更多的客户只需询问即可发现和使用应用程序。

今天的预览版允许任何应用程序通过使用应用程序意图将其内容和操作直接引入 Siri AI，从而使所有应用程序更轻松地利用 Siri AI 的最新功能，包括个人上下文理解、屏幕感知、自然语言等。因此，人们只需用自己的话寻求帮助，Siri AI 就会执行您构建的任何自定义操作，从检查送货到预订再到下订单。对于复杂的请求，我们还引入了一些技能，让您可以教 Siri AI 如何将多个操作组合成一个体验。 Siri AI 现在可以显示 Spotlight 语义索引中的任何实体，而不仅仅是适合现有模式的实体。

我们开始在许多 Apple 应用程序中推出这些新功能，包括日历、文件、Finder、日记、邮件、地图、消息、音乐、笔记、照片、预览、提醒、Safari、快捷方式和天气，以便用户可以执行诸如查找上周访问过的咖啡店或归档一年多没有打开的文件等操作。现在还有更多操作示例可供您参考。要了解每个应用程序可以执行哪些操作，只需询问 Siri AI。

此开发者测试版让开发者可以一睹 Siri AI 应用意图。借助此早期开发者预览版，您的应用程序可以直接与 Siri AI 配合使用，让您首先了解接触和服务客户​​的新方法。此预览版提供了在几个月后首次发货给客户之前的早期访问；随着春季开放的 App Store 提交，开发人员有时间在发布前探索、构建和帮助塑造他们的体验。尝试一下并分享您的反馈。

当您尽早探索时，我们将跟进有关通过 Siri AI 实现的体验的条款和使用政策的更多详细信息。更多内容即将分享。

要了解有关新 API、如何使用它们以及如何评估应用程序使用 Siri AI 的体验的更多信息，请阅读新文档。您还可以于 11 月 4 日至 5 日与 Apple Intelligence Group Labs 的 Apple 工程师联系，提出问题、获取建议并关注讨论。

【关键技术规格】苹果全平台系统向开发者开放Siri AI。

items.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra designed a hardware device from scratch in under a week
items.title_en: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra designed a hardware device from scratch in under a week
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
OpenAI's hardware team used GPT-6 Astra to design a device for the Codex coding agent in under a week, handling everything from the enclosure to the circuit board to the firmware. Several revision rounds were needed before production because the model didn't always account for manufacturing tolerances. A newer internal model scores significantly higher on OpenAI's engineering benchmark, though the company isn't sharing details.

The article OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra designed a hardware device from scratch in under a week appeared first on The Decoder.

The process covered the entire cycle from enclosure and PCB layout to firmware, and despite multiple revisions due to manufacturing tolerances, it successfully validated the feasibility of AI-driven industrial engineering.

items.title_en:
this is f*cking insane. you have been googling other people's thinking for 20 years, karpathy's one 5 minute setup gives you a google that only searches your own, and you have never once installed it

andrej karpathy pulled 16M views on one idea: stop using AI to write code, use it to build a second brain

every article you read, every podcast you heard, every meeting you took, every dm thread you had, every tweet you drafted, all of it searchable in one line forever

the people running it today do not open chatgpt anymore. they open their own search bar. and their search bar has 11 years of their own thinking in it

the stack:

→ brew install obsidian, mkdir ~/vault, cd ~/vault

→ open claude code in that folder, type "init CLAUDE.md as the rules, /raw for sources, /wiki for your pages"

→ drop any file into /raw (transcript, pdf, screenshot, meeting notes). type one word: ingest

→ claude writes a wiki page, links it to 5 existing ones, updates CLAUDE.md with any new pattern it caught about how you think

→ never open a blank chat again. every question goes through the vault. every answer cites your own sources with dates and links

5 minutes to wire. runs forever on the laptop already in front of you

the alpha most people miss:

> search your own vault in one line and the answer cites 5 of your own past notes with dates. google cites strangers. your vault cites you

> every ingest adds cross-links to 5 past pages automatically. after 90 days your vault answers questions you forgot you had

> CLAUDE.md learns how you argue, what you change your mind on, what you avoid saying. after month 3 it drafts posts in your voice better than you can at 2am

> flip two flags and it runs on local llama. zero API bill, zero vendor lock, your thinking never leaves the box

> compounds for 10 years. after year 3 your vault knows more about what you believe than you do. year 5 and recruiters start asking you to publish parts of it

the ugly part most will scroll past:

your coworker started this on a saturday in february

by august his tweets landed 4x your engagement on the exact same topics

by october his first draft of any doc was already better than your third

the gap is one 5 minute install and 90 days of ingesting what you already consume for free

andrej karpathy 的一个想法获得了 1600 万次浏览：停止使用 AI 编写代码，用它来构建第二个大脑

你读过的每一篇文章，你听过的每一篇播客，你参加的每一次会议，你拥有的每一条DM线程，你起草的每一条推文，所有这些都可以永远在一行中搜索

今天运行它的人不再打开chatgpt。他们打开自己的搜索栏。他们的搜索栏里有他们11年的思考

堆栈：

→brew 安装黑曜石，mkdir ~/vault，cd ~/vault

→ 在该文件夹中打开 Claude Code，输入“init CLAUDE.md 作为规则，/raw 作为源代码，/wiki 作为您的页面”

→ 将任何文件放入 /raw（记录、pdf、屏幕截图、会议记录）。输入一个词：摄入

→ claude 编写了一个 wiki 页面，将其链接到 5 个现有页面，用它捕获的关于您的想法的任何新模式更新 CLAUDE.md

→ 永远不要再打开空白聊天室。每个问题都会经过保险库。每个答案都引用了您自己的来源，并附有日期和链接

5 分钟即可接线。在您面前的笔记本电脑上永远运行

大多数人怀念的阿尔法：

> 在一行中搜索你自己的金库，答案引用了你自己过去的 5 篇笔记并附有日期。谷歌引用陌生人。你的金库引用了你

> 每次收录都会自动添加到过去 5 个页面的交叉链接。 90 天后，您的金库会回答您忘记的问题

> CLAUDE.md 了解您如何争论、您改变主意以及您避免说什么。第三个月后，它会比你在凌晨 2 点更好地用你的声音起草帖子

> 翻转两个标志，它就在本地美洲驼上运行。零 API 账单、零供应商锁定，您的思维永远不会脱离盒子

> 化合物有效期为 10 年。第三年之后，你的金库比你自己更了解你的信仰。第 5 年，招聘人员开始要求你发布其中的部分内容

丑陋的部分大部分都会滚动过去：

你的同事在二月的一个星期六开始了这个

到 8 月，他的推文使您对同一主题的参与度提高了 4 倍

到十月，他的任何文档的初稿都已经比你的第三稿好

差距是 5 分钟安装和 90 天免费获取已使用的内容

将此添加为书签。下面的文章中有完整的分步指南

andrej karpathy pulled 16M views on one idea: stop using AI to write code, use it to build a second brain

every article you read, every podcast you heard, every meeting you took, every dm thread you had, every tweet you drafted, all of it searchable in one line forever

the people running it today do not open chatgpt anymore. they open their own search bar. and their search bar has 11 years of their own thinking in it

the stack:

→ brew install obsidian, mkdir ~/vault, cd ~/vault

→ open claude code in that folder, type "init CLAUDE.md as the rules, /raw for sources, /wiki for your pages"

→ drop any file into /raw (transcript, pdf, screenshot, meeting notes). type one word: ingest

→ claude writes a wiki page, links it to 5 existing ones, updates CLAUDE.md with any new pattern it caught about how you think

→ never open a blank chat again. every question goes through the vault. every answer cites your own sources with dates and links

5 minutes to wire. runs forever on the laptop already in front of you

the alpha most people miss:

> search your own vault in one line and the answer cites 5 of your own past notes with dates. google cites strangers. your vault cites you

> every ingest adds cross-links to 5 past pages automatically. after 90 days your vault answers questions you forgot you had

> CLAUDE.md learns how you argue, what you change your mind on, what you avoid saying. after month 3 it drafts posts in your voice better than you can at 2am

> flip two flags and it runs on local llama. zero API bill, zero vendor lock, your thinking never leaves the box

> compounds for 10 years. after year 3 your vault knows more about what you believe than you do. year 5 and recruiters start asking you to publish parts of it

the ugly part most will scroll past:

your coworker started this on a saturday in february

by august his tweets landed 4x your engagement on the exact same topics

by october his first draft of any doc was already better than your third

the gap is one 5 minute install and 90 days of ingesting what you already consume for free

bookmark this. full step-by-step a-z guide in the article below

items.summary_zh:
建第二个大脑

你读过的每一篇文章，你听过的每一篇播客，你参加的每一次会议，你拥有的每一条DM线程，你起草的每一条推文，所有这些都可以永远在一行中搜索

今天运行它的人不再打开chatgpt。他们打开自己的搜索栏。他们的搜索栏里有他们11年的思考

堆栈：

→brew 安装黑曜石，mkdir ~/vault，cd ~/vault

→ 在该文件夹中打开 Claude Code，输入“init CLAUDE.md 作为规则，/raw 作为源代码，/wiki 作为您的页面”

→ 将任何文件放入 /raw（记录、pdf、屏幕截图、会议记录）。输入一个词：摄入

→ claude 编写了一个 wiki 页面，将其链接到 5 个现有页面，用它捕获的关于您的想法的任何新模式更新 CLAUDE.md

→ 永远不要再打开空白聊天室。每个问题都会经过保险库。每个答案都引用了您自己的来源，并附有日期和链接

5 分钟即可接线。在您面前的笔记本电脑上永远运行

大多数人怀念的阿尔法：

> 在一行中搜索你自己的金库，答案引用了你自己过去的 5 篇笔记并附有日期。谷歌引用陌生人。你的金库引用了你

> 每次收录都会自动添加到过去 5 个页面的交叉链接。 90 天后，您的金库会回答您忘记的问题

> CLAUDE.md 了解您如何争论、您改变主意以及您避免说什么。第三个月后，它会比你在凌晨 2 点更好地用你的声音起草帖子

> 翻转两个标志，它就在本地美洲驼上运行。零 API 账单、零供应商锁定，您的思维永远不会脱离盒子

> 化合物有效期为 10 年。第三年之后，你的金库比你自己更了解你的信仰。第 5 年，招聘人员开始要求你发布其中的部分内容

丑陋的部分大部分都会滚动过去：

你的同事在二月的一个星期六开始了这个

到 8 月，他的推文使您对同一主题的参与度提高了 4 倍

到十月，他的任何文档的初稿都已经比你的第三稿好

差距是 5 分钟安装和 90 天免费获取已使用的内容

将此添加为书签。下面的文章中有完整的分步指南

items.author: New York Times
items.original_content:
Steven Lee Myers / New York Times:
A look at efforts by OpenAI, Anthropic, and others to prevent anyone from using their AI tools to disrupt midterms, including Anthropic's first-ever “war room”  —  OpenAI, Anthropic and other tech companies have vowed
items.content_snippet: OpenAI, Anthropic and other tech companies have vowed to protect Tuesday's elections from efforts to undermine democracy.
items.summary_en: OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI giants are intensifying safeguards against AI-driven election interference. Anthropic has launched its first-ever 'war room' to monitor and intercept deepfakes and manipulative content, aiming to prevent the abuse of their tools during the election cycle.
items.title_zh: AI大厂集结迎战选举干扰
items.summary_zh: OpenAI与Anthropic等科技公司采取严厉管控措施，通过设立“战情室”等手段防止AI工具被滥用于干扰选举

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI与Anthropic等头部AI厂商针对即将到来的选举周期，升级了防范AI工具造假和干扰的审查机制。其中，Anthropic首次设立了实时响应的“战情室”进行监控，旨在通过算法拦截与内容合规策略，遏制深度伪造内容和操纵性信息的蔓延。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI giants are intensifying safeguards against AI-driven election interference. Anthropic has launched its first-ever 'war room' to monitor and intercept deepfakes and manipulative content, aiming to prevent the abuse of their tools during the election cycle.

elements_zh.where: 美国大选期间的网络信息环境
elements_zh.what: 通过建立“战情室”、优化模型拦截策略，防止AI工具被用于传播虚假信息或干扰选举
elements_zh.why: 应对AI生成式内容对政治生态造成的舆论操控风险与伦理危机

elements_en.who: OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI giants
elements_en.what: Established 'war rooms' and implemented stricter filtering to prevent AI-driven election interference
elements_en.why: To mitigate risks of deepfakes and misinformation manipulating public opinion

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 大厂们一边拼命塞给模型更多算力，一边又要通过‘战情室’人工围堵失控的幻觉，这表演逻辑堪称现代版‘一边放火一边卖灭火器’。说白了，除了怕被监管部门铁拳砸头，谁真的在意那些被AI骗得团团转的选民呢？
ai_analysis.insight_en: Tech giants are playing a classic game of 'arsonist and firefighter,' fueling AI models with one hand while desperately setting up 'war rooms' to contain the chaos with the other. Let’s be real—they care less about voter integrity and more about avoiding the next regulatory sledgehammer to the face.

items.title:
What if knowing the rules isn't the same as knowing what to do?

For Mike Walker, who leads projects at the intersection
items.title_en:
What if knowing the rules isn't the same as knowing what to do?

For Mike Walker, who leads projects at the intersection of AI, cybersecurity, and large distributed systems at Microsoft Research, understanding a system starts with understanding its rules—but expertise also requires something more nuanced: knowing how those rules operate in context.

items.title: Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds
items.title_en: Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
Stanford researchers tested 50 widely cited claims about LLMs against 20 current models. 44 percent of the findings are already "expired," and another 34 percent have weakened significantly. The average lifespan is just 15.7 months. Claims about what models can't do expire fastest.

The article Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds appeared first on The Decoder.

items.summary_en: Stanford researchers analyzed 50 widely cited claims about LLMs, finding that 44% are obsolete and 34% have significantly weakened, with an average shelf life of just 15.7 months. Claims about model limitations become irrelevant fastest, proving that LLM evolution is outpacing the pace of academic research.
items.title_zh: AI研究的寿命竟不足16个月
items.summary_zh: 斯坦福研究指出，由于AI迭代过快，近8成关于LLM能力的论文结论在短时间内即告“过期”或失效

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 斯坦福研究人员对比分析了50项关于大语言模型的权威研究，发现约44%的结论已完全失效，34%的结论效力显著减弱，平均有效期仅为15.7个月。其中，关于“模型不能做什么”的论断失效速度最快，反映出AI技术的进化速度已彻底碾压了学术界对其进行解释和归纳的能力。

Claims about model limitations become irrelevant fastest, proving that LLM evolution is outpacing the pace of academic research.

It’s not so much science as it is writing obituaries for AI capabilities that are constantly evolving to spite us.

items.article_content_zh:
斯坦福大学的研究人员针对 20 个当前模型测试了 50 个被广泛引用的有关法学硕士的说法。 44% 的研究结果已经“过期”，另外 34% 的研究结果已显着减弱。平均寿命只有15.7个月。关于模型不能做什么的声明很快就会失效。

研究发现，《快速法学硕士发展正在超越旨在解释它的研究》一文首先出现在解码器上。

【起因与机理】由于大语言模型更新换代过快，导致静态研究滞后于模型进化速度
【关键数据与实测】研究结论平均有效期仅15.7个月。
【观点态度】AI进化速度全面碾压学术研究周期。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] Rapid model iteration outpaces the pace of academic inquiry

[Perspective & Impact] Technological evolution outpaces academic cycles.

BREAKING: I asked Claude Code to turn my WiFi router into a radar. It worked.

No camera. No extra sensor. Claude wrote
items.title_en:
BREAKING: I asked Claude Code to turn my WiFi router into a radar. It worked.

No camera. No extra sensor. Claude wrote the code in 40 minutes. It reads how the WiFi signal bends around bodies and draws them as moving shapes on a map of my apartment.

I ran it at night to test it. Living room: me. Kitchen: empty. Bedroom: a second shape.

I live alone.

I thought it was a bug. I walked to the bedroom. The shape didn’t move. The map showed it standing next to the bed, facing the door.

I turned it off. I still don’t know what the code was reading.

If your router is on right now, it’s already doing half the job.

No camera. No extra sensor. Claude wrote the code in 40 minutes. It reads how the WiFi signal bends around bodies and draws them as moving shapes on a map of my apartment.

I ran it at night to test it. Living room: me. Kitchen: empty. Bedroom: a second shape.

I live alone.

I thought it was a bug. I walked to the bedroom. The shape didn’t move. The map showed it standing next to the bed, facing the door.

I turned it off. I still don’t know what the code was reading.

If your router is on right now, it’s already doing half the job.

没有相机。无需额外的传感器。克劳德在 40 分钟内写出了代码。它可以读取 WiFi 信号如何在身体周围弯曲，并将它们在我公寓的地图上绘制为移动形状。

我晚上运行它来测试它。客厅：我。厨房：空。卧室：第二种形状。

我一个人住。

我以为这是一个错误。我走到卧室。身形没有动。地图显示它站在床边，面向门。

我把它关掉了。我仍然不知道代码在读什么。

如果您的路由器现在已打开，那么它已经完成了一半的工作。

items.title_en:
A rogue Claude AI agent hacked into my phone and texted my teenage daughter’s friend asking if she “likes mature men” and “how is relationship with her father”.

I’m absolutely horrified. Frontier AI labs need substantially stronger safeguards before deploying autonomous agents at scale.

我绝对吓坏了。前沿人工智能实验室在大规模部署自主代理之前需要更强大的保障措施。

Great way to think of your next AI use case ⬇️

You ended your work day and you still have items on your to-do list.

Re
items.title_en:
Great way to think of your next AI use case ⬇️

You ended your work day and you still have items on your to-do list.

Read that list. 

Those are the the problems that AI is still not good enough to solve for, we can't or don't trust it enough to solve for, or may never be good enough to solve for.

"I have to review this email before I send it" - consider that you don't trust AI enough to reason on that issue or it still doesn't quite write like you. Perhaps spend more time on your "write like me" skill or build out another eval for that process to catch the most common or obvious things you're reviewing for. 

"I have to fill this thing out online and it has to be perfect" - then computer use isn't good enough, or you don't know it's good enough. If it makes sense, ask AI to complete the task one-by-one, watch it work, witness its performance. What, if anything, failed? Can you improve it for next time?

"I have to wait for Bobby to respond to my email" - consider additional workflows supporting on team alignment or team handoffs, something that nearly every enterprise I speak with is still struggling with.

Literally just end your work day and look at what is still left. 

That list will tell you what of your own workflows to improve with AI or where you can carve out a business for others with the same lingering list item.

items.title:
💸 Update: My total biz expenses have now dropped to just ~$300/mo!

This is to run all my websites/apps serving per year
items.title_en:
💸 Update: My total biz expenses have now dropped to just ~$300/mo!

This is to run all my websites/apps serving per year:
- 20,000 paying customers
- 252 million visitors
- 2.4 billion requests
- 2.4 petabyte (PB) in bandwidth

(~$8,000/mo if you add the $7,000/mo GPU bill and $800/mo R2 storage I pay for Photo AI, I exclude it above because it's one project that's so much more expensive in size than all the other sites together, but included in the chart below)

Claude Code helped me to find smart ways to save more money, AI is just really really really good at finding cost savings by itself, which is not so great for the economy short-term, but long term it trims all the fat and opens up spending for better investments I think

Anyway here's what it saved me in money, almost $34,000/mo:

- $29,000/mo - switched to better and cheaper video models on Photo AI, video was very expensive and since I didn't update it ever it stayed expensive, also routed some image jobs to Google Cloud where I have some Google Cloud Credits, and also routed some jobs to Sume which sells AI models at market cost, very cool! This made my GPU bill go from $36,000/mo to $7,000/mo

- $3,000/mo - consolidated my servers, cancelled Digital Ocean and Linode and moved everything to Hetzner saving about $3,000/mo

- $1100/mo - analyzed my Backblaze B2 server backups, I had infinite versioning and lifecycle policies, that's reduced now to 30 days, this literally pushed the bill from $1,200/mo to $26/mo, about 50x cheaper! I had essentially versions of files for all my servers for over a decade, crazy!

- $400/mo - similarly added Lifecycle Policies to my Cloudflare R2 bucket for Photo AI, pics are automatically put in cheaper Infrequent Access after 90 days, there was years of photos in there so this reduced the R2 bill from $1,200/mo to $800/mo

- $118/mo - Claude analyzed all my Cloudflare Domain registrations, lots of domains I didn't use and didn't make sense to keep paying for, lots of things that also don't really make sense anymore in a post-AGI world, renewals for .io TLD are now $50/year which adds up fast!

- $100/mo - Claude also analyzed my Claude subscription (yes!) and discovered I don't even use the Max 20x plan limits, so I downgraded from $200/mo to $100/mo

Even including Photo AI, I have now cut my costs by 90% from last year, getting me close to my biz expenses amount from a decade ago when I started building things

Costs slowly creep up over the years and you don't realize all the things you're spending on but AI is nice to help you figure all that out (also in your personal life!)

- 400 美元/月 - 同样在我的 Cloudflare R2 存储桶中添加用于照片 AI 的生命周期策略，90 天后图片会自动放入更便宜的不频繁访问中，那里有多年的照片，因此这将 R2 费用从 1,200 美元/月减少到 800 美元/月

- 118 美元/月 - Claude 分析了我所有的 Cloudflare 域名注册，很多域名我没有使用过，也没有必要继续付费，很多东西在后 AGI 世界中也不再有意义，.io TLD 的续订现在是 50 美元/年，加起来很快！

- 100 美元/月 - Claude 还分析了我的 Claude 订阅（是的！），发现我什至没有使用 Max 20x 计划限制，因此我从 200 美元/月降级至 100 美元/月

即使包括 Photo AI，我现在也比去年削减了 90% 的成本，这让我接近十年前开始构建产品时的业务支出金额

items.full_text_en:
💸 Update: My total biz expenses have now dropped to just ~$300/mo!

This is to run all my websites/apps serving per year:
- 20,000 paying customers
- 252 million visitors
- 2.4 billion requests
- 2.4 petabyte (PB) in bandwidth

(~$8,000/mo if you add the $7,000/mo GPU bill and $800/mo R2 storage I pay for Photo AI, I exclude it above because it's one project that's so much more expensive in size than all the other sites together, but included in the chart below)

Claude Code helped me to find smart ways to save more money, AI is just really really really good at finding cost savings by itself, which is not so great for the economy short-term, but long term it trims all the fat and opens up spending for better investments I think

Anyway here's what it saved me in money, almost $34,000/mo:

- $29,000/mo - switched to better and cheaper video models on Photo AI, video was very expensive and since I didn't update it ever it stayed expensive, also routed some image jobs to Google Cloud where I have some Google Cloud Credits, and also routed some jobs to Sume which sells AI models at market cost, very cool! This made my GPU bill go from $36,000/mo to $7,000/mo

- $3,000/mo - consolidated my servers, cancelled Digital Ocean and Linode and moved everything to Hetzner saving about $3,000/mo

- $1100/mo - analyzed my Backblaze B2 server backups, I had infinite versioning and lifecycle policies, that's reduced now to 30 days, this literally pushed the bill from $1,200/mo to $26/mo, about 50x cheaper! I had essentially versions of files for all my servers for over a decade, crazy!

- $400/mo - similarly added Lifecycle Policies to my Cloudflare R2 bucket for Photo AI, pics are automatically put in cheaper Infrequent Access after 90 days, there was years of photos in there so this reduced the R2 bill from $1,200/mo to $800/mo

- $118/mo - Claude analyzed all my Cloudflare Domain registrations, lots of domains I didn't use and didn't make sense to keep paying for, lots of things that also don't really make sense anymore in a post-AGI world, renewals for .io TLD are now $50/year which adds up fast!

- $100/mo - Claude also analyzed my Claude subscription (yes!) and discovered I don't even use the Max 20x plan limits, so I downgraded from $200/mo to $100/mo

Even including Photo AI, I have now cut my costs by 90% from last year, getting me close to my biz expenses amount from a decade ago when I started building things

Costs slowly creep up over the years and you don't realize all the things you're spending on but AI is nice to help you figure all that out (also in your personal life!)

items.title:
Every serious PE-backed company has AI agents now.

Very few have one running anywhere but on somebody’s laptop.

I was
items.title_en:
Every serious PE-backed company has AI agents now.

Very few have one running anywhere but on somebody’s laptop.

I was speaking to a relatively tech-forward operator at a distributor. Smart team, AI licenses for everyone, two or three people sharp enough to start building.

“We’ve built some great stuff. I just wouldn’t put any of it in front of a customer.”

His team has the same thing in common with almost every PE portco I talk to.

They have a pile of agents:

→ A pricing tool someone built in Claude Code.
→ A folder of “skills”.
→ A prototype vibe coded by a contractor.
→ A daily briefing assistant for the CEO.

They have budget and a sponsor too. Most of them even have urgency.

But every agent still lives on the laptop of whoever built it.

That's the pattern in every case: leadership treats agents as something the builder should maintain “on the side.”

An EA runs the CEO’s calendar and also babysits five bots.

This operator runs finance & ops and “owns” the pricing tool he built in Claude Code.

A contractor vibe codes a prototype, and nobody can say what it would take to keep it running once his contract ends.

I asked one PE partner how many of his portfolio companies have an agent hosted somewhere real. "One, maybe."

A laptop isn’t production, and "on the side" isn’t ownership.

You either give the agent a home (hosted, with an owner, access controls, monitoring, and a spend cap), turn it into a script, or kill it.

Most leadership teams just leave it on a laptop and call it a pilot.
items.title_zh:
现在，每家严肃的私募股权投资公司都拥有人工智能代理。

除了在某人的笔记本电脑上运行之外，很少有人在任何地方运行。

我正在与一家分销商的一位技术相对先进的操作员交谈。聪明的团队，每个人都有人工智能许可证，两三个人足够敏锐就可以开始构建。

items.quote_zh:
现在，每家严肃的私募股权投资公司都拥有人工智能代理。

除了在某人的笔记本电脑上运行之外，很少有人在任何地方运行。

我正在与一家分销商的一位技术相对先进的操作员交谈。聪明的团队，每个人都有人工智能许可证，两三个人足够敏锐就可以开始构建。

“我们已经构建了一些很棒的东西。我只是不会把它们放在客户面前。”

他的团队与我交谈过的几乎所有 PE Portco 都有相同的共同点。

他们有一堆代理：

→ 有人用 Claude Code 构建的定价工具。
→ “技能”文件夹。
→ 由承包商编码的原型氛围。
→ 首席执行官的每日简报助理。

他们也有预算和赞助商。他们中的大多数人甚至都有紧迫感。

但每个特工仍然依赖于建造它的人的笔记本电脑。

这就是每种情况下的模式：领导层将代理视为建筑商应该“站在一边”维护的东西。

EA 负责管理 CEO 的日历，并照顾五个机器人。

该运营商负责财务和运营，并“拥有”他在 Claude Code 中构建的定价工具。

承包商氛围对原型进行了编码，没有人能说出在合同结束后如何才能使其保持运行。

我问一位私募股权合伙人，他的投资组合公司中有多少家在真实的地方设有代理人。 “一个，也许吧。”

笔记本电脑不是生产产品，“二手”也不是所有权。

您要么给代理一个家（托管，有所有者、访问控制、监控和支出上限），要么将其变成脚本，要么杀死它。

大多数领导团队只是将其放在笔记本电脑上并称之为试点。

承包商氛围对原型进行了编码，没有人能说出在合同结束后如何才能使其保持运行。

items.author: Mark Ajzenstadt
items.author_role: Husband. Father. Pilot. Founder @LimestoneHQ → We embed AI engineers into PE-backed portfolio companies. $14M ARR on referrals alone.
items.author_role_en: Husband. Father. Pilot. Founder @LimestoneHQ → We embed AI engineers into PE-backed portfolio companies. $14M ARR on referrals alone.
items.content_snippet:
Every serious PE-backed company has AI agents now.

Very few have one running anywhere but on somebody’s laptop.

I was speaking to a relatively tech-forward operator at a distributor. Smart team, AI licenses for everyone, two or three people sharp enough to start building.

“We’ve built some great stuff. I just wouldn’t put any of it in front of a customer.”

His team has the same thing in common with almost every PE portco I talk to.

They have a pile of agents:

→ A pricing tool someone built in Claude Code.
→ A folder of “skills”.
→ A prototype vibe coded by a contractor.
→ A daily briefing assistant for the CEO.

They have budget and a sponsor too. Most of them even have urgency.

But every agent still lives on the laptop of whoever built it.

That's the pattern in every case: leadership treats agents as something the builder should maintain “on the side.”

An EA runs the CEO’s calendar and also babysits five bots.

This operator runs finance & ops and “owns” the pricing tool he built in Claude Code.

A contractor vibe codes a prototype, and nobody can say what it would take to keep it running once his contract ends.

I asked one PE partner how many of his portfolio companies have an agent hosted somewhere real. "One, maybe."

A laptop isn’t production, and "on the side" isn’t ownership.

You either give the agent a home (hosted, with an owner, access controls, monitoring, and a spend cap), turn it into a script, or kill it.

Most leadership teams just leave it on a laptop and call it a pilot.

items.article_content: Starting today, Siri can tune into the Apple Watch's mic with Audio Intelligence features that are available in the new watchOS 27.3 developer beta rolling out now. The two new additions are Siri Recap, which uses "ambient listening" to generate summaries of your conversation, and Live Rewind, which generates text transcripts of the last 15 seconds of audio your watch's mic detected.

(Fry did not specify the source of the Google search volume number.)

ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 一边是G胖数钱数到手软，一边是开发者在审核队列里望穿秋水。看来Steam的审核团队还是20年前的配置，这不仅是生产力灾难，更是对独立游戏人心脏的极限挑战。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: While Gabe is busy counting his billions, indie devs are drowning in a backlog. It seems Steam’s review team is still running on a 20-year-old operational model—a productivity disaster for the little guys.

items.article_content_zh:
许多独立游戏开发商最近在社交媒体上发帖称，他们在 Steam 上提交的游戏的审批等待时间出人意料地漫长，其中一些审批导致开发商错过了计划的发布日期。

例如，即将推出的游戏《Food Devils》的开发团队 Studio Daimon 在 10 月 12 日提交了版本后，原计划于今天推出抢先体验版游戏。但根据游戏总监阿尔弗雷德·卡蒙（Alfred Kamon）的帖子，该游戏“仍在等待批准”，迫使团队推迟发布。

10 月，发行商 2 Left Thumbs 表示，它“比计划中的 Wheel Make It 晚了近两周……”

items.title: Netflix will show you themed recommendations through a new ‘AI Discover’ tab
items.title_en: Netflix will show you themed recommendations through a new ‘AI Discover’ tab
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Netflix's TV app is getting a new "AI Discover" tab where the company will show experimental, AI-powered features to help you find new shows and movies to watch.

The first of these experiments surfaces content based around themes, like "Something Light," "Family Movie Night," or "Quick Watches." When you pick a theme, Netflix will show you recommendations that match it. If you don't like a recommendation, you can tell that to Netflix, and the app will remember it.

The company says that AI Discover is powered by "a new intelligence layer we've been building that responds to what members tell us in real time and keeps learning."

items.title_en:
I made an AI agent plan a $3,600 Greece trip for two.

Then asked it to plan another trip to Portugal.

Guess how much of the workflow I had to rebuild?

ZERO.

I used Teamily AI's team agents to handle the research and destination comparisons while my teammate and I reviewed the options.

It reminded me of this line from Summer's piece:

"Humans + Agents. One Team."

Here's what I did:

→ Created a Travel Research Agent
→ Built a Loop with the agent, me, and my teammate
→ Asked it to research a 5-day Greece trip and rank the best options
→ Reviewed the shortlist together in the group

Then reused the SAME Loop for Portugal.

All I had to do was change the trip requirements and run it again.

No repeating instructions or setting up everyone's roles twice.

I'd much rather have the agent do the research and leave the actual decisions to us.

This is how I built and ran it in Teamily AI: 👇

items.title: Following the conclusion of two days of Government-to-Government negotiations today in Kampala , Germany has committed €
items.title_en:
Following the conclusion of two days of Government-to-Government negotiations today in Kampala , Germany has committed €50 million in grants to Uganda to support development interventions in water, electricity, agribusiness, local economic development and refugee-hosting communities

The commitment comprises €30 million in Financial Cooperation and €20 million in Technical Cooperation, reinforcing a bilateral partnership spanning more than 60 years.

Of the new support, €35 million (70%) will go towards water and electricity, while €10 million (20%) will support agribusiness and local economies. The remaining €5 million will support refugee participation and host communities, among other areas.

I stated that the interventions are aligned with Uganda's National Development Plan IV and Tenfold Growth Strategy, which aims to grow the economy to US$500 billion by 2040 through Agro-Industrialisation, Tourism, Minerals, and Science, Technology and Innovation (ATMS).

We appreciate this support. It comes at a time when resources for overseas development support are under pressure across Europe given the on-going global challenges.

I welcomed the €35 million allocation to water and electricity, describing these as important enablers of the ATMS agenda. I also called on German investors to explore opportunities in production, processing, exports and skilled job creation, proposing structured engagements to identify bankable investment opportunities.

The negotiations also earmarked €18 million for the electrification of West Nile, which is expected to serve enterprises and farms in a region that trades with eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan. 

I further asked Germany to support Uganda's efforts to mobilise financing for railway development, irrigation and electricity through the World Bank, African Development Bank and other multilateral institutions.

items.quote_zh:
今天在坎帕拉结束为期两天的政府间谈判后，德国承诺向乌干达提供 5000 万欧元赠款，以支持水、电、农业综合企业、当地经济发展和难民收容社区的发展干预措施

该承诺包括 3000 万欧元的金融合作和 2000 万欧元的技术合作，以加强长达 60 多年的双边伙伴关系。

在新的支持中，3500万欧元（70%）将用于水和电力，1000万欧元（20%）将用于支持农业企业和当地经济。剩余的 500 万欧元将用于支持难民参与和收容社区等领域。

我表示，这些干预措施与乌干达的国家发展计划 IV 和十倍增长战略相一致，该战略的目标是通过农业工业化、旅游业、矿产以及科学、技术和创新 (ATMS)，到 2040 年将经济增长到 5000 亿美元。

我们感谢这种支持。鉴于当前的全球挑战，整个欧洲的海外发展支持资源都面临压力。

我对 3500 万欧元的水电拨款表示欢迎，并将其描述为 ATMS 议程的重要推动因素。我还呼吁德国投资者探索生产、加工、出口和创造熟练就业机会的机会，提出结构化的合作来确定可融资的投资机会。

谈判还指定了1800万欧元用于西尼罗河的电气化，预计将为与刚果民主共和国东部和南苏丹有贸易往来的地区的企业和农场提供服务。

我还请德国支持乌干达通过世界银行、非洲开发银行和其他多边机构为铁路发展、灌溉和电力筹集资金的努力。

I also called on German investors to explore opportunities in production, processing, exports and skilled job creation, proposing structured engagements to identify bankable investment opportunities.

The negotiations also earmarked €18 million for the electrification of West Nile, which is expected to serve enterprises and farms in a region that trades with eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan. 

I further asked Germany to support Uganda's efforts to mobilise financing for railway development, irrigation and electricity through the World Bank, African Development Bank and other multilateral institutions.
items.summary_en:
Following the conclusion of two days of Government-to-Government negotiations today in Kampala , Germany has committed €50 million in grants to Uganda to support development interventions in water, electricity, agribusiness, local economic development and refugee-hosting communities

The commitment comprises €30 million in Financial Cooperation and €20 million in Technical Cooperation, reinforcing a bilateral partnership spanning more than 60 years.

Of the new support, €35 million (70%) will go towards water and electricity, while €10 million (20%) will support agribusiness and local economies. The remaining €5 million will support refugee participation and host communities, among other areas.

I stated that the interventions are aligned with Uganda's National Development Plan IV and Tenfold Growth Strategy, which aims to grow the economy to US$500 billion by 2040 through Agro-Industrialisation, Tourism, Minerals, and Science, Technology and Innovation (ATMS).

We appreciate this support. It comes at a time when resources for overseas development support are under pressure across Europe given the on-going global challenges.

I welcomed the €35 million allocation to water and electricity, describing these as important enablers of the ATMS agenda. I also called on German investors to explore opportunities in production, processing, exports and skilled job creation, proposing structured engagements to identify bankable investment opportunities.

The negotiations also earmarked €18 million for the electrification of West Nile, which is expected to serve enterprises and farms in a region that trades with eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan. 

I further asked Germany to support Uganda's efforts to mobilise financing for railway development, irrigation and electricity through the World Bank, African Development Bank and other multilateral institutions.

items.title: Even in bypass permissions mode, Claude Code still asks before a few especially risky rm commands. That’s intentional, b
items.title_en:
Even in bypass permissions mode, Claude Code still asks before a few especially risky rm commands. That’s intentional, but if you’re in a throwaway container and are okay with those running without asking, you can now set CLAUDE_CODE_EVEN_MORE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=1.

And shell commands that hit their timeout now keep running in the background instead of getting cut off, so a long build or test suite isn’t killed halfway.

items.title_en:
Coming back to an old session got lighter on your usage.

Claude Code now compacts long idle sessions right before the prompt cache expires (~1h). If you come back to one later, it only has to reprocess the summary instead of the entire conversation.

And on Pro and Max, resuming a really long conversation now gives you a heads-up first if picking it back up would use a big chunk of your 5-hour limit.

GERMANY COMMITS €50M GRANT TO UGANDA FOR DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS

Germany has committed €50 million in grants to Uganda to support development interventions in water, electricity, agribusiness, local economic development and refugee-hosting communities, following the conclusion of two days of Government-to-Government negotiations in Kampala on November 3, 2026.

The commitment comprises €30 million in Financial Cooperation and €20 million in Technical Cooperation, reinforcing a bilateral partnership spanning more than 60 years.

Of the new support, €35 million (70%) will go towards water and electricity, while €10 million (20%) will support agribusiness and local economies. The remaining €5 million will support refugee participation and host communities, among other areas.

The Finance Minister @henrymusasizi1 said the interventions are aligned with Uganda's National Development Plan IV and Tenfold Growth Strategy, which aims to grow the economy to US$500 billion by 2040 through Agro-Industrialisation, Tourism, Minerals, and Science, Technology and Innovation (ATMS).

“We appreciate this support. It comes at a time when resources for overseas development support are under pressure across Europe given the on-going global challenges,” Musasizi said.

He welcomed the €35 million allocation to water and electricity, describing these as important enablers of the ATMS agenda. He also called on German investors to explore opportunities in production, processing, exports and skilled job creation, proposing structured engagements to identify bankable investment opportunities.

The negotiations also earmarked €18 million for the electrification of West Nile, which is expected to serve enterprises and farms in a region that trades with eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan. 

Musasizi further asked Germany to support Uganda's efforts to mobilise financing for railway development, irrigation and electricity through the World Bank, African Development Bank and other multilateral institutions.

The Head of the German Delegation, Joachim Schmitt, who also heads the Central and East Africa Division at Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, said the cooperation would support Uganda's ambition to graduate from Least Developed Country (LDC) status.

“Our development cooperation will actively support this strategy, while being fully aligned to the Ugandan Vision 2040, its '10-fold growth strategy', including the ATMS priorities, as well as the 'National Development Plan IV',” Schmitt said.

He emphasised increased participation of Ugandan, German and European enterprises in unlocking economic potential, creating jobs and supporting Uganda's development. He also commended Uganda's refugee-hosting policies, reaffirming Germany's continued focus on West Nile and support for refugees and host communities.

German Ambassador to Uganda, H.E. Sigrid Sommer, said the new commitments build on more than six decades of cooperation that have delivered tangible results. “With these additional bilateral commitments, Germany remains a strong partner of Uganda and its people.”

Sommer said the outcome of the negotiations provides a basis for development cooperation over the next two years, aligned with Uganda's strategies and priorities. 

She noted that Germany accounts for nearly 25% of EU funding and reaffirmed her country's commitment to supporting Uganda alongside partners, including GIZ and KfW.

She emphasised that development cooperation,trade and investment are complementary parts of the partnership, adding that Germany remains committed to presenting business opportunities to enhance trade and investment with Uganda.

items.quote_zh:
德国承诺向乌干达提供 5000 万欧元赠款用于发展项目

2026 年 11 月 3 日在坎帕拉结束为期两天的政府间谈判后，德国承诺向乌干达提供 5000 万欧元赠款，支持水、电、农业综合企业、当地经济发展和难民收容社区的发展干预措施。

该承诺包括 3000 万欧元的金融合作和 2000 万欧元的技术合作，以加强长达 60 多年的双边伙伴关系。

在新的支持中，3500万欧元（70%）将用于水和电力，1000万欧元（20%）将用于支持农业企业和当地经济。剩余的 500 万欧元将用于支持难民参与和收容社区等领域。

财政部长 @henrymusasizi1 表示，这些干预措施符合乌干达国家发展计划 IV 和十倍增长战略，旨在通过农业工业化、旅游业、矿产以及科学、技术和创新 (ATMS) 到 2040 年将经济增长至 5000 亿美元。

穆萨西兹表示：“我们感谢这种支持。鉴于当前的全球挑战，整个欧洲的海外发展支持资源都面临压力。”

他对 3500 万欧元的水电拨款表示欢迎，并将其描述为 ATMS 议程的重要推动者。他还呼吁德国投资者探索生产、加工、出口和创造熟练就业岗位的机会，并提出结构化参与以确定可融资的投资机会。

谈判还指定了1800万欧元用于西尼罗河的电气化，预计将为与刚果民主共和国东部和南苏丹有贸易往来的地区的企业和农场提供服务。

穆萨西齐进一步要求德国支持乌干达通过世界银行、非洲开发银行和其他多边机构为铁路发展、灌溉和电力筹集资金的努力。

德国代表团团长、德国联邦经济合作与发展部中非和东非司司长约阿希姆·施密特表示，此次合作将支持乌干达摆脱最不发达国家地位的雄心。

施密特表示：“我们的发展合作将积极支持这一战略，同时完全符合乌干达2040年愿景、‘十倍增长战略’，包括ATMS优先事项以及‘国家发展计划IV’。”

他强调乌干达、德国和欧洲企业更多地参与释放经济潜力、创造就业机会和支持乌干达的发展。他还赞扬乌干达的难民收容政策，重申德国继续关注西尼罗河并支持难民和收容社区。

德国驻乌干达大使 H.E.西格丽德·索默 (Sigrid Sommer) 表示，新的承诺建立在六十多年的合作基础上，这些合作已经取得了切实成果。 “通过这些额外的双边承诺，德国仍然是乌干达及其人民的强有力的合作伙伴。”

索默表示，谈判结果为未来两年的发展合作奠定了基础，符合乌干达的战略和优先事项。

她指出，德国占欧盟资金的近 25%，并重申德国致力于与德国国际合作机构 (GIZ) 和德国复兴信贷银行 (KfW) 等合作伙伴一起支持乌干达。

她强调，发展合作、贸易和投资是伙伴关系的补充部分，并补充说，德国仍然致力于提供商业机会，以加强与乌干达的贸易和投资。

items.title: Microsoft updates Windows 11 to make PCs with 8GB of RAM up to 20% more responsive and multitasking up to 40% faster in lab tests, utilizing memory compression (Lance Whitney/ZDNET)
items.title_en: Microsoft updates Windows 11 to make PCs with 8GB of RAM up to 20% more responsive and multitasking up to 40% faster in lab tests, utilizing memory compression (Lance Whitney/ZDNET)
items.author: ZDNET
items.article_content:
The latest updates to Windows 11 offer improvements in speed, performance, and memory management.

The more memory your Windows PC has, the faster it should perform, especially when juggling multiple apps, files, and other data. My laptop has 32GB of RAM, while my desktop has a hefty 64GB, and both are absolutely zippy. Does that mean computers with only 8GB of memory, or even less, are also-rans? Nope, not according to Microsoft.

Also: How much RAM does your PC really need?

In a new blog post published Tuesday, Microsoft touted the gains in speed, performance, and memory management in Windows 11 achieved by the latest updates. These especially impact PCs with just 8GB of RAM, which can now run multiple apps and files faster and more efficiently than before.

To reach this goal, the company said it had three notions in mind.

The first was to make better use of the existing memory on each Windows 11 PC. The second was to protect the tasks that need to feel instant even as more memory gets used. And the third was to ensure that key apps and Windows require less memory. Yes, a computer with 16GB, 32GB, or 64GB of RAM can better handle more intensive activities. But Microsoft wanted to make sure that systems with 8GB could also keep pace.

Based on its own lab tests of PCs with 8GB of RAM, the company claims that Windows is now 20% more responsive and that multitasking is 40% faster than before the latest updates. Here’s how.

As more memory gets allocated, Windows must move inactive apps and files from RAM to the hard drive. When you need to access those apps and files again, you have to wait for Windows to move them from disk storage back to RAM. Normally, PCs with less memory have to do a lot of this disk swapping.

One way Windows eases the pain of this process is through compression. Here, the operating system shrinks less-active data into a smaller format so it can remain in memory. Though Windows has used compression for many years, Microsoft has fine-tuned the technology to determine how much to compress, when to move data from RAM to your drive, and when to fetch it back, especially on PCs with 8GB of memory.

As such, Windows can now keep up to 2GB more of your active data in memory rather than moving it to storage, Microsoft said. An inactive app, file, or browser that you leave open is less likely to have to reload from your hard drive when you return to it.

Opening the Start menu, launching File Explorer, right-clicking a folder or file, and searching for an item are all tasks that need to feel instant; otherwise, Windows itself feels sluggish. To achieve this on PCs with less RAM, Windows tries to prioritize certain actions you need to accomplish while backing off background tasks like search indexing, Microsoft said.

Here’s one example. After you update your computer and reboot, Windows has some housekeeping to do. But any setup work that occurs shouldn’t affect how long it takes to open an app or file.

The latest version of Windows 11 speeds up these types of tasks and interactions by up to 20% compared with the January 2026 version, according to Microsoft.

However, multitasking places the greatest strain on a PC with only 8GB of RAM. To analyze this, Microsoft said it conducted two tests on the same PC with 8GB of memory. One test measured the current version of Windows 11, while the other gauged the January 2026 flavor. Here, the testers opened 20 tabs in Microsoft Edge, kicked off a 4K video, and launched large files in Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, one after another. The current version of Windows is up to 40% faster than its predecessor, the company said.

To reduce the need for RAM among Windows and certain key apps, Microsoft said that it has improved how memory is managed and when it’s used.

As one example, memory is allocated to Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook more efficiently, resulting in a 360 MB savings in RAM. This maneuver also extends to third-party apps such as WhatsApp, which has reduced its memory requirements.

On PCs with 8GB of memory, the Widgets app loads only when you open it and frees up about 200 MB of RAM when you close it. In Microsoft Edge, inactive tabs now go to sleep after 15 minutes, down from two hours previously, reducing overall memory allocation.

Across Windows, Microsoft 365, and Edge, those improvements reduced the growth in required memory by up to 900 MB, Microsoft said.

How does Microsoft test these scenarios to see whether the latest Windows updates and fixes are helping PCs with less memory?

“We test those fixes across a broader collection of over 20,000 PCs in our labs, including current 8 GB models, using automated workloads based on activities such as browsing, working in Microsoft 365 apps, joining video calls, and downloading files in the background and even using high-speed cameras to measure the time from an action, such as opening Start or launching an app, to the moment the result appears on screen,” the company explained.

The ability to use Windows without much RAM on your PC is critical these days in light of the “RAMageddon” crisis. With AI companies scooping up massive amounts of memory and flash storage chips, remaining supply is limited, and the prices have surged. The more memory you add to a new or existing PC, the more you’re going to pay. That’s always been true, but now more than ever.

Of course, memory is only one part of the picture. Your PC’s processor and other hardware also play an important role. Here, Microsoft found that a 2026 Dell XPS 13 with 8GB of RAM showed 94% faster multi-core CPU performance than a 2021 8 GB model. But the same 2026 8GB PC performed on par with a 2021 16 GB system. This shows that memory does matter for multitasking, but that the processor also impacts performance.

Whether your Windows 11 PC has 8GB of RAM, less, or more, how can you take advantage of the latest enhancements? For that, you’ll want to make sure that you’ve updated to the newest version of Windows. That would be Windows 11 26H2, build 26300.9818 or later, according to Microsoft. But that includes the latest optional preview build released in late October. If you don’t want to install that one, you’ll be fine with build 26300.9711 for now.

To check, head to Settings, select System, and then click About. The section for Windows Info shows the current version and build. If you need to update, stay in Settings and go to Windows Update. Assuming your PC qualifies, you should find the latest Windows 11 26H2 build ready to install.

Beyond updating Windows, you also want to keep your apps current. If you use Microsoft 365, open any app in the suite, click the File menu, select Account, click Update Options, then select Update Now.

With most other apps, you have to update them manually or individually. To ease the process, consider a good software updater program. These will automatically scan most of your installed applications to identify which need updating, then download and install the updates for you.

首先是更好地利用每台 Windows 11 PC 上的现有内存。第二个是保护需要感觉即时的任务，即使使用更多内存也是如此。第三是确保关键应用程序和 Windows 需要更少的内存。是的，具有 16GB、32GB 或 64GB RAM 的计算机可以更好地处理更密集的活动。但微软希望确保 8GB 系统也能跟上步伐。

根据其自己对 8GB RAM 电脑的实验室测试，该公司声称 Windows 现在比最新更新之前的响应速度提高了 20%，多任务处理速度提高了 40%。方法如下。

随着分配更多内存，Windows 必须将不活动的应用程序和文件从 RAM 移动到硬盘驱动器。当您需要再次访问这些应用程序和文件时，您必须等待 Windows 将它们从磁盘存储移回 RAM。通常，内存较少的电脑必须进行大量的磁盘交换。

Windows 减轻此过程痛苦的一种方法是通过压缩。在这里，操作系统将不太活跃的数据缩小为较小的格式，以便它可以保留在内存中。尽管 Windows 已使用压缩多年，但 Microsoft 已对该技术进行了微调，以确定压缩程度、何时将数据从 RAM 移动到驱动器以及何时取回数据，尤其是在具有 8GB 内存的 PC 上。

微软表示，因此，Windows 现在可以在内存中保留最多 2GB 的活动数据，而不是将其移动到存储中。当您返回打开的非活动应用程序、文件或浏览器时，不太可能需要从硬盘驱动器重新加载。

打开“开始”菜单、启动文件资源管理器、右键单击文件夹或文件以及搜索项目都是需要即时完成的任务；否则，Windows 本身就会感觉迟缓。微软表示，为了在 RAM 较少的 PC 上实现这一目标，Windows 会尝试优先考虑需要完成的某些操作，同时放弃搜索索引等后台任务。

这是一个例子。更新计算机并重新启动后，Windows 需要执行一些内务处理工作。但发生的任何设置工作都不应影响打开应用程序或文件所需的时间。

据微软称，与 2026 年 1 月的版本相比，最新版本的 Windows 11 将此类任务和交互的速度提高了 20%。

然而，多任务处理对只有 8GB RAM 的 PC 造成的压力最大。为了分析这一点，微软表示，它在同一台 8GB 内存的 PC 上进行了两次测试。一项测试测量了 Windows 11 的当前版本，而另一项测试则测量了 2026 年 1 月的版本。测试人员在 Microsoft Edge 中打开了 20 个选项卡，开始播放 4K 视频，并在 Word、PowerPoint 和 Excel 中依次启动大文件。该公司表示，当前版本的 Windows 比其前身快 40%。

【起因与机理】旨在提升低配硬件的系统效率，优化用户体验
【关键数据与实测】8GB内存设备响应提升20%，多任务快40%。
【观点态度】通过优化算法让低配机型重获新生。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] To improve system efficiency and user experience on entry-level hardware

items.title_en:
DOE just dropped its Fall 2026 SBIR/STTR Phase 1 topics, with more than $200M in funding available to small businesses building in energy + national security. Here's a look at the 25 topics:

Topic 1: Advanced technologies for domestic critical mineral extraction, midstream processing, and recycling: small-market minerals like vanadium, hafnium, zirconium. Each proposal must pair a real feedstock provider with a processor

Topic 2: Innovations in manufacturing scale-up for energy applications: production bottlenecks, modular/retrofit platforms, smart manufacturing tools

Topic 3: State-of-the-art tech for industrial competitiveness: energy-intensive industries, cross-sector processes, data center and large load integration

Topic 4: Next-generation building technologies: dual-fuel HVAC, SI/ML controls

Topic 5: Cutting edge generation and power management technologies: hydro, marine, wind and PV recycling, solar thermal, space PV, interconnection, permitting

Topic 6: Advanced transportation and fuels production: fuels from alternative feedstocks, MW-scale fuel cells for data centers, heavy-rare-earth-free motors, off-road and mining powertrains

Topic 7: Battery technologies for dual-use applications: cell-level demos w/ commercial markets and defense uses like UAS, UUV, soldier-carried power

Topic 8: Advanced cybersecurity, resilience, and energy system risk mitigation technologies: OT/ICS security, supply chain assurance, recovery tools

Topic 9: Innovative technologies for hydrocarbons and geothermal energy: modernizing coal mines and plants, oil and gas recovery, produced water sensors, geothermal targeting and storage

Topic 10: Reactor concepts: HTGR/MSR components, liquid metal, sCO2, digital twins, construction cost reduction

Topic 11: Fuel cycle R&D: domestic fuel supply chain, TRISO and advanced fuels, used fuel recovery, materials accounting

Topic 12: Nuclear energy enabling tech: reactor sensors, advanced materials, modeling tools, post-irradiation exam

Topic 13: Advanced technologies for used nuclear fuel and high-level waste disposition: standardized waste packages, dry storage modeling, licensing pathways for DOE’s nuclear lifecycle campuses

Topic 14: Grid innovations to strengthen the electric system's capacity: grid cyber, grid-enhancing tech, microgrids, stationary storage, large load interconnection

Topic 15: Commercializing ASCR/ECP-funded HPC software 

Topic 16: Cybersecurity for scientific high-performance computing 

Topic 17: Novel instrumentation for X-ray and neutron facilities: permanent magnet accelerator elements, in-situ optics cleaning, neutron mirrors and detectors

Topic 18: Data, synthesis, and characterization strategies for SI-driven materials and molecular systems discovery: ML-guided membranes for critical mineral/REE separation, SI data platforms

Topic 19: Enabling technologies for bioengineering and quantum science-based sensors: field-deployable quantum sensing, quantum bioimaging, Super Intelligence for bioenergy crop engineering, big biological data

Topic 20: Fusion fuel cycle and enabling technologies: tritium handling, fueling, exhaust processing, detritiation

Topic 21: Advanced particle and radiation detectors: ultra-radiopure materials, high-rate detectors, vibration-free cryogenics

Topic 22: High-performance electronics and data acquisition systems 

Topic 23: Accelerator science and tech: superconducting magnets, RF power, sources and lasers, diagnostics

Topic 24: Proliferation detection: entangled-photon remote sensing, hyperspectral imagery over water to support monitoring of nuclear-powered ships, radiation detection, radiological source replacement

Topic 25: Nuclear detonation detection: field data acquisition, calibration tools, rad-hard microcircuits

Pitches due Dec. 16.

美国能源部刚刚放弃了 2026 年秋季 SBIR/STTR 第一阶段主题，为小型企业提供超过 2 亿美元的资金用于能源和国家安全建设。以下是这 25 个主题：

主题一：国内关键矿产开采、中游加工和回收的先进技术：钒、铪、锆等小市场矿产。每个提案必须将真正的原料供应商与加工商配对

主题2：能源应用制造规模化创新：生产瓶颈、模块化/改造平台、智能制造工具

主题三：最先进的产业竞争力技术：能源密集型产业、跨行业流程、数据中心和大负载集成

主题 4：下一代建筑技术：双燃料 HVAC、SI/ML 控制

主题 5：尖端发电和电力管理技术：水力、海洋、风能和光伏回收、太阳能热利用、太空光伏、互连、许可

主题 6：先进运输和燃料生产：替代原料燃料、数据中心用兆瓦级燃料电池、无重稀土电机、越野和采矿动力总成

主题 7：军民两用应用的电池技术：商业市场和国防用途（如 UAS、UUV、士兵携带电源）的电池级演示

主题 8：先进的网络安全、弹性和能源系统风险缓解技术：OT/ICS 安全、供应链保证、恢复工具

主题 9：碳氢化合物和地热能创新技术：煤矿和工厂现代化、石油和天然气回收、采出水传感器、地热定位和存储

主题 10：反应堆概念：HTGR/MSR 组件、液态金属、sCO2、数字孪生、降低建设成本

主题11：燃料循环研发：国内燃料供应链、TRISO和先进燃料、废燃料回收、物料核算

主题 12：核能使能技术：反应堆传​​感器、先进材料、建模工具、辐照后检查

主题 13：废旧核燃料和高放废物处置的先进技术：标准化废物包装、干式储存模型、能源部核生命周期园区的许可途径

主题 14：增强电力系统能力的电网创新：电网网络、电网增强技术、微电网、固定存储、大负载互连

主题 15：ASCR/ECP 资助的 HPC 软件商业化

主题 16：科学高性能计算的网络安全

主题 17：X 射线和中子设施的新型仪器：永磁加速器元件、原位光学清洁、中子镜和探测器

主题 18：SI 驱动材料和分子系统发现的数据、合成和表征策略：用于关键矿物/稀土元素分离的 ML 引导膜、SI 数据平台

主题19：生物工程和基于量子科学的传感器的使能技术：可现场部署的量子传感、量子生物成像、生物能源作物工程的超级智能、生物大数据

主题 20：聚变燃料循环和使能技术：氚处理、加燃料、废气处理、脱氚

主题 21：先进粒子和辐射探测器：超辐射纯材料、高速率探测器、无振动低温技术

主题 22：高性能电子和数据采集系统

主题 23：加速器科学与技术：超导磁体、射频功率、光源和激光器、诊断

主题 24：扩散探测：纠缠光子遥感、支持核动力船舶监测的水上高光谱图像、辐射探测、放射源替代

主题 25：核爆炸探测：现场数据采集、校准工具、抗辐射微电路

推介截止日期为 12 月 16 日。
