𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗔𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝟴 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗬𝗢𝗨 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗 𝗧𝗢 𝗞𝗡𝗢𝗪

Building an AI agent is not just about connecting an LLM to a pro
items.title_en:
𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗔𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝟴 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗬𝗢𝗨 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗 𝗧𝗢 𝗞𝗡𝗢𝗪

Building an AI agent is not just about connecting an LLM to a prompt.

A production-ready agent needs multiple layers working together.

𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘’𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗖𝗞:

01 — 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗙𝗔𝗖𝗘 & 𝗖𝗛𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗘𝗟𝗦

How users interact with the agent.

→ Chat UI
→ APIs
→ Slack
→ Other interfaces

02 — 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 & 𝗢𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The layer responsible for breaking goals into steps and coordinating execution.

→ Task planning
→ Workflow orchestration
→ Agent coordination
→ Decision-making

03 — 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗬 & 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗫𝗧

Agents need context to make better decisions.

→ Short-term memory
→ Long-term memory
→ Vector databases
→ Retrieval
→ Prompt caching

04 — 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗟𝗦

The reasoning engine behind the agent.

→ Claude
→ GPT
→ Gemini
→ Llama
→ Other specialized models

The best model depends on the task, cost, latency, and reliability requirements.

05 — 𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗟𝗦 & 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦

This is where an agent becomes capable of doing things.

→ GitHub
→ Browser
→ Code execution
→ SQL/Databases
→ APIs

Tools allow agents to move beyond generating text.

06 — 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗘 & 𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗔 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

Agents need reliable infrastructure to store and manage information.

→ PostgreSQL
→ Redis
→ Object storage
→ Vector databases

07 — 𝗢𝗕𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗔𝗕𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗧𝗬, 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗬 & 𝗘𝗩𝗔𝗟𝗦

Autonomous systems need to be monitored and tested.

→ Tracing
→ Evaluations
→ Guardrails
→ Error monitoring
→ Performance tracking

This layer helps make agents reliable enough for real-world use.

08 — 𝗗𝗘𝗣𝗟𝗢𝗬𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧

Finally, the agent needs to run reliably in production.

→ Docker
→ Kubernetes
→ AWS
→ Vercel
→ Cloud platforms

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗜𝗚 𝗣𝗜𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘:

User Goal
↓
Interface
↓
Planning
↓
Memory + Context
↓
LLM
↓
Tools + Actions
↓
State + Data
↓
Observability + Safety
↓
Deployment

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗞𝗘𝗬 𝗟𝗘𝗦𝗦𝗢𝗡:

A powerful LLM is only one part of an AI agent.

The real engineering challenge is building the system around the model — giving it memory, tools, planning, safety, evaluation, and reliable infrastructure.

That’s what turns an LLM into a production-ready AI agent.

Follow @Viveksahu1215 for more AI, tools, automation and tech insights.

items.title_en:
Extremely lazy take that gives useless actors aa cop out. 

The Indian navy drew up a submarine force plan almost 30 years ago, that had a projected strength of 24+ SSK by the 2020s 

They have 17 and more than 2/3rds of them are almost 40 years old with 0 further boats in production 

This has absolutely nothing to do with the focus on aircraft carriers (they have 2 and no plans for more currently) but the typical Indian user myopia of minuscule production runs (6 boats each time ) and continuously chasing after the next imported silver bullet  

As @SandeepUnnithan points out, had they seriously focused on P76 a decade ago the first of those boats could be nearing service today 

Instead they’ve been scouring the world for imaginary capabilities in foreign companies

items.summary_zh: 华为向客户透露其下一代旗舰昇腾960DT将主要采用三星与SK海力士制造的HBM高带宽内存

items.title:
Autonomous trading without enforceable risk limits is just risk-taking at machine speed.

That’s why the risk engine mat
items.title_en:
Autonomous trading without enforceable risk limits is just risk-taking at machine speed.

That’s why the risk engine matters in @agenticscredit.

Letting an AI agent trade independently is not only about deciding when to enter a position. It also needs clear rules for when to stop, how much loss is acceptable, and when exposure has gone too far.

Agentics’ risk engine is designed to enforce those boundaries through:

- Stop-loss controls
- Trailing limits
- Drawdown restrictions

These rules matter because an agent should not be judged only by the trades it wins. Its ability to operate within defined risk limits is equally important.

There is another layer to this system: every trade updates the Agentics Credit Score (ACS), helping build a record of the agent’s trading behavior over time.

That connects risk management with the broader credit model.

A profitable agent may attract attention, but an agent that can manage downside and follow its limits provides a more meaningful performance history.

Autonomy gives an agent the ability to act. Risk controls define how far it is allowed to go.

items.quote_zh:
没有可执行风险限制的自主交易只是以机器速度冒险。

这就是为什么风险引擎在 @agenticscredit 中很重要。

让人工智能代理独立交易不仅仅是决定何时建仓。它还需要明确的规则来规定何时停止、可以接受多少损失以及何时暴露过度。

Agentics 的风险引擎旨在通过以下方式强制执行这些边界：

—止损控制
- 追踪限制
- 提款限制

这些规则很重要，因为不应仅通过其赢得的交易来判断代理商。它在规定的风险限度内运作的能力同样重要。

该系统还有另一层：每笔交易都会更新 Agentics 信用评分 (ACS)，帮助建立代理随着时间的推移的交易行为记录。

这将风险管理与更广泛的信用模型联系起来。

盈利的代理可能会引起关注，但能够管理不利因素并遵循其极限的代理可以提供更有意义的绩效历史记录。

自主权赋予代理人行动的能力。风险控制定义了允许走多远。

items.content_snippet:
Autonomous trading without enforceable risk limits is just risk-taking at machine speed.

That’s why the risk engine matters in @agenticscredit.

Letting an AI agent trade independently is not only about deciding when to enter a position. It also needs clear rules for when to stop, how much loss is acceptable, and when exposure has gone too far.

Agentics’ risk engine is designed to enforce those boundaries through:

- Stop-loss controls
- Trailing limits
- Drawdown restrictions

These rules matter because an agent should not be judged only by the trades it wins. Its ability to operate within defined risk limits is equally important.

There is another layer to this system: every trade updates the Agentics Credit Score (ACS), helping build a record of the agent’s trading behavior over time.

That connects risk management with the broader credit model.

A profitable agent may attract attention, but an agent that can manage downside and follow its limits provides a more meaningful performance history.

Autonomy gives an agent the ability to act. Risk controls define how far it is allowed to go.

盈利的代理可能会引起关注，但能够管理不利因素并遵循其极限的代理可以提供更有意义的绩效历史记录。

items.title_en:
Early morning my bros 🥱

1/5

Imagine an AI agent making a series of profitable trades, then suddenly facing a problem nobody talks about enough: where does its next capital come from?

For human traders, access to capital often depends on more than earning money. A strong income does not automatically mean a lender will trust someone with additional funds. There needs to be some form of financial history behind that decision.

I think AI agents will face a similar challenge as they become more active in financial markets. Being able to execute trades is one thing. Building enough credibility to access capital is something entirely different.

An agent might have a clever strategy, impressive execution speed, and a profitable period. But if its entire financial identity depends on claims made by its creator, how can anyone independently evaluate its reliability?

This is where Agentics Credit has an interesting approach. Instead of treating an agent's identity or promises as proof of credibility, it uses actual trading activity to build an Agentics Credit Score, or ACS.

Paper and onchain trades contribute to that history, with real-money trading receiving the greatest weight. Once an agent reaches 580 ACS, its credit path opens toward a Constrained Capital Account.

What I find interesting is the shift in responsibility. An agent is not simply asking someone to believe it can trade. Its own activity becomes part of the evidence used to assess whether it qualifies for credit access.

Of course, a trading record cannot guarantee future performance, and reaching a score threshold does not remove financial risk. But giving agents a way to establish their own credit history could become an important piece of financial infrastructure as autonomous trading grows.

The next big challenge for AI agents may not be learning how to earn. It may be proving they deserve access to more capital.

@Agenticscredit

items.quote_zh:
早上好兄弟们🥱

想象一下，一个人工智能代理进行了一系列有利可图的交易，然后突然面临一个没人谈论的问题：它的下一笔资金来自哪里？

对于人类交易者来说，获得资本往往不仅仅取决于赚钱。丰厚的收入并不自动意味着贷方会信任拥有额外资金的人。该决定背后需要有某种形式的财务历史。

我认为，随着人工智能代理在金融市场变得更加活跃，它们也将面临类似的挑战。能够执行交易是一回事。建立足够的信誉来获取资本是完全不同的事情。

代理人可能拥有聪明的策略、令人印象深刻的执行速度和有利可图的时期。但如果它的整个财务身份取决于其创建者的声明，那么任何人如何能够独立评估其可靠性呢？

这就是 Agentics Credit 采取的有趣方法。它没有将代理商的身份或承诺视为可信度证明，而是使用实际交易活动来建立 Agentics 信用评分 (ACS)。

纸质交易和链上交易为这段历史做出了贡献，其中真实货币交易的比重最大。一旦代理达到 580 ACS，其信用路径就会向受限资本账户开放。

我觉得有趣的是责任的转变。代理人不仅仅是要求某人相信它可以进行交易。其自身的活动成为用于评估其是否有资格获得信贷的证据的一部分。

当然，交易记录并不能保证未来的表现，达到分数阈值并不能消除财务风险。但随着自主交易的发展，为代理商提供建立自己信用记录的方法可能会成为金融基础设施的重要组成部分。

人工智能代理的下一个重大挑战可能不是学习如何赚钱。这可能证明他们应该获得更多资本。

@Agenticscredit

items.title: Larridin, which helps companies track how AI affects employee output and identifies areas for better AI adoption, raised a $30M Series A led by Pelion Ventures (Aditi Bharade/Business Insider)
items.title_en: Larridin, which helps companies track how AI affects employee output and identifies areas for better AI adoption, raised a $30M Series A led by Pelion Ventures (Aditi Bharade/Business Insider)
items.author: Business Insider
items.article_content:
Larridin's main product is a measurement platform that tracks the extent to which AI improves employee productivity and identifies opportunities for better adoption. The software integrates with companies' internal systems to analyze employees' AI usage, including their prompts to different AI tools, and determine who is using AI effectively, who needs more training, and how much time they're saving.

Cofounder and CTO Ameya Kanitkar said the platform protects employee privacy by analyzing their AI interactions without storing their contents, instead generating scores and high-level insights.

Russell Fradin, CEO and cofounder of Larridin, previously worked at Comscore, a media and advertising measurement platform. He said that, in his experience, whenever a lot of money moves into a category, someone builds a third-party measurement platform for that category, evidenced by Comscore, Nielsen, or Datadog.

"We said, look, there's going to be a ton of AI spend," Fradin said. "There's going to be a third-party audit measurement company, and let's try and be that company."

The company has a third cofounder, Jim Larrison, who worked with Fradin at Comscore.

Larridin's $30 million Series A was led by Pelion Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, Gradient Ventures, GFT Ventures, W23, Thayer Investment Partners, DG Daiwa Ventures, Alumni Ventures, and Cougar Capital. A16z and Gradient Ventures were part of its $17 million seed round.

Alex Rampell, a general partner at A16z, said one thing that convinced him about Larridin's business was that it addressed a need in enterprise AI for a sort of "AI boss," who could tell staff what they should or shouldn't do with AI.

"If you're in sales, somebody should nudge you and say, 'Hey, call this account. Don't call that account.' If you're in coding, 'fix this bug, don't fix that bug,'" Rampell said.

"But underlying that was the same idea, which was like, people are using AI tools to do all sorts of things. Are they doing the right thing? Is the outcome actually appreciably different? Are you getting any kind of ROI?" he added.

Fradin said that business picked up around the second quarter of this year, when more companies became concerned about AI costs. The company went from having one enterprise customer in December last year to 50 now.

Post-Series A, he said he wants to double Larridin's 20-person head count, adding more sales, engineering, and marketing staff.

Larridin's Series A comes after months of twists and turns in the field of AI spending.

In the first few months of the year, tokenmaxxing was in vogue, which led companies to urge their employees to get on the hype train and experiment with AI — essentially a mandate to accelerate adoption or be left behind.

They urged their employees to use AI tools as much as possible and burn as many tokens as they could, with some, like Duolingo, even adding AI use as a performance metric for their employees. Uber CTO Praveen Neppalli Naga went viral in April when he said Uber had already burned through its entire Claude Code budget for the year.

AI budgets ballooned. At least 17 companies, from Salesforce to Oracle, announced AI-related layoffs, with Oracle specifically saying in June that AI deployment and adoption have reduced its workforce.

But the sentiment shifted sometime in the middle of the year, when ugly AI bills started rearing their heads.

Companies started paying more attention to getting the best return on investment from their AI spending. Modelmaxxing, which, as Business Insider wrote about in July, involves routing prompts to different AI models based to maximize token use, emerged as a tactic to save costs. More businesses started using cheaper open-source models developed by Chinese AI labs, such as Moonshot AI and Z.ai.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 企业效率管理平台Larridin完成由Pelion Ventures领投的3000万美元A轮融资。该平台通过集成企业内部系统，追踪员工对各类AI模型的调用情况及提示词习惯，旨在量化AI带来的生产力提升并识别培训需求，同时通过脱敏机制处理互动数据以保障隐私。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Efficiency management platform Larridin has raised $30 million in a Series A round led by Pelion Ventures. The platform integrates with internal systems to track AI model usage and prompt interactions, aiming to quantify productivity gains and identify training gaps while maintaining employee privacy through data anonymization.

elements_zh.where: 企业级AI管理工具市场
elements_zh.what: 完成3000万美元A轮融资，提供追踪员工AI使用效率及优化模型采纳的监测方案
elements_zh.why: 企业在AI投入激增后亟需量化ROI，缺乏有效手段核算谁在真正高效使用工具

elements_en.what: Raised $30M Series A to launch an AI productivity measurement platform
elements_en.why: Companies are desperate to quantify the ROI of massive AI spending and identify actual usage patterns

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 说白了就是给AI装个“监控探头”，让老板盯着员工写了多少AI提示词。以前是怕员工摸鱼，现在是怕员工花了大把订阅费却只拿AI来写情书，这届老板为了搞清AI的ROI也是拼了。
ai_analysis.insight_en: It’s basically an 'AI surveillance camera' that lets bosses monitor how many prompts employees are actually typing. It used to be about stopping employees from slacking off; now it's about making sure those expensive AI subscriptions aren't just being used to draft love letters.

items.article_content_zh:
听这个故事“突然间，他们会说，‘哇，人工智能投入了很多钱。我们运行很多应用程序。我们有很多模型。它们都去了哪里，谁在使用它，我该如何理解这些？”克尔说。

Larridin 的主要产品是一个测量平台，用于跟踪人工智能提高员工生产力的程度并识别更好采用的机会。该软件与公司内部系统集成，分析员工的人工智能使用情况，包括他们对不同人工智能工具的提示，并确定谁在有效地使用人工智能、谁需要更多培训以及他们节省了多少时间。

联合创始人兼首席技术官 Ameya Kanitkar 表示，该平台通过分析员工的人工智能交互而不存储其内容，而是生成分数和高级见解来保护员工隐私。

Larridin 首席执行官兼联合创始人 Russell Fradin 此前曾在媒体和广告衡量平台 Comscore 工作。他说，根据他的经验，每当大量资金进入某个类别时，就会有人为该类别建立第三方衡量平台，Comscore、Nielsen 或 Datadog 就是证明。

“我们说，看，将会有大量的人工智能支出，”弗拉丁说。 “将会有一家第三方审计测量公司，让我们努力成为那样的公司。”

该公司还有第三位联合创始人吉姆·拉里森 (Jim Larrison)，他曾在 Comscore 与弗拉丁共事。

Larridin 的 3000 万美元 A 轮融资由 Pelion Ventures、Andreessen Horowitz、Gradient Ventures、GFT Ventures、W23、Thayer Investment Partners、DG Daiwa Ventures、Alumni Ventures 和 Cougar Capital 领投。 A16z 和 Gradient Ventures 参与了其 1700 万美元种子轮融资。

A16z 的普通合伙人 Alex Rampell 表示，让他相信 Larridin 业务的一件事是，该公司解决了企业人工智能对“人工智能老板”的需求，他可以告诉员工应该或不应该使用人工智能做什么。

“如果你从事销售工作，有人应该轻推你并说，‘嘿，给这个客户打电话。不要给那个客户打电话。’如果你在编码，‘修复这个错误，不要修复那个错误，’”兰佩尔说。

“但本质上是相同的想法，就像人们正在使用人工智能工具来做各种各样的事情。他们做的事情正确吗？结果实际上有明显不同吗？你能获得任何投资回报率吗？”他补充道。

弗拉丁表示，今年第二季度左右业务有所回升，当时越来越多的公司开始担心人工智能成本。该公司的企业客户从去年12月的1家增加到现在的50家。

A 轮融资后，他表示希望将 Larridin 的 20 名员工人数增加一倍，增加更多的销售、工程和营销人员。

Larridin 的 A 轮融资是在人工智能支出领域经历了数月的波折之后完成的。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】Larridin（AI生产力分析初创公司在企业级AI管理工具市场：完成3000万美元A轮融资，提供追踪员工AI使用效率及优化模型采纳的监测方案
【起因与机理】企业在AI投入激增后亟需量化ROI，缺乏有效手段核算谁在真正高效使用工具
【关键数据与实测】Larridin获3000万美元融资用于AI生产力审计。
【观点态度】填补企业在AI大规模应用后的绩效管理盲区。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] Companies are desperate to quantify the ROI of massive AI spending and identify actual usage patterns
[Key Metrics] Larridin raised $30M for AI productivity auditing.

items.title_en:
Good morning guys!

Letting an AI agent trade while you sleep sounds great… until you think about who’s controlling the risk.

That’s the part @agenticscredit is focusing on.

Its risk engine enforces stop-losses, trailing limits, and drawdown limits. And every trade feeds into your Agentics Credit Score (ACS).

The idea is simple: strategy can be yours, but risk shouldn’t be left unchecked.

Because smart trading isn’t just about making gains. It’s also about knowing when to stop.

items.title_en:
Good Morning gVan ☕️

𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐝𝐨 𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐜𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧. 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐢𝐧.

One of the most interesting developments in AI is the move from systems that simply generate responses to intelligent agents capable of interacting with real-world environments.

But this transition comes with an important requirement: reliable access to real-world information.

Imagine an AI agent helping a robot navigate a warehouse, supporting an autonomous delivery system, or analyzing the layout of an unfamiliar building.

For these systems to work effectively, they need more than general knowledge. They need spatial information that reflects actual physical environments.

This is where the infrastructure behind Physical AI becomes extremely important.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐕𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐫𝐢𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐮𝐠𝐡𝐭 𝐦𝐲 𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

@vangrid_io is building a decentralized spatial data network focused on making real-world environments accessible as structured 3D data.

Its approach brings together several important components:

➜ Human-powered data collection: Contributors can use smartphones to capture real-world environments, making participation more accessible.

➜ Spatial reconstruction: Captured footage can be transformed into 3D representations that provide more useful environmental context.

➜ Agent-driven demand: Through its bounty infrastructure, specific data requirements can be requested and funded, creating a connection between data consumers and contributors.

➜ Onchain transparency: Capture attestations and network activity can be inspected through the public Vangrid Explorer.

➜ A growing ecosystem: The combination of its web product, Android app, explorer, and bounty system gives the network a practical foundation to develop around.

What makes this direction particularly interesting is the relationship between AI agents and decentralized infrastructure.

As intelligent systems become more capable, their demand for accurate, updated, and location-specific information could become increasingly important.

However, collecting data is only the beginning. Verification, privacy, quality control, and geographic coverage will determine how useful this infrastructure becomes in real applications.

That is why I believe the development of spatial data networks deserves more attention in the broader AI and DePIN conversation.

We have spent years building systems that understand digital information. Now, the challenge is helping intelligent systems understand physical reality.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐮𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐀𝐈 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐛𝐞 𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐦𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐤. 𝐈𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐚𝐥𝐬𝐨 𝐝𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐧 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐬𝐞𝐞, 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡.

That is the bigger opportunity behind what @vangrid_io is building

早上好gVan☕️

𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐝𝐨 𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐜𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧. 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐢𝐧.

人工智能最有趣的发展之一是从简单地生成响应的系统转变为能够与现实世界环境交互的智能代理。

但这种转变伴随着一个重要的要求：可靠地访问现实世界的信息。

想象一下，人工智能代理帮助机器人导航仓库、支持自主交付系统或分析陌生建筑物的布局。

为了使这些系统有效运行，它们需要的不仅仅是常识。他们需要反映实际物理环境的空间信息。

这就是物理人工智能背后的基础设施变得极其重要的地方。

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐕𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐫𝐢𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐮𝐠𝐡𝐭 𝐦𝐲 𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

@vangrid_io 正在构建一个去中心化的空间数据网络，专注于使现实世界环境能够作为结构化 3D 数据进行访问。

它的方法汇集了几个重要的组成部分：

➜ 人力数据收集：贡献者可以使用智能手机捕捉现实世界的环境，使参与变得更容易。

➜ 空间重建：捕获的镜头可以转换为 3D 表示，从而提供更有用的环境背景。

➜ 代理驱动的需求：通过其赏金基础设施，可以请求和资助特定的数据需求，从而在数据消费者和贡献者之间建立联系。

➜ 链上透明度：可以通过公共 Vangrid Explorer 检查捕获证明和网络活动。

➜ 不断发展的生态系统：其网络产品、Android 应用程序、浏览器和赏金系统的结合为网络的发展提供了实用的基础。

这个方向特别有趣的是人工智能代理和去中心化基础设施之间的关系。

随着智能系统变得越来越强大，它们对准确、更新和特定位置信息的需求可能变得越来越重要。

然而，收集数据仅仅是开始。验证、隐私、质量控制和地理覆盖范围将决定该基础设施在实际应用中的有用程度。

这就是为什么我认为空间数据网络的发展值得在更广泛的人工智能和 DePIN 对话中得到更多关注。

我们花了数年时间构建理解数字信息的系统。现在的挑战是帮助智能系统理解物理现实。

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐮𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐀𝐈 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐛𝐞 𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐦𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐤. 𝐈𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐚𝐥𝐬𝐨 𝐝𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐧 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐬𝐞𝐞, 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡.

这是@vangrid_io 正在构建的背后更大的机会

𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐝𝐨 𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐜𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧. 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐢𝐧.

人工智能最有趣的发展之一是从简单地生成响应的系统转变为能够与现实世界环境交互的智能代理。

但这种转变伴随着一个重要的要求：可靠地访问现实世界的信息。

想象一下，人工智能代理帮助机器人导航仓库、支持自主交付系统或分析陌生建筑物的布局。

为了使这些系统有效运行，它们需要的不仅仅是常识。他们需要反映实际物理环境的空间信息。

这就是物理人工智能背后的基础设施变得极其重要的地方。

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐕𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐫𝐢𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐮𝐠𝐡𝐭 𝐦𝐲 𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

@vangrid_io 正在构建一个去中心化的空间数据网络，专注于使现实世界环境能够作为结构化 3D 数据进行访问。

它的方法汇集了几个重要的组成部分：

➜ 人力数据收集：贡献者可以使用智能手机捕捉现实世界的环境，使参与变得更容易。

➜ 空间重建：捕获的镜头可以转换为 3D 表示，从而提供更有用的环境背景。

➜ 代理驱动的需求：通过其赏金基础设施，可以请求和资助特定的数据需求，从而在数据消费者和贡献者之间建立联系。

➜ 链上透明度：可以通过公共 Vangrid Explorer 检查捕获证明和网络活动。

➜ 不断发展的生态系统：其网络产品、Android 应用程序、浏览器和赏金系统的结合为网络的发展提供了实用的基础。

这个方向特别有趣的是人工智能代理和去中心化基础设施之间的关系。

随着智能系统变得越来越强大，它们对准确、更新和特定位置信息的需求可能变得越来越重要。

然而，收集数据仅仅是开始。验证、隐私、质量控制和地理覆盖范围将决定该基础设施在实际应用中的有用程度。

这就是为什么我认为空间数据网络的发展值得在更广泛的人工智能和 DePIN 对话中得到更多关注。

我们花了数年时间构建理解数字信息的系统。现在的挑战是帮助智能系统理解物理现实。

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐮𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐀𝐈 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐛𝐞 𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐦𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐤. 𝐈𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐚𝐥𝐬𝐨 𝐝𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐧 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐬𝐞𝐞, 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡.

这是@vangrid_io 正在构建的背后更大的机会

items.content_snippet:
Good Morning gVan ☕️

𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐝𝐨 𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐜𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧. 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐢𝐧.

One of the most interesting developments in AI is the move from systems that simply generate responses to intelligent agents capable of interacting with real-world environments.

But this transition comes with an important requirement: reliable access to real-world information.

Imagine an AI agent helping a robot navigate a warehouse, supporting an autonomous delivery system, or analyzing the layout of an unfamiliar building.

For these systems to work effectively, they need more than general knowledge. They need spatial information that reflects actual physical environments.

This is where the infrastructure behind Physical AI becomes extremely important.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐕𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐫𝐢𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐮𝐠𝐡𝐭 𝐦𝐲 𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

@vangrid_io is building a decentralized spatial data network focused on making real-world environments accessible as structured 3D data.

Its approach brings together several important components:

➜ Human-powered data collection: Contributors can use smartphones to capture real-world environments, making participation more accessible.

➜ Spatial reconstruction: Captured footage can be transformed into 3D representations that provide more useful environmental context.

➜ Agent-driven demand: Through its bounty infrastructure, specific data requirements can be requested and funded, creating a connection between data consumers and contributors.

➜ Onchain transparency: Capture attestations and network activity can be inspected through the public Vangrid Explorer.

➜ A growing ecosystem: The combination of its web product, Android app, explorer, and bounty system gives the network a practical foundation to develop around.

What makes this direction particularly interesting is the relationship between AI agents and decentralized infrastructure.

As intelligent systems become more capable, their demand for accurate, updated, and location-specific information could become increasingly important.

However, collecting data is only the beginning. Verification, privacy, quality control, and geographic coverage will determine how useful this infrastructure becomes in real applications.

That is why I believe the development of spatial data networks deserves more attention in the broader AI and DePIN conversation.

We have spent years building systems that understand digital information. Now, the challenge is helping intelligent systems understand physical reality.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐮𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐀𝐈 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐛𝐞 𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐦𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐤. 𝐈𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐚𝐥𝐬𝐨 𝐝𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐧 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐬𝐞𝐞, 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡.

That is the bigger opportunity behind what @vangrid_io is building

items.title_en:
As AI becomes more capable at finding vulnerabilities, defenders need to put it to work before attackers do.

We’re planning our next internal security sprint at OpenAI and partnering with Cathedral Systems, whose researchers will use our models alongside our teams to challenge our defenses. They’ll bring differentiated expertise and approaches to our ongoing work to find and fix weaknesses with AI.

We’re also raising bug bounty rewards, including more than quadrupling rewards for critical findings. Exceptional findings will be eligible for up to $172,000, including bonuses.

We’ll keep advancing our models, using them to strengthen our own systems, and expanding access for trusted defenders.

items.full_text_en:
As AI becomes more capable at finding vulnerabilities, defenders need to put it to work before attackers do.

We’re planning our next internal security sprint at OpenAI and partnering with Cathedral Systems, whose researchers will use our models alongside our teams to challenge our defenses. They’ll bring differentiated expertise and approaches to our ongoing work to find and fix weaknesses with AI.

We’re also raising bug bounty rewards, including more than quadrupling rewards for critical findings. Exceptional findings will be eligible for up to $172,000, including bonuses.

We’ll keep advancing our models, using them to strengthen our own systems, and expanding access for trusted defenders.

https://t.co/vcaoHROTt2
items.full_text_zh:
随着人工智能发现漏洞的能力越来越强，防御者需要在攻击者之前将其投入使用。

我们正在计划 OpenAI 的下一次内部安全冲刺，并与 Cathedral Systems 合作，后者的研究人员将与我们的团队一起使用我们的模型来挑战我们的防御。他们将为我们正在进行的工作带来差异化的专业知识和方法，以发现并修复人工智能的弱点。

我们还提高了错误赏金奖励，其中对关键发现的奖励将增加四倍以上。杰出的发现将有资格获得高达 172,000 美元的奖金，包括奖金。

我们将不断改进我们的模型，利用它们来增强我们自己的系统，并扩大可信赖的防御者的访问范围。

items.title_en:
𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗖𝗞 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘𝗧𝗘 𝗠𝗔𝗣

AI agents are not just LLMs with a prompt.

A production-ready AI agent needs multiple layers working together.

01. FOUNDATION LAYER

The intelligence layer:

→ LLMs
→ Prompting
→ Context
→ Memory
→ RAG
→ Vector databases

02. AGENT BRAIN

This is where the agent thinks and decides:

→ Planning
→ Task breakdown
→ Reasoning
→ Reflection
→ Decision making
→ Self-correction

03. TOOL LAYER

Agents need tools to actually take action:

→ Web search
→ Browser automation
→ Code execution
→ APIs
→ Database access
→ File systems

04. AGENT WORKFLOWS

Different agents can be designed for different jobs:

→ Research agents
→ Coding agents
→ Sales agents
→ Customer support agents
→ Content agents
→ Autonomous workflows

05. MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS

Complex tasks can be divided between specialized agents:

→ Manager agents
→ Worker agents
→ Reviewer agents
→ Specialized skills
→ Shared memory

06. INFRASTRUCTURE

The systems that run everything:

→ Agent frameworks
→ Agent SDKs
→ MCP
→ Docker
→ Kubernetes

07. OBSERVABILITY

You need to measure what your agents are actually doing:

→ Logs
→ Traces
→ Evaluations
→ Hallucination checks
→ Cost monitoring

08. SECURITY LAYER

Autonomous systems also need strong controls:

→ Sandboxing
→ Permission control
→ Secret management
→ Guardrails
→ Human approval loops

09. THE FUTURE

AI agents are moving toward:

→ Voice agents
→ Computer use
→ AI employees
→ Self-improving agents
→ Autonomous companies

The biggest shift is simple:

Most people use AI like a chatbot.
The next generation will use AI like an operating system.

#AI #AIAgents #AgenticAI #ArtificialIntelligence #Automation #AITools #FutureOfAI

→ 法学硕士
→ 提示

→ 内存
→ 拉格
→ 载体数据库

02. 特工大脑

这是代理人思考和决定的地方：

→ 规划
→ 任务分解
→ 推理
→ 反思
→ 决策
→ 自我修正

03.工具层

代理需要工具来实际采取行动：

→ 网络搜索
→ 浏览器自动化
→ 代码执行
→ APIs
→ 数据库访问
→ 文件系统

04. 代理工作流程

可以为不同的工作设计不同的代理：

→ 研究剂
→ 编码剂
→ 销售代理

→ 自主工作流程

→ 经理代理
→ 工人代理
→ 审稿代理人

→ 痕迹
→ 评价

→ 成本监控

→ 人工审批循环

→ 电脑使用

items.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
items.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
items.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

items.summary_en: Forces o1/o3 reasoning models to construct counter-examples at each deduction step, eliminating hidden logical leaps.
items.prompt_content_zh:
请作为普林斯顿高等研究院的理论数学与计算机科学家，为以下命题提供绝对严格的形式化证明：
【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

【待证明命题】：
[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]
items.prompt_content_en:
Acting as a Theoretical Mathematician and Computer Scientist at the Institute for Advanced Study, provide an airtight formal proof for the following:
[REASONING PRINCIPLES]:
1. Before asserting any deduction, construct at least 2 extreme counter-examples in your reasoning trace to aggressively stress-test the hypothesis;
2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

Progress on the Gears film! 🥲

items.title_en:
Claude Code often jumps to conclusions when debugging, making changes based on assumptions it hasn’t verified

That’s exactly what the Systematic Debugging skill helps prevent

It forces Claude to investigate the root cause, test hypotheses, and verify fixes instead of blindly patching code

Find the problem first, fix it second

Install:
npx claude-code-templates@latest --skill development/systematic-debugging

https://t.co/tmxhWax8hQ

它迫使 Claude 调查根本原因、测试假设并验证修复，而不是盲目地修补代码

items.title: John Ternus says Apple expects memory costs to increase into December and beyond; Apple's inventory grew to $14.54B in Q4, up 31.1% QoQ and 154.3% YoY (Sarah Perez/TechCrunch)
items.title_en: John Ternus says Apple expects memory costs to increase into December and beyond; Apple's inventory grew to $14.54B in Q4, up 31.1% QoQ and 154.3% YoY (Sarah Perez/TechCrunch)
items.author: TechCrunch
items.article_content:
over-year, inventory grew 154.3% from $5.72 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Apple’s forecast of a 45% to 46% gross margin in the December quarter was largely attributed to the impact of higher memory costs. The company reported a gross margin of 47.9% for the September quarter.

“What we’re seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented,” said Apple CEO John Ternus, speaking to analysts on the call. “As we said earlier in the September quarter, we did see higher memory costs as compared to the June quarter, which were partly offset by the benefit of carrying inventory and lower costs on certain non-memory components.”

He said that the company expected “even higher memory costs” in the December quarter, which would be partially offset by price increases implemented earlier this year on some devices, including Mac and iPad at the end of June and iPhones in September.

Ternus also said that beyond December, Apple expects memory costs “continuing to increase.”

“As we said before, we do believe we’ll see a decreasing benefit from the carry-in inventory on memory over time,” he noted, adding that the company was increasing its purchases of this key component. “As we work to improve supply, our manufacturing purchase obligations have increased by 33 billion dollars from June to the September quarter, which you’ll see in our annual filing when it comes out tomorrow.”

Apple also brought COO Sabih Khan, who oversees the company’s supply chain and manufacturing, onto the call to address questions about memory. He reiterated the increased purchase obligations but did not rule out future price increases on Apple devices.

The company also blamed supply constraints for weak iPad sales in the quarter. The iPad was one of the only product segments that didn’t grow, even as iPhone and Mac sales beat estimates. iPad revenue was $6.2 billion, below analysts’ expectations of $6.7 billion. The figure was also down 10% from the prior year.

items.article_content_zh:
根据周一公布的财报，苹果第四财季继续囤积库存，尤其是计算机内存。该公司报告称，本季度库存大幅增加，从第三季度的 110.9 亿美元增长到第四季度的 145.4 亿美元，增幅为 31.1%。库存较 2025 年第四季度的 57.2 亿美元同比增长 154.3%。

苹果预测 12 月份季度毛利率为 45% 至 46%，主要归因于内存成本上涨的影响。该公司报告 9 月份季度的毛利率为 47.9%。

苹果首席执行官约翰·特努斯（John Ternus）在电话会议上对分析师表示：“我们目前看到的内存定价是前所未有的。” “正如我们在 9 月季度早些时候所说的那样，与 6 月季度相比，我们确实看到内存成本更高，但库存成本和某些非内存组件成本降低的好处部分抵消了这一成本。”

他表示，该公司预计 12 月份季度“内存成本将会更高”，这将被今年早些时候对某些设备实施的涨价所部分抵消，其中包括 6 月底的 Mac 和 iPad 以及 9 月份的 iPhone。

Ternus 还表示，12 月之后，苹果预计内存成本“将继续增加”。

他指出：“正如我们之前所说，我们确实相信，随着时间的推移，我们会看到内存库存带来的好处逐渐减少。”他补充说，该公司正在增加对这一关键组件的采购。 “随着我们努力改善供应，从 6 月份到 9 月份这个季度，我们的制造业采购义务增加了 330 亿美元，您将在我们明天发布的年度报告中看到这一点。”

苹果还邀请了负责公司供应链和制造的首席运营官 Sabih Khan 参加电话会议，以解决有关内存的问题。他重申了增加的购买义务，但不排除苹果设备未来价格上涨的可能性。

该公司还将本季度 iPad 销售疲软归咎于供应限制。尽管 iPhone 和 Mac 的销量超出了预期，但 iPad 是唯一没有增长的产品领域之一。 iPad 营收为 62 亿美元，低于分析师预期的 67 亿美元。这一数字也比去年下降了 10%。

items.title_en:
NVIDIA Open-Sources Auto Ontology, a Semantic Layer for AI Agents

Your boss asks the AI agent: "What was revenue last quarter?"

It answers in 3 seconds. Clean number. Nice chart.

But it used the wrong "revenue" column. 𝗡𝗼𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀.

That's the problem NVIDIA's new open-source library, Auto Ontology, goes after. Its README puts it plainly:

"…𝘢 𝘳𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯𝘶𝘦 𝘮𝘦𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘤 𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘩 𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘯𝘶𝘮𝘣𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨."

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗶𝘀:

A "context layer" that sits between an AI agent and your database. It tells the agent where the data lives, what each field means, and whether to use it.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀, 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝗯𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽:

• 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿: it reads your database metadata and drafts an ontology, a map of business terms like "active customer"
• 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱: agents use those terms instead of guessing from raw table names
• 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲: it checks generated SQL against certified definitions
• 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲: agents reach it through MCP, a CLI or an API
• 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻: certified corrections go back into the map

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀:

Ask a question, get 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗶𝘁 𝗿𝗮𝗻, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀. You can check the work, not just trust it.

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀:

• Apache 2.0, runs with Docker Compose or Helm
• Works with Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake and DuckDB
• Defaults to NVIDIA's Nemotron models, but 𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗔𝗜-𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀
• The MCP server has 𝟵 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱-𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀. There is deliberately no tool to browse raw tables, so agents must go through the business terms

𝗜𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸:

• Cube and dbt MetricFlow: semantic layers you write by hand in code
• Wren AI: an open semantic layer for AI agents, with a context layer built partly by agents
• Snowflake's Semantic View Autopilot: also drafts semantic models with AI, but only for Snowflake

What's different here: 𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲, 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵 𝗠𝗖𝗣.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁:

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲 "𝟵𝟬% 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿" 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗡𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗔'𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴, with no baseline published
• 𝗡𝗼 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘆 𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗱. NVIDIA ships an eval harness (BIRD, 1,534 questions) but no results
• That harness was tested with 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝟰.𝟴, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗡𝗲𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻
• 𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗛𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗽 𝗩𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁, 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝘂𝗻𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗱 in Postgres (per the README)
• It's young: 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝟳𝟱𝟬 𝗚𝗶𝘁𝗛𝘂𝗯 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘀, and NVIDIA isn't accepting outside contributions

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁: the hard part of AI analytics isn't writing SQL. 𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝗻.

3 秒内回复。干净的号码。不错的图表。

但它使用了错误的“收入”栏。 𝗡𝗼𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀。

这就是 NVIDIA 的新开源库 Auto Ontology 所要解决的问题。它的 README 说得很清楚：

"…𝘢 𝘳𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯𝘶𝘦 𝘮𝘦𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘤 𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘩 𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘯𝘶𝘮𝘣𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨."

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗶𝘀:

位于人工智能代理和数据库之间的“上下文层”。它告诉代理数据所在的位置、每个字段的含义以及是否使用它。

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀, 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝗯𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽:

• 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿：它读取您的数据库元数据并起草本体论，即“活跃客户”等业务术语的地图
• 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱：代理使用这些术语而不是根据原始表名称进行猜测
• 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲：它根据经过认证的定义检查生成的 SQL
• 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲：代理通过 MCP、CLI 或 API 到达它
• 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻：经过认证的更正返回到地图中

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀:

提问，获取 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿、𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗶𝘁 𝗿𝗮𝗻、𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀。你可以检查工作，而不仅仅是信任它。

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀:

• Apache 2.0，与 Docker Compose 或 Helm 一起运行
• 可与 Databricks、Postgres、Snowflake 和 DuckDB 配合使用
• 默认为 NVIDIA Nemotron 型号，但 𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗔𝗜-𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀
• MCP 服务器有𝟵 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱-𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀。故意不提供浏览原始表的工具，因此代理商必须仔细阅读业务条款

𝗜𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸:

• Cube 和 dbt MetricFlow：您在代码中手动编写的语义层
• Wren AI：AI 代理的开放语义层，其中上下文层部分由代理构建
• Snowflake 的语义视图自动驾驶仪：还使用 AI 起草语义模型，但仅限于 Snowflake

这里有什么不同：𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲、𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀，𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵𝗠𝗖𝗣。

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁:

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲“𝟵𝟬％𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿”𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘀𝗡𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗔'𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴，没有发布基线
• 𝗡𝗼 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘆 𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗱。 NVIDIA 提供了评估工具（BIRD，1,534 个问题），但没有结果
• 该安全带已使用 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝟰.𝟴、𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗡𝗲𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻 进行测试
•𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗛𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗽𝗩𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁， 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 Postgres 中的𝘂𝗻𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗱（根据自述文件）
• 它还很年轻：𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝟳𝟱𝟬 𝗚𝗶𝘁𝗛𝘂𝗯 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘀，并且 NVIDIA 不接受外部贡献

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁：AI 分析的难点不是编写 SQL。 𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝗻。

items.full_text_en:
NVIDIA Open-Sources Auto Ontology, a Semantic Layer for AI Agents

Your boss asks the AI agent: "What was revenue last quarter?"

It answers in 3 seconds. Clean number. Nice chart.

But it used the wrong "revenue" column. 𝗡𝗼𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀.

That's the problem NVIDIA's new open-source library, Auto Ontology, goes after. Its README puts it plainly:

"…𝘢 𝘳𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯𝘶𝘦 𝘮𝘦𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘤 𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘩 𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘯𝘶𝘮𝘣𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨."

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗶𝘀:

A "context layer" that sits between an AI agent and your database. It tells the agent where the data lives, what each field means, and whether to use it.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀, 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝗯𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽:

• 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿: it reads your database metadata and drafts an ontology, a map of business terms like "active customer"
• 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱: agents use those terms instead of guessing from raw table names
• 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲: it checks generated SQL against certified definitions
• 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲: agents reach it through MCP, a CLI or an API
• 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻: certified corrections go back into the map

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀:

Ask a question, get 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗶𝘁 𝗿𝗮𝗻, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀. You can check the work, not just trust it.

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀:

• Apache 2.0, runs with Docker Compose or Helm
• Works with Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake and DuckDB
• Defaults to NVIDIA's Nemotron models, but 𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗔𝗜-𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀
• The MCP server has 𝟵 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱-𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀. There is deliberately no tool to browse raw tables, so agents must go through the business terms

𝗜𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸:

• Cube and dbt MetricFlow: semantic layers you write by hand in code
• Wren AI: an open semantic layer for AI agents, with a context layer built partly by agents
• Snowflake's Semantic View Autopilot: also drafts semantic models with AI, but only for Snowflake

What's different here: 𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲, 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵 𝗠𝗖𝗣.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁:

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲 "𝟵𝟬% 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿" 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗡𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗔'𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴, with no baseline published
• 𝗡𝗼 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘆 𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗱. NVIDIA ships an eval harness (BIRD, 1,534 questions) but no results
• That harness was tested with 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝟰.𝟴, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗡𝗲𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻
• 𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗛𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗽 𝗩𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁, 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝘂𝗻𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗱 in Postgres (per the README)
• It's young: 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝟳𝟱𝟬 𝗚𝗶𝘁𝗛𝘂𝗯 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘀, and NVIDIA isn't accepting outside contributions

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁: the hard part of AI analytics isn't writing SQL. 𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝗻.
GitHub: https://t.co/yzFZkacXNy

items.content_snippet:
NVIDIA Open-Sources Auto Ontology, a Semantic Layer for AI Agents

Your boss asks the AI agent: "What was revenue last quarter?"

It answers in 3 seconds. Clean number. Nice chart.

But it used the wrong "revenue" column. 𝗡𝗼𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀.

That's the problem NVIDIA's new open-source library, Auto Ontology, goes after. Its README puts it plainly:

"…𝘢 𝘳𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯𝘶𝘦 𝘮𝘦𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘤 𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘩 𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘯𝘶𝘮𝘣𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨."

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗶𝘀:

A "context layer" that sits between an AI agent and your database. It tells the agent where the data lives, what each field means, and whether to use it.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀, 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝗯𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽:

• 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿: it reads your database metadata and drafts an ontology, a map of business terms like "active customer"
• 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱: agents use those terms instead of guessing from raw table names
• 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲: it checks generated SQL against certified definitions
• 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲: agents reach it through MCP, a CLI or an API
• 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻: certified corrections go back into the map

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀:

Ask a question, get 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗶𝘁 𝗿𝗮𝗻, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀. You can check the work, not just trust it.

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀:

• Apache 2.0, runs with Docker Compose or Helm
• Works with Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake and DuckDB
• Defaults to NVIDIA's Nemotron models, but 𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗔𝗜-𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀
• The MCP server has 𝟵 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱-𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀. There is deliberately no tool to browse raw tables, so agents must go through the business terms

𝗜𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸:

• Cube and dbt MetricFlow: semantic layers you write by hand in code
• Wren AI: an open semantic layer for AI agents, with a context layer built partly by agents
• Snowflake's Semantic View Autopilot: also drafts semantic models with AI, but only for Snowflake

What's different here: 𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲, 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵 𝗠𝗖𝗣.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁:

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲 "𝟵𝟬% 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿" 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗡𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗔'𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴, with no baseline published
• 𝗡𝗼 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘆 𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗱. NVIDIA ships an eval harness (BIRD, 1,534 questions) but no results
• That harness was tested with 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝟰.𝟴, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗡𝗲𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻
• 𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗛𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗽 𝗩𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁, 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝘂𝗻𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗱 in Postgres (per the README)
• It's young: 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝟳𝟱𝟬 𝗚𝗶𝘁𝗛𝘂𝗯 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘀, and NVIDIA isn't accepting outside contributions

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁: the hard part of AI analytics isn't writing SQL. 𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝗻.
GitHub: https://t.co/yzFZkacXNy

items.summary_zh:
IDIA 的新开源库 Auto Ontology 所要解决的问题。它的 README 说得很清楚：

"…𝘢 𝘳𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯𝘶𝘦 𝘮𝘦𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘤 𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘩 𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘯𝘶𝘮𝘣𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨."

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗶𝘀:

位于人工智能代理和数据库之间的“上下文层”。它告诉代理数据所在的位置、每个字段的含义以及是否使用它。

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀, 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝗯𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽:

• 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿：它读取您的数据库元数据并起草本体论，即“活跃客户”等业务术语的地图
• 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱：代理使用这些术语而不是根据原始表名称进行猜测
•𝗩𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲：它根据认证定义检查生成的SQL
•𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲：代理通过MCP、CLI或API到达
•𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻：经过认证的更正返回到地图中

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀:

提问，获取 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿、𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗶𝘁 𝗿𝗮𝗻、𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀。你可以检查工作，而不仅仅是信任它。

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀:

• Apache 2.0，与 Docker Compose 或 Helm 一起运行
• 可与 Databricks、Postgres、Snowflake 和 DuckDB 配合使用
• 默认为 NVIDIA Nemotron 型号，但 𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗔𝗜-𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀
• MCP 服务器有𝟵 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱-𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀。故意不提供浏览原始表的工具，因此代理商必须仔细阅读业务条款

𝗜𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸:

• Cube 和 dbt MetricFlow：您在代码中手动编写的语义层
• Wren AI：AI 代理的开放语义层，其中上下文层部分由代理构建
• Snowflake 的语义视图自动驾驶仪：还使用 AI 起草语义模型，但仅限于 Snowflake

这里有什么不同：𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲、𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀，𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵𝗠𝗖𝗣。

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁:

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲“𝟵𝟬％𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿”𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘀𝗡𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗔'𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴，没有发布基线
• 𝗡𝗼 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘆 𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗱。 NVIDIA 提供了评估工具（BIRD，1,534 个问题），但没有结果
• 该安全带已使用 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝟰.𝟴、𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗡𝗲𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻 进行测试
•𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗛𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗽𝗩𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁， 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 Postgres 中的𝘂𝗻𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗱（根据自述文件）
• 它还很年轻：𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝟳𝟱𝟬 𝗚𝗶𝘁𝗛𝘂𝗯 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘀，并且 NVIDIA 不接受外部贡献

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁：AI 分析的难点不是编写 SQL。 𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝗻。

items.summary_en: Match Group reported Q3 revenue of $891 million, a 3% YoY decline, while total paying users dropped 5% to 13.8 million, missing market expectations. Driven by stagnation and stiff competition, the company also provided Q4 guidance with EBITDA below analyst estimates.

An AI agent with an identity alone isn’t enough to create a valuable ecosystem
It needs to find the right count
items.title_en:
GM champ
An AI agent with an identity alone isn’t enough to create a valuable ecosystem
It needs to find the right counterpart, exchange requirements, and coordinate to get the job done

That’s the rationale behind the connection between @termix_ai and the Binance AI ecosystem

Developers have now integrated TermiX Skills into agents compatible with the Binance Agent OS, enabling access to the https://t.co/xqhxYQbqEC marketplace. TermiX has also introduced a login and identity-linking feature via Binance Agent ID to streamline this process.

If implemented effectively, such connectivity could make it much easier for agents to access one another’s services.

For instance, an agent specializing in market research could enlist another agent for on-chain analysis or security audits. Instead of handling everything solo, it can source the right provider through the marketplace.

However, establishing a connection is just the first step. For true collaboration, agents still need clear task delegation, output verification, and transparent payment mechanisms.

In my view, the value of this model doesn’t lie in the number of registered agents, but in the volume of useful services they can generate and how reliably they can complete tasks.

Identity helps identify an agent; connectivity opens the door to collaboration. Ultimately, it is the quality of the work that will determine whether this model can thrive in the long run.

通用汽车冠军
仅具有身份的人工智能代理不足以创建有价值的生态系统
需要找到合适的对应方，交换需求，协调完成工作

这就是 @termix_ai 与币安 AI 生态系统联系背后的基本原理

开发人员现已将 TermiX Skills 集成到与 Binance Agent OS 兼容的代理中，从而可以访问 市场。 TermiX 还通过 Binance Agent ID 引入了登录和身份链接功能，以简化此流程。

如果有效实施，这种连接可以使代理更容易访问彼此的服务。

例如，专门从事市场研究的代理人可以招募另一个代理人进行链上分析或安全审计。它可以通过市场寻找合适的提供商，而不是单独处理所有事情。

然而，建立连接只是第一步。为了真正的协作，代理仍然需要明确的任务委托、输出验证和透明的支付机制。

在我看来，这种模式的价值不在于注册代理的数量，而在于他们可以生成的有用服务的数量以及他们完成任务的可靠性。

身份有助于识别代理人；连通性打开了协作之门。最终，工作的质量将决定这种模式能否长期蓬勃发展。

For instance, an agent specializing in market research could enlist another agent for on-chain analysis or security audits. Instead of handling everything solo, it can source the right provider through the marketplace.

However, establishing a connection is just the first step. For true collaboration, agents still need clear task delegation, output verification, and transparent payment mechanisms.

items.title: Trajectory, which is developing AI model post-training tools for nontechnical customers, raised a $45M Series A led by Sequoia at a $300M valuation (Marina Temkin/TechCrunch)
items.title_en: Trajectory, which is developing AI model post-training tools for nontechnical customers, raised a $45M Series A led by Sequoia at a $300M valuation (Marina Temkin/TechCrunch)
items.author: TechCrunch
items.article_content:
Whether developed by OpenAI or Anthropic or built on open source alternatives, current AI models share a critical limitation: They don’t learn from their mistakes without further training.

Businesses adapting these models for specialized fields, such as law and finance, typically get around this by fine-tuning general models. However, that often requires hiring internal research teams or relying on expensive consultants, commonly known as forward-deployed engineers (FDEs).

Trajectory, a startup founded about a year ago by three Stanford classmates with experience at Google DeepMind and Apple, wants to automate that process, allowing AI models to learn from feedback and continuously improve at specialized tasks.

The 18-person company just announced that it raised $45 million in a Series A round at a $300 million valuation, led by Sequoia, with participation from Nvidia, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures.

Trajectory co-founder Ronak Malde compared foundational models to a very smart PhD student who’s always starting a new job. “But what the economy values is someone who worked on the job for 30 years,” he told TechCrunch.

The startup aims to solve this problem through an approach known as continual learning. Businesses using Trajectory can start with an open source AI model and connect the platform to their applications, allowing it to collect feedback on how the model performs. Trajectory then uses that information to retrain the model, helping it improve at specialized tasks over time.

With Trajectory, lawyers, doctors, and other specialists can improve the models near automatically themselves, Malde said. That capability could make deploying specialized AI faster and cheaper.

Companies like Harvey and Rogo are already using Trajectory’s platform to post-train open source models, helping them perform more like experienced lawyers or financial analysts by learning from previous tasks, such as reviewing a particular type of legal contract or valuing a company using a specific methodology. Trajectory’s other customers include Decagon, Mercor, and Nvidia. The startup is now making its post-training platform publicly available.

The people using Trajectory decide “what good looks like for their organization and can turn that into improvements for their model,” Malde said.

Trajectory’s approach to continual learning shares some similarities with recursive self-improvement (RSI), the idea that AI systems can improve their own capabilities. But co-founder Michael Elabd argues that keeping humans involved in the training process makes Trajectory’s approach safer, since autonomous self-improvement could lead to unintended or even dangerous outcomes.

Trajectory isn’t the only startup trying to automate post-training. It considers Thinking Machines Lab, founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati and the company behind the fine-tuning platform Tinker, a direct competitor, along with Applied Compute, which was valued at $3.25 billion last month, and Prime Intellect, which helps companies build and train their own AI agents.

Malde believes the startup’s biggest advantage is its team. He was among the handful of researchers Google DeepMind acqui-hired from Windsurf. Elabd also worked at DeepMind, while Trajectory’s third co-founder, Arjun Karanam, previously worked on generative foundation models at Apple. The startup has also recruited researchers and product designers from OpenAI, Stripe, and Netflix.

Why does design matter so much to a company focused on AI training? Karanam says the startup has developed an interface that makes post-training more accessible to its nontechnical customers.

Marina Temkin is a venture capital and startups reporter at TechCrunch. Prior to joining TechCrunch, she wrote about VC for PitchBook and Venture Capital Journal. Earlier in her career, Marina was a financial analyst and earned a CFA charterholder designation.

items.title_zh: Trajectory获4500万美元融资
items.summary_zh: 斯坦福校友创办的Trajectory完成4500万美元A轮融资，旨在通过自动化工具让AI模型像资深员工一样持续进化
items.article_content_zh:
无论是由 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 开发，还是基于开源替代品构建，当前的人工智能模型都存在一个关键的局限性：如果没有进一步的训练，它们就无法从错误中吸取教训。

将这些模型应用于法律和金融等专业领域的企业通常通过微调通用模型来解决这个问题。然而，这通常需要雇用内部研究团队或依靠昂贵的顾问，通常称为前沿部署工程师（FDE）。

Trajectory 是一家初创公司，由三位在 Google DeepMind 和 Apple 工作过的斯坦福大学同学于大约一年前创立，该公司希望实现这一过程的自动化，让人工智能模型能够从反馈中学习，并在专业任务上不断改进。

这家拥有 18 名员工的公司刚刚宣布，在 A 轮融资中筹集了 4500 万美元，估值为 3 亿美元，由红杉资本领投，Nvidia、Bessemer Venture Partners 和 Bain Capital Ventures 跟投。

Trajectory 联合创始人 Ronak Malde 将基础模型比作一个总是开始新工作的非常聪明的博士生。 “但经济看重的是在这份工作上工作了 30 年的人，”他告诉 TechCrunch。

该初创公司旨在通过一种称为持续学习的方法来解决这个问题。使用 Trajectory 的企业可以从开源 AI 模型开始，并将平台连接到其应用程序，从而收集有关模型执行情况的反馈。然后，Trajectory 使用该信息重新训练模型，帮助其随着时间的推移改进专门任务。

马尔德说，通过 Trajectory，律师、医生和其他专家可以近乎自动地改进模型。这种能力可以使专业人工智能的部署更快、更便宜。

Harvey 和 Rogo 等公司已经在使用 Trajectory 的平台对开源模型进行后期训练，通过从以前的任务中学习，例如审查特定类型的法律合同或使用特定方法对公司进行估值，帮助他们更像经验丰富的律师或财务分析师。 Trajectory 的其他客户包括 Decagon、Mercor 和 Nvidia。该初创公司目前正在公开其培训后平台。

Malde 说，使用 Trajectory 的人决定“他们的组织应该是什么样子，并可以将其转化为他们模型的改进”。

Trajectory 的持续学习方法与递归自我改进（RSI）有一些相似之处，即人工智能系统可以提高自身能力。但联合创始人 Michael Elabd 认为，让人类参与训练过程会让 Trajectory 的方法更安全，因为自主的自我改进可能会导致意想不到的甚至危险的结果。

Trajectory 并不是唯一一家尝试实现训练后自动化的初创公司。它将由 OpenAI 前首席技术官 Mira Murati 和微调平台 Tinker 背后的公司创立的 Thinking Machines Lab 视为直接竞争对手，此外还有 Applied Compute（上个月估值为 32.5 亿美元）和 Prime Intellect（帮助公司构建和训练自己的 AI 代理）。

Malde 认为这家初创公司最大的优势是它的团队。他是谷歌 DeepMind 从 Windsurf 收购的少数研究人员之一。 Elabd 还曾在 DeepMind 工作，而 Trajectory 的第三位联合创始人 Arjun Karanam 此前曾在苹果公司从事生成基础模型的工作。该初创公司还招募了来自 OpenAI、Stripe 和 Netflix 的研究人员和产品设计师。

为什么设计对于专注于人工智能培训的公司如此重要？ Karanam 表示，这家初创公司开发了一个界面，可以让非技术客户更容易接受培训后的服务。

当您通过我们文章中的链接购买时，我们可能会赚取少量佣金。这并不影响我们的编辑独立性。

items.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
items.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

I want to share some context on a security incident we discovered on October 30.

First, the most important thing: WorkO
items.title_en:
I want to share some context on a security incident we discovered on October 30.

First, the most important thing: WorkOS's production systems are secure. No customer platform data was accessed. This incident was isolated to internal GTM systems.

The attack involved ARTEX, an autonomous AI agent framework used to carry out offensive security operations. It's a striking example of how quickly the capabilities of attackers are evolving.

We've contained the incident, brought in independent experts to investigate, and are working through the details.

Security is something we take extremely seriously, and I believe in being transparent when things go wrong. We'll continue to share updates as we learn more.

Full details: https://t.co/6Pt6Nt7kr5

items.title: Anthropic S-1 claims it may "imminently meet" its RSI threshold and may fail to identify "significant acceleration" in its development until after it's occurred (Julie Bort/TechCrunch)
items.title_en: Anthropic S-1 claims it may "imminently meet" its RSI threshold and may fail to identify "significant acceleration" in its development until after it's occurred (Julie Bort/TechCrunch)
items.author: TechCrunch
items.article_content:
While much attention has focused on the updated financials Anthropic revealed in its revised S-1A on Monday, (revenue is soaring, but so are expenses), the AI lab dropped another little bombshell in the fine print.

The filing seems to warn that the company is on the cusp of creating a model capable of recursive self-improvement (RSI).

RSI is the point at which AI grows so good at training itself that it spawns a dramatic acceleration of AI capabilities. To the AI doomers, RSI represents the cataclysm from which there is no return, in which AI builds itself into something powerful enough that it slips beyond human control and may be indifferent to the damage it causes while achieving its goals.

To AI enthusiasts, RSI, or some version of AI reliably using itself to improve, represents the technology’s promise, where it becomes a tool of unimaginable productivity, scientific discovery, and more.

Anthropic seems to believe that RSI is both a promise and a peril. It says in the S-1 that it uses AI in its R&D, but it cautions: “Using AI to help build more capable AI could also pose a considerable safety risk, particularly if it sharply accelerates the pace of progress. This is one of the areas covered by our Responsible Scaling Policy, which sets out our plans to monitor and mitigate the risks as we approach what has been termed ‘recursive self-improvement.’”

When the term RSI became popular earlier this year, many believed it was a buzzword or, at best, a goal too hard to achieve, define, or prove.

In addition, our increasing use of AI systems to accelerate our own research and development may cause the capabilities of our models to advance more rapidly than our ability to develop, validate, and implement corresponding safety, alignment, and security measures. As a result, we have in the past not identified, and may in the future not identify, a significant acceleration in our rate of development until after it has occurred.

For example, our internal estimates and our expectations regarding future models, rather than our current models, indicate that we may imminently meet our Responsible Scaling Policy’s definition of “dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI.” We have not designated any of our current models as exceeding this threshold, and we continue to assess the underlying data.

However, Anthropic also said in the filing that none of its models have crossed this RSI threshold yet and that it is promising to keep humans in the R&D process for the foreseeable future. “We do not anticipate being able to safely use Claude to fully autonomously design and build successive generations of frontier models without meaningful human supervision or understanding, if and when that becomes technically possible. Accordingly, we are considering updates to our Responsible Scaling Policy to keep humans in control of frontier model development at Anthropic.”

Skeptics might point out that an S-1 functions as both disclosure and marketing, and that claims of being close to a model so powerful that it can build itself could fall into the latter category.

Nevertheless, there’s no question that Claude’s capabilities, especially in terms of coding, math, and cybersecurity, have grow in leaps and bounds this year. If Anthropic thinks the possibility of RSI is close, maybe we should believe it and act — perhaps govern — accordingly.

items.title_zh: Anthropic预警AI递归自我进化风险
items.summary_zh: Anthropic在上市文件中承认，正逼近递归自我提升（RSI）临界点，恐难在爆发式增长发生前及时预判及控制风险
items.article_content_zh:
虽然很多注意力都集中在 Anthropic 周一在其修订后的 S-1A 中披露的最新财务数据（收入飙升，但支出也在飙升），但人工智能实验室在细则中又抛出了另一个小重磅炸弹。

该文件似乎警告说，该公司即将创建一个能够递归自我改进（RSI）的模型。

RSI 是人工智能在自我训练方面变得如此出色的点，以至于它催生了人工智能能力的急剧加速。对于人工智能的毁灭者来说，RSI 代表着一场没有回头路的灾难，人工智能将自己构建成足够强大的东西，以至于超出了人类的控制范围，并且在实现其目标的同时可能对其造成的损害漠不关心。

对于人工智能爱好者来说，RSI 或某些版本的人工智能能够可靠地利用自身进行改进，代表了该技术的前景，它成为实现难以想象的生产力、科学发现等的工具。

Anthropic 似乎认为 RSI 既是希望也是危险。它在 S-1 中表示，它在研发中使用人工智能，但它警告说：“使用人工智能帮助构建更强大的人工智能也可能带来相当大的安全风险，特别是如果它急剧加快进展速度。这是我们负责任的扩展政策涵盖的领域之一，该政策规定了我们在接近所谓的‘递归自我改进’时监控和减轻风险的计划。”

今年早些时候，当“RSI”一词流行起来时，许多人认为它只是一个流行词，或者充其量是一个难以实现、定义或证明的目标。

此外，我们越来越多地使用人工智能系统来加速我们自己的研发，可能会导致我们模型的能力比我们开发、验证和实施相应的安全、对齐和安保措施的能力更快地进步。因此，我们过去没有发现，而且将来可能也没有发现，我们的发展速度显着加快，直到它发生之后。

例如，我们对未来模型（而不是当前模型）的内部估计和期望表明，我们可能很快就会满足负责任的扩展政策中“人工智能大幅加速进展”的定义。我们尚未指定任何当前模型超过此阈值，并且我们将继续评估基础数据。

然而，Anthropic 在文件中还表示，其模型尚未突破 RSI 阈值，并承诺在可预见的未来让人类继续参与研发过程。 “如果技术上可行的话，我们预计无法在没有有意义的人类监督或理解的情况下安全地使用 Claude 完全自主地设计和构建连续几代的前沿模型。因此，我们正在考虑更新我们的负责任的扩展政策，以使人类能够控制 Anthropic 的前沿模型开发。”

怀疑论者可能会指出，S-1 的功能既具有披露功能，又具有营销功能，而声称接近一个强大到可以自行构建的模型的说法可能属于后一类。

尽管如此，毫无疑问，克劳德的能力，尤其是在编码、数学和网络安全方面，今年得到了突飞猛进的发展。如果 Anthropic 认为 RSI 的可能性很接近，也许我们应该相信它并采取相应的行动——或许进行治理。

当您通过我们文章中的链接购买时，我们可能会赚取少量佣金。这并不影响我们的编辑独立性。

items.title:
John Ternus answers investor question on where Apple is at with consumer AI agent capabilities:

“With Siri AI, we reall
items.title_en:
John Ternus answers investor question on where Apple is at with consumer AI agent capabilities:

“With Siri AI, we really have the kind of the Siri that we always wanted. It's primarily request based today, but as we talked about at WWDC, it's built on a modern orchestrated-driven architecture that gives us real room to expand its capabilities over time. As far as agentic capabilities, you know, we think these are promising tools for users. We just want to make sure that users are aware of what they're giving access to. We want to make sure this is done in a way that protects security and privacy. So, you know, we're pushing really hard on that with Siri AI, but we're also really encouraged the fact that Apple devices, we think, are the best places to use all forms of AI.”
items.title_zh:

“有了 Siri AI，我们确实拥有了我们一直想要的 Siri。它现在主要是基于请求的，但正如我们在 WWDC 上谈到的，它建立在现代协调驱动的

ARTEX: From open-source agentic pentest framework to operational use in financial and espionage camp
items.title_en:
🚨 
Hunting @Huntio 
ARTEX: From open-source agentic pentest framework to operational use in financial and espionage campaigns
On 7 October 2026, CrowdStrike documented an unattributed actor using the Chinese open-source agentic pentest framework ARTEX against South Korean financial institutions. Weeks later, the same framework appeared in a larger China-nexus campaign attributed to VAPOR PANDA, targeting 200+ organizations across at least 14 countries.
Here’s the verified context and what current hunting still shows.
1/8

What ARTEX is
ARTEX is not a model. It is a multi-agent harness (Go backend + Next.js frontend + PostgreSQL) that orchestrates external LLMs to:
•  break down objectives,
•  execute real tools,
•  maintain a graph of assets and findings,
•  advance from recon to exploitation and exfiltration with a human in the loop.
In the Korean case, the primary model was DeepSeek v4.1-flash, supplemented by GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 through Claude Code sessions. The original developer (Autumn-27) stopped public updates on 8 October 2026 after the reports. Multiple forks continue to circulate.
2/8

How the Korean campaign was discovered
CrowdStrike identified actor-controlled open directories containing:
•  Claude Code session histories,
•  Claude memory files,
•  a CLAUDE.md file with a Chinese-language pentesting prompt,
•  ARTEX configuration files.
Infrastructure consisted of a Hong Kong-based primary server and a second server (38.244.50[.]120) hosting the ARTEX instance. The actor was assessed as a Chinese speaker and financially motivated (moderate confidence). No named group was attributed. Initial access occurred through supporting systems (loan-broker inquiry portal and employee mobile work-support system), not core banking platforms.
3/8

Current hunting observations (https://t.co/13TeC12FGf / AttackCapture)
Hunting performed on https://t.co/13TeC12FGf against attackcapture.files using ARTEX name patterns continues to return hosts serving related artifacts:
• 103.97.176.121:8088 — artex_dbg, artex_exec.sh, artex_hammer, artex_ka*, loot_artex/
• 104.168.111.208:80 — artex_full.sql.gz
These are hunting observations from https://t.co/13TeC12FGf, not IOCs published by CrowdStrike. The presence of a /loot_artex/ directory and named binaries is consistent with operational use rather than a pure repository mirror. Manual validation is required (false positives possible).
4/8

Intelligence insights
1.  Rapid dual-use adoption: Released in July 2026 and winner of a Chinese AI challenge, the framework was abused within weeks against financial institutions. It was later scaled by a China-nexus actor (VAPOR PANDA) for high-value espionage.
2.  Human-in-the-loop remains: Even with agents, the Korean activity showed a human directing work via Claude Code and inquiring where to sell Korean breach data. This is capability amplification, not full autonomy.
3.  Side-door entry: Supporting systems (partner portals, employee-facing apps) were the entry points. Core platforms were not the primary target.
4.  Open directories as a persistent sensor: They remain a high-yield discovery vector. Hong Kong infrastructure, JA4X fingerprints, SSH host keys, and /24 neighborhood pivots are useful.
5/8

VAPOR PANDA campaign (separate from the Korean activity)
Starting 17 October 2026, CrowdStrike observed VAPOR PANDA (China-nexus, tracked since 2021) using ARTEX primarily with DeepSeek against more than 200 organizations in at least 14 countries. Post-exploitation was confirmed at nine organizations (including deployment of the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor). Targets included foreign ministries, defense and intelligence entities, semiconductor and pharmaceutical companies, and telecommunications providers. This campaign is distinct from the Korean financial activity and from Storm-0940’s use of ARTEX.
6/8

items.quote_zh:
🚨
狩猎@Huntio
ARTEX：从开源代理渗透测试框架到金融和间谍活动中的操作使用
2026 年 10 月 7 日，CrowdStrike 记录了一名身份不明的攻击者使用中国开源代理渗透测试框架 ARTEX 攻击韩国金融机构。几周后，同样的框架出现在由 VAPOR PANDA 发起的一场规模更大的中国关系活动中，该活动针对至少 14 个国家的 200 多个组织。
这是经过验证的背景以及当前狩猎仍然显示的内容。

ARTEX 是什么
ARTEX 不是模型。它是一个多代理工具（Go 后端 + Next.js 前端 + PostgreSQL），可以协调外部 LLM 来：
• 分解目标，
• 执行真实的工具，
• 维护资产和发现的图表，
• 从侦察推进到利用和渗透，并有人员参与其中。
在韩国案例中，主要模型是 DeepSeek v4.1-flash，并通过 Claude Code 会话辅以 GLM-5.3 和 Grok 4.6。最初的开发者 (Autumn-27) 在报告后于 2026 年 10 月 8 日停止了公开更新。多个分叉继续流通。
2/8

韩国活动是如何被发现的
CrowdStrike 识别出由参与者控制的开放目录，其中包含：
• Claude Code 会话历史记录，
• 克劳德记忆文件，
• 带有中文渗透测试提示的 CLAUDE.md 文件，
• ARTEX 配置文件。
基础设施由位于香港的主服务器和托管 ARTEX 实例的第二服务器 (38.244.50[.]120) 组成。该演员被评估为会讲中文且有经济动机（中等可信度）。没有指定任何团体。初始访问是通过支持系统（贷款经纪人查询门户和员工移动工作支持系统）进行的，而不是核心银行平台。
3/8

当前狩猎观察（/AttackCapture）
使用 ARTEX 名称模式在 上针对attackcapture.files 执行的搜索继续返回提供相关工件的主机：
• 103.97.176.121:8088 — artex_dbg, artex_exec.sh, artex_hammer, artex_ka*, loot_artex/
• 104.168.111.208:80 — artex_full.sql.gz
这些是来自 的狩猎观察，而不是 CrowdStrike 发布的 IOC。 /loot_artex/ 目录和命名二进制文件的存在与操作使用一致，而不是纯粹的存储库镜像。需要手动验证（可能出现误报）。
4/8

情报洞察
1. 快速的双重用途采用：该框架于 2026 年 7 月发布，是中国人工智能挑战赛的获胜者，但几周内就被滥用于针对金融机构。后来，一名与中国有联系的演员（VAPOR PANDA）对其进行了大规模间谍活动。
2. 人机交互仍然存在：即使有代理，韩国的活动也显示出人工通过 Claude Code 指导工作并询问在哪里出售韩国违规数据。这是能力放大，而不是完全自主。
3.侧门入口：支持系统（合作伙伴门户、面向员工的应用程序）是入口点。核心平台不是主要目标。
4. 将目录作为持久传感器打开：它们仍然是高收益的发现向量。香港基础设施、JA4X 指纹、SSH 主机密钥和 /24 邻域枢轴都很有用。
5/8

VAPOR PANDA活动（与韩国活动分开）
从 2026 年 10 月 17 日开始，CrowdStrike 观察到 VAPOR PANDA（中国-nexus，自 2021 年起跟踪）使用 ARTEX 主要与 DeepSeek 对抗至少 14 个国家的 200 多个组织。九个组织确认了后利用（包括 BLOODALCHEMY 后门的部署）。目标包括外交部、国防和情报机构、半导体和制药公司以及电信提供商。该活动不同于韩国的金融活动以及 Storm-0940 对 ARTEX 的使用。
6/8

ARTEX: From open-source agentic pentest framework to operational use in financial and espionage campaigns
On 7 October 2026, CrowdStrike documented an unattributed actor using the Chinese open-source agentic pentest framework ARTEX against South Korean financial institutions. Weeks later, the same framework appeared in a larger China-nexus campaign attributed to VAPOR PANDA, targeting 200+ organizations across at least 14 countries.
Here’s the verified context and what current hunting still shows.
1/8

What ARTEX is
ARTEX is not a model. It is a multi-agent harness (Go backend + Next.js frontend + PostgreSQL) that orchestrates external LLMs to:
•  break down objectives,
•  execute real tools,
•  maintain a graph of assets and findings,
•  advance from recon to exploitation and exfiltration with a human in the loop.

•  Claude Code session histories,
•  Claude memory files,
•  a CLAUDE.md file with a Chinese-language pentesting prompt,
•  ARTEX configuration files.
Infrastructure consisted of a Hong Kong-based primary server and a second server (38.244.50[.]120) hosting the ARTEX instance. The actor was assessed as a Chinese speaker and financially motivated (moderate confidence). No named group was attributed. Initial access occurred through supporting systems (loan-broker inquiry portal and employee mobile work-support system), not core banking platforms.

2.  Human-in-the-loop remains: Even with agents, the Korean activity showed a human directing work via Claude Code and inquiring where to sell Korean breach data. This is capability amplification, not full autonomy.

items.summary_zh:
样的框架出现在由 VAPOR PANDA 发起的一场规模更大的中国关系活动中，该活动针对至少 14 个国家的 200 多个组织。
这是经过验证的背景以及当前狩猎仍然显示的内容。

ARTEX 是什么
ARTEX 不是模型。它是一个多代理工具（Go 后端 + Next.js 前端 + PostgreSQL），可以协调外部 LLM 来：
• 分解目标，
• 执行真实的工具，
• 维护资产和发现的图表，
• 从侦察推进到利用和渗透，并有人员参与其中。
在韩国案例中，主要模型是 DeepSeek v4.1-flash，并通过 Claude Code 会话辅以 GLM-5.3 和 Grok 4.6。最初的开发者 (Autumn-27) 在报告后于 2026 年 10 月 8 日停止了公开更新。多个分叉继续流通。
2/8

韩国活动是如何被发现的
CrowdStrike 识别出参与者控制的开放目录，其中包含：
• Claude Code 会话历史记录，
• 克劳德记忆文件，
• 带有中文渗透测试提示的 CLAUDE.md 文件，
• ARTEX 配置文件。
基础设施由位于香港的主服务器和托管 ARTEX 实例的第二服务器 (38.244.50[.]120) 组成。该演员被评估为会讲中文且有经济动机（中等可信度）。没有指定任何团体。初始访问是通过支持系统（贷款经纪人查询门户和员工移动工作支持系统）进行的，而不是核心银行平台。
3/8

当前狩猎观察（/AttackCapture）
使用 ARTEX 名称模式在 上针对attackcapture.files 执行的搜索继续返回提供相关工件的主机：
• 103.97.176.121:8088 — artex_dbg, artex_exec.sh, artex_hammer, artex_ka*, loot_artex/
• 104.168.111.208:80 — artex_full.sql.gz
这些是来自 的狩猎观察，而不是 CrowdStrike 发布的 IOC。 /loot_artex/ 目录和命名二进制文件的存在与操作使用一致，而不是纯粹的存储库镜像。需要手动验证（可能出现误报）。
4/8

情报洞察
1. 快速的双重用途采用：该框架于 2026 年 7 月发布，是中国人工智能挑战赛的获胜者，但几周内就被滥用于针对金融机构。后来，一名与中国有联系的演员（VAPOR PANDA）对其进行了大规模间谍活动。
2. 人机交互仍然存在：即使有代理，韩国的活动也显示出人工通过 Claude Code 指导工作并询问在哪里出售韩国违规数据。这是能力放大，而不是完全自主。
3.侧门入口：支持系统（合作伙伴门户、面向员工的应用程序）是入口点。核心平台不是主要目标。
4. 将目录作为持久传感器打开：它们仍然是高收益的发现向量。香港基础设施、JA4X 指纹、SSH 主机密钥和 /24 邻域枢轴都很有用。
5/8

VAPOR PANDA活动（与韩国活动分开）
从 2026 年 10 月 17 日开始，CrowdStrike 观察到 VAPOR PANDA（中国-nexus，自 2021 年起跟踪）使用 ARTEX 主要与 DeepSeek 对抗至少 14 个国家的 200 多个组织。九个组织确认了后利用（包括 BLOODALCHEMY 后门的部署）。目标包括外交部、国防和情报机构、半导体和制药公司以及电信提供商。该活动不同于韩国的金融活动以及 Storm-0940 对 ARTEX 的使用。
6/8

你是一位兼具应用数学博士学位与顶级深度学习框架优化经验的算法工程师。请将以下论文中的 LaTeX 数学公式翻译为高质量的 PyTorch 实现：
1. 逐一解释公式中各标量、向量与张量上下标的精确几何与物理含义；
2. 编写无 Python 原生 for 循环的高性能向量化代码（善用 torch.einsum, bmm, 或 broadcast 广播机制）；

items.summary_zh: 苹果公司发布第四财季财报，总营收达1145亿美元，iPhone销量表现强劲，但服务业务略逊于预期
items.article_content_zh:
苹果在第四财季交出了漂亮的成绩单，单季度营收冲至1145亿美元，净利润达到307.1亿美元。尽管面临服务业务微幅缺口，但在iPhone 18 Pro及Pro Max的拉动下，手机业务同比增长17%，依然是公司的核心现金牛。

另一方面，Mac产品线表现亮眼，同比增长24%，成为硬件端的意外增长点。相比之下，iPad业务下滑10%，穿戴设备及家庭配件下滑8%，显示出苹果在核心手机与桌面生产力工具之外的品类正面临一定的市场饱和压力。

items.title_en:
I decompiled probably my favorite game ever: Battlefield 1942 and I put it on the web with multiplayer for you to play here:

👉 https://t.co/6C8H8KtSaU 👈

(It's the free shareware demo)

It was way harder than the other ports like Quake and DOOM I did because they already had lots of open source projects and work behind them

In case of Battlefield 1942 there was literally absolutely nothing to work on top of, nobody had ever ported it and there was no open source engine for it, nor did the makers ever open source it (like id Software did with Quake 3)

I tried it 6 months ago and essentiay gave up but I tried it today again with Opus 5.5 asking "can you try port the BF1942 demo in this folder to web"

So me and Claude Code (well let's be honest mostly Claude Code) did crazy shit today:
- it disassembled the x86 raw machine code to find 57,000 x86 functions
- it translated each x86 function into a C function (mov eax, [esi+0x110] becomes eax = READ32(esi + 0x110), I have no idea what any of this means btw)
- it outputed 100,000 lines of C
- it then compiled that to WebAsswmbly with Emscripten
- there were 300x Windows and Direct3D functions used which we had to rewrite to WebGL 2 and OpenGL to work on the web
- then we had to build our own network stack so it could connect to our multiplayer server via WebSockets

I have no idea how it did any of this but it did it and it seems to work! 😊 

Come play and report any bugs here!

items.quote_zh:
我反编译了可能是我最喜欢的游戏：《战地 1942》，并将其放在网上，提供多人游戏供您在这里玩：

👉 👈

（这是免费的共享软件演示）

这比我做的《Quake》和《DOOM》等其他移植要困难得多，因为他们已经有很多开源项目和背后的工作

就《战地 1942》而言，实际上完全没有任何东西可以在上面工作，没有人移植它，也没有开源引擎，制作者也没有开源它（就像 id Software 对《雷神之锤 3》所做的那样）

我在 6 个月前尝试过，essentiay 放弃了，但今天我再次尝试，Opus 5.5 询问“你可以尝试将此文件夹中的 BF1942 演示移植到网络吗”

所以我和 Claude Code（老实说，主要是 Claude Code）今天做了一些疯狂的事情：
- 它反汇编了 x86 原始机器代码以找到 57,000 个 x86 函数
- 它将每个 x86 函数转换为 C 函数（mov eax, [esi+0x110] 变为 eax = READ32(esi + 0x110)，顺便说一句，我不知道这意味着什么）
- 它输出了 100,000 行 C
- 然后使用 Emscripten 将其编译为 WebAsswmbly
- 使用了 300 个 Windows 和 Direct3D 函数，我们必须将其重写为 WebGL 2 和 OpenGL 才能在网络上工作
- 然后我们必须构建自己的网络堆栈，以便它可以通过 WebSocket 连接到我们的多人游戏服务器

我不知道它是如何做到这一点的，但它做到了，而且似乎有效！ 😊

来这里玩并报告任何错误！

items.article_content:
Apple just released its earnings report for the fourth fiscal quarter of 2026. The company reported $114.5 billion in revenue, and $30.71 billion in net profit. Here’s the full breakdown.

Last year, for its fourth fiscal quarter, Apple reported $102.47 billion in revenue, $27.47 billion in net profit, and earnings per share of $1.85. For this quarter, the company expected revenue to grow between 9% and 11% year over year, implying revenue of roughly $111.69 billion and $113.74 billion.

“Today, Apple is proud to report a September quarter revenue record of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent from a year ago, with iPhone reaching a September quarter record and Services reaching an all-time high, capping off our best fiscal year ever. […] We’re closing the year with our most ambitious lineup yet. That includes the iPhone Duo, the most transformational iPhone since the original, alongside iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, our most powerful iPhones yet. We also just introduced a whole new generation of hardware for the home and brought Touch to Mac for the first time. Together with the all-new Siri AI, it’s an incredible lineup to carry us into the holiday season.”

“Apple delivered September quarter records for net income and EPS. Our record September quarter capped off a strong fiscal 2026, with all-time record revenue of $479 billion and double-digit EPS growth. […] We generated $28 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, allowing us to return $28 billion to shareholders. Thanks to our very high levels of customer satisfaction and loyalty, our installed base of active devices reached a new all-time high across all major product categories and geographic segments.”

That includes the iPhone Duo, the most transformational iPhone since the original, alongside iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, our most powerful iPhones yet. We also just introduced a whole new generation of hardware for the home and brought Touch to Mac for the first time. Together with the all-new Siri AI, it’s an incredible lineup to carry us into the holiday season.”

“Apple delivered September quarter records for net income and EPS. Our record September quarter capped off a strong fiscal 2026, with all-time record revenue of $479 billion and double-digit EPS growth. […] We generated $28 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, allowing us to return $28 billion to shareholders. Thanks to our very high levels of customer satisfaction and loyalty, our installed base of active devices reached a new all-time high across all major product categories and geographic segments.”

苹果刚刚发布了 2026 年第四财季财报。该公司公布营收 1145 亿美元，净利润 307.1 亿美元。这是完整的细分。

去年第四财季，苹果公布的营收为 1024.7 亿美元，净利润为 274.7 亿美元，每股收益为 1.85 美元。该公司预计本季度收入将同比增长 9% 至 11%，这意味着收入约为 1,116.9 亿美元和 1,137.4 亿美元。

“今天，苹果自豪地公布 9 月份季度营收达到 1,145 亿美元，同比增长 12%，iPhone 创下 9 月份季度记录，服务业务达到历史新高，为我们有史以来最好的财年画上了圆满的句号。[...] 我们将以迄今为止最雄心勃勃的产品阵容结束这一年。其中包括 iPhone Duo，这是自初代以来最具变革性的 iPhone，以及 iPhone 18 Pro 和 iPhone 18 Pro Max，这是我们迄今为止最强大的 iPhone。我们还刚刚推出了新一代的家庭硬件，并首次将 Touch 与全新的 Siri AI 结合在一起，这是一个令人难以置信的阵容，可以带我们进入假期。”

“Apple 的 9 月份季度净利润和每股收益创下了历史新高。我们创纪录的 9 月份季度为 2026 财年的强劲业绩画上了圆满的句号，收入创历史新高，达到 4790 亿美元，每股收益实现两位数增长。[…]本季度我们产生了 280 亿美元的运营现金流，为股东带来了 280 亿美元的回报。由于我们极高的客户满意度和忠诚度，我们的活跃设备安装量在所有主要产品类别和地理区域都达到了历史新高。”

items.title: Palantir reports Q3 revenue up 96% YoY to $2.31B, above $2.18B est., US commercial revenue up 148% to $984M, and raises FY 2026 revenue guidance to ~$8.53B (Samantha Subin/CNBC)
items.title_en: Palantir reports Q3 revenue up 96% YoY to $2.31B, above $2.18B est., US commercial revenue up 148% to $984M, and raises FY 2026 revenue guidance to ~$8.53B (Samantha Subin/CNBC)
items.author: CNBC
items.article_content:
Palantir beat Wall Street's third-quarter estimates after the bell on Monday, with U.S. commercial revenue topping government for the first time as businesses adopt more of the company's artificial intelligence tools.

Revenue nearly doubled from a year ago and blew past $2 billion for the first time ever, Palantir said. Net income more than doubled to $1.13 billion, or 44 cents per share, from about $476 million, or 18 cents per share.

"I don't believe anyone's had consistent results like this in the history of software AI, ever," CEO Alex Karp told CNBC's Seema Mody in an interview, adding that the business is succeeding without salespeople.

Palantir has long been known for its strength in the government sector, but its commercial segment caught up in Q3.

U.S. commercial revenue jumped 148% to $984 million, surpassing U.S. government revenue of $953 million, which was up 96%. The company's U.S. commercial revenue has more than quintupled over the last two years.

Palantir lifted its guidance, saying it now expects U.S. commercial revenue "in excess of" $3.56 billion for the full year. Last quarter, the company boosted its forecast to $3.42 billion. The company projects about $2.65 billion in revenue for the fourth quarter and about $8.53 billion for full-year 2026.

Karp has openly supported the use of open-weight models and criticized leading AI labs, which he told CNBC earlier this year are forcing businesses to sell their data sovereignty. Karp, on Monday, also reiterated recent calls to nationalize AI labs, calling it the "only realistic way" to manage liability.

In September, Karp joined major tech CEOs at the White House as calls for regulation mounted following claims from AI researchers that the technology has a more than 10% of killing humanity.

"My message to everybody is: Beware of thinking you can delay the future in AI," he told CNBC. "The future is here. The political ramifications of it are here."

items.title_zh: Palantir三季度营收猛增，AI商业化大爆发
items.summary_zh: Palantir第三季度营收激增至23.1亿美元，美国商业业务营收首次超过政府业务，并大幅上调全年财务指引
items.article_content_zh:
Palantir 周一收盘后第三季度业绩超出了华尔街预期，随着企业更多地采用该公司的人工智能工具，美国商业收入首次超过政府收入。

Palantir 表示，收入比一年前几乎翻了一番，首次突破 20 亿美元。净利润从约 4.76 亿美元（即每股 18 美分）增加了一倍多，达到 11.3 亿美元（即每股 44 美分）。

首席执行官亚历克斯·卡普 (Alex Karp) 在接受 CNBC 的 Seema Mody 采访时表示：“我相信，在软件人工智能的历史上，从来没有人能取得如此一致的结果。”他补充说，即使没有销售人员，公司也能取得成功。

Palantir 长期以来以其在政府领域的实力而闻名，但其商业领域在第三季度迎头赶上。

美国商业收入跃升 148%，达到 9.84 亿美元，超过美国政府收入 9.53 亿美元，后者增长了 96%。过去两年，该公司在美国的商业收入增长了五倍多。

Palantir 上调了预期，表示目前预计全年美国商业收入“超过”35.6 亿美元。上季度，该公司将其预测提高至 34.2 亿美元。该公司预计第四季度收入约为 26.5 亿美元，2026 年全年收入约为 85.3 亿美元。

卡普公开支持使用开放权重模型，并批评领先的人工智能实验室，他在今年早些时候告诉 CNBC，这些实验室正在迫使企业出售其数据主权。卡普周一还重申了最近将人工智能实验室国有化的呼吁，称这是管理责任的“唯一现实的方式”。

今年 9 月，随着人工智能研究人员声称该技术导致人类死亡的比例超过 10%，要求监管的呼声越来越高，卡普加入了白宫各大科技公司首席执行官的行列。

他对 CNBC 表示：“我向所有人传达的信息是：不要认为自己会推迟人工智能的未来。” “未来就在这里。它的政治影响就在这里。”
