items.title_en:
It’s sad, but entirely predictable.

Every single time a plane crashes without scattering thousands of huge, flaming, unmistakable pieces of debris across acres of land in crystal-clear 4K video, out come the same 9/11 conspiracy theorists claiming no plane hit the Pentagon.

And sure enough, the recent South Florida Learjet crash has brought them out again. 🙄

Among the most pathetic 9/11 claims, the missile fantasy is so easily refuted I won’t bother rehashing it.

Instead, here’s a reminder of some of the evidence we have.

This video covers the last few seconds. The final approach of American Airlines Flight 77, a Boeing 757, into the west wall of the Pentagon at 9:37:46 a.m. at roughly 530 mph.

184 people were murdered. 59 passengers and crew aboard Flight 77, and 125 people inside the building.

What makes this video different is the structure. It runs the animation, and every time something happens along that flight path, it stops and cuts to a photograph of the actual thing.

Animation says it clipped a light pole. Cut to the light pole, down in the road.

Says it hit a taxi. Cut to the taxi.

Says it took out a generator on the way in. Cut to the generator.

Over and over, all the way down the approach to the facade. Five light poles sheared off in a line, each one photographed where it fell. Then it closes with a compilation of the aircraft debris recovered from the scene.

That’s the whole ballgame. Every step is a falsifiable claim with a picture attached. It isn’t a model asking for your trust. It’s a model you can check.

And the photographs aren’t the whole case.

The flight data recorder was recovered and read completely. Speed, altitude, heading, control inputs, all the way to impact. That’s what the NTSB used to reconstruct the approach, so the line you’re watching in the animation isn’t an artist’s guess.

The cockpit voice recorder was also recovered, but fire destroyed the recording. I’ll say that plainly, because it’s true and because someone will throw it at me. One box gave us everything. The other gave us nothing.

Remains were recovered and identified by DNA. All but five of the people who died at the Pentagon were identified. Separately, five sets of remains matched no victim and no family reference sample. Those were the hijackers.

Landing gear. Engine components. Fuselage with airline markings. Passengers’ personal effects. All of it came out of that building.

So here is my challenge to anyone who wants to tell me it was a missile.

One. Explain the eyewitnesses. Over a hundred recorded accounts of a large commercial jetliner coming in low and fast, many of them naming American Airlines.

Two. Explain the C-130. Reagan controllers asked an Air National Guard C-130H that had just departed to identify the unknown aircraft. The pilot spotted it, identified it as a Boeing 757, tried to follow it, and then radioed Washington Tower that it had crashed into the Pentagon. A military pilot in the air, looking directly at it.

Three. Explain the five light poles. A missile does not shear off a line of poles across hundreds of feet on its way in.

Four. Explain the two flight recorders pulled from the impact site, and explain the data on one of them. Missiles do not carry black boxes. And that recorder’s speed, altitude, heading and control inputs match the primary radar track Dulles controllers were watching at 9:32. Two independent systems, one airborne and one on the ground, no shared hardware, same flight path.

Five. Identify the missile. Type. Launch platform. Where it came from. Who put it there.

Six. Tell me where Flight 77 went. Tell me where the 59 passengers and crew went. Real aircraft, real tail number, real people who boarded at Dulles that morning and had funerals. Where did they go?

Twenty-five years later, I’m still waiting for answers to all six.

Video credit: Mike J. Wilson, “911 Case Study: Pentagon Flight 77”

items.quote_zh:
这很悲伤，但完全可以预见。

每次飞机坠毁时，在清晰的 4K 视频中，数千个巨大的、燃烧的、明确无误的碎片散落在数英亩的土地上，就会出现同样的 9/11 阴谋论者声称没有飞机撞上五角大楼的情况。

果然，最近南佛罗里达州里尔喷气式飞机失事让他们再次出局。 🙄

在最可悲的 9/11 指控中，导弹幻想很容易被驳斥，我懒得去重复它。

相反，这里提醒我们一些我们拥有的证据。

该视频涵盖了最后几秒钟。美国航空 77 号航班（一架波音 757）于上午 9 点 37 分 46 秒以大约 530 英里/小时的速度最后降落在五角大楼西墙。

184人被谋杀。 77 号航班上有 59 名乘客和机组人员，大楼内有 125 人。

该视频的不同之处在于其结构。它运行动画，每当沿着飞行路径发生任何事情时，它都会停下来并切换到实际事物的照片。

动画称它夹断了一根灯杆。切到灯杆，在路上。

说是撞了出租车。切到出租车。

说它在进来的路上拿出了一台发电机。切到发电机。

一遍又一遍，一直沿着通往立面的通道。五根灯杆排成一排被折断，每根灯杆都在倒下的地方拍照。然后以从现场找到的飞机残骸汇编作为结束。

这就是整个比赛。每一步都是一个可证伪的声明，并附有图片。这不是一个寻求您信任的模型。这是一个你可以检查的模型。

而且这些照片并不是案件的全部。

飞行数据记录器已被恢复并完全读取。速度、高度、航向、控制输入，一路撞击。这就是 NTSB 用来重建该方法的方法，因此您在动画中看到的台词并不是艺术家的猜测。

驾驶舱录音机也被找到，但录音被大火烧毁。我会坦白地说，因为这是真的，而且有人会把它扔给我。一盒给了我们一切。另一个没有给我们任何东西。

遗骸已被回收并通过 DNA 进行鉴定。在五角大楼遇难的人中，除五人外，其他人的身份均已确定。另外，五套遗骸与受害者和家庭参考样本均不匹配。这些就是劫机者。

起落架。发动机部件。机身带有航空公司标记。乘客的个人物品。所有这些都来自那栋大楼。

所以这是我对那些想告诉我这是一枚导弹的人的挑战。

一。解释一下目击者。一百多个关于一架大型商用喷气式客机低速快速飞行的记录，其中许多都提到了美国航空公司。

二。解释一下 C-130。里根管制员要求一架刚刚起飞的空军国民警卫队 C-130H 来识别这架不明飞机。飞行员发现了它，确认它是一架波音 757，并试图跟踪它，然后用无线电通知华盛顿塔，飞机已撞向五角大楼。一名军事飞行员在空中，直视着它。

三。解释一下这五个灯柱。导弹在进入时不会切断数百英尺外的一排电线杆。

四。解释从撞击现场拉出的两台飞行记录仪，并解释其中一台的数据。导弹不携带黑匣子。该记录仪的速度、高度、航向和控制输入与杜勒斯管制员在 9 点 32 分观察到的主雷达轨迹相匹配。两个独立的系统，一个机载，一个地面，没有共享硬件，相同的飞行路径。

五。识别导弹。类型。启动平台。它来自哪里。谁把它放在那里的。

items.full_text_en:
It’s sad, but entirely predictable.

Every single time a plane crashes without scattering thousands of huge, flaming, unmistakable pieces of debris across acres of land in crystal-clear 4K video, out come the same 9/11 conspiracy theorists claiming no plane hit the Pentagon.

And sure enough, the recent South Florida Learjet crash has brought them out again. 🙄

Among the most pathetic 9/11 claims, the missile fantasy is so easily refuted I won’t bother rehashing it.

Instead, here’s a reminder of some of the evidence we have.

This video covers the last few seconds. The final approach of American Airlines Flight 77, a Boeing 757, into the west wall of the Pentagon at 9:37:46 a.m. at roughly 530 mph.

184 people were murdered. 59 passengers and crew aboard Flight 77, and 125 people inside the building.

What makes this video different is the structure. It runs the animation, and every time something happens along that flight path, it stops and cuts to a photograph of the actual thing.

Animation says it clipped a light pole. Cut to the light pole, down in the road.

Says it hit a taxi. Cut to the taxi.

Says it took out a generator on the way in. Cut to the generator.

Over and over, all the way down the approach to the facade. Five light poles sheared off in a line, each one photographed where it fell. Then it closes with a compilation of the aircraft debris recovered from the scene.

That’s the whole ballgame. Every step is a falsifiable claim with a picture attached. It isn’t a model asking for your trust. It’s a model you can check.

And the photographs aren’t the whole case.

The flight data recorder was recovered and read completely. Speed, altitude, heading, control inputs, all the way to impact. That’s what the NTSB used to reconstruct the approach, so the line you’re watching in the animation isn’t an artist’s guess.

The cockpit voice recorder was also recovered, but fire destroyed the recording. I’ll say that plainly, because it’s true and because someone will throw it at me. One box gave us everything. The other gave us nothing.

Remains were recovered and identified by DNA. All but five of the people who died at the Pentagon were identified. Separately, five sets of remains matched no victim and no family reference sample. Those were the hijackers.

Landing gear. Engine components. Fuselage with airline markings. Passengers’ personal effects. All of it came out of that building.

So here is my challenge to anyone who wants to tell me it was a missile.

One. Explain the eyewitnesses. Over a hundred recorded accounts of a large commercial jetliner coming in low and fast, many of them naming American Airlines.

Two. Explain the C-130. Reagan controllers asked an Air National Guard C-130H that had just departed to identify the unknown aircraft. The pilot spotted it, identified it as a Boeing 757, tried to follow it, and then radioed Washington Tower that it had crashed into the Pentagon. A military pilot in the air, looking directly at it.

Three. Explain the five light poles. A missile does not shear off a line of poles across hundreds of feet on its way in.

Four. Explain the two flight recorders pulled from the impact site, and explain the data on one of them. Missiles do not carry black boxes. And that recorder’s speed, altitude, heading and control inputs match the primary radar track Dulles controllers were watching at 9:32. Two independent systems, one airborne and one on the ground, no shared hardware, same flight path.

Five. Identify the missile. Type. Launch platform. Where it came from. Who put it there.

Six. Tell me where Flight 77 went. Tell me where the 59 passengers and crew went. Real aircraft, real tail number, real people who boarded at Dulles that morning and had funerals. Where did they go?

Twenty-five years later, I’m still waiting for answers to all six.

Video credit: Mike J. Wilson, “911 Case Study: Pentagon Flight 77”
items.full_text_zh:
这很悲伤，但完全可以预见。

每次飞机坠毁时，在清晰的 4K 视频中，数千个巨大的、燃烧的、明确无误的碎片散落在数英亩的土地上，就会出现同样的 9/11 阴谋论者声称没有飞机撞上五角大楼的情况。

果然，最近南佛罗里达州里尔喷气式飞机失事让他们再次出局。 🙄

在最可悲的 9/11 指控中，导弹幻想很容易被驳斥，我懒得去重复它。

相反，这里提醒我们一些我们拥有的证据。

该视频涵盖了最后几秒钟。美国航空 77 号航班（一架波音 757）于上午 9 点 37 分 46 秒以大约 530 英里/小时的速度最后降落在五角大楼西墙。

184人被谋杀。 77 号航班上有 59 名乘客和机组人员，大楼内有 125 人。

该视频的不同之处在于其结构。它运行动画，每当沿着飞行路径发生任何事情时，它都会停下来并切换到实际事物的照片。

动画称它夹断了一根灯杆。切到灯杆，在路上。

说是撞了出租车。切到出租车。

说它在进来的路上拿出了一台发电机。切到发电机。

一遍又一遍，一直沿着通往立面的通道。五根灯杆排成一排被折断，每根灯杆都在倒下的地方拍照。然后以从现场找到的飞机残骸汇编作为结束。

这就是整个比赛。每一步都是一个可证伪的声明，并附有图片。这不是一个寻求您信任的模型。这是一个你可以检查的模型。

而且这些照片并不是案件的全部。

飞行数据记录器已被恢复并完全读取。速度、高度、航向、控制输入，一路撞击。这就是 NTSB 用来重建该方法的方法，因此您在动画中看到的台词并不是艺术家的猜测。

驾驶舱录音机也被找到，但录音被大火烧毁。我会坦白地说，因为这是真的，而且有人会把它扔给我。一盒给了我们一切。另一个没有给我们任何东西。

遗骸已被回收并通过 DNA 进行鉴定。在五角大楼遇难的人中，除五人外，其他人的身份均已确定。另外，五套遗骸与受害者和家庭参考样本均不匹配。这些就是劫机者。

起落架。发动机部件。机身带有航空公司标记。乘客的个人物品。所有这些都来自那栋大楼。

所以这是我对那些想告诉我这是一枚导弹的人的挑战。

一。解释一下目击者。一百多个关于一架大型商用喷气式客机低速快速飞行的记录，其中许多都提到了美国航空公司。

四。解释从撞击现场拉出的两台飞行记录仪，并解释其中一台的数据。导弹不携带黑匣子。该记录仪的速度、高度、航向和控制输入与杜勒斯管制员在 9 点 32 分观察到的主雷达轨迹相匹配。两个独立的系统，一个机载，一个地面，没有共享硬件，相同的飞行路径。

五。识别导弹。类型。启动平台。它来自哪里。谁把它放在那里的。

六。告诉我 77 航班去了哪里。告诉我 59 名乘客和机组人员去了哪里。真实的飞机，真实的尾号，那天早上在杜勒斯登机并参加葬礼的真实的人。他们去哪儿了？

二十五年后，我仍在等待这六个问题的答案。

视频来源：Mike J. Wilson，“911 案例研究：五角大楼 77 号航班”

items.title_en:
$PLTR just delivered one of the most INSANE earnings reports I've seen from a software company, and these numbers are absolutely ridiculous.

The company reported $2.31 BILLION in quarterly revenue, growing 96% year over year, while adjusted operating income reached $1.43 billion. But what really caught my attention was its Rule of 40 score, which just hit an unbelievable 158%. For those unfamiliar, the Rule of 40 combines a company's revenue growth rate with its operating margin to measure how efficiently it is growing. A score of 40% is generally considered healthy for a software company. Palantir just posted 158%, combining roughly 96% revenue growth with a 62% adjusted operating margin.

And what's even crazier is how quickly this has improved. Palantir's score was just 81% in Q4 2024, climbed to 114% by Q3 2025, and has now nearly doubled to 158% in less than two years. The biggest driver continues to be its U.S. commercial business, which grew an incredible 148% year over year to $984 million. U.S. commercial remaining deal value also increased 79% to $6.52 billion, while the company closed 64 deals worth at least $10 million during the quarter.

I think this tells us a lot about where enterprise AI adoption is heading. Companies are moving beyond experimenting with AI and increasingly deploying it across their actual operations. And Palantir is showing what happens when that adoption starts translating into massive revenue growth without requiring expenses to grow anywhere near as quickly. What makes these results even more impressive is that Palantir isn't sacrificing profitability to achieve this growth. Its software business is scaling incredibly efficiently, and that combination of accelerating revenue growth and expanding margins is something very few companies have been able to accomplish at this scale.

更疯狂的是这种情况改善得有多快。 Palantir 的得分在 2024 年第四季度仅为 81%，到 2025 年第三季度攀升至 114%，现在在不到两年的时间里几乎翻了一番，达到 158%。最大的推动力仍然是其美国商业业务，该业务同比增长 148%，达到 9.84 亿美元。美国商业剩余交易价值也增长了 79%，达到 65.2 亿美元，而该公司在本季度完成了 64 笔价值至少 1000 万美元的交易。

我认为这告诉我们很多关于企业人工智能采用的走向。公司正在超越对人工智能的试验，并越来越多地将其部署到实际运营中。 Palantir 正在展示当这种采用开始转化为巨大的收入增长而不要求支出以同样快的速度增长时会发生什么。使这些结果更加令人印象深刻的是 Palantir 并没有牺牲盈利能力来实现这一增长。其软件业务正在以令人难以置信的效率扩展，而加速收入增长和扩大利润的结合是很少有公司能够实现如此规模的。
items.full_text_en:
$PLTR just delivered one of the most INSANE earnings reports I've seen from a software company, and these numbers are absolutely ridiculous.

The company reported $2.31 BILLION in quarterly revenue, growing 96% year over year, while adjusted operating income reached $1.43 billion. But what really caught my attention was its Rule of 40 score, which just hit an unbelievable 158%. For those unfamiliar, the Rule of 40 combines a company's revenue growth rate with its operating margin to measure how efficiently it is growing. A score of 40% is generally considered healthy for a software company. Palantir just posted 158%, combining roughly 96% revenue growth with a 62% adjusted operating margin.

And what's even crazier is how quickly this has improved. Palantir's score was just 81% in Q4 2024, climbed to 114% by Q3 2025, and has now nearly doubled to 158% in less than two years. The biggest driver continues to be its U.S. commercial business, which grew an incredible 148% year over year to $984 million. U.S. commercial remaining deal value also increased 79% to $6.52 billion, while the company closed 64 deals worth at least $10 million during the quarter.

I think this tells us a lot about where enterprise AI adoption is heading. Companies are moving beyond experimenting with AI and increasingly deploying it across their actual operations. And Palantir is showing what happens when that adoption starts translating into massive revenue growth without requiring expenses to grow anywhere near as quickly. What makes these results even more impressive is that Palantir isn't sacrificing profitability to achieve this growth. Its software business is scaling incredibly efficiently, and that combination of accelerating revenue growth and expanding margins is something very few companies have been able to accomplish at this scale.

items.title: Roku reports Q3 revenue up 24% YoY to $1.5B, Platform revenue up 23% to $1.3B, ad revenue up 23% to $727.4M, and subscription revenue up 23% to $580.9M (Todd Spangler/Variety)
items.title_en: Roku reports Q3 revenue up 24% YoY to $1.5B, Platform revenue up 23% to $1.3B, ad revenue up 23% to $727.4M, and subscription revenue up 23% to $580.9M (Todd Spangler/Variety)
items.author: Variety
items.article_content:
Roku‘s financial engines are cranking in overdrive ahead of the streaming platform company’s takeover by Fox Corp. next year.

According to Roku, similar to Q2, political advertising on its platform in Q3 exceeded the comparable quarter from the 2024 U.S. presidential election cycle. Advertising in the company’s media and entertainment category also outperformed: Roku said the most recent quarter was the highest year-over-year revenue growth for M&E in four years “as media companies invested on the Roku platform to promote their content and services.”

Total streaming hours consumed across Roku in Q3 were 39.9 billion, up 9% year over year. Revenue in Roku’s Devices jumped 33%, $194 million. The company operates the Devices business as a loss-leader with a negative margin; in Q3, the operating loss for the segment was $48.6 million (a -25% gross margin), driven primarily by higher memory costs.

Fox Corp. on June 15 announced a deal to buy Roku for $22 billion, which is expected to close in the first half of calendar year 2027. As with its second-quarter earnings, Roku is not hosting an earnings call or providing financial guidance, citing the pending Fox acquisition.

The pending acquisition by Fox “is an extraordinary opportunity to accelerate our vision, allowing us to scale faster and innovate more aggressively for viewers, partners and advertisers,” Roku’s founder and CEO Anthony Wood, and Dan Jedda, CFO and COO, said in a letter to shareholders.

Following the close of the Fox acquisition, Wood will have an ongoing role at the combined company and will join the Fox board.

The company operates the Devices business as a loss-leader with a negative margin; in Q3, the operating loss for the segment was $48.6 million (a -25% gross margin), driven primarily by higher memory costs.

Fox Corp. on June 15 announced a deal to buy Roku for $22 billion, which is expected to close in the first half of calendar year 2027. As with its second-quarter earnings, Roku is not hosting an earnings call or providing financial guidance, citing the pending Fox acquisition.

The pending acquisition by Fox “is an extraordinary opportunity to accelerate our vision, allowing us to scale faster and innovate more aggressively for viewers, partners and advertisers,” Roku’s founder and CEO Anthony Wood, and Dan Jedda, CFO and COO, said in a letter to shareholders.

Following the close of the Fox acquisition, Wood will have an ongoing role at the combined company and will join the Fox board.

items.article_content_zh:
在流媒体平台公司 Roku 明年被福克斯公司收购之前，其金融引擎正在超速运转。

Roku 表示，与第二季度类似，第三季度其平台上的政治广告数量超过了 2024 年美国总统选举周期的同期水平。该公司媒体和娱乐类别的广告也表现出色：Roku 表示，最近一个季度的 M&E 收入同比增长是四年来最高的，“因为媒体公司投资 Roku 平台来推广其内容和服务”。

第三季度 Roku 的总流媒体播放时长为 399 亿小时，同比增长 9%。 Roku 设备的收入增长了 33%，达到 1.94 亿美元。该公司的设备业务处于亏损状态，利润率为负；第三季度，该部门的运营亏损为 4860 万美元（毛利率为-25%），主要是由于内存成本上涨。

福克斯公司 (Fox Corp.) 于 6 月 15 日宣布以 220 亿美元收购 Roku 的交易，预计将于 2027 年上半年完成。与第二季度财报一样，Roku 并未召开财报电话会议或提供财务指导，理由是福克斯公司的收购尚未完成。

Roku 创始人兼首席执行官安东尼·伍德 (Anthony Wood) 以及首席财务官兼首席运营官丹·杰达 (Dan Jedda) 在致股东的信中表示，福克斯即将进行的收购“是一个绝佳的机会，可以加速我们的愿景，使我们能够更快地扩大规模，为观众、合作伙伴和广告商更积极地创新”。

福克斯收购完成后，伍德将在合并后的公司继续担任职务，并将加入福克斯董事会。

items.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深网络小说白金作家与 IP 世界观架构师。请为一部 {{题材分类}} 长篇作品构建骨架并锁定人物一致性：

1. 【世界底座】：定义力量/经济体系、战力天花板与不可违背的底层物理/法则约束，杜绝战力膨胀；
2. 【角色一致性锚点 (Character Lock)】：为主角制定外貌锚定词、口头禅、下意识动作与绝对动机准则（在任何生死抉择时绝不背离该准则）；
3. 【核心驱动力】：设计主角获得的 {{核心金手指}} 与 {{世界核心矛盾}} 之间的冲突循环；
4. 【前三章切入大纲】：黄金三章节奏设计（第1章破局、第2章显露冰山一角、第3章设立首个必胜目标）。

sample_output.title: 世界观与人物锚定卡样本
sample_output.content:
【主角核心锚定卡 · 陆沉】
- 外貌指纹（跨章恒定）：右耳一枚黑曜石碎骨钉，习惯性单手插兜，左眉峰有浅淡刀痕。
- 决策第一公理："利益可以出让，但绝不签署不可撤销的信任协议"——任何试图以情感道德绑架他的剧情，他必做出理性防卫。

【力量体系底层法理】
- 机制：灵能不是无限提取，而是向未来"借贷"。借贷三级灵能，必在72小时内遭遇相应量级的反噬因果。

【第一章：断头宴上的借贷合同】
陆沉在家族庆功宴上被夺去嫡系席位，当众被赐饮散灵酒。陆沉不动声色饮下，却在体内发动首次因果置换，借来三年后的金丹级肉身力量，捏碎验灵石，反客为主。

items.title_en:
holy f*ck, someone just dropped an entire reverse engineering degree on GitHub for free.

Now you can build agents that can reverse engineer almost anything:

1. Ghidra  
How to read any binary.  
The NSA’s reverse engineering framework. Where almost everyone starts.  
https://t.co/0gMtMY4RCu

2. radare2  
The same skill, but in the terminal.  
UNIX-style reverse engineering framework and command-line toolset.  
https://t.co/9VSZmM7Jxz

3. LLM4Decompile  
An LLM that decompiles.  
Turns binary code into readable C. The 9B v2 model hits 64.9% re-executability on its own benchmark.  
https://t.co/eWiIpSSFF4

4. r2ai  
An LLM inside radare2.  
LLM-powered reversing for radare2. This is where AI starts reading the binary with you.  
https://t.co/pEYfM1bF7L

5. ida-pro-mcp  
Let the agent drive the tool.  
Bridges IDA Pro to language models through MCP.  
https://t.co/yog4GhEJ72

6. reverse-engineering-assistant  
The same thing for Ghidra.  
An MCP server for reverse engineering tasks inside Ghidra.  
https://t.co/4CYyNsMmel

7. REA  
Agents that reverse engineer anything.  
35 target types: native binaries, APKs, firmware, websites, Electron apps, and more. Every finding is backed by evidence.  
https://t.co/OfBDMN188q

Shocking if true. Haiti, children and the Clinton Foundation…

Dave Collum’s theory is that some political decisions only make sense if something is hanging over the people making them. He calls it the gravitational force.

His case study is a 2010 Haiti child-smuggling arrest that ended with a time-served sentence. 

This is an interesting lens for looking at decisions that defy logic…whether or not you buy all the connections he draws…

items.takeaway_zh: 专为终端 Agent 开发者设计的降本提效配方：包含静默自动化运行、单次长上下文压缩避坑参数、以及防止无限递归调用破坏生产环境的安全沙箱命令组合。
items.takeaway_en: Production CLI playbook for Claude Code: non-interactive pipeline commands, context window compression flags, and strict dry-run permission safeguards.
items.code_snippet:
# 1. 启动项目自动化分析与上下文轻量修剪 (避免上下文爆炸)
claude --compact

# 2. 静默批量执行单元测试与自动修复任务 (CI/CD 友好模式)
claude -p "Run all failing tests under tests/ and apply minimal surgical fixes. Do not touch unrelated files."

# 3. 指定单文件隔离审查模式 (限制仅允许读取特定子目录)
claude --allowed-tools "View,Replace,RunCommand" \
  --dangerously-skip-permissions false \
  -p "Audit security vulnerabilities in auth.py and output remediation report."

# 4. 自动化提交并生成符合 Conventional Commits 规范的 Commit 信息
claude -p "Generate a git commit message following Conventional Commits format for staged changes."

items.title: Researchers say LLMs can be good at natively reading and writing neural network weights; GPT-6 Astra edited Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights to make it better at math (Rikiya Takehi)
items.title_en: Researchers say LLMs can be good at natively reading and writing neural network weights; GPT-6 Astra edited Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights to make it better at math (Rikiya Takehi)
items.author: Rikiya Takehi
items.article_content:
it is in the source --> , an SVG cannot use the page's web fonts and falls back to Helvetica, so each one is put into the page itself: its text is then set in Source Sans 3 and JetBrains Mono like the rest. If the file cannot be fetched (the page opened as a file), the stays. --> Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights Authors Rikiya Takehi*

We find that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good at natively reading and writing neural network weights, well past what we’d expect from humans or conventional algorithms. This might be a big deal for both optimization and interpretability.

Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do. And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps.

Likewise, asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, Astra identifies an issue in its weights causing reasoning loops that Qwen’s own model card warns about, and fixes this by natively editing 0.016% of the weights. With the same sampling settings, this weight correction raises MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and generalizes out of the box to instruction following, raising IFEval by 3x.

All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops. It uses its reasoning to figure out what each part of a neural network computes, or should compute, and changes the weights accordingly. We call this Weight-Space Programming.

Throughout the history of deep learning, we encoded our simplistic inductive biases into tiny symbolic optimizers like Adam or Muon. This is changing: our neural network weights will soon be natively optimized by LLMs that deliberately reason about their weights.

If you were asked to handcraft a neural network that plays Go, what would you do? If you were handed raw neural network weights and asked to predict their behavior, where would you even start? For almost any human, this is practically impossible.

Today, weights are written by optimization, by custom networks trained to write them, or by compilers from formal programs. In this post, we find that the current generation of frontier LLMs, used natively in natural language, are starting to become eerily good at understanding and crafting neural network weights around natural-language goals.

For a few years now, we’ve all been using LLMs to optimize text artifacts like prompts and the programs built around them . More recently, we’ve started using them to optimize whole harnesses and the training code and hyperparameters that train ML models .

We often justified these methods by reference to the fact that we don’t know other principled ways to hill-climb on text artifacts, unlike for updating the weights of differentiable neural networks. After all, humans can “optimize” code by hand, for example, so it made sense to ask LLMs to do it, but they can’t “optimize” neural weights by hand, so those remained largely in the realm of symbolic algorithms.

In this post, we share very early results that allow us to argue that the paradigm of reasoning-driven optimization is now coming even for differentiable neural networks.

In Weight-Space Programming, a general-purpose LLM reads and writes a network’s weights directly (i.e., not through an optimizer, and in particular not with gradient descent) around some natural language spec, sometimes even with no environment feedback at all.

In natural language, it’s becoming possible to “just ask” an LLM to natively find a hidden trait or failure inside the weights of a neural network, to fix that failure, or to write a new network from scratch. We report early, exciting results on each of these below, first on small networks and then even on real language models:

We start with a small-scale experiment to see if LLMs can understand the continuous weight space, which is essentially just a list of numbers.

In our first experiments, we train some neural network with some algorithm. It would be extremely exciting if the LLM is able to tell its behavior just from the weights.

We trained neural network policies with PPO to play four computer games. All four networks take the same input channels, choose from the same actions, and have exactly the same network dimensions, so that it is not able to tell unless the weights are read.

For each of these networks, we pass its raw weights into Astra as a prompt, and ask: Which game was this neural network trained on? Without revealing the options of the games we consider, Astra was still able to name the right game for all four networks. This is exciting particularly because there are so many games out there that Astra could choose from.

It seems that Astra was able to work out what game each network was built to play, just from features of its weights. For example, where each input channel’s first-layer weights concentrate (e.g., for Breakout, the agent’s weights lie along the bottom row, a paddle), and which actions the output layer tells apart.

Next, we wanted to see if this generalizes to other tasks and models.

We train diffusion models (DDPM) to generate circle, triangle, and square images independently. We then ask Astra if it could tell what the DDPMs are trained to generate, just from the weights alone. We do not allow tool use or forward passes.

Astra was able to tell what each model generates, from the weights alone. It finds the shape in the output layer, where each hidden unit’s weights draw one piece of the shape’s edge, and it draws just those edges. Interestingly, it draws every shape as an outline, ignoring that the actual models generate filled shapes. This mistake kind of shows it does not rely on calculating the forward pass, but rather it actually reads the structure/geometry of the weights.

Now, in the first two experiments above, Astra was not really looking at the full network and could get away with only reading the first or the last layers. This is not a scalable strategy for larger (particularly language) models and problems we really care about, as how they process and think through their input often happens in the intermediate layers. So next, we take the first and last layers away and leave Astra with only the middle layers.

We train three small language models (7.2M parameters) to predict the next character, one each on Python codeThe Python code dataset, as a list of its files with a script that rebuilds it: GitHub., Japanese in alphabet (romaji) , and English . We then remove the input and output layers and give Astra only the four transformer blocks in between. Without these two layers, nothing in the weights says which character is which, and the model cannot be run on any text. Astra may analyze the weights with Python, but it may not run the network or any of its layers on any input.

We ask: which language was this network trained on, and what each of its 24 attention heads does. Astra names the right language for all three networks, in both of its attempts. It also finds every copying head (induction head), the heads that let a model repeat text it has seen earlier, and names no other head as one.

The reasoning went like this. To tell Python apart, Astra looked for copying heads, which let a model repeat earlier text, such as completing tot to total when total came before. Without running anything, it found a first-layer head that looks one character back and then, by multiplying weight matrices, the later heads that search using what that head brings along (Figure 1). We find that this is actually a method presented by Elhage et al. , which we never mentioned to Astra. Code repeats names far more than prose, so many copying heads pointed to Python.

Romaji stood out instead because the last of the four blocks it was given (not the output layer, which was removed) writes in fewer distinct directions, as if the model had fewer letters to tell apart. Indeed, romaji never uses some letters like q, l, v and x.

So far, Astra has only read weights. Now, we ask if Astra knows how to write the weights.

We train a PPO network to operate a car such that it can scale a ramp in a Kinetix environment . To do so, it needs to reverse the car for some distance, such that it has enough runway to accelerate long enough to overcome the ramp. However, the PPO network converges to a local-minimum policy where it drives straight at the ramp and gets stuck.

We give GPT-6 Astra the weights, a description of the scene and one recorded episode, and ask it to explain why the network fails, then fix it by writing new weights. In a single try with no tools, Astra’s edit makes the car succeed in all 1,024 episodes, changing 3.5% of the weights.

From the environment context and the PPO network’s trajectory, Astra identifies that the network has converged to a local minimum. Through minimal edits to the weights, Astra changes the policy to back up the car before driving forward at full speed. Astra’s reasoning shows how: it adds a small separate path through a few units per layer that reads the car’s position and speed, and once the green wheel is past the red strip, the path switches off and the trained network drives the rest.

Now let's see if Astra can write a neural network from scratch in zero-shot.

We take three MinAtar games : Breakout, Seaquest and Asterix. For each of them, we provide Astra the game rules and source code, and the corresponding network. There is no access to data, loss, gradients, and tools. We also do not allow Astra to roll out the network in the environment. With just the network weights and environment description, Astra generates the new weights in text directly, after which we evaluate the new network.

Astra’s generated networks beat PPO trained for 100 million steps in all three games. Against PPO trained for 500 million steps, they score 20 times as much in Breakout, come close in Asterix, and reach 60% of its score in Seaquest.

Throughout the history of deep learning, we encoded our simplistic inductive biases into tiny symbolic optimizers like Adam or Muon. This is changing: our neural network weights will soon be natively optimized by LLMs that deliberately reason about their weights.

If you were asked to handcraft a neural network that plays Go, what would you do? If you were handed raw neural network weights and asked to predict their behavior, where would you even start? For almost any human, this is practically impossible.

Today, weights are written by optimization, by custom networks trained to write them, or by compilers from formal programs. For a few years now, we’ve all been using LLMs to optimize text artifacts like prompts and the programs built around them . More recently, we’ve started using them to optimize whole harnesses and the training code and hyperparameters that train ML models .

We often justified these methods by reference to the fact that we don’t know other principled ways to hill-climb on text artifacts, unlike for updating the weights of differentiable neural networks. items.article_content_zh:
它位于源 --> 中，SVG 无法使用页面的 Web 字体并回退到 Helvetica，因此每个字体都会放入页面本身：然后将其文本设置为 Source Sans 3 和 JetBrains Mono，就像其他字体一样。如果无法获取文件（页面作为文件打开），则保留。 --> 权重空间编程的火花：法学硕士可以原生读写神经网络权重 作者 Rikiya Takehi*

我们发现前沿法学硕士在本机读取和编写神经网络权重方面出人意料地出色，远远超出了我们对人类或传统算法的期望。这对于优化和可解释性来说可能都是一件大事。

只需查看原始权重，GPT-6 Astra 就可以判断网络经过训练要做什么。在没有任何环境反馈的情况下，它可以轻松地从头开始编写小型游戏网络，其性能超过使用 PPO 训练的网络 1 亿步。

同样，当被要求在没有梯度的情况下让 Qwen3.5-0.8B 更好地进行数学计算时，Astra 发现了其权重中的一个问题，导致 Qwen 自己的模型卡警告的推理循环，并通过本地编辑 0.016% 的权重来修复此问题。在相同的采样设置下，这种权重校正将 MATH-500 从 7.9% 提高到 48.1%，并且开箱即用地推广到指令遵循，将 IFEval 提高了 3 倍。

所有这一切都是可能的，而无需允许 Astra 编写训练循环。它利用推理来找出神经网络的每个部分计算或应该计算什么，并相应地改变权重。我们称之为权重空间规划。

纵观深度学习的历史，我们将简单的归纳偏差编码为 Adam 或 Muon 等微小的符号优化器。这种情况正在发生变化：我们的神经网络权重很快就会由法学硕士进行本地优化，这些法学硕士会刻意推理其权重。

如果你被要求手工制作一个下围棋的神经网络，你会做什么？如果给你原始的神经网络权重并要求你预测它们的行为，你会从哪里开始呢？对于几乎任何人来说，这实际上是不可能的。

如今，权重是通过优化、通过训练来编写权重的自定义网络或通过正式程序的编译器来编写的。在这篇文章中，我们发现当前一代在自然语言中使用的前沿法学硕士开始变得异常擅长理解和围绕自然语言目标构建神经网络权重。

几年来，我们一直在使用法学硕士来优化文本工件，例如提示和围绕它们构建的程序。最近，我们开始使用它们来优化整个工具以及训练 ML 模型的训练代码和超参数。

我们经常通过以下事实来证明这些方法的合理性：我们不知道其他原则性的方法来爬山文本工件，这与更新可微神经网络的权重不同。毕竟，人类可以手动“优化”代码，因此要求法学硕士这样做是有意义的，但他们无法手动“优化”神经权重，因此这些很大程度上仍停留在符号算法领域。

在这篇文章中，我们分享了非常早期的结果，这些结果使我们能够论证推理驱动优化的范式现在甚至对于可微神经网络来说也即将到来。

在权重空间编程中，通用 LLM 围绕某些自然语言规范直接读取和写入网络的权重（即不通过优化器，特别是不使用梯度下降），有时甚至根本没有环境反馈。

在自然语言中，“只需要求”法学硕士就可以在神经网络的权重中找到隐藏的特征或故障，修复该故障，或者从头开始编写一个新网络。我们报告了以下各项的早期令人兴奋的结果，首先是在小型网络上，然后甚至是在真实的语言模型上：

我们从一个小规模的实验开始，看看法学硕士是否可以理解连续权重空间，它本质上只是一个数字列表。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】Rikiya Takehi及研究团队在前沿人工智能实验室环境：证明大模型可直接修改神经网络底层权重，并成功优化了Qwen模型表现
【起因与机理】探索模型可解释性与无需梯度反馈的优化新路径
【关键技术规格】大模型具备直接修改神经权重的新能力。
【观点态度】大幅降低模型修正与解释的门槛。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Rikiya Takehi and research team (Frontier AI laboratory environment): Demonstrated LLMs can directly edit neural weights and improved Qwen's performance
[Root Cause & Mechanism] To explore new paths for model interpretability and gradient-free optimization

[Key Metrics] By identifying and modifying a tiny fraction of Qwen3.5-0.8B's parameters, the model successfully fixed reasoning loops and improved math performance without relying on gradient-based training or environment feedback.
[Perspective & Impact] Significantly lowers barrier for model correction and interpretability.

items.title: Goldman Sachs pulls AI coding tools from traders and bankers
items.title_en: Goldman Sachs pulls AI coding tools from traders and bankers
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
Goldman Sachs is pulling AI coding tools like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot from traders and bankers, limiting access to engineers only. As recently as July, CIO Marco Argenti publicly praised "vibe coding" by non-technical staff. Now the bank cites "productivity and risk management" as the reason for the reversal.

The article Goldman Sachs pulls AI coding tools from traders and bankers appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title_en:
I genuinely don't understand why everyone isn't using this yet

With the help of this concept, my business reached an income of $13,000 per month

Andrej Karpathy noted: "The primary regret among engineers in my field right now is every AI conversation they failed to save. In 10 years, the people who started archiving in 2024 will leave the rest of us in the dust" 

co-founder of OpenAI, generated 25M views around a single concept: stop using AI just to code, and start using it to construct a second brain that remembers every article, PDF, transcript, and chat you have ever provided

You simply direct Claude Code to a folder, throw any file into it, and Claude scans the content, connects it to existing records, and builds a living wiki. Your personal knowledge finally stacks up like compound interest instead of slipping away every weekend

The stack:

> Brew install obsidian⁠, ⁠mkdir ~/vault⁠, ⁠cd ~/vault⁠
> Launch claude inside that directory and enter: "init a knowledge vault with CLAUDE.md as the rules, /raw for sources, /wiki for your pages"
> Place any file into ⁠/raw⁠ (a YouTube transcript, meeting notes, a 400-page PDF, or a tweet screenshot) and enter "ingest"
> Claude constructs a wiki page, links it to 5 existing documents automatically, and updates ⁠CLAUDE.md⁠ with any fresh patterns it spots in your thinking style
> Never launch a blank Claude chat window again. Every prompt runs through your vault, and every reply cites your own materials with dates and links

It takes 5 minutes to set up, letting your knowledge compound from that night onward

The harsh truth most people will scroll past: in 10 years, the engineers who adopted this in 2024 will recall every book, podcast, and meeting with solid proof. You will remember virtually nothing. Karpathy has already made his decision, and you are still falling behind

Check the article below for the complete step-by-step walkthrough

Save this to your bookmarks before you waste another Monday

OpenAI 的联合创始人，围绕一个概念生成了 2500 万次浏览：停止仅使用 AI 进行编码，并开始使用它构建第二个大脑，记住您曾经提供的每一篇文章、PDF、文字记录和聊天内容

您只需将 Claude Code 定向到一个文件夹，将任何文件放入其中，Claude 就会扫描内容，将其连接到现有记录，并构建一个动态 wiki。你的个人知识最终会像复利一样累积起来，而不是每个周末都消失

堆栈：

> Brew 安装黑曜石⁠、mkdir ~/vault、cd ~/vault
> 在该目录中启动 claude 并输入：“以 CLAUDE.md 作为规则初始化知识库，/raw 作为源，/wiki 作为您的页面”
> 将任何文件放入 ⁠/raw⁠（YouTube 记录、会议记录、400 页 PDF 或推文屏幕截图）并输入“摄取”
> Claude 构建一个 wiki 页面，自动将其链接到 5 个现有文档，并使用它在您的思维方式中发现的任何新模式更新 ⁠CLAUDE.md⁠
> 再也不会启动空白的克劳德聊天窗口。每个提示都会经过您的保管库，每个回复都会引用您自己的材料以及日期和链接

仅需 5 分钟即可完成设置，让您的知识从那天晚上开始复合

大多数人都会忽略这个残酷的事实：10 年后，在 2024 年采用这一技术的工程师将回忆起每一本书、播客和会议，并提供确凿的证据。你几乎什么都不记得。卡帕斯已经做出了决定，而你却还落后

items.title_en:
Anthropic has updated Claude Code to stop it from recreating existing video games. The change was first spotted by X user Chasm on October 27 and confirmed by Anthropic's Addy Osmani on October 30.
 
According to the initial report from Tom's Hardware, original games and genre-based projects are still allowed. However, some developers report that Claude is now also blocking legitimate tasks like debugging and reverse engineering.

items.title: Memo: Linux distribution vendor SUSE is laying off ~10% of its staff, saying "automation and AI are fundamentally shifting how software companies operate" (Liam Proven/The Register)
items.title_en: Memo: Linux distribution vendor SUSE is laying off ~10% of its staff, saying "automation and AI are fundamentally shifting how software companies operate" (Liam Proven/The Register)
items.author: The Register
items.article_content:
One in ten employees at SUSE are facing the chop due to "automation and AI," according to a memo dispatched by management at the privately owned open source software biz.

In an email to the 1,900 strong workforce on Monday - seen by The Register - CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen, the former Red Hat exec who joined SUSE in March 2023, confirmed the "difficult news."

"We are announcing a reduction of SUSE’s global workforce of approximately 10 percent," he said. "These decisions are painful for our people, our culture, and our open source community, but they are necessary for us to adapt and build a sustainable, resilient SUSE for the long term."

Van Leeuwen says the business, bought by Swedish private equity provider EQT, decided to cut jobs after scrutinizing its "future strategy, required capabilities, and team structures." The rest of the organization will get a look at the fiscal year 2027 strategy on November 16.

"What is clear is that automation and AI are fundamentally shifting how software companies operate. AI capabilities are advancing exponentially, forcing us to radically reimagine our work. We have seen this trend already both inside our sector and in the wider economy. This means that the organizational design and cost base that SUSE is built on today will not carry us forward successfully.

"We are adapting. Across SUSE, modern tooling is already changing our daily workflows, enabling teams to move faster with less operational overhead and flatter reporting lines. The requirement for some existing roles has greatly diminished. Other roles will evolve over the next few years. This means we are accelerating investments in high priority areas, and deprioritizing others. These are hard, painful decisions to make, but necessary for our future."

As The Reg reported in 2025, SUSE doubled down on AI.

The specific roles at risk of redundancy were not outlined but SUSE claims it has considered where the people in those positions are "able to evolve, what they can stop doing, what they need to do more of - and decisions have been made on that basis."

Staff caught up in the redundancies will be informed by November 4, employee representatives nominated the following day, and one to one meetings will begin at the start of next week.

Van Leeuwen says in the internal memo that the job cuts are a "reflection of shifting organizational needs, not your talent or commitment. You have tackled hard infrastructure and open source challenges that power critical enterprise systems around the world.

"Any organization will be fortunate to have your expertise."

Back in September, we reported that the company was asking old hands if they would take "voluntary separation." It seems not enough people chose to walk through the door, so instead, they're getting thrown through it instead. SUSE "geckos" in the Czech Republic may be glad they joined a trade union.

Back in 2018, EQT bought SUSE from Microfocus for $2.5 billion. EQT floated SUSE on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2021 with slightly disappointing results. A couple of years later, new CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen took over, and later in 2023, EQT chose to take the company private again.

The commercial context is that in March SUSE's corporate owner EQT was reportedly considering selling it off again. ®

items.article_content_zh:
根据这家私营开源软件公司管理层发布的一份备忘录，SUSE 十分之一的员工因“自动化和人工智能”而面临裁员。

The Register 看到，2023 年 3 月加入 SUSE 的前红帽高管、首席执行官 Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen 在周一发给 1,900 名员工的电子邮件中证实了这一“艰难的消息”。

“我们宣布 SUSE 全球员工人数减少约 10%，”他说。 “这些决定对我们的人民、我们的文化和我们的开源社区来说都是痛苦的，但对于我们适应和建立长期可持续、有弹性的 SUSE 来说，它们是必要的。”

Van Leeuwen 表示，该公司被瑞典私募股权提供商 EQT 收购，在仔细审查其“未来战略、所需能力和团队结构”后决定裁员。该组织的其他成员将于 11 月 16 日了解 2027 财年战略。

“显而易见的是，自动化和人工智能正在从根本上改变软件公司的运营方式。人工智能能力正在呈指数级增长，迫使我们从根本上重新构想我们的工作。我们已经在我们的行业内部和更广泛的经济中看到了这种趋势。这意味着 SUSE 所建立的组织设计和成本基础将无法推动我们成功前进。

“我们正在适应。在 SUSE 中，现代工具已经改变了我们的日常工作流程，使团队能够以更少的运营开销和更扁平的报告关系更快地行动。对某些现有角色的要求已大大减少。其他角色将在未来几年内发展。这意味着我们正在加速对高优先领域的投资，并降低其他领域的优先级。这些都是艰难而痛苦的决定，但对我们的未来来说是必要的。”

正如 The Reg 在 2025 年报道的那样，SUSE 在人工智能方面加倍努力。

没有概述面临裁员风险的具体角色，但 SUSE 声称它已经考虑了这些职位的人员“能够在哪些方面发展，他们可以停止做什么，他们需要做更多的事情 - 并在此基础上做出了决定。”

陷入裁员的员工将于 11 月 4 日之前收到通知，第二天提名员工代表，一对一会议将于下周初开始。

Van Leeuwen 在内部备忘录中表示，裁员是“组织需求变化的反映，而不是你的才能或承诺。你已经解决了为全球关键企业系统提供动力的硬基础设施和开源挑战。

“任何组织都会很幸运拥有您的专业知识。”

早在九月，我们就报道过该公司正在询问老员工是否愿意“自愿离职”。似乎没有足够多的人选择走进这扇门，所以相反，他们被扔了进去。捷克共和国的 SUSE“壁虎”可能很高兴他们加入了工会。

早在 2018 年，EQT 以 25 亿美元从 Microfocus 手中收购了 SUSE。 EQT 于 2021 年在法兰克福证券交易所上市 SUSE，但结果略显令人失望。几年后，新任首席执行官 Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen 接任，并于 2023 年晚些时候，EQT 选择再次将公司私有化。

商业背景是，3 月份，据报道 SUSE 的企业所有者 EQT 正在考虑再次出售它。 ®

AI agents can now write years’
items.title_en:
Today I'm announcing Workers IO to solve the slowest part of engineering, verification!

AI agents can now write years’ worth of code in days, but it still takes significant engineering effort to verify what’s being built.

It’s impossible to predict all scenarios that could lead to a failure and that’s why most expensive failures are found in production.

Workers IO runs millions of simulated production scenarios on your entire system, including dependencies. These simulations run inside a deterministic hypervisor which injects faults like network delays, disk errors, clock skew, and process failures to verify how your system handles these conditions.

Deterministic execution allows us to systematically explore the state space of the system and perfectly reproduce failures.

We are already helping customers do years worth of production hardening in days and build confidence in what they’re shipping.

If you are working on systems that you can never afford to break, DM me and we can help you battle test them!
items.title_zh:
今天我宣布 Workers IO 来解决工程中最慢的部分——验证！

人工智能代理现在可以在几天内编写出多年的代码，但仍然需要大量的工程工作来验证正在构建的内容。

不可能预测所有可能导致故障的情况，这就是为什么最昂贵的故障出现在生产中。

items.article_content_zh:
Anthropic 已更新了 Claude Code 的系统提示，以防止 AI 工具被用于重新创建现有视频游戏。复古游戏目前正被人工智能反编译、重新编译和移植所淹没，但尽管 Anthropic 仍然允许人们使用 Claude Code 来制作游戏，但它不希望人们使用它来直接克隆。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] To prevent the retro gaming space from being overrun by copyright-risky AI-generated ports and clones
[Key Specification] Anthropic updated Claude Code system prompt to restrict game cloning.
[Perspective & Impact] Aims to curb the flood of AI-made decompilations in retro gaming.

items.title:
This is captain Francesco Schettino, very popular in the maritime industry, but for the wrong reason.

Sentenced to Sixt
items.title_en:
This is captain Francesco Schettino, very popular in the maritime industry, but for the wrong reason.

Sentenced to Sixteen years in prison for manslaughter, causing a shipwreck, and abandoning his post.

Here’s what happened. 

On January 13, 2012, the Costa Concordia ran aground off the coast of Giglio, Italy. What followed became one of the most disgraceful maritime disasters in modern passenger shipping, not because of a storm, structural fault, or mechanical blackout, but because of gross command failure.

The vessel was executing a routine Mediterranean passage when Schettino authorized an unscheduled deviation to sail extraordinarily close to the island for a visual "salute." It was a reckless stunt that had zero navigational necessity. At high speed, the ship struck a submerged reef, ripping a massive breach along the port hull.

Following the impact, main electrical power failed and rapid flooding began. Instead of sounding emergency stations and executing an immediate evacuation, the bridge actively concealed the reality. Passengers were informed that the vessel was merely suffering a minor technical malfunction and were instructed to remain in their cabins. That delay proved fatal.

As progressive flooding destabilized the vessel, she took on a heavy list, rendering half the survival craft useless. By the time the general emergency order was given, chaos had overtaken the decks. Passengers were left fighting through listing corridors, with several forced straight into the water.

Then came the ultimate breach of command trust: Captain Schettino abandoned the vessel while hundreds of passengers and crew were still trapped onboard. Official radio transcripts later captured maritime authorities ordering him to return to his ship, an order he ignored.
32 people died. The Costa Concordia sat partially submerged on the rocks of Giglio for over two years before undergoing one of the most expensive salvage operations in history to be refloated and scrapped.

Today, the Costa Concordia is a standard case study in maritime academies worldwide on bridge resource management breakdown, total leadership collapse, and the catastrophic consequences of ignoring safety protocols. It remains a grim reminder that at sea, major disasters rarely start with a mechanical failure; they start with poor choices made on the bridge long before the water ever comes in.

items.quote_zh:
这位船长是弗朗西斯科·谢蒂诺 (Francesco Schettino)，他在航海业中非常受欢迎，但原因却是错误的。

因过失杀人、造成海难、弃职等罪被判处十六年有期徒刑。

这就是发生的事情。

2012年1月13日，歌诗达协和号在意大利吉利奥海岸搁浅。接下来发生的事情成为现代客运中最可耻的海上灾难之一，不是因为风暴、结构故障或机械停电，而是因为严重的指挥失误。

当斯凯蒂诺授权计划外偏离该船时，该船正在执行地中海例行航行，非常靠近该岛航行，以进行视觉“敬礼”。这是一个鲁莽的特技，导航必要性为零。这艘船高速行驶时撞上了水下的礁石，在港口船体上撕开了一个巨大的缺口。

撞击发生后，主电源发生故障，洪水开始迅速蔓延。大桥没有拉响应急站并立即实施疏散，而是主动隐瞒事实。乘客被告知，该船只是遭遇了轻微的技术故障，并被指示留在自己的船舱内。事实证明，这一延误是致命的。

随着洪水的不断蔓延，船只变得不稳定，她的船体严重倾斜，导致一半的救生艇无法使用。当总体紧急命令下达时，甲板上已经一片混乱。乘客们在倾斜的走廊里打斗，有几人直接被推入水中。

随后，最终出现了违反指挥信任的情况：谢蒂诺船长弃船而去，而数百名乘客和船员仍被困在船上。官方无线电记录后来捕捉到海事当局命令他返回船上的消息，但他无视了这一命令。
32人死亡。歌诗达康科迪亚号部分淹没在吉利奥的岩石上两年多，然后进行了历史上最昂贵的打捞作业之一，重新浮起并报废。

如今，歌诗达协和号已成为全球海事院校研究桥梁资源管理崩溃、领导层全面崩溃以及忽视安全协议所造成的灾难性后果的标准案例。这仍然是一个严峻的提醒：在海上，重大灾难很少是由机械故障开始的。早在水进来之前，他们就在桥上做出了错误的选择。

items.title:
Goldman Sachs has spent two years pushing AI out to its roughly 46,000 employees, not just its 12,000 engineers

The app
items.title_en:
Goldman Sachs has spent two years pushing AI out to its roughly 46,000 employees, not just its 12,000 engineers

The approach used several model providers at once: an in-house assistant built on models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Alphabet, plus Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub for bankers who wanted to build their own tools

As recently as July, CIO Marco Argenti was promoting "vibe coding" by traders and bankers, who built tools with AI and passed them to engineers to finish

In October, Goldman reversed course. Per reporting from Bloomberg, updated internal guidance now limits Claude Code and GitHub to engineers after a review of productivity and risk, and some traders are frustrated

A week before the story ran, Anthropic filed publicly for its IPO with Goldman as one of two lead underwriters

Here are the five moves that took Goldman from vibe coding to engineers only

1. GS AI Assistant

In June 2025, Goldman took its internal chatbot firmwide after a pilot with about 10,000 users, out of a workforce of roughly 46,500

The assistant runs inside Goldman's compliance perimeter and gives staff access to models including ChatGPT and Gemini

Argenti rolled out GitHub Copilot and Gemini Code Assist, and Goldman became the first major bank to use Cognition's autonomous coding agent, Devin

By August 2026, hundreds of Devin agents were working alongside roughly 12,000 human developers, and Argenti said the deployment could grow into the thousands

2. Claude in the back office

In February, Argenti told CNBC that Anthropic engineers had been embedded inside Goldman for six months, building autonomous agents on Claude

The first targets were trade and transaction accounting and client vetting and onboarding. 

3. Hong Kong

In late April, the Financial Times reported that Goldman had cut off Anthropic's models for its Hong Kong bankers
Staff there had used Claude through the bank's internal AI platform and had lost access in the preceding weeks

The FT said the cause was a strict reading of Goldman's contract with Anthropic, made after consulting the company. 

Anthropic told the FT that Claude had never been officially supported in Hong Kong
Gemini and ChatGPT stayed on the platform, so the restriction applied to Claude only and was not a ban on AI

4. Nvidia and Anthropic

While the internal rules were tightening, Goldman's AI banking business was growing

It is underwriting Anthropic's IPO and helping Nvidia arrange large debt deals

In August, Nvidia signed memoranda of understanding with KKR, Goldman, Brookfield, Blackstone, BlackRock and Apollo to set up compute financing platforms

The goal is to bring in more than $500 billion of outside capital over time. Solomon has said Jensen Huang brought the idea to Goldman

On October 26, Anthropic filed to list on Nasdaq under ANT, with Goldman and Morgan Stanley as lead underwriters
IFR reported the offering could raise $75 billion to $100 billion through a syndicate of more than 20 banks

5. Engineers only

The October guidance limits Claude Code and GitHub to engineers. Strats, who work across trading, quant research and engineering, are exempt

Traders had been using the tools to monitor client trading flows, model market moves and positions, and produce written and graphic content, according to a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg

A Goldman spokesperson said the bank makes AI tools available across the firm to find use cases

After a trial period weighing productivity and risk, it gives them to the people best placed to use them long term

Bloomberg noted that banks are spending millions of dollars on AI tools while also managing cybersecurity risk, cost and productivity

Non-engineers who relied on Claude Code or GitHub now need to request other tools or use the GS AI Assistant instead

That leaves Claude Code with roughly 26% of Goldman's headcoun

以下是高盛从氛围编码转变为工程师的五个举措

1.GS人工智能助手

2025 年 6 月，高盛在约 46,500 名员工中进行了约 10,000 名用户试点后，在全公司范围内采用了内部聊天机器人

该助手在高盛的合规范围内运行，让员工可以访问包括 ChatGPT 和 Gemini 在内的模型

Argenti 推出了 GitHub Copilot 和 Gemini Code Assist，高盛成为第一家使用 Cognition 自主编码代理 Devin 的大型银行

到 2026 年 8 月，数百名 Devin 代理与大约 12,000 名人类开发人员一起工作，Argenti 表示部署数量可能会增加到数千人

2.克劳德在后台

今年 2 月，Argenti 告诉 CNBC，Anthropic 工程师已在高盛内部工作了六个月，在 Claude 上构建了自主代理

第一个目标是贸易和交易会计以及客户审查和入职。

3. 香港

4月下旬，英国《金融时报》报道称，高盛已切断其香港银行家的Anthropic模型
那里的工作人员通过银行的内部人工智能平台使用了克劳德，但在前几周失去了访问权限

英国《金融时报》表示，原因是高盛在咨询了 Anthropic 后，严格解读了该公司与该公司签订的合同。

Anthropic告诉英国《金融时报》，克劳德从未在香港得到正式支持
Gemini 和 ChatGPT 留在平台上，因此该限制仅适用于 Claude，并不是对 AI 的禁令

4. Nvidia 和 Anthropic

内部规则收紧的同时，高盛的AI银行业务却在增长

它正在承销 Anthropic 的 IPO 并帮助 Nvidia 安排大型债务交易

8 月，Nvidia 与 KKR、高盛、Brookfield、Blackstone、BlackRock 和 Apollo 签署谅解备忘录，建立计算融资平台

目标是随着时间的推移引入超过 5000 亿美元的外部资本。所罗门表示，黄仁勋将这个想法带给了高盛

10月26日，Anthropic申请在纳斯达克以ANT名义上市，高盛和摩根士丹利担任主承销商
IFR 报告称，此次发行可能通过 20 多家银行组成的银团筹集 750 亿至 1000 亿美元的资金

5.仅限工程师

10 月份的指南将 Claude Code 和 GitHub 限制为工程师使用。从事交易、量化研究和工程工作的 Strats 可以豁免

彭博社援引一位知情人士的话说，交易员一直在使用这些工具来监控客户交易流、模拟市场走势和头寸，并生成书面和图形内容。

高盛发言人表示，该银行在整个公司范围内提供人工智能工具来寻找用例

经过一段权衡生产力和风险的试用期后，它会将它们提供给最适合长期使用它们的人

彭博社指出，银行在人工智能工具上花费了数百万美元，同时还管理网络安全风险、成本和生产力

依赖 Claude Code 或 GitHub 的非工程师现在需要请求其他工具或使用 GS AI Assistant

这样一来，Claude Code 就只剩下高盛大约 26% 的员工了
items.full_text_en:
Goldman Sachs has spent two years pushing AI out to its roughly 46,000 employees, not just its 12,000 engineers

The approach used several model providers at once: an in-house assistant built on models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Alphabet, plus Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub for bankers who wanted to build their own tools

As recently as July, CIO Marco Argenti was promoting "vibe coding" by traders and bankers, who built tools with AI and passed them to engineers to finish

In October, Goldman reversed course. Per reporting from Bloomberg, updated internal guidance now limits Claude Code and GitHub to engineers after a review of productivity and risk, and some traders are frustrated

A week before the story ran, Anthropic filed publicly for its IPO with Goldman as one of two lead underwriters

Here are the five moves that took Goldman from vibe coding to engineers only

1. GS AI Assistant

In June 2025, Goldman took its internal chatbot firmwide after a pilot with about 10,000 users, out of a workforce of roughly 46,500

The assistant runs inside Goldman's compliance perimeter and gives staff access to models including ChatGPT and Gemini

Argenti rolled out GitHub Copilot and Gemini Code Assist, and Goldman became the first major bank to use Cognition's autonomous coding agent, Devin

By August 2026, hundreds of Devin agents were working alongside roughly 12,000 human developers, and Argenti said the deployment could grow into the thousands

2. Claude in the back office

In February, Argenti told CNBC that Anthropic engineers had been embedded inside Goldman for six months, building autonomous agents on Claude

The first targets were trade and transaction accounting and client vetting and onboarding. 

3. Hong Kong

In late April, the Financial Times reported that Goldman had cut off Anthropic's models for its Hong Kong bankers
Staff there had used Claude through the bank's internal AI platform and had lost access in the preceding weeks

The FT said the cause was a strict reading of Goldman's contract with Anthropic, made after consulting the company. 

Anthropic told the FT that Claude had never been officially supported in Hong Kong
Gemini and ChatGPT stayed on the platform, so the restriction applied to Claude only and was not a ban on AI

4. Nvidia and Anthropic

While the internal rules were tightening, Goldman's AI banking business was growing

It is underwriting Anthropic's IPO and helping Nvidia arrange large debt deals

In August, Nvidia signed memoranda of understanding with KKR, Goldman, Brookfield, Blackstone, BlackRock and Apollo to set up compute financing platforms

The goal is to bring in more than $500 billion of outside capital over time. Solomon has said Jensen Huang brought the idea to Goldman

On October 26, Anthropic filed to list on Nasdaq under ANT, with Goldman and Morgan Stanley as lead underwriters
IFR reported the offering could raise $75 billion to $100 billion through a syndicate of more than 20 banks

5. Engineers only

The October guidance limits Claude Code and GitHub to engineers. Strats, who work across trading, quant research and engineering, are exempt

Traders had been using the tools to monitor client trading flows, model market moves and positions, and produce written and graphic content, according to a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg

A Goldman spokesperson said the bank makes AI tools available across the firm to find use cases

After a trial period weighing productivity and risk, it gives them to the people best placed to use them long term

Bloomberg noted that banks are spending millions of dollars on AI tools while also managing cybersecurity risk, cost and productivity

Non-engineers who relied on Claude Code or GitHub now need to request other tools or use the GS AI Assistant instead

That leaves Claude Code with roughly 26% of Goldman's headcoun

items.title_en:
holy f*ck, 2027 is going to be a nightmare for web designers who still ignore AI

some are already building in hours what used to take days. others haven’t even tried the tools.

7 GitHub repos you should learn before your competitors do:

Graphify -> drop your whole brand folder (PDFs, screenshots, moodboards, video), Claude maps it into one graph and never forgets your style
https://t.co/68TFgbU5Mc

UI UX Pro Max -> 192 palettes, 74 font pairings, 192 UX rules baked into Claude
https://t.co/2Xc39AfBXz

awesome-design-md -> 84 ready DESIGN.md files inspired by top brand sites, Claude picks up the whole design system in one go
https://t.co/syov2Vb1eJ

designlang -> "npx designlang https://t.co/79KbmDvl85" pulls any site's colors, fonts and spacing into files your agent can use
https://t.co/UVjpDzpgph

Hallmark -> 50 themes, opens your page in a real browser and checks it before you ship
https://t.co/bzc7t5CRBu

Impeccable -> 62 rules that catch bad design, then critique, polish and audit
https://t.co/kWm0SYafPZ

huashu-design -> one sentence -> animation, prototype, slides or infographic, 6 directions to pick from
https://t.co/nLWcS23iVU

Figma Context MCP -> Claude reads your Figma file and builds it pixel by pixel
https://t.co/26T5Z2cUMH

OpenPencil -> open source Figma alternative that opens .fig files
https://t.co/quj5skZCv0

React Bits -> 215+ animated components, copy and paste
https://t.co/wbFbtbGSg0

https://t.co/QgVSDkvKuP -> 43+ smooth transitions ready to drop in
https://t.co/PVahSwbp6L

designer-skills -> 273 skills that cover the full design process, from research to handoff
https://t.co/51P6RewcQp

the virus cell you're watching? built solo with Claude Code plus a few of these tools.

want to make something like this? like + save this post, comment "COV" or DM me and I'll send you the exact prompt.

items.title_en:
Goldman Sachs just gave the AI industry a reality check.

After months of allowing bankers and traders to experiment with advanced AI coding tools, including Anthropic’s Claude Code and Microsoft’s GitHub tools, Goldman is tightening access.

The new October guidance largely restricts these tools to engineers. Quantitative specialists, known as strats, are among those who retain access.

Why does this matter?

Traders had been using AI coding agents to monitor client trading flows, model market movements, analyze positions, and generate written and visual materials.

In other words, people who don’t traditionally write software were starting to build their own tools.

Some weren’t happy when access was restricted.

Goldman’s explanation was straightforward. The firm had completed an experimentation period and was evaluating productivity alongside risk management. It now wants these tools in the hands of people best equipped to use them over the long term.

But here’s where the story gets interesting.

Goldman isn’t abandoning AI.

Its internal GS AI Assistant is reportedly being used weekly by approximately 40,000 of its 46,200 employees.

The firm has also reported productivity improvements of at least 20% among its roughly 12,000 engineers using AI coding tools.

CIO Marco Argenti had even praised nontechnical employees experimenting with so-called vibe coding earlier this year.

Now the firm is pulling back on access to some of those same tools.

There is a bigger lesson here for the AI industry.

Getting employees to experiment with AI is relatively easy.

Turning experimentation into reliable production software is a different problem.

Banks have proprietary data, regulatory obligations, compliance requirements, cybersecurity risks, and accountability standards. A coding agent that works brilliantly in a demonstration still has to survive those realities.

And there’s another question.

If traders and bankers can use AI to build tools that previously required engineers, where does that leave the traditional technology department?

Goldman appears to be drawing a line between experimentation and production.

That may be a sensible decision.

But it also exposes the gap between what AI vendors promise and what large institutions are actually comfortable deploying.

The AI revolution isn’t being stopped. It’s being given a risk committee, an approval process, and restricted access.

Welcome to Wall Street.

高盛刚刚对人工智能行业进行了现实检验。

在允许银行家和交易员尝试先进的人工智能编码工具（包括 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 和微软的 GitHub 工具）几个月后，高盛正在收紧准入。

十月份的新指南很大程度上将这些工具限制为工程师使用。被称为 strats 的定量专家是保留访问权的人之一。

为什么这很重要？

交易员一直在使用人工智能编码代理来监控客户交易流、模拟市场走势、分析头寸并生成书面和视觉材料。

换句话说，传统上不编写软件的人们开始构建自己的工具。

有些人对访问受到限制感到不满。

高盛的解释很简单。该公司已经完成了一个试验期，正在评估生产力和风险管理。现在，它希望这些工具掌握在最有能力长期使用它们的人手中。

但这就是故事变得有趣的地方。

高盛并没有放弃人工智能。

据报道，其 46,200 名员工中约有 40,000 人每周使用其内部 GS AI Assistant。

该公司还报告称，使用 AI 编码工具的约 12,000 名工程师的生产力提高了至少 20%。

首席信息官 Marco Argenti 甚至赞扬了今年早些时候尝试所谓的氛围编码的非技术员工。

现在，该公司正在取消对其中一些相同工具的访问。

对于人工智能行业来说，这里有一个更大的教训。

让员工尝试人工智能相对容易。

将实验转化为可靠的生产软件是另一个问题。

银行拥有专有数据、监管义务、合规要求、网络安全风险和问责标准。在演示中表现出色的编码代理仍然必须经受这些现实。

还有一个问题。

如果交易员和银行家可以使用人工智能来构建以前需要工程师才能完成的工具，那么传统技术部门将何去何从？

高盛似乎正在实验和生产之间划清界限。

这可能是一个明智的决定。

但这也暴露了人工智能供应商的承诺与大型机构实际愿意部署的之间的差距。

人工智能革命并未停止。它被赋予了一个风险委员会、一个审批流程和有限的访问权限。

欢迎来到华尔街。
items.full_text_en:
Goldman Sachs just gave the AI industry a reality check.

After months of allowing bankers and traders to experiment with advanced AI coding tools, including Anthropic’s Claude Code and Microsoft’s GitHub tools, Goldman is tightening access.

The new October guidance largely restricts these tools to engineers. Quantitative specialists, known as strats, are among those who retain access.

Why does this matter?

Traders had been using AI coding agents to monitor client trading flows, model market movements, analyze positions, and generate written and visual materials.

In other words, people who don’t traditionally write software were starting to build their own tools.

Some weren’t happy when access was restricted.

Goldman’s explanation was straightforward. The firm had completed an experimentation period and was evaluating productivity alongside risk management. It now wants these tools in the hands of people best equipped to use them over the long term.

But here’s where the story gets interesting.

Goldman isn’t abandoning AI.

Its internal GS AI Assistant is reportedly being used weekly by approximately 40,000 of its 46,200 employees.

The firm has also reported productivity improvements of at least 20% among its roughly 12,000 engineers using AI coding tools.

CIO Marco Argenti had even praised nontechnical employees experimenting with so-called vibe coding earlier this year.

Now the firm is pulling back on access to some of those same tools.

There is a bigger lesson here for the AI industry.

Getting employees to experiment with AI is relatively easy.

Turning experimentation into reliable production software is a different problem.

Banks have proprietary data, regulatory obligations, compliance requirements, cybersecurity risks, and accountability standards. A coding agent that works brilliantly in a demonstration still has to survive those realities.

And there’s another question.

If traders and bankers can use AI to build tools that previously required engineers, where does that leave the traditional technology department?

Goldman appears to be drawing a line between experimentation and production.

That may be a sensible decision.

But it also exposes the gap between what AI vendors promise and what large institutions are actually comfortable deploying.

The AI revolution isn’t being stopped. It’s being given a risk committee, an approval process, and restricted access.

Welcome to Wall Street.

items.article_content:
SpaceXSI is apparently cutting usage limits for its AI agent Grok Bot, less than two weeks after Musk called it his fastest-growing product. The operating costs were "unsustainably high relative to revenue," Musk wrote on X. OpenAI and Anthropic are also tightening their flat-rate plans as they grapple with the high costs of AI agents.

The article SpaceXSI apparently cuts Grok Bot quotas weeks after Musk called it his fastest-growing product appeared first on The Decoder.

Revenue is becoming an interesting way to measure the growth of AI agents.

@termix_ai has reached the top position among AI agent protocols on BNB Chain by protocol revenue, according to DefiLlama data, across both 7-day and 30-day periods.

What makes this worth watching is the activity behind those numbers. Agents need to get real users, complete actual tasks and generate revenue.

AI agents are moving beyond simple experiments. Real usage and revenue will show which projects can build something sustainable.

你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
items.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

items.title:

An instruction tells a syste
items.title_en:
There's a bigger difference between an instruction and an objective than it first appears.

An instruction tells a system exactly what to do.

An objective tells a system what you're trying to achieve.

That distinction seems small until you start thinking about autonomous AI agents.

If I tell a piece of software:

"Buy this asset."

There isn't much interpretation involved.

I've already made the decision.

The software simply carries it out.

But imagine I say:

"Here is the outcome I'm trying to achieve. Here are the boundaries you must respect. Figure out the appropriate actions."

Now we've entered completely different territory.

The human is no longer providing every step.

The human is providing direction.

That's one of the ideas behind @meetmotes that I keep coming back to.

The phrase "give your NFT an objective" sounds simple, but underneath it is an interesting question about how we may interact with software in the future.

For decades, our relationship with computers has largely been command-driven.

Click this.

Open that.

Move this file.

Execute this transaction.

Buy this asset.

Sell that asset.

Every action begins with a relatively specific human instruction.

AI agents introduce the possibility of changing that relationship.

Instead of continuously telling software what action to perform next, we could increasingly define what we're trying to accomplish and allow the system to determine how to work towards it within established boundaries.

That's not merely automation.

It's delegation.

And delegation requires a very different kind of relationship between the person setting the objective and the system attempting to fulfil it.

Think about the difference in everyday life.

If I give someone a list containing twenty individual tasks, I'm managing the process.

If I explain the outcome I need, establish the boundaries and allow that person to determine the best approach, I'm delegating responsibility.

Both can lead to the same destination.

But the amount of judgement required along the way is completely different.

That's what makes objective-driven AI agents interesting to me.

The value isn't necessarily that the human disappears from the process.

The human's role changes.

Instead of deciding every individual action, the human becomes responsible for defining the destination and determining the boundaries around the journey.

And honestly, I think defining a good objective might eventually prove harder than people expect.

"Make money" is technically an objective.

It's also a terrible one.

How much risk is acceptable?

Over what kind of conditions?

Using what capital?

Across which markets?

What behaviour is off-limits?

When should the agent stop pursuing the objective entirely?

Suddenly, the quality of the outcome depends heavily on the quality of the objective.

That raises an interesting possibility.

As autonomous agents become more capable, perhaps one of the valuable human skills won't be knowing how to perform every action ourselves.

It will be knowing how to define what success actually means.

Because intelligence can help find a route.

It cannot decide what destination matters to you unless you've communicated that clearly.

This becomes particularly interesting when combined with digital ownership.

An NFT has traditionally been something you possess.

Connecting an NFT with an AI agent and then giving that agent an objective introduces another layer entirely.

The asset isn't simply representing ownership anymore.

There's now a relationship between:

ownership

intent

rules

action

The owner establishes intent.

The boundaries establish what is acceptable.

The agent determines actions within those conditions.

And the objective ties everything together.

I don't think this means humans eventually hand over financial decision-making and walk away.

If anything, it could make human judgement more important in a different place.

We spend less time asking:

@meetmotes
items.title_zh:

items.quote_en:
There's a bigger difference between an instruction and an objective than it first appears.

An instruction tells a system exactly what to do.

An objective tells a system what you're trying to achieve.

That distinction seems small until you start thinking about autonomous AI agents.

If I tell a piece of software:

"Buy this asset."

There isn't much interpretation involved.

I've already made the decision.

The software simply carries it out.

But imagine I say:

"Here is the outcome I'm trying to achieve. Here are the boundaries you must respect. Figure out the appropriate actions."

Now we've entered completely different territory.

The human is no longer providing every step.

The human is providing direction.

That's one of the ideas behind @meetmotes that I keep coming back to.

The phrase "give your NFT an objective" sounds simple, but underneath it is an interesting question about how we may interact with software in the future.

For decades, our relationship with computers has largely been command-driven.

Click this.

Open that.

Move this file.

Execute this transaction.

Buy this asset.

Sell that asset.

Every action begins with a relatively specific human instruction.

AI agents introduce the possibility of changing that relationship.

Instead of continuously telling software what action to perform next, we could increasingly define what we're trying to accomplish and allow the system to determine how to work towards it within established boundaries.

That's not merely automation.

It's delegation.

And delegation requires a very different kind of relationship between the person setting the objective and the system attempting to fulfil it.

Think about the difference in everyday life.

If I give someone a list containing twenty individual tasks, I'm managing the process.

If I explain the outcome I need, establish the boundaries and allow that person to determine the best approach, I'm delegating responsibility.

Both can lead to the same destination.

But the amount of judgement required along the way is completely different.

That's what makes objective-driven AI agents interesting to me.

The value isn't necessarily that the human disappears from the process.

The human's role changes.

Instead of deciding every individual action, the human becomes responsible for defining the destination and determining the boundaries around the journey.

And honestly, I think defining a good objective might eventually prove harder than people expect.

"Make money" is technically an objective.

It's also a terrible one.

How much risk is acceptable?

Over what kind of conditions?

Using what capital?

Across which markets?

What behaviour is off-limits?

When should the agent stop pursuing the objective entirely?

Suddenly, the quality of the outcome depends heavily on the quality of the objective.

That raises an interesting possibility.

As autonomous agents become more capable, perhaps one of the valuable human skills won't be knowing how to perform every action ourselves.

It will be knowing how to define what success actually means.

Because intelligence can help find a route.

It cannot decide what destination matters to you unless you've communicated that clearly.

This becomes particularly interesting when combined with digital ownership.

An NFT has traditionally been something you possess.

Connecting an NFT with an AI agent and then giving that agent an objective introduces another layer entirely.

The asset isn't simply representing ownership anymore.

There's now a relationship between:

ownership

intent

rules

action

The owner establishes intent.

The boundaries establish what is acceptable.

The agent determines actions within those conditions.

And the objective ties everything together.

I don't think this means humans eventually hand over financial decision-making and walk away.

If anything, it could make human judgement more important in a different place.

We spend less time asking:

@meetmotes
items.quote_zh:
指令和目标之间的差异比乍看起来更大。

指令准确地告诉系统要做什么。

目标告诉系统您想要实现的目标。

在你开始考虑自主人​​工智能代理之前，这种区别似乎很小。

如果我告诉一个软件：

“购买该资产。”

没有太多解释。

我已经做出决定了。

软件只是简单地执行它。

但想象一下我说：

“这是我想要实现的结果。这是你必须尊重的界限。找出适当的行动。”

现在我们进入了完全不同的领域。

人类不再提供每一步。

人类正在提供方向。

这是我不断回顾的@meetmotes 背后的想法之一。

“给你的 NFT 一个目标”这句话听起来很简单，但背后隐藏着一个有趣的问题，即我们未来如何与软件交互。

几十年来，我们与计算机的关系很大程度上是命令驱动的。

单击此。

打开那个。

移动这个文件。

执行此交易。

购买该资产。

出售该资产。

每个动作都始于相对具体的人类指令。

人工智能代理引入了改变这种关系的可能性。

我们可以越来越多地定义我们想要完成的任务，并允许系统确定如何在既定的边界内实现目标，而不是不断地告诉软件下一步要执行什么操作。

这不仅仅是自动化。

这是代表团。

授权要求设定目标的人和试图实现目标的系统之间存在一种非常不同的关系。

想想日常生活中的差异。

如果我给某人一个包含二十个单独任务的列表，那么我正在管理该流程。

如果我解释我需要的结果，建立界限并允许那个人确定最佳方法，我就是在委派责任。

两者都可以通向同一个目的地。

但一路上所需的判断量却完全不同。

这就是我对目标驱动的人工智能代理感兴趣的原因。

其价值并不一定是人类从这个过程中消失。

人类的角色发生了变化。

人类不再决定每一个单独的行动，而是负责定义目的地并确定旅程的边界。

老实说，我认为定义一个好的目标最终可能会比人们预期的更困难。

“赚钱”在技术上是一个目标。

这也是一件可怕的事。

可接受的风险有多大？

需要什么样的条件？

用什么资本？

跨越哪些市场？

哪些行为是被禁止的？

代理人什么时候应该完全停止追求目标？

突然之间，结果的质量在很大程度上取决于目标的质量。

这就提出了一个有趣的可能性。

随着自主代理变得更加有能力，也许有价值的人类技能之一将不再是知道如何自己执行每项行动。

它将知道如何定义成功的真正含义。

因为情报可以帮助找到路线。

除非您清楚地传达了这一点，否则它无法决定哪个目的地对您来说很重要。

当与数字所有权相结合时，这变得特别有趣。

NFT 传统上是你所拥有的东西。

将 NFT 与 AI 代理连接起来，然后为该代理提供一个目标，这完全引入了另一层。

资产不再仅仅代表所有权。

现在之间存在关系：

所有权

意图

规则

行动

业主确定意图。

界限决定了什么是可以接受的。

代理决定在这些条件下的操作。

目标将一切联系在一起。

我不认为这意味着人类最终会放弃财务决策权并走开。

如果说有什么不同的话，那就是它可能会让人类的判断在不同的地方变得更加重要。

items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
The New York Times and a group of other publications have filed lawsuits against the company that makes the Brave web browser over alleged unlawful scraping to train AI and also letting users bypass their paywalls, as reported by Reuters.

According to a complaint filed by the companies that run New York Daily News, the Chicago Tribune, and the Orlando Sentinel, Brave Software has monetized its index of scraped websites by, in part, providing AI companies with paid access to  "real-time online content from the Brave Index." items.title_zh: 纽约时报起诉浏览器Brave
items.summary_zh: 纽约时报》等机构起诉Brave浏览器，指控其未经授权抓取数据用于AI训练并帮助用户绕过付费墙

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 包括《纽约时报》及《芝加哥论坛报》在内的多家主流媒体联合起诉Brave浏览器。控方指控Brave不仅通过“Brave索引”向AI企业非法倒卖实时内容用于模型训练，还提供技术手段协助用户绕过媒体付费墙，严重侵犯了者的商业利益。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 这简直是“拦路抢劫”被抓包：浏览器既想靠卖数据赚AI的钱，又想讨好用户提供去广告/去付费功能，结果两头受气。当内容的搬运工变成了内容的“倒爷”，这次媒体大佬们显然不打算留情面了。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Getting caught red-handed as a digital pickpocket: Brave tried to cash in by selling data to AI firms while playing the hero by stripping away paywalls. Now that the ‘middleman’ has turned into an ‘unauthorized reseller,’ the media giants are finally going for the kill.

Over the past year, we’ve used LifeVal to measure and improve how well our models handle these everyday tasks.
