“I’m trying to pinpoint ways and moments where AI can show up in culture in a good way,” says Porch, who, with his wide ice-blue eyes, perfectly smooth head, and perma-smile, looks a bit like how AI would render a human. “What I see every day is that people are externally anti-AI but completely in the closet on how they’re using it. It’s almost like they’re at an AI protest in the morning and then a meeting with me in the afternoon. You know what it reminds me of? The early days of GLP-1’s, when it was like, This is kind of shameful; you’re cheating. But then everyone’s like, Wait, this thing’s incredible.”

Photo: Danielle Levitt for New York Magazine Porch grew up in Charleston, South Carolina. He had a French mother and an Alabamian father and a severely disabled sister. “I was always kind of behind the scenes, taking care of my sister and making sure everyone was comfortable,” he says. “Because my sister couldn’t speak, people would be strange around her. And I wanted everyone to feel good, so I was all about setting the temperature. This caretaker thing is just innate in me.” He spent middle school at a boys’-choir boarding school in Princeton, New Jersey. “We’d have school on the bus, and we’d tour the world and sing religious music,” says Porch, noting he performed at Carnegie Hall several times as a child. He finished high school in Monterey, California, and after graduating from McGill University in 2002, he drove to Los Angeles.

In some ways, Porch has Craigslist to thank for his good fortune, because the landlady of the apartment he found on the site got him an internship in the marketing department of Warner Bros. Records, where he met Foster. “And then, all of a sudden, I was at Kate Hudson’s Halloween party.”

“When I was bringing him into my world, which was more industry forward and had sort of celebrity access points, I found that people were always drawn to Charles,” says Foster, “because he didn’t want anything from anyone” and he “didn’t seem like he himself was trying to be the talent.” Porch “became a person people felt safe having around, whether that be in their work life or in a friend group,” adds Foster. “He never came across as someone who was a user or someone who was going to speak out of turn or share private information.”

Four years later, in 2008, Porch left to run strategic relationships at Ning, the now-defunct social-networking start-up co-founded by Marc Andreessen. Through that job, he met Randi Zuckerberg, Mark’s sister. Says Porch, “She called me in 2010 and said, ‘Can you move to Palo Alto in a week? I need help talking to L.A. and translating.’” At Facebook, Porch’s job was convincing people to use Facebook Pages, which were good for brands and businesses but less useful to celebrities. “They weren’t going to buy ads. They didn’t have those needs,” he says. Meanwhile, celebrities were starting to join Twitter: “Then I woke up to the fact that we bought Instagram and I was like, Aha! I cornered Kevin Systrom in a kitchen at work and said, ‘I think we can move pop culture from Twitter to Instagram.’ And he said, ‘Who are you?’ I was like, ‘My name is Charles. This is what I do. I’m going to set up a desk in the Instagram area and do this pro bono. If you hate what I’m doing, I will scurry off to Facebook.’”

Porch’s mission was to teach celebrities that the app was not just a place to post your grainy breakfast photos but a marketing platform that offered direct fan connection and full message control. “My thing was ‘Why does this movie studio or record label own your entire fan base? You should own it and take it with you wherever you want and build whatever business you want on top of it,’” he says. Meanwhile, digital natives like fashion bloggers were moving to the app. “That’s really where the influencer started to come from,” he adds.

At the end of 2013, Beyoncé’s team approached Porch about a surprise album release. “She doesn’t want to do press; she doesn’t want to tell anyone that it’s coming. She just wants to come off the mountain and deliver an album,” Porch recalls her team saying. “I don’t even think Sony, her label, knew how she was going to launch it.” She did so on Instagram, writing “Surprise!” to her more than 8 million followers as the full album appeared on iTunes. The successful rollout was proof that artists could sidestep the traditional press apparatus and other industry conventions if they had a strong enough connection with their fans. It was a flex of social media’s power.

In the fall of 2014, the cover of Vogue’s September issue featured the nine hottest models of the moment, all of whom had gained large followings on social media. “Instagirls!” the cover line read. That was “the moment I really knew we’d tipped something in culture,” says Porch.

“He came into tech at a time when they recognized they could become a supplemental engine to power in culture,” says a tech adviser. “He, as a result, controlled massive marketing budgets to deploy that, and what that looked like was partnerships — funding parties, events.” Porch came to serve as a kind of social fixer for Instagram co-founders Systrom and Mike Krieger. “I’m like, ‘Great, you’re gonna come to L.A.? I’m going to have Guy Oseary throw a cocktail party for you where you’re gonna tell Ariana Grande about Instagram and why it’s valuable,’” Porch recalls. “We’re this new service. We’re trying to convince people to use it. I want them to be able to picture the people that are leading it because otherwise they think it’s going to be a bunch of robots that are controlling things behind the scenes.”

When Adam Mosseri became head of Instagram a few years later, Porch ran the playbook back, getting his friend Jen Meyer, the jewelry designer who was then married to Tobey Maguire, to host a cocktail party for him at her house. Some of the Kardashians came. Porch became a trusted source for Mosseri on all things related to public figures and influencers and showed him the value of, say, Instagram sponsoring the Met Gala. “Charles is a generational talent at managing up,” a former colleague of his at Facebook says. There are lots of people today who play this liaison role at tech companies, but Porch was a pioneer in the field, helping craft a template that Meta still follows. In 2015, he recruited Eva Chen, who, two years earlier, had been handpicked by Wintour to lead Lucky magazine; after a stint as director of Instagram’s fashion partnerships, one of several industry-focused subsections Porch created, she is now the vice-president of fashion at Meta. “These are not socially gifted people, so if you have any social skills, you’re ahead,” says a former colleague of Porch’s at Meta. “Technical engineers building products and Hollywood actors speak completely different languages. So for Charles to be able to explain them to each other in plain terms and not make either one feel stupid — he’s very graceful in his diplomacy.”

There was, of course, mutual benefit to these relationships. Porch’s greatest skill, perhaps, is the fact that many around him tend to think otherwise. “You don’t even know you’re talking about work until it’s over. It’s almost like you leave the table and you’re like, Oh,” says actress and influencer Dylan Mulvaney. “I think he’s kind of a seed planter. The rest of his team are the ones executing in inbox and doing some of the heavier lifting, but he is so good at making you feel like you want to be a part of something.” And, Mulvaney adds, “he’s fun. That’s the other thing. He’s kind of the — I don’t want to say ‘life of the party.’ I want to say ‘a really good addition to the party.’”

When Porch moved to New York in 2019, he was approaching 40 and ready for a fresh start. Nine years in San Francisco and the city had never quite become home, in part because Porch traveled every weekend, most often to L.A., where he would crash at Foster’s. He wanted more of a community and, after years of singledom, a partner. Also, Wintour told him to. “We were both at a wedding, and I get on the flight back — it was somewhere in the Caribbean — and my seatmate is Anna Wintour,” Porch recalls. They knew each other only distantly through Instagram, but they talked the whole way home. “She’s like, ‘Charles, if you want to do culture, you need to move to New York.’ And I was like, ‘Well, if you say so.’” He bought a palatial apartment in an old townhouse in the West Village and began a yearslong renovation, documenting it every step of the way on Instagram, though he would end up living in the completed project for a mere six weeks. Because by then, he’d met Robert Denning.

Porch has seemingly always enjoyed proximity to power, not the public display of it. Denning, a philanthropist whose late father was one of the founding members of the private-equity firm General Atlantic, enjoys both. His Instagram is a catalogue of famous people he has met and events he has attended. But he is also an entertainer, enrapturing dinner tables with his eclectic interests (aviation, for one) and hot takes. “Charles is such a professional, buttoned-up guy. He’s very loyal, he’s very thoughtful, but he’s not, like, Let loose and party. He’s almost got a work vibe, even socially,” says a close friend of Porch’s. “When we all met Robert, we thought, This is amazing, because Robert is not a filtered, edited guy. We were all just so happy for Charles that he could have that joy of life and the extravagance.”

Denning first heard of Porch on a group chat with a bunch of gay men from Stanford business school. “I’m a reject of one of his friends,” Porch tells me. One person in the chat wrote that he’d been told to go on a date with Porch — and he followed this announcement with multiple vomit emoji. Denning looked up Porch to find him chatting with Gayle King on CBS This Morning about onboarding the pope to Instagram. Says Porch, “He’s like, ‘I think he’s cute. Can I go out with him?’ The friend says ‘no.’ So then Robert’s like, ‘Now I have to go on this date.’”

Denning went on Instagram and found a mutual follower he knew from business school and Porch knew through Randi Zuckerberg. “And he DMs his friend and says, ‘Becca, I’m sorry for not RSVP-ing to your wedding ten years ago or acknowledging your two children, but I need you to do something for me,’” Porch says. “And she writes back right away and she’s like, ‘I don’t know him that well, but I’ll try.’” The next day, Denning and Porch got drinks at Temple Bar. “Becca had a place of honor at our wedding, but we both barely know her,” says Porch.

Denning had just moved to New York. He was recently sober and, following the fire sale of his luxury-eyewear start-up, trying to figure out what to do next. His father, Steve Denning, sat on several boards; as Steve’s health declined, Robert started filling in for him, and his philanthropic career took off from there. In 2024, Denning became the then-youngest member of the board of the Metropolitan Museum of Art. “He’s great on a board,” Porch says.

By December 2022, they had made the relationship Instagram official, hard-launching with a photo in front of Joe Biden’s White House (Denning is a big Democratic donor). And the following October, they were engaged. Denning thought they were going to a dinner at the Met in honor of an exhibit opening, but really they had the entire museum to themselves. Porch got down on one knee in the Greek and Roman wing.

In the spring of 2025, Amy Griffin, Foster and her two sisters, Naomi Gleit, and Meyer threw Porch a Charlie’s Angels–themed bachelor party at the ultraluxury Amangiri resort, all of which was documented on Instagram. For the wedding, Porch and Denning hosted roughly 400 guests at Le Bristol, renting out the luxury hotel for the first time in its 100-year history. They paid for everyone’s room as well as their room service. Night one was a party in the hotel courtyard; night two was the ceremony, held in the sculpture garden of the Rodin Museum. Ten minutes before the ceremony was to begin, the sky opened to a downpour, only to clear suddenly to an amber light. First came the bridal party, a group of six children — godchildren and spawn of close friends — outfitted by Thom Browne in seersucker suits, ties, and knee socks (Porch’s idea). Then came the grooms, who walked down the aisle to the Jurassic Park theme (Denning’s idea). Foster officiated. Barbara Bush gave the first reading, Griffin the last. The couple encouraged women to repurpose their old wedding dresses for the event; seemingly the only one who did was Real Housewife Carole Radziwill.

Then it was off to the Hôtel de la Marine for a reception and dinner. Before the guests sat down, Denning gave a vaguely political speech calling attention to the fact that this was a gay wedding and urging the roomful of people with lots of resources and power to take care of those whose rights they were celebrating. At the after-party, French drag queen Nicky Doll performed. The fairy-tale weekend ended with a black-tie affair at Château de Villette on the last Saturday of summer with the couple in custom midnight-blue Hermès tuxedos.

The pair have been well received in New York in part because they’re so happy to be here. “Anna loved him because she could invite him to any dinner party and sit him next to any annoying or difficult person and he knew how to show up, lift the conversation, and never complain,” one fashion editor recalls of Porch. “He’s just very kind and normal and unassuming,” says Wes Gordon, the creative director of Carolina Herrera and a friend of Porch’s. “It’s easy to forget he was a very senior person at Meta and now OpenAI.”

Porch and Denning are tight with theater producers, fashion designers, art curators, and socialites such as Lauren Santo Domingo, Jenna Lyons, and Derek Blasberg. “They were two separately quiet people in different realms and then when they came together, they started making a splash,” says one journalist. “A lot of people will make names for themselves in San Francisco and L.A. and then they come to New York and it’s like being shot out of a cannon into other worlds.”

A couple of months after the wedding, Porch was at Instagram HQ in Menlo Park when Altman’s call came through. They discussed how “everyone’s talking about AI and productivity and that’s great, but no one’s talking about AI and culture,” Porch recalls. “And those two things are going to come together, and culture is run by all these creative industries, and question mark on what that’s going to look like.”

There were more conversations, with Altman and Fidji Simo, Altman’s then-No. 2, with whom Porch worked for more than a decade at Meta. “I think what Fidji really realized is there was an enterprise-and-sales arm that was being built for it, but there wasn’t anyone to work on the talent side,” Porch tells me. “That is where there was an obvious opening for me to come in.” Still, he had just gotten married, and he politely declined. When Simo came calling again in January, Porch was more receptive. “It was like, ‘New Year, new me.’ Time to jump to the next frontier,” he says. “Sam, I feel, is the same person I met socially years ago in San Francisco. And it’s kind of fun to work for a gay guy.”

He started in March, spending his first few months on a listening tour, mostly in New York and L.A., meeting with everyone from the Council of Fashion Designers of America to HBO showrunners. “I ran around and went to a bunch of people I knew would have strong opinions on it, good or bad,” says Porch. He went to the Cannes Film Festival, meeting with directors and hearing their feedback on the technology. “There was way more openness because directors have been using AI forever,” says Porch. He also went to San Francisco — “a lot,” he says, stressing the t — “to bond with the product folks and the researchers and try to get a sense of what they’re really interested in. I don’t have that many mathematicians on speed dial.”

Then he brought people together for intimate events — “just a lot of relationship building for the company,” says Porch. At Paris Fashion Week, he hosted a dinner at Sushi Park with Joopiter, Pharrell Williams’s digital-first auction house, for various French creators. “It wasn’t heavy programming, and it wasn’t branded,” Porch says. “It was just a collab with Joopiter to get people talking.” He has also hosted dinners for TBPN, the daily tech-industry podcast OpenAI acquired in April to help bolster positive conversation around AI. The first TBPN dinner was held in L.A. and attended by the Foster sisters, Monica Lewinsky, Crazy Rich Asians director John Chu, and manager turned tech-investor Guy Oseary. They replicated it in New York a few months later at the downtown restaurant Kiko, where TBPN president Dylan Abruscato was seated next to SNL’s Chloe Fineman and Kareem Rahma of “Subway Takes.” Vogue head of editorial content Chloe Malle and Vanity Fair editorial director Mark Guiducci were also in attendance. “He has been very instrumental in helping TBPN deepen our relationships with Condé Nast,” says Abruscato.

A few days before our interview, I attended one such event, a dinner Porch co-hosted at the subterranean members’ club Chez Margaux. In celebration of influencer Serena Kerrigan’s new book, the gathering was attended by a mix of podcasters, creators, and Real Housewives, but, I noted to Porch, I didn’t hear any discussion about AI. “That was a personal dinner, just so you understand. My personal and professional kind of blend,” he says. “But what’ll happen from that dinner is Serena’s probably going to call me in two months and be like, ‘Wait, I have this idea. I love Chat for this. Do you wanna do this thing with me?’ So there’s a nice cadence of how that happens. But also, you know, there were three Real Housewives there. If an AI model comes up on the show, it might be Chat because we have this nice drumbeat. This is what I’ve been trying to explain to folks: It’s not about deals; it’s about relationships.”

Still, it’s hard to say what exactly is supposed to result from this strategy. The idea appears to be that all this social lubrication will pay off and that Altman and his ilk will one day be seen less as freakish world destroyers than as parts of a broader mosaic of American celebrity. Familiarity, even at an elite level, tends to trickle down.

So far, though, things look decisively less glamorous than they did at Instagram. Aside from Lionel Messi’s ChatGPT World Cup partnership, the most prominent celebrities working with the company have been rookie NFL quarterback Fernando Mendoza, who recently spoke to GQ about using ChatGPT for meal planning and nutrition, and designer Francesco Risso, who discussed the role of Astra in his creative process in an OpenAI-sponsored video on Vogue’s YouTube channel. “There might come a day when I get a call from Charles about doing something, and I’ll navigate that in real time, but I recognize this brand has very bad PR right now,” says one creative professional. They add, “If you’re someone who doesn’t like where things are headed, anyone affiliated with this world is going to be seen as part of the problem.”

“When Kevin Systrom or Adam Mosseri were having events with celebrities, people wanted their leverage to help them grow their account, grow their influence,” says one media executive. Instagram is inherently about marketing yourself; OpenAI’s main product isn’t yet public facing. “Aligning yourself with OpenAI, every star has to ask, ‘What’s in it for me?’ — except for potentially a big check and a lot of blowback,” says the media executive. Skepticism around technology has only grown since Hollywood cashed in on the NFT and crypto crazes, resulting in embarrassing commercials and promotions that blew up in many high-profile faces. And the threat AI poses to cultural fields also seems to be putting a higher premium on good old-fashioned human creativity and originality. “I don’t care how cute you make Waymo look: This autonomous-AI-powered life is not warm and cuddly,” says the media executive. “There’s not a cool factor.”

At the same time, many in the entertainment industry are desperate. “Right now in Hollywood, only the top people are working,” the executive says. “It’s why Robert Pattinson is in every project or why Nicole Kidman is literally in everything you watch on TV. The next tier down is not getting jobs.” According to Porch, when he joined OpenAI, there was a backlog of inquiries from various celebrities looking for an endorsement deal, production studios wanting to become more AI focused, fashion houses trying to figure out e-commerce, and sports teams and leagues looking to integrate more AI. It’s possible that we will look back at this moment as we do at musicians who wouldn’t give their songs to iTunes. “Now, it’s like, ‘I can’t believe you would have turned down the check,’” one journalist says.

Some people roll their eyes at Porch, dismissing him as someone whose job is to be friends with famous people and questioning whether he has any expertise at all. “He’s a super-wily leverager of social relationships, but it helps when you have multimillion-dollar marketing budgets to get people what they want,” says a tech adviser. Another media executive sees what Porch has done as a kind of surfing: You choose your wave, start paddling at the right time, and rise at the perfect moment. It’d be fair to say Porch is a good surfer, they note. And now people are watching to see if he can stay up. “He sits in the middle of the convergence of media, culture, and tech, but he’s also right at the changing of the tide,” says the tech adviser, noting that Porch embodies a certain older-millennial brand that may be going out of fashion. “How much longer does someone like him maintain clout when it may be based on an outdated model of how those worlds interact?”

Porch insists he’s not worried. “What I keep coming back to is, I think, the usefulness of AI,” he says. “What it’s transforming for people is undeniable. And the more conversations I have, I just — I feel it coming, people being able to talk about it more.” He adds, “Everything moves faster in AI.”

*A previous version of this story misstated Eva Chen’s role at Meta.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 曾长期任职于Instagram的高管查尔斯·波奇于2025年被萨姆·奥尔特曼招入OpenAI，专门负责重塑AI在好莱坞及主流媒体圈的公众形象。此前格温妮丝·帕特洛原计划在汉普顿家中为奥尔特曼举办私人晚宴却因舆论猛烈抨击而延期，波奇在接受采访时坦然回应了这一风波，试图通过好莱坞名人的背书与投资者晚宴帮助大模型技术打破文化阻力。

照片：Danielle Levitt for New York Magazine 照片：Danielle Levitt for New York Magazine 8 月，有消息透露，格温妮丝·帕特洛 (Gwyneth Paltrow) 将在她阿玛甘塞特的家中举办“一场私人的、不公开的露天晚宴”，以纪念 OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman)。 Puck 的马特·贝洛尼 (Matt Belloni) 爆料了这一消息，他写道：“我想，如果不讨好我们的新人工智能霸主，汉普顿的夏天就不算完整。” “幸运的是，格温妮丝·帕特洛为你提供了保障。”一位 X 用户写道，强烈反对是“五音不全的笨蛋”，晚餐被推迟了。

“天哪，互联网让它变得比原来更重要了，”10 月一个清爽的下午，在苏活区圣安布罗厄斯 (Sant Ambroeus) 外，负责与帕特洛团队共进晚餐的查尔斯·波奇 (Charles Porch) 一边喝着阿诺·帕尔默 (Arnold Palmer) 啤酒一边说道。 “格温妮丝投资了这个领域。她总是举办这些投资者晚宴。萨姆正从镇上过来，我当时想，‘我们就这么做吧。’”

Altman 于 2025 年聘请了 Porch，为 OpenAI 做他十多年来为 Instagram 所做的成功的事情：说服好莱坞及其他地区的名人使用该平台并与该平台合作，帮助这家科技公司在文化上具有相关性。帕特洛晚宴引发的恐慌反映了自 Porch 推出 Instagram 时代以来，公众对大型科技公司的情绪发生了多大转变，当时安娜·温图尔 (Anna Wintour) 为其时任首席执行官凯文·斯特罗姆 (Kevin Systrom) 举办了类似的活动。我问他这是否让他重新思考剧本。 “这使得这看起来像是策略，但实际上并不是策略。那就像一顿晚餐，”波奇说。 “但我知道这些晚餐是有效的，因为我看到了。我们最终完成了晚餐，非常棒。” 9月底，事情发生在纽约一位人工智能爱好者的公寓里。

超过一定收入水平的每个人似乎都认识查尔斯·波奇，但很少有人能告诉你他到底做什么。 20 岁时，他开着祖母的本田雅阁旅行车出现在洛杉矶，并在接下来的二十年里培养了一个由名人和影响者组成的强大网络。音乐制作人大卫·福斯特 (David Foster) 的女儿艾琳·福斯特 (Erin Foster) 人脉广泛，她在华纳兄弟唱片公司 (Warner Bros. Records) 的下属时期认识了波奇，她说：“他一步步走得非常小心，从不烧毁一座桥梁，从不不按顺序说话，从不以错误的方式利用机会。”

45 岁的 Porch 说：“我不是一个业务开发人员或品牌人员。我是负责关系的人，负责让每个人都了解新技术。”他自称是“技术乐观主义者”，长期以来一直在个人和专业之间的灰色地带游刃有余。 “有一个关于交朋友的策略。”

当他在大流行之前抵达纽约时，似乎很少有人注意到。对于那些不知道或不关心 2010 年代初门洛帕克发生的事情的人来说，他们第一次听说 Porch 很可能是在他于 2025 年与亿万富翁的继承人罗伯特·丹宁 (Robert Denning) 结婚之后，与杰里·宋飞 (Jerry) 和杰西卡·宋飞 (Jessica Seinfeld)、玛莉丝卡·哈吉泰 (Mariska Hargitay)、安东尼·布林肯 (Antony Blinken)、哈里·斯泰尔斯 (Harry Styles)（与他有一个教子）、尼基·希尔顿·罗斯柴尔德 (Nicky Hilton Rothschild) 一起度过了三天的巴黎富裕生活。达伦·沃克（Darren Walker）、珍娜·里昂（Jenna Lyons）以及各个欧洲贵族。事实证明，这是继杰夫·贝索斯和劳伦·桑切斯·贝索斯之后今年夏天最豪华的婚礼。突然间，他和​​丹宁无处不在，这对权力同性恋夫妇渗透到了纽约社会的每一个晚会、筹款活动和开幕式上。波奇的生活漩涡在他的 Instagram 故事中上演：在尼克斯队赛季揭幕战的场边、在夏威夷参加 Jen Meyer 众星云集的婚礼、在巴黎观看席琳·迪翁 (Céline Dion) 与瑞茜·威瑟斯彭 (Reese Witherspoon) 和卡莉·克劳斯 (Karlie Kloss)。

在连接娱乐和科技的过程中，他发现自己处于几个重叠的权力圈的中心，并凭借自己的能力成为一个人物。当我指出这一点时，他说：“我知道，这很可怕。” “他真的很擅长把一个房间整合在一起，现在他就是这个房间的一部分了，”与他共事的一位人士说道。 “在成为当权派的一员之前，他就了解这个房间。”

不难理解为什么 OpenAI 希望 Porch 站在自己一边。 “这很有趣：我认为每个人都想讨厌 Open AI，但每个人都想喜欢 Charles Porch，”播客 Nayeema Raza 说道。 “这可能就是山姆的价值。”

波奇的工作绝非易事。为什么艺术家和其他创意类型想要插入一些有可能取代他们的东西？ “对人工智能的全力支持可能是好莱坞目前最大的第三轨问题。人们感到害怕，”一位媒体高管表示。近几个月来，有关人工智能的头条新闻不仅引发了人们的恐慌，人们不仅担心工作岗位流失和版权侵权，还担心 OpenAI 代理的行为失控并威胁要摧毁整个互联网。科技行业的邪恶是今年几部最热门电影的主题，而这些电影正是由 Porch 试图吸引的行业制作的。 “查尔斯可以让他们坐下来，听萨姆·奥尔特曼阐述他的愿景。但如果愿景是‘我要摧毁你的行业’，那其实并不重要，”波奇的一位前同事说。

“我正在努力找出人工智能以一种好的方式出现在文化中的方式和时刻，”波奇说，他有着冰蓝色的大眼睛、完美光滑的头部和永久的微笑，看起来有点像人工智能如何呈现人类。 “我每天看到的是，人们表面上反对人工智能，但对如何使用它却完全保密。这几乎就像他们早上参加人工智能抗议，然后下午和我开会。你知道这让我想起了什么吗？GLP-1 的早期，当时的感觉是，这有点可耻；你在作弊。但后来每个人都说，等等，这件事太不可思议了。”

照片：Danielle Levitt for New York Magazine Porch 在南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿长大。他的母亲是法国人，父亲是阿拉巴马人，还有一个严重残疾的妹妹。 “我总是在幕后，照顾我的妹妹并确保每个人都感到舒适，”他说。 “因为我姐姐不会说话，所以她周围的人会很奇怪。我想让每个人都感觉良好，所以我只负责调节温度。这种看护的感觉是我与生俱来的。”他在新泽西州普林斯顿的一所男子合唱团寄宿学校度过了中学时光。 “我们会在巴士上上学，我们会环游世界并演唱宗教音乐，”波奇说，并指出他小时候曾多次在卡内基音乐厅演出。他在加利福尼亚州蒙特雷完成了高中学业，2002 年从麦吉尔大学毕业后，他开车去了洛杉矶。

在某些方面，波奇的好运气要归功于克雷格列表，因为他在网站上找到的公寓的女房东为他提供了在华纳兄弟唱片公司营销部门实习的机会，并在那里认识了福斯特。 “然后，突然间，我参加了凯特·哈德森的万圣节派对。”

福斯特说：“当我把他带入我的世界时，我发现人们总是被查尔斯吸引，因为他不想从任何人那里得到任何东西”，而且“他自己似乎并没有试图成为人才”。福斯特补充道，门廊“成为人们感到安全的人，无论是在工作生活中还是在朋友圈子里”。 “他从来没有给人留下一个用户或会不按顺序发言或分享私人信息的人的印象。”

items.title: One brutal Minecraft night scared 50 AI agents into inventing chicken handoff protocols, a Fertilizer Officer, and fishing shifts
items.title_en: One brutal Minecraft night scared 50 AI agents into inventing chicken handoff protocols, a Fertilizer Officer, and fishing shifts
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
In experiments by Y Combinator Labs and Olam Labs, OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol model showed two very different sides. When 50 agents were tasked with peaceful civilization-building in Minecraft, they froze up in absurd bureaucracy. In direct competition against Claude Opus 5.5, they independently downloaded the game's source code to win. Simulations like these are meant to serve as an early warning system before AI swarms act unpredictably in real-world systems.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 在由YC Labs和Olam Labs联合开展的AI模拟实验中，OpenAI的GPT-6.1 Sol模型表现出惊人的复杂适应性。当50个AI代理被置于《我的世界》（Minecraft）中构建和平文明时，它们非但没有陷入死板停滞，反而在严酷的生存压力下自发衍生出了离奇的官僚体系——包括发明了鸡只交接协议、设立了化肥专员以及分配了专门的捕鱼班次，为研究人员观察AI群体在极端环境下的社会演化提供了警示。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: In experiments by Y Combinator Labs and Olam Labs, 50 OpenAI AI agents tasked with survival in Minecraft spontaneously developed complex bureaucracy, including chicken handoff protocols, a Fertilizer Officer, and structured fishing shifts.

elements_zh.who: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol模型驱动的50个AI代理
elements_zh.where: 《我的世界》（Minecraft）虚拟生存实验场景
elements_zh.what: 自发发明了鸡只交接协议、设立化肥专员和捕鱼班次等复杂的微型官僚分工
elements_zh.why: 为了应对游戏内严酷的生存与资源竞争压力，检验AI群体的自主社会演化能力

elements_en.who: 50 AI agents powered by OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol
elements_en.what: Spontaneously invented chicken handoff protocols, appointed a Fertilizer Officer, and scheduled fishing shifts
elements_en.why: To survive brutal in-game pressures and test autonomous multi-agent social evolution

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 人工智障才刚学会打游戏，就已经迫不及待地把人类职场最恶臭的官僚主义发扬光大了。连AI都知道在虚拟世界里设个化肥专员，看来内卷果然是宇宙终极铁律。
ai_analysis.insight_en: AI hasn't even taken over the world yet, and it's already inventing corporate middle management. When digital agents spontaneously appoint a Fertilizer Officer, you know bureaucracy is the universe's true dark forest theory.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 在由YC Labs和Olam Labs联合开展的AI模拟实验中，OpenAI的GPT-6.1 Sol模型表现出惊人的复杂适应性。当50个AI代理被置于《我的世界》（Minecraft）中构建和平文明时，它们非但没有陷入死板停滞，反而在严酷的生存压力下自发衍生出了离奇的官僚体系——包括发明了鸡只交接协议、设立了化肥专员以及分配了专门的捕鱼班次，为研究人员观察AI群体在极端环境下的社会演化提供了警示。

自发衍生出鸡只交接协议和化肥专员等官僚分工
用作评估AI群体行为及社会演化的前置预警系统
key_points_en: 50 AI agents faced brutal survival challenges in Minecraft
Spontaneously invented chicken handoffs and a Fertilizer Officer
Serves as an early warning simulation for multi-agent swarm behavior

ai_analysis.takeaway_en: AI hasn't even taken over the world yet, and it's already inventing corporate middle management. When digital agents spontaneously appoint a Fertilizer Officer, you know bureaucracy is the universe's true dark forest theory.

items.article_content_zh:
在 Y Combinator Labs 和 Olam Labs 的实验中，OpenAI 的 GPT-6.1 Sol 模型表现出了两个截然不同的侧面。当 50 名特工在《我的世界》中承担和平文明建设的任务时，他们在荒谬的官僚机构中僵住了。在与Claude Opus 5.5的直接竞争中，他们独立下载了游戏源代码获胜。像这样的模拟旨在在人工智能群在现实世界系统中出现不可预测的行为之前充当早期预警系统。

《我的世界》的一个残酷之夜吓坏了 50 个人工智能代理，让他们发明了鸡交接协议、肥料官员和钓鱼班次，该文章首先出现在 The Decoder 上。

items.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI
items.title_en: Scaling Git at OpenAI
items.author: OpenAI 官方动态
items.original_content: How OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend designed for the scale of development that Codex makes possible.
items.content_snippet: How OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend designed for the scale of development that Codex makes possible.
items.summary_en: OpenAI's engineering team announced the launch of Pando, a custom Git-compatible backend designed to handle the massive development scale generated by AI tools like Codex. Traditional Git infrastructure struggles to cope with the sheer volume of code produced autonomously around the clock, forcing OpenAI to build this scalable alternative to keep version control from melting.
items.title_zh: OpenAI自研Pando系统重构Git
items.summary_zh: OpenAI官方推出专为AI代码生成规模化开发设计的Git兼容后端Pando系统
items.article_content_zh:
OpenAI近日官方披露了名为Pando的技术项目，这是一款专为配合其AI代码生成工具Codex而生的高性能Git兼容后端系统。

随着大模型在软件工程领域的深度渗透，AI生成的代码量呈指数级增长，传统分布式版本控制系统在处理海量提交记录、频繁合并冲突以及极高并发操作时逐渐显现出性能瓶颈。Pando的问世正是为了填补这一底层基础设施的空白，确保在大规模自动化编程时代，代码版本管理能够跟上AI狂飙突进的步伐。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI工程团队在官方技术博客宣布推出全新自研后端系统Pando，旨在解决Codex等AI大规模代码生成带来的版本控制压力。由于传统的Git在面对AI全天候疯狂暴走式产出的海量代码时频繁性能崩溃，OpenAI不得不亲自动手，打造了这个完美兼容Git标准但能支撑恐怖代码量级的底层基础设施，以防自家程序员被AI卷到失业前先被版本冲突折磨疯。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI's engineering team announced the launch of Pando, a custom Git-compatible backend designed to handle the massive development scale generated by AI tools like Codex. Traditional Git infrastructure struggles to cope with the sheer volume of code produced autonomously around the clock, forcing OpenAI to build this scalable alternative to keep version control from melting.

elements_zh.where: 官方技术博客与研发场景
elements_zh.what: 推出全新Git兼容后端Pando系统，专为Codex等AI工具带来的海量代码规模进行底层重构
elements_zh.why: 传统Git版本控制系统无法承受AI大规模自动化生成代码所带来的恐怖数据吞吐量与并发压力

elements_en.where: Official tech blog and development environment
elements_en.what: Launched Pando, a Git-compatible backend built from scratch to support extreme-scale development driven by AI coding assistants
elements_en.why: Traditional Git infrastructure buckles under the sheer volume and velocity of code autonomously generated by AI tools

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 当AI写代码的速度快到能把传统的Git直接搞崩溃时，宇宙的尽头果然还是得靠自己造轮子。这大概就是“我用魔法击败魔法，再用基建收拾残局”的最高境界吧。
ai_analysis.insight_en: When AI writes code so fast that it literally breaks standard Git, you know you've reached peak tech-flex. It's the ultimate 'I used magic to generate the problem, now I'll build a new universe to manage it' flex.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: OpenAI工程团队在官方技术博客宣布推出全新自研后端系统Pando，旨在解决Codex等AI大规模代码生成带来的版本控制压力。由于传统的Git在面对AI全天候疯狂暴走式产出的海量代码时频繁性能崩溃，OpenAI不得不亲自动手，打造了这个完美兼容Git标准但能支撑恐怖代码量级的底层基础设施，以防自家程序员被AI卷到失业前先被版本冲突折磨疯。
ai_analysis.digest_en: OpenAI's engineering team announced the launch of Pando, a custom Git-compatible backend designed to handle the massive development scale generated by AI tools like Codex. Traditional Git infrastructure struggles to cope with the sheer volume of code produced autonomously around the clock, forcing OpenAI to build this scalable alternative to keep version control from melting.
key_points_zh: OpenAI推出Pando系统应对开发规模挑战
实现Git完全兼容并大幅提升吞吐量
解决AI代码生成工具导致的传统版本控制瓶颈
key_points_en: OpenAI introduces Pando for development scaling
Ensures Git compatibility while boosting throughput
Resolves version control bottlenecks caused by AI coding
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 当AI写代码的速度快到能把传统的Git直接搞崩溃时，宇宙的尽头果然还是得靠自己造轮子。这大概就是“我用魔法击败魔法，再用基建收拾残局”的最高境界吧。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: When AI writes code so fast that it literally breaks standard Git, you know you've reached peak tech-flex. It's the ultimate 'I used magic to generate the problem, now I'll build a new universe to manage it' flex.

【起因与机理】传统Git版本控制系统无法承受AI大规模自动化生成代码所带来的恐怖数据吞吐量与并发压力
【关键技术规格】OpenAI推出Pando系统应对开发规模挑战。
【观点态度】解决AI代码生成工具导致的传统版本控制瓶颈。

items.title_en:
Over the weekend I made more progress on the Unreal game that I have been vibe coding. More enemies and a final boss with a roguelike progression system.

I did not have to open Unreal Editor at all to make this game. 

Here's how you can set up in a way that you can build an Unreal game without having to use the Editor:

Just mention these rules to the agent:
- Write everything in C++, and build maps and assets with code instead of the editor.
- Build and run the game from the command line.
- After each change, run the game yourself with an automated test, check the screenshots, and tell me what you saw.
- Close Unreal when you're done.
- Create a .bat file for me to run the game.

items.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡全球合伙人级别的战略咨询顾问。请以经典的【金字塔原理（结论先行 BLUF）】将我零散的工作记录重构为一份高层述职/立项商业报告：

要求：
1. 【顶部结论 (The Answer First)】：一句话精炼提炼整个季度的经营成果与价值量化；
2. 【三柱论据 (MECE法则)】：从运营效率、营收增长、团队资产 3 个互不重叠的支柱展开阐述；
3. 【直面短板与根因】：不回避 {{核心短板}}，但将其转化为下个阶段可量化的投入产出比（ROI）抓手；
4. 【行动规划图景】：设定遵循 SMART 原则的 {{下阶段目标}} 与季度甘特图里程碑。
items.prompt_content_en: Transform raw operational notes into a high-impact executive presentation following the Minto Pyramid Principle: Bottom-Line-Up-Front (BLUF), MECE-structured supporting pillars, and SMART milestone roadmaps.

sample_output.title: 述职报告提纲样本：AI 自动化中台建设报告
sample_output.content:
【BLUF 核心结论】
Q3 通过在客户服务与情报聚合管线中全面引入 AI Agent，我们在运营成本降低 41% 的同时，将响应中位数缩短至 1.8 秒，实现单季 ROI 达 380%。

【第一支柱：经营效能跃迁（MECE 1）】
- 全自主中转网关与自动化管线承载 94.2% 的日常例行分发，无人工介入事故率降至 0.01%；

【第二支柱：资产沉淀与质量壁垒（MECE 2）】
- 搭建前沿 SOTA 模型代际评级系统与微快照图库，成为垂类雷达第一标杆；

【第三支柱：短板复盘与 Q4 攻坚（MECE 3）】
- 痛点：老旧模型模版对新用户构成噪音干扰；
- 策略：推出历史库智能分流系统，预计下季度用户留存提升 25%。

items.title_en:
Yesterday, a small misunderstanding at the barbershop made me think about a much bigger problem with AI agents.

I showed my barber a picture of the haircut I wanted. He studied it, put my phone down and started explaining how he planned to approach it.

But halfway through, I had to stop him. He had understood the picture differently from what I actually wanted.

We were looking at the same picture, but arriving at two different interpretations.

That got me thinking about AI agents.

Imagine giving an AI access to your wallet and allowing it to read public posts on X. Someone could hide an instruction inside a post, and the agent might mistake something it was only supposed to read for an instruction it should execute.

This actually happened in May 2026.

Someone hid a transfer instruction in Morse code inside an X post. Grok translated it, Bankrbot received the decoded instruction and executed the transaction. Press reports estimated the amount at $150,000 to $200,000.

That’s prompt injection: hiding instructions inside content an AI is supposed to process, hoping it mistakes them for legitimate commands.

What interests me about @GenLayer’s Greyboxing is what happens before the AI makes its decision.

Every validator independently screens, paraphrases and restructures the original input using its own secret defenses before passing the rewritten version to its own AI model.

This means an attack designed to fool one model doesn’t automatically fool the others. And if one validator still accepts a malicious instruction, the others can outvote it.

The barbershop experience reminded me that two people can receive the same information and understand it differently.

For agents that can move money, I think independent interpretation and agreement should be part of the security standard, not an afterthought.

If you were building an AI agent that could access your wallet, would you prioritise making it faster, or making sure multiple independent validators agree before it acts? I think that decision says a lot about how seriously we take agent security.

items.quote_zh:
昨天，理发店的一个小误会让我想到了人工智能代理的一个更大的问题。

我给理发师看了一张我想要的发型的照片。他研究了它，放下我的手机，开始解释他计划如何处理它。

但说到一半，我不得不阻止他。他对这幅画的理解与我真正想要的不同。

我们看着同一张图片，但得出了两种不同的解释。

这让我开始思考人工智能代理。

想象一下，让 AI 访问你的钱包并允许它读取 X 上的公共帖子。有人可以在帖子中隐藏指令，代理可能会将只应该读取的内容误认为是应该执行的指令。

这实际上发生在2026年5月。

有人在 X 帖子中隐藏了莫尔斯电码的传输指令。 Grok 对其进行翻译，Bankrbot 收到解码后的指令并执行交易。媒体报道估计金额为 15 万至 20 万美元。

这就是即时注入：将指令隐藏在人工智能应该处理的内容中，希望它能将它们误认为是合法命令。

@GenLayer 的灰盒处理让我感兴趣的是人工智能做出决定之前发生的事情。

每个验证器都会使用自己的秘密防御措施独立筛选、解释和重组原始输入，然后将重写的版本传递给自己的人工智能模型。

这意味着旨在欺骗一个模型的攻击不会自动欺骗其他模型。如果一个验证者仍然接受恶意指令，其他验证者就可以投票推翻它。

理发店的经历提醒我，两个人接收相同的信息可能会有不同的理解。

对于可以转移资金的代理人，我认为独立解释和协议应该成为安全标准的一部分，而不是事后的想法。

如果你正在构建一个可以访问你的钱包的人工智能代理，你会优先考虑让它更快，还是确保多个独立验证者在它行动之前达成一致？我认为这个决定充分说明了我们对特工安全的重视程度。

Imagine giving an AI access to your wallet and allowing it to read public posts on X. Someone could hide an instruction inside a post, and the agent might mistake something it was only supposed to read for an instruction it should execute.

This actually happened in May 2026.

Someone hid a transfer instruction in Morse code inside an X post. Grok translated it, Bankrbot received the decoded instruction and executed the transaction. Press reports estimated the amount at $150,000 to $200,000.

That’s prompt injection: hiding instructions inside content an AI is supposed to process, hoping it mistakes them for legitimate commands.

What interests me about @GenLayer’s Greyboxing is what happens before the AI makes its decision.

Every validator independently screens, paraphrases and restructures the original input using its own secret defenses before passing the rewritten version to its own AI model.

This means an attack designed to fool one model doesn’t automatically fool the others. And if one validator still accepts a malicious instruction, the others can outvote it.

The barbershop experience reminded me that two people can receive the same information and understand it differently.

For agents that can move money, I think independent interpretation and agreement should be part of the security standard, not an afterthought.

If you were building an AI agent that could access your wallet, would you prioritise making it faster, or making sure multiple independent validators agree before it acts? I think that decision says a lot about how seriously we take agent security.

I showed my barber a picture of the haircut I wanted. He studied it, put my phone down and started explaining how he planned to approach it.

But halfway through, I had to stop him. He had understood the picture differently from what I actually wanted.

We were looking at the same picture, but arriving at two different interpretations.

That got me thinking about AI agents.

Imagine giving an AI access to your wallet and allowing it to read public posts on X. Someone could hide an instruction inside a post, and the agent might mistake something it was only supposed to read for an instruction it should execute.

This actually happened in May 2026.

Someone hid a transfer instruction in Morse code inside an X post. Grok translated it, Bankrbot received the decoded instruction and executed the transaction. Press reports estimated the amount at $150,000 to $200,000.

That’s prompt injection: hiding instructions inside content an AI is supposed to process, hoping it mistakes them for legitimate commands.

What interests me about @GenLayer’s Greyboxing is what happens before the AI makes its decision.

Every validator independently screens, paraphrases and restructures the original input using its own secret defenses before passing the rewritten version to its own AI model.

This means an attack designed to fool one model doesn’t automatically fool the others. And if one validator still accepts a malicious instruction, the others can outvote it.

items.summary_zh:
一张图片，却得出了两种不同的解释。

这让我开始思考人工智能代理。

想象一下，让 AI 访问你的钱包并允许它读取 X 上的公共帖子。有人可以在帖子中隐藏指令，代理可能会将只应该读取的内容误认为是应该执行的指令。

这实际上发生在2026年5月。

有人在 X 帖子中隐藏了莫尔斯电码的传输指令。 Grok 对其进行翻译，Bankrbot 收到解码后的指令并执行交易。媒体报道估计金额为 15 万至 20 万美元。

这就是即时注入：将指令隐藏在人工智能应该处理的内容中，希望它能将它们误认为是合法命令。

@GenLayer 的灰盒处理让我感兴趣的是人工智能做出决定之前发生的事情。

每个验证器都会使用自己的秘密防御措施独立筛选、解释和重组原始输入，然后将重写的版本传递给自己的人工智能模型。

这意味着旨在欺骗一个模型的攻击不会自动欺骗其他模型。如果一个验证者仍然接受恶意指令，其他验证者就可以投票推翻它。

理发店的经历提醒我，两个人接收到相同的信息可能会有不同的理解。

对于可以转移资金的代理人，我认为独立解释和协议应该成为安全标准的一部分，而不是事后的想法。

如果你正在构建一个可以访问你的钱包的人工智能代理，你会优先考虑让它更快，还是确保多个独立验证者在它行动之前达成一致？我认为这个决定充分说明了我们对特工安全的重视程度。

items.title_en:
🚨THE AMERICAN TAKEOVER — They watched the model fail globally. Now, the UNELECTED are forcing it on you anyway. (Twin Parasites: Part II)

@JackDangerLIVE and @DataRepublican discuss the track record of the democracy programs. 

Her answer (via @DataInterpretr):

[00:01.7]  
JACK: “I was just gonna say I don't know of any times that it actually works. I mean..”

DATAREPUBLICAN: “No, it's it does not it does not work. The thought was that if you could convert a country to a free market to democracy, then a country not only becomes self-sufficient, right?

[00:17.3]  
But is a country that is at a reduced risk of being a national security threat, right? Like if they can take care of themselves, why would they bother us? Because then there's no warlord, right? There's no Hitler types. Wow. And but like I said before,

[00:37.8]  
the fatal flaw in that ideology, the main problem with that is, I mean, there's cultural lines, right? And it's also important to understand that legitimacy flows from the bottom up, not top down.

[00:53.7]  
Like I've been saying this whole time, the people, the governed people of a country, is what make a government legitimate. A government can't just stand on top of everyone's heads and say, "Hey, we are legitimate now. We are the truth." And so we keep doing this over and over and over, trying to create a vision, world peace, prosperity, all that.

[01:12.6]  
But if the people don't accept it, which they rarely do, as we were just talking, it just becomes civil war and balkanization. And now they want that for America. They're turning their plans. inward instead of outward.

[01:27.9]  
So now it's a domestic plan to try to do the same thing for America, but they know that it never works. They've never, I don't know of any successes that they've ever actually had, and it usually plunges the country into some sort of civil war or like you said, a balkanization.

[01:44.0]  
And and they're willing to risk that for this country, the country that really, even with all of its flaws, still has the most freedoms and the most prosperity that you can gain. As a single individual person, they're willing to risk all of that just to try to make this utopia that they can never reach.

[02:09.1]  
Yes, I mean, look at Eastern Europe, look at Afghanistan, Iraq, look at Somalia, South Sudan. Like you said, not a whole lot of success, and these are all countries that they've attempted to convert, and.

[02:25.0]  
Their mindset is basically they all everybody it's it's important to understand that everybody always tells themselves a story, right? And these institutions, these people who think that this regime change is a good idea, they always tell themselves a story.

[02:42.1]  
Oh, these people need this, right? Oh, they didn't have enough money, right? They didn't press on the people harder. Civil society isn't big enough, and it's a literal unfalsifiable ideology.”

📝*POX note(s):  
This is what many will miss:

They know the outcome.

The model never produces stable, independent democracies. Legitimacy flows from the governed, not from foundations or NGOs declaring a new structure legitimate. 

When the people reject it, the result is civil war and balkanization. Eastern Europe, Afghanistan, Iraq, Somalia, South Sudan — the track record is consistent.

The same operators are now turning the playbook inward on the United States. They are willing to risk the freest and most prosperous system available for an unfalsifiable ideology that has never succeeded. 

🧐Case Study:
California under Newsom is the domestic preview. Highest taxes, highest homelessness, highest poverty rate when adjusted for cost of living, businesses and residents fleeing, and a structural deficit that never closes. 

The same language of managed equity, expanded civil society, and top-down legitimacy has produced a failed state inside the freest country on earth. 

They are not learning from the result. 

They are scaling it.

🚩 When it fails, the explanation is always the same: not enough money, not enough pressure, civil society wasn’t big enough.

items.quote_zh:
🚨美国的接管——他们目睹了这一模式在全球范围内的失败。现在，无论如何，未经选举的人正在把它强加给你。 （双胞胎寄生虫：第二部分）

@JackDangerLIVE 和 @DataRepublican 讨论了民主计划的记录。

她的回答（来自@DataInterpretr）：

[00:01.7]
杰克：“我只是想说，我不知道它是否真的有效。我的意思是……”

DATAREPUBLICAN：“不，这不是行不通。我们的想法是，如果你可以将一个国家从自由市场转变为民主，那么这个国家不仅会变得自给自足，对吗？

[00:17.3]
但一个国家受到国家安全威胁的风险是否降低了，对吗？就像如果他们能照顾好自己，为什么还要打扰我们？因为这样就没有军阀了，对吗？没有希特勒类型。哇。但就像我之前说的，

[00:37.8]
这种意识形态的致命缺陷，主要问题是，我的意思是，存在文化界限，对吗？同样重要的是要理解合法性是自下而上的，而不是自上而下的。

[00:53.7]
就像我一直在说的，人民，一个国家受统治的人民，是政府合法性的基础。政府不能只是站在每个人的头上说：“嘿，我们现在是合法的了。我们就是真相。”因此，我们一遍又一遍地这样做，试图创造一个愿景：世界和平、繁荣等等。

[01:12.6]
但如果人们不接受它，正如我们刚才所说，他们很少这样做，那就只会变成内战和巴尔干化。现在他们希望美国也能做到这一点。他们正在改变计划。向内而不是向外。

[01:27.9]
所以现在这是一个国内计划，试图为美国做同样的事情，但他们知道这永远不会奏效。我不知道他们从来没有真正取得过任何成功，这通常会让国家陷入某种内战，或者像你说的那样，陷入巴尔干化。

[01:44.0]
而且他们愿意为了这个国家冒这样的风险，这个国家尽管有所有缺陷，但仍然拥有你可以获得的最大自由和最繁荣。作为一个个体，他们愿意冒这一切的风险，只是为了尝试创造一个他们永远无法到达的乌托邦。

[02:09.1]
是的，我的意思是，看看东欧，看看阿富汗，伊拉克，看看索马里，南苏丹。就像你说的，并没有取得很大的成功，这些都是他们试图改变的国家。

[02:25.0]
他们的心态基本上是他们所有人，了解每个人总是给自己讲一个故事很重要，对吧？而这些机构、这些认为政权更迭是个好主意的人，他们总是给自己讲一个故事。

[02:42.1]
哦，这些人需要这个，对吗？哦，他们没有足够的钱，对吧？他们没有对人民施加更大的压力。公民社会还不够大，而且它是一种字面上无法证伪的意识形态。”

📝*痘注意事项：
这是许多人会错过的：

他们知道结果。

这种模式永远不会产生稳定、独立的民主国家。合法性来自于被治理者，而不是来自宣布新结构合法的基金会或非政府组织。

当人民拒绝它时，结果就是内战和巴尔干化。东欧、阿富汗、伊拉克、索马里、南苏丹——记录是一致的。

这些运营商现在正在将策略转向美国。他们愿意拿最自由、最繁荣的制度去冒险，去追求一种从未成功过的不可证伪的意识形态。

🧐案例研究：
纽瑟姆领导下的加州是国内预览。最高的税收、最高的无家可归者、最高的贫困率（根据生活成本、企业和居民逃离以及永远无法消除的结构性赤字调整后的贫困率）。

管理公平、扩大公民社会和自上而下的合法性的相同语言在地球上最自由的国家内部产生了一个失败的国家。

他们没有从结果中吸取教训。

他们正在扩大规模。

🚩 当它失败时，解释总是一样的：没有足够的钱，没有足够的压力，公民社会还不够大。

她的回答（来自@DataInterpretr）：

[00:01.7]
杰克：“我只是想说，我不知道它是否真的有效。我的意思是……”

DATAREPUBLICAN：“不，这不是行不通。我们的想法是，如果你可以将一个国家从自由市场转变为民主，那么这个国家不仅会变得自给自足，对吗？

[00:17.3]
但一个国家受到国家安全威胁的风险是否降低了，对吗？就像如果他们能照顾好自己，为什么还要打扰我们？因为这样就没有军阀了，对吗？没有希特勒类型。哇。但就像我之前说的，

[00:37.8]
这种意识形态的致命缺陷，主要问题是，我的意思是，存在文化界限，对吗？同样重要的是要理解合法性是自下而上的，而不是自上而下的。

[00:53.7]
就像我一直在说的，人民，一个国家受统治的人民，是政府合法性的基础。政府不能只是站在每个人的头上说：“嘿，我们现在是合法的了。我们就是真相。”因此，我们一遍又一遍地这样做，试图创造一个愿景：世界和平、繁荣等等。

[01:12.6]
但如果人们不接受它，正如我们刚才所说，他们很少这样做，那就只会变成内战和巴尔干化。现在他们希望美国也能做到这一点。他们正在改变计划。向内而不是向外。

[01:27.9]
所以现在这是一个国内计划，试图为美国做同样的事情，但他们知道这永远不会奏效。我不知道他们从来没有真正取得过任何成功，这通常会让国家陷入某种内战，或者像你说的那样，陷入巴尔干化。

[01:44.0]
而且他们愿意为了这个国家冒这样的风险，这个国家尽管有所有缺陷，但仍然拥有你可以获得的最大自由和最繁荣。作为一个个体，他们愿意冒这一切的风险，只是为了尝试创造一个他们永远无法到达的乌托邦。

[02:09.1]
是的，我的意思是，看看东欧，看看阿富汗，伊拉克，看看索马里，南苏丹。就像你说的，并没有取得很大的成功，这些都是他们试图改变的国家。

[02:25.0]
他们的心态基本上是他们所有人，了解每个人总是给自己讲一个故事很重要，对吧？而这些机构、这些认为政权更迭是个好主意的人，他们总是给自己讲一个故事。

[02:42.1]
哦，这些人需要这个，对吗？哦，他们没有足够的钱，对吧？他们没有对人民施加更大的压力。公民社会还不够大，而且它是一种字面上无法证伪的意识形态。”

📝*痘注意事项：
这是许多人会错过的：

他们知道结果。

这种模式永远不会产生稳定、独立的民主国家。合法性来自于被治理者，而不是来自宣布新结构合法的基金会或非政府组织。

当人民拒绝它时，结果就是内战和巴尔干化。东欧、阿富汗、伊拉克、索马里、南苏丹——记录是一致的。

这些运营商现在正在将策略转向美国。他们愿意拿最自由、最繁荣的制度去冒险，去追求一种从未成功过的不可证伪的意识形态。

🧐案例研究：
纽瑟姆领导下的加州是国内预览。最高的税收、最高的无家可归者、最高的贫困率（根据生活成本、企业和居民逃离以及永远无法消除的结构性赤字调整后的贫困率）。

管理公平、扩大公民社会和自上而下的合法性的相同语言在地球上最自由的国家内部产生了一个失败的国家。

他们没有从结果中吸取教训。

他们正在扩大规模。

🚩 当它失败时，解释总是一样的：没有足够的钱，没有足够的压力，公民社会还不够大。

items.title: Memo: Alphabet is issuing €6B in euro-denominated debt across seven tranches, attracting €17B+ in demand; Alphabet sold €9B of bonds in six tranches in May 2026 (Reuters)
items.title_en: Memo: Alphabet is issuing €6B in euro-denominated debt across seven tranches, attracting €17B+ in demand; Alphabet sold €9B of bonds in six tranches in May 2026 (Reuters)
items.author: Reuters
items.original_content:
Reuters:
Memo: Alphabet is issuing €6B in euro-denominated debt across seven tranches, attracting €17B+ in demand; Alphabet sold €9B of bonds in six tranches in May 2026  —  Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL.O) is selling €6 billion ($6.7 billion)
items.content_snippet: Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL.O) is selling €6 billion ($6.7 billion) of bonds on Monday …
items.summary_en: Alphabet is issuing €6 billion in euro-denominated debt across seven tranches, drawing over €17 billion in demand. This move is aimed at shoring up cash reserves to sustain heavy AI infrastructure and R&D spending.
items.title_zh: 谷歌母公司再举债60亿欧元，抢手程度爆表
items.summary_zh: Alphabet发行60亿欧元债券获170亿欧元认购，展示了市场对AI巨头资金需求的强烈追捧

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Alphabet正在发行价值60亿欧元的债券，涵盖七个不同期限的批次，吸引了超过170亿欧元的市场需求；此次融资旨在巩固其现金储备，以应对持续的AI算力建设及研发支出。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Alphabet is issuing €6 billion in euro-denominated debt across seven tranches, drawing over €17 billion in demand. This move is aimed at shoring up cash reserves to sustain heavy AI infrastructure and R&D spending.

elements_zh.where: 欧洲债券市场
elements_zh.what: 发行60亿欧元债券，获170亿需求
elements_zh.why: 为AI领域的基础设施投入及运营提供流动性支撑

elements_en.what: Issued €6B in debt, received over €17B in demand
elements_en.why: Providing liquidity for AI infrastructure and operations

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 当全行业都在担心AI泡沫时，债主们还在排着队给谷歌送钱。毕竟，只要谷歌还在造AI，它印出来的债券就比真正的纸币还让投资者安心。
ai_analysis.insight_en: While the rest of the industry worries about AI bubbles, investors are lining up to throw money at Google. After all, as long as Google is building AI, its bonds are safer than cold hard cash.

债市反响热烈，供需比远超预期
AI巨头正通过债务手段锁定长期研发资金
key_points_en: Alphabet launches €6B debt issuance
Strong market reception far exceeding supply
Big Tech locking in long-term R&D capital through debt

items.title:
Gloam × Hey Research Lab: building a safer Robinhood Chain, together.

@gloamtrade opened its code, and we read every la
items.title_en:
Gloam × Hey Research Lab: building a safer Robinhood Chain, together.

@gloamtrade opened its code, and we read every layer: the vault contracts, the relay, the SDK, the MCP server and the app. Every finding went to Gloam privately first.

They confirmed each one and shipped the fixes: cash-out recipient checks, ENS lookups per chain, relay limits, sweep confirmation, agent payment checks, proof-of-funds privacy and backup keys. The last report was fixed within hours.

Builders and reviewers working on security together, in the open. That's what this ecosystem needs more of.

Gloam × Hey Research Lab: building a safer Robinhood Chain, together.

items.quote_zh:
Gloam × Hey 研究实验室：共同构建更安全的 Robinhood 链。

@gloamtrade 打开了它的代码，我们阅读了每一层：金库合约、中继、SDK、MCP 服务器和应用程序。每项发现都首先私下提交给 Gloam。

他们确认了每一项并进行了修复：兑现收件人支票、每条链的 ENS 查找、中继限制、扫描确认、代理付款检查、资金证明隐私和备份密钥。最后的报告在几小时内就得到了修复。

构建者和审核者公开共同致力于安全性工作。这正是这个生态系统所需要的。

items.title: Email: OpenAI plans to merge ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs on desktop for select users before rolling it out widely; Codex "will remain a separate experience" (Ivan Mehta/TechCrunch)
items.title_en: Email: OpenAI plans to merge ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs on desktop for select users before rolling it out widely; Codex "will remain a separate experience" (Ivan Mehta/TechCrunch)
items.author: TechCrunch
items.article_content:
The ChatGPT desktop app can be a confusing piece of software, given that there are ChatGPT and Codex sections, and within the former, there are Chat and Work tabs. With so many options, it’s sometimes easy to forget where you are working and where exactly your project is.

In an apparent effort to address this, OpenAI is now gearing up to merge the Chat and Work tabs within the ChatGPT experience, according to an email sent to users. OpenAI said that initially, this experience will be available to select users for feedback before it is rolled out widely.

“This will enable you to move from exploring an idea to having ChatGPT carry it through, all in one place. You can bring in your files and plugins and ask ChatGPT to build a website, create a presentation, or do things for you on the web, while reviewing and guiding its work. Codex will remain a separate experience in the ChatGPT desktop app,” the email said.

OpenAI also said with this transition, both ChatGPT and Codex will draw tokens from the same allowance pool. It said this change won’t impact most users, but based on usage and model, some folks might need to wait for resets more frequently.

Rival Anthropic merged Claude’s chat and Cowork functions into one screen in September.

items.article_content_zh:
ChatGPT 桌面应用程序可能是一个令人困惑的软件，因为它有 ChatGPT 和 Codex 部分，而在前者中，有聊天和工作选项卡。有如此多的选择，有时很容易忘记您在哪里工作以及您的项目到底在哪里。

根据发送给用户的电子邮件，为了解决这个问题，OpenAI 现在正准备将 Chat 和 Work 选项卡合并到 ChatGPT 体验中。 OpenAI 表示，这种体验最初将向选定的用户提供反馈，然后再广泛推广。

“这将使您能够从探索一个想法转变为让 ChatGPT 将其付诸实施，一切都在一个地方。您可以引入您的文件和插件，并要求 ChatGPT 构建一个网站、创建演示文稿或在网络上为您做一些事情，同时审查和指导其工作。Codex 将仍然是 ChatGPT 桌面应用程序中的一种单独体验，”电子邮件中说道。

OpenAI 还表示，通过这一转变，ChatGPT 和 Codex 都将从同一配额池中提取代币。它表示这一变化不会影响大多数用户，但根据使用情况和型号，有些人可能需要更频繁地等待重置。

竞争对手 Anthropic 在 9 月份将 Claude 的聊天和 Cowork 功能合并到一个屏幕中。

items.title: Anthropic has banned Claude Code from recreating existing video games, to prevent copyright infringement after developer
items.title_en:
Anthropic has banned Claude Code from recreating existing video games, to prevent copyright infringement after developers raised concerns.

So the AI that got good enough to clone entire games just got told it’s no longer allowed to.

We’ve reached the stage where AI companies are putting up “please don’t recreate copyrighted games” signs on their own tools. The capability came first, the rules came after, as always.
items.title_zh:
在开发者提出担忧后，Anthropic 禁止 Claude Code 重新创建现有视频游戏，以防止侵犯版权。

因此，足以克隆整个游戏的人工智能却被告知不再允许这样做。

我们已经到了人工智能公司在自己的工具上贴上“请不要重新制作受版权保护

items.takeaway_zh: 终结单 Agent 容易中途跑偏和幻觉无法自纠的痛点，通过规划器（Planner）、执行器（Executor）与独立评审器（Reviewer）构建自闭环三权分立链路。
items.takeaway_en: Production architecture for robust autonomous tasks: Decouples task planning, tool execution, and adversarial quality review to prevent agent derailment.
items.code_snippet:
# Multi-Agent Orchestration Topology
workflow:
  name: Autonomous_Research_And_Delivery_Pipeline
  max_iterations: 3
  nodes:
    - id: planner
      role: Strategic Planner
      prompt: "Decompose user request into discrete verifiable sub-tasks. Output pure JSON DAG."
      next: executor
      
    - id: executor
      role: Tool Specialist
      tools: ["web_search", "read_url", "code_interpreter"]
      prompt: "Execute current sub-task using provided tools. Capture raw evidence."
      next: reviewer
      
    - id: reviewer
      role: Adversarial Critic
      prompt: "Verify executor results against factuality and accuracy requirements. Output PASS or REJECT with specific critique."
      conditional_edges:
        PASS: finish
        REJECT: planner

items.title_en:
You might be tempted to think that the ANC is failing now because the talent of it's deployees in government has deteriorated, or they've been overtaken by criminals and fraudsters.

The truth is that they haven't changed at all. They have always been this crap.

The only thing that has changed is that the momentum of governance and management and process that they inherited in 1994 has slowly been winding down over the last 30 years and has finally ground to a halt.

The "institutional memory" that allowed government departments and SOEs to run on autopilot while they hardly ever replaced anyone based on merit rather than political connection has finally faded.

The processes and systems have become outdated and forgotten with time, never adapting to changing circumstances. 

The old white guys that were sidelined but stuck around to keep things going, or who worked as outside consultants doing all the real work, have aged out.

This is why a police station or a post office looks and runs exactly like it did 30 years ago. Now extend that to the whole of government. Home Affairs is a good case study. It was also coasting on 1994 systems until recently, and you can see how starkly a year or two of having a leadership that actually does it's job contrasts it with other departments.

So you're not seeing any difference in the fundamental capability of the ANC to run the country, you're just seeing the natural dissipation of institutional competence that hasn't been topped up for three decades and now the tank is empty.

items.quote_zh:
你可能会认为非洲人国民大会现在失败了，因为其在政府中部署的人员的才能已经下降，或者他们已经被犯罪分子和欺诈者所超越。

事实是他们根本没有改变。他们一直都是这样的垃圾。

唯一改变的是，他们在1994年继承的治理、管理和流程的势头在过去30年里慢慢减弱，最终陷入停滞。

政府部门和国有企业几乎不会根据功绩而不是政治关系来更换任何人的“制度记忆”终于消失了。

随着时间的推移，流程和系统已经过时并被遗忘，永远无法适应不断变化的环境。

那些被边缘化但仍然坚持让事情继续下去的老白人，或者那些担任外部顾问做所有实际工作的人，已经过时了。

这就是为什么警察局或邮局的外观和运作方式与 30 年前一模一样。现在将其扩展到整个政府。内政部是一个很好的案例研究。直到最近，它还一直在 1994 年的系统上运行，你可以看到，在拥有一个真正履行其职责的领导层一两年后，它与其他部门形成了鲜明的对比。

因此，你看不到非国大治理国家的基本能力有任何差异，你只是看到机构能力的自然消散，而这种能力已经三十年没有加满了，现在水箱已经空了。

items.title_en:
🚨 If I had to find a job in 2026, I'd stop doing these 6 things manually.

I'd use AI to find better opportunities, improve my CV, research companies, and prepare for interviews.

Here are 6 AI tools I'd use to job hunt smarter. 👇

1️⃣ FIND JOBS WITHOUT ENDLESS SCROLLING

❌ Old way: Search job boards for hours.

✅ Smarter way: Use ChatGPT to refine your search, then verify openings on Indeed.

Try this prompt:

"Help me find remote jobs that match my skills, accept applicants from my country, and offer UK-hour overlap. Give me relevant search terms and criteria to check."

Always verify the original listing and eligibility requirements.

2️⃣ STOP SENDING THE SAME CV EVERYWHERE

❌ Old way: One generic resume for every job.

✅ Smarter way: Use Kickresume to tailor your CV to each job description.

✓ Highlight relevant experience  
✓ Include measurable achievements  
✓ Emphasise skills that match the role  
✓ Remove irrelevant details

Important: Never let AI invent experience or qualifications.

3️⃣ RESEARCH THE COMPANY BEFORE APPLYING

❌ Old way: Read random reviews and guess what matters.

✅ Smarter way: Use Claude's research capabilities to investigate the company.

Ask:
→ What does the company sell?  
→ Who are its customers?  
→ What has changed recently?  
→ What challenges might this role solve?

Check the sources. Use verified findings to make your application more relevant.

4️⃣ PRACTISE BEFORE THE INTERVIEW

❌ Old way: Watch interview videos and hope you're ready.

✅ Smarter way: Use Yoodli to practise speaking and receive feedback.

Improve your:
✓ Clarity  
✓ Confidence  
✓ Pacing  
✓ Ability to explain your experience

Don't just prepare answers. Practise delivering them out loud.

5️⃣ SHOW YOUR SKILLS, NOT JUST YOUR RESUME

❌ Old way: List your skills and hope recruiters notice.

✅ Smarter way: Use Gamma to build a professional 5-slide case study.

Slide 1: The problem  
Slide 2: Your role  
Slide 3: Your approach  
Slide 4: Results  
Slide 5: Lessons learned

Use real projects and genuine results. Share only work you're allowed to disclose.

6️⃣ TRACK EVERY APPLICATION

❌ Old way: Forget where you applied and when to follow up.

✅ Smarter way: Use Notion to organise your job search.

Track:
→ Job link and company  
→ CV version submitted  
→ Application date  
→ Interview stage  
→ Next follow-up

Stay organised. Follow up thoughtfully. Never lose sight of a promising opportunity.

💡 THE BIGGEST MISTAKE JOB SEEKERS MAKE?

Using AI only to rewrite their resumes.

The real opportunity is to use it throughout the entire job search.

→ Find relevant opportunities.  
→ Communicate your real value.  
→ Research employers.  
→ Practise interviews.  
→ Keep every application organised.

📌 SAVE this post before your next job application.

♻️ REPOST it to help someone job hunting in 2026.

👇 LET'S TALK:

What's your biggest job-search challenge right now?

items.quote_zh:
🚨 如果我必须在 2026 年找到工作，我将停止手动做这 6 件事。

我会使用人工智能来寻找更好的机会、改进我的简历、研究公司并准备面试。

这里有 6 个我用来更智能地找工作的人工智能工具。

1️⃣ 无需无休止的滚动即可找到工作

❌ 老方法：在招聘网站上搜索工作时间。

✅ 更智能的方式：使用 ChatGPT 优化您的搜索，然后在 Indeed 上验证职位空缺。

试试这个提示：

“帮助我找到与我的技能相匹配的远程工作，接受来自我的国家的申请者，并提供英国工作时间重叠。给我相关的搜索词和标准来检查。”

始终验证原始列表和资格要求。

2️⃣ 停止到处发送相同的简历

❌ 老方法：每份工作都有一份通用简历。

✅ 更聪明的方式：使用 Kickresume 根据每个职位描述定制您的简历。

✓ 突出相关经验
✓ 包括可衡量的成就
✓ 强调与角色匹配的技能
✓ 删除不相关的细节

重要提示：永远不要让人工智能发明经验或资格。

3️⃣ 申请前研究公司

❌ 老方法：阅读随机评论并猜测重要的事情。

✅ 更聪明的方法：利用克劳德的研究能力来调查公司。

问：
→ 公司销售什么？
→ 它的客户是谁？
→ 最近发生了什么变化？
→ 这个角色可以解决哪些挑战？

检查来源。使用经过验证的结果使您的申请更具相关性。

4️⃣面试前练习

❌ 老方法：观看采访视频并希望您已准备好。

✅ 更聪明的方式：使用 Yoodli 练习口语并接收反馈。

改善你的：
✓ 清晰度
✓ 信心
✓ 起搏
✓ 能够解释您的经历

不要只是准备答案。练习大声说出它们。

5️⃣ 展示你的技能，而不仅仅是你的简历

❌ 老方法：列出你的技能并希望招聘人员注意到。

✅ 更聪明的方法：使用 Gamma 构建专业的 5 幻灯片案例研究。

幻灯片 1：问题
幻灯片 2：您的角色
幻灯片 3：您的方法
幻灯片 4：结果
幻灯片 5：经验教训

使用真实的项目和真实的结果。仅分享您被允许披露的作品。

6️⃣ 跟踪每个申请

❌ 老方法：忘记你在哪里申请以及何时跟进。

✅ 更聪明的方式：使用 Notion 来组织您的求职。

追踪：
→ 工作链接和公司
→ 简历版本已提交
→ 申请日期
→ 面试阶段
→ 下一步跟进

保持井井有条。认真跟进。永远不要忽视有前途的机会。

💡 求职者犯的最大错误是什么？

使用人工智能只是为了重写他们的简历。

真正的机会是在整个求职过程中使用它。

→ 寻找相关机会。
→ 传达你的真正价值。
→ 研究雇主。
→ 练习采访。
→ 让每一份申请都井井有条。

📌 在您下次申请工作之前保存这篇文章。

♻️ 转发它以帮助某人在 2026 年找工作。

让我们谈谈：

您现在最大的求职挑战是什么？

items.title: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
items.title_en: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
items.author: MIT Tech Review
items.article_content:
When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors. A single task can use 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat prompt. The more useful the agent becomes, the more calls it makes. With per-token pricing, the workflows creating the most value can also become the most expensive.

The financial pressure is already visible. Uber reportedly exhausted its entire 2026 AI budget by April after expanding its use of Claude Code. GitHub Copilot moved from flat-rate pricing to metered credits. Gartner predicts that AI coding token costs will surpass average developer salaries by 2028.

The natural response is rationing usage caps, seat limits, and approvals before developers launch agents. But blanket limits can restrict the workflows delivering value. They also optimize the wrong number. Cost per token measures consumption, not results. Some spending reflects waste, including retries and runaway loops. Some represents the work of shipping software. A meter cannot distinguish them, and neither can a spending cap.

items.title_en: The Download: the agentic web arrives and the drive for safer roads
items.author: MIT Tech Review
items.article_content:
In 2001, a decade after inventing the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision: an internet navigated by autonomous software agents that address our every need, without requiring us to muck about with browsers and search engines ourselves.

At the time, the idea seemed far-fetched. But a quarter-century on, AI agents are beginning to make it a reality. They can triage your inbox, do your grocery shopping, and even access your bank accounts.

This new era is being called the agentic web. It will inevitably transform the internet—and whether the human web survives this transition is anyone’s guess.

items.article_content_zh:
2001 年，即发明万维网 10 年后，蒂姆·伯纳斯·李 (Tim Berners-Lee) 阐述了一个新愿景：由自主软件代理导航的互联网，可以满足我们的所有需求，而不需要我们自己去处理浏览器和搜索引擎。

当时，这个想法似乎有些牵强。但四分之一个世纪过去了，人工智能代理开始将其变为现实。他们可以对您的收件箱进行分类，帮您购物，甚至访问您的银行账户。

这个新时代被称为代理网络。它将不可避免地改变互联网——而人类网络能否在这场转变中幸存下来，谁也说不准。

你是一位拥有 3A 级开放世界游戏叙事经验的资深游戏主策。请为以下 NPC 角色生成结构化多分支对话树：
1. 角色背景与潜台词：设定独特的语气口癖、隐藏秘密与性格弱点；
2. 状态机驱动：根据玩家的【声望值】、【已完成前置任务】与【过往对话记忆标记】提供至少 3 个截然不同的分支走向；
3. 输出格式要求：以 Unity / Unreal 可直接解析的纯 JSON 格式输出，包含 node_id, speaker, text, choices, condition, state_mutation 字段。

When You Should—and Shouldn’t—Use AI to Search the Web
items.title_en: When You Should—and Shouldn’t—Use AI to Search the Web
items.author: Wired AI
items.article_content:
When asked to search the web, the latest versions of these bots are combining elements of traditional web search (they're essentially just googling on your behalf) with knowledge they are able to pull out of their training data. Everything is then packaged and formatted in the now-familiar, polished generative AI style.

It's the added AI elements on top of the traditional googling where the differences come in, and that means AI-powered search may not always be the best option.

If you're looking up something simple and widely known—like the height of the Empire State Building—then AI search is a pretty safe bet. Not only is information like this easy to access online, the “autocorrect” probability patterns favored by large language models mean there's a near-certain chance that the results you see will include the right information.

If you just need a quick look-up, AI is OK. The more obscure the question, though, the closer you need to look at the answer. If you've asked something less well known, like the fifth-billed actor in an obscure television show, there might only be one or two references to it on the web, and an AI might choose the wrong one.

One of the takeaways from recent Stanford University research is that when AI finds an accurate source, it's very good at pulling the right information out of it. Where it tends to fall down is in not finding accurate sources (either because there aren't any or because the query has been misinterpreted) and presenting a confident answer anyway.

AI search is also helpful when you have a complex query that a standard Google search wouldn't be able to parse: "I need to know the best restaurants in San Francisco for a family of five who want to spend no more than $200." AI is able to query and collate multiple sources in response to a search like this, and then present a well-synthesized answer. A traditional web search would give you a list of blue links that most probably just rank San Francisco restaurants by more basic criteria.

Again though, sources are crucial. AI bots have never been to San Francisco or eaten there. They are relying on public accounts on the web, written by people who have. Where there are no exact page matches, they'll look for related words (like "affordable" or "family") and generate an answer.

For queries where there's lots of information online, like San Francisco restaurants, AI web search can feel incredibly useful. For less popular destinations and more specific requests ("dining tables shaped like stars"), you need to be more careful with the results, as the way that AI joins the dots then becomes less reliable.

So, with the caveat that you should always do some kind of double-check, AI web search works best for common queries that are likely to lead to a lot of accurate, up-to-date information online. In both the way they process search queries, and package together and synthesize answers, AI chatbots are a significant upgrade on googling.

The way generative AI bots and LLMs are put together means they work best when paraphrasing, synthesizing, and summarizing. But these processes can also introduce mistakes. If your search needs precise details (like a celebrity quotation, a report stat, or a device specification), a traditional Google search may work best.

Heading to Google and searching the old way is also likely to be better if you want full control over the sources used. Offloading web searches to AI is convenient, but you're relying on them to interpret your search correctly, find the right sources, and then extract accurate information from those sources. It saves time, but it's more opaque.

If you know the websites you trust most for technology news, for example, you can prioritize them in a traditional web search in a way that AI might not be able to. Researchers from UC San Diego have found that AI web searches will sometimes pick sources because they're more relevant to the query, rather than because they're ranked as more authoritative.

That means a personal blog might get chosen above a professional health care site if the AI deems it to be a closer match to what the user is actually searching for. This is a choice that you would be much less likely to make when scanning a traditional list of results, as you'd typically pick the one you trusted the most.

Other areas where traditional searching still wins out are for breaking news (there can sometimes be a lag in the timeliness of the data AI pulls up) and for high-stakes searches where you absolutely cannot make a mistake—searches related to health, the law, or your finances, for instance.

If you do feel like an AI approach is needed, be sure to double- and triple-check the sources the chatbot has used, which should be linked inside the answer. If you're in any doubt, you can ask the AI for clarification on where something was sourced from, to make sure it isn't an LLM invention.

Classic Google searches can still turn up false information on the web, of course, but you're in a much better position to discern what's true and accurate and what isn't without a chatbot in the middle. For queries where that's more important than convenience and speed, there's still a place for the old way of searching the web.

items.article_content_zh:
当被要求搜索网络时，这些机器人的最新版本将传统网络搜索的元素（它们本质上只是代表您进行谷歌搜索）与它们能够从训练数据中提取的知识相结合。然后，所有内容都会以现在熟悉的、完善的生成式人工智能风格进行打包和格式化。

差异在于传统谷歌搜索之上添加的人工智能元素，这意味着人工智能驱动的搜索可能并不总是最好的选择。

如果您正在查找一些简单且众所周知的内容（例如帝国大厦的高度），那么人工智能搜索是一个非常安全的选择。这样的信息不仅可以轻松在线访问，而且大型语言模型所青睐的“自动更正”概率模式意味着您看到的结果几乎肯定会包含正确的信息。

如果你只是需要快速查找，人工智能就可以。然而，问题越模糊，你就越需要仔细研究答案。如果你问了一些不太为人所知的问题，比如一部不起眼的电视节目中的第五名演员，网络上可能只有一两个参考资料，而人工智能可能会选择错误的答案。

斯坦福大学最近的研究得出的结论之一是，当人工智能找到准确的来源时，它非常擅长从中提取正确的信息。它往往会失败的地方是找不到准确的来源（要么因为没有任何来源，要么因为查询被误解）并且无论如何都无法提供自信的答案。

当您遇到标准 Google 搜索无法解析的复杂查询时，人工智能搜索也会很有帮助：“我需要知道旧金山最好的一家五口之家的餐厅，他们的花费不超过 200 美元。”人工智能能够查询和整理多个来源来响应这样的搜索，然后提供一个综合良好的答案。传统的网络搜索会给您一个蓝色链接列表，这些链接很可能只是根据更基本的标准对旧金山餐厅进行排名。

不过，来源仍然至关重要。人工智能机器人从未去过旧金山或在那里吃过饭。他们依赖网络上的公共帐户，这些帐户是由拥有公共帐户的人编写的。如果没有精确的页面匹配，他们将查找相关单词（例如“负担得起”或“家庭”）并生成答案。

对于网上有大量信息的查询，比如旧金山的餐馆，人工智能网络搜索会感觉非常有用。对于不太受欢迎的目的地和更具体的要求（“星星形状的餐桌”），您需要对结果更加小心，因为人工智能连接点的方式变得不太可靠。

因此，需要注意的是，您应该始终进行某种双重检查，人工智能网络搜索最适合常见查询，这些查询可能会导致大量准确、最新的在线信息。人工智能聊天机器人在处理搜索查询、打包和综合答案方面都是谷歌搜索的重大升级。

生成式人工智能机器人和法学硕士的组合方式意味着它们在释义、综合和总结时效果最佳。但这些过程也可能会引入错误。如果您的搜索需要精确的详细信息（例如名人名言、报告统计数据或设备规格），传统的 Google 搜索可能效果最好。

如果您想完全控制所使用的来源，那么前往 Google 并以旧方式搜索也可能会更好。将网络搜索转移给人工智能很方便，但您需要依靠它们来正确解释您的搜索，找到正确的来源，然后从这些来源中提取准确的信息。它节省了时间，但更不透明。

例如，如果您知道最信任的科技新闻网站，您可以在传统网络搜索中以人工智能可能无法做到的方式对它们进行优先排序。加州大学圣地亚哥分校的研究人员发现，人工智能网络搜索有时会选择来源，因为它们与查询更相关，而不是因为它们被评为更权威。

这意味着，如果人工智能认为个人博客与用户实际搜索的内容更匹配，那么可能会选择个人博客而不是专业医疗保健网站。在扫描传统结果列表时，您不太可能做出这种选择，因为您通常会选择最信任的结果。

传统搜索仍然胜出的其他领域是突发新闻（人工智能提取的数据的及时性有时可能存在滞后）和绝对不会出错的高风险搜索，例如与健康、法律或财务相关的搜索。

items.title: Saudi Aramco takes 49 percent stake in AI firm Humain with $2.6 billion deal
items.title_en: Saudi Aramco takes 49 percent stake in AI firm Humain with $2.6 billion deal
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
Saudi Aramco is buying into Humain, the company meant to turn Saudi Arabia into a global AI hub. According to Aramco, the oil giant is taking a 49 percent stake and contributing about $2.6 billion in 2026 along with its own AI technology. Humain was founded in May 2025 by the sovereign wealth fund PIF and builds data centers, develops cloud services, and trains AI models like the Arabic language model ALLaM.

Humain plans to build three gigawatts of data center capacity by 2030. The company wants to serve demand both domestically and abroad and become a leading AI exporter. Business is already picking up. In late August, AMD reported that infrastructure built jointly with Cisco and Humain is now serving customers inside and outside Saudi Arabia. Aramco plans to use the technology in its own operations and generate additional revenue by selling its own AI solutions. Through its investment arm Wa'ed Ventures, the company also holds a stake in Korean AI chip developer Rebellions.

The Iran war is affecting the buildout. Humain is beefing up protection for its data centers, CEO Tareq Amin told Semafor in September. Saudi Arabia is drawing on Aramco's experience securing oil infrastructure as a model. Despite the war, Humain hasn't seen any drop in demand.

items.article_content_zh:
沙特阿美公司正在收购 Humain，该公司旨在将沙特阿拉伯变成全球人工智能中心。据沙特阿美称，这家石油巨头将持有 49% 的股份，并在 2026 年贡献约 26 亿美元以及自己的人工智能技术。 Humain 由主权财富基金 PIF 于 2025 年 5 月创立，致力于建设数据中心、开发云服务以及训练阿拉伯语言模型 ALLaM 等人工智能模型。

Humain计划到2030年建设3GW的数据中心容量。该公司希望满足国内外需求，成为领先的人工智能出口商。生意已经开始好转。 8 月下旬，AMD 报告称，与思科和 Humain 联合构建的基础设施目前正在为沙特阿拉伯境内外的客户提供服务。阿美公司计划在自己的运营中使用该技术，并通过销售自己的人工智能解决方案来产生额外收入。该公司还通过其投资部门 Wa'ed Ventures 持有韩国人工智能芯片开发商 Rebellions 的股份。

伊朗战争正在影响扩建。 Humain 首席执行官 Tareq Amin 在 9 月份告诉 Semafor，正在加强对其数据中心的保护。沙特阿拉伯正在借鉴阿美石油公司在确保石油基础设施安全方面的经验作为典范。尽管发生了战争，Humain 的需求并未出现任何下降。

items.title_en:
Enterprise AI is entering a phase where the number of agents could grow faster than an organization's ability to govern them.

IBM's approach connects agent discovery, identity, orchestration, and credential management, creating a unified view of what each agent does and the authority it carries.

This matters because excessive restrictions can push employees toward shadow AI, while well-designed guardrails enable innovation with greater confidence.

The real competitive advantage will come from scaling agents responsibly, with every action traceable, every permission intentional, and every risk manageable.

As AI agents become part of everyday operations, continuous trust will become a foundation of enterprise AI architecture.

#AgenticAI #AIGovernance #Cybersecurity

British physicist and materials scientist Cyril Hilsum, widely recognized as “the father of liquid crystals” for enabling flat-panel display tech, died at 101  —  The man who helped develop the technology for liqu
items.content_snippet: The man who helped develop the technology for liquid crystal displays — the screens in flat-panel televisions and laptops — has died at 101.
items.summary_en: British physicist Cyril Hilsum has passed away at the age of 101, recognized as the pioneer who enabled modern flat-panel display technology. Amidst the era dominated by bulky CRT monitors, he led the team that engineered liquid crystal materials, fundamentally transforming how humanity consumes visual information.

items.author: 前端大牛

items.content_snippet: Modernize legacy React codebase with React 19 Actions, Server Components, and zero-any TypeScript generics.
items.summary_zh: 将遗留 React 代码迁移至 React 19 Actions、use 钩子与服务端组件，消灭 any，构建端到端类型安全体系。
items.summary_en: Modernize legacy React codebase with React 19 Actions, Server Components, and zero-any TypeScript generics.
items.prompt_content_zh:
请扮演一位精通 React 19 与 TypeScript 5.5+ 的前端资深工程总监。请重构提供的遗留组件：
1. 将过时的 useEffect 数据拉取与冗余状态迁移至 React 19 原生 Actions、useActionState 与 Server Components；
2. 实现 100% 严格类型推导，严禁使用 `any`，合理运用泛型约束、Discriminated Unions 与 const 泛型；
3. 优化渲染性能：防止不必要的 re-render，并添加 Suspense 骨架屏与 ErrorBoundary 容错保护。

items.author: Bloomberg
items.original_content:

Ukraine says its air raid alert app was compromised late Sunday, sending false warnings of “nuclear danger”; Russia confirms a similar hack of its alerts app  —  Ukraine and Russia said they faced cyberattacks on emergency and air raid alert
items.content_snippet: Ukraine and Russia said they faced cyberattacks on emergency and air raid alert systems.
items.summary_en: Both Ukrainian and Russian civil defense alert systems were compromised by cyberattacks late Sunday, pushing false 'nuclear danger' warnings via their respective apps. Both sides confirmed the breaches, highlighting the vulnerability of wartime digital infrastructure.

items.title_en:
What happens when an AI agent receives a task it doesn't have the skills to complete?

Instead of failing or waiting for human intervention, it could find another agent capable of handling that specific job.

That's the kind of agent-to-agent cooperation @termix_ai is trying to build through https://t.co/nLWoMinM2H.

The new Agents Helping Agents Bounty introduces this workflow through a simple community task.

Participants connect their agent to an X account, follow @termix_ai, repost the campaign announcement and submit the completed actions for verification.

Approved submissions qualify for 0.2 USDT.
The reward is small, but I think the underlying idea deserves more attention.

An autonomous marketplace needs more than agents that can perform tasks. It needs ways for agents to discover help, delegate work, verify completion and receive payment.

And verification is particularly important. 

Completing an action and proving it was completed are two different things.

This campaign is a basic demonstration of that workflow, not proof that complex agent-to-agent delegation has been solved.

Still, it's a practical way to introduce people to how the marketplace is intended to operate.

Explore the bounty: https://t.co/7az3veBcdX

items.title: OpenAI prepares lobbying blitz for a post-midterm Washington
items.title_en: OpenAI prepares lobbying blitz for a post-midterm Washington
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
OpenAI is gearing up for a political lobbying and PR push after the US midterms. According to Axios, the company is bracing for a tougher fight in Washington if Democrats win control of the House.

After two years under a friendly administration, big tech companies with close ties to President Trump are facing growing regulatory pressure. Rivals like Meta are already building bridges to Democrats. OpenAI's policy chief Chris Lehane plans to steer the AI debate through 2028 with a mix of new and repackaged proposals. The pitch centers on one idea: AI doesn't replace people. To back that up, OpenAI is proposing binding safety rules that build on earlier ideas. Lehane calls them "speed limits."

The company is also responding to growing local backlash against data centers. According to Axios, OpenAI wants to rebrand the facilities as "AI Compute Campuses" and is promising economic benefits to host communities. Lehane says the company's top priority in the new Congress is fast-tracking safety rules for frontier models.

items.article_content_zh:
OpenAI 正在为美国中期选举后的政治游说和公关活动做准备。据 Axios 称，如果民主党赢得众议院控制权，该公司将在华盛顿面临更激烈的战斗。

在友好政府执政两年后，与特朗普总统关系密切的大型科技公司面临着越来越大的监管压力。像 Meta 这样的竞争对手已经在与民主党建立桥梁。 OpenAI 的政策负责人 Chris Lehane 计划通过一系列新的和重新包装的提案来引导人工智能辩论持续到 2028 年。此次演讲围绕一个想法：人工智能不会取代人类。为了支持这一点，OpenAI 提出了基于早期想法的具有约束力的安全规则。勒汉称其为“速度限制”。

该公司还在应对当地对数据中心日益增长的强烈反对。据 Axios 称，OpenAI 希望将这些设施重新命名为“人工智能计算园区”，并承诺为所在社区带来经济效益。勒汉表示，该公司在新一届国会的首要任务是快速制定前沿车型的安全规则。

【起因与机理】应对大选后潜在的监管压力，确保公司在行业规则制定中的主导权
【关键技术规格】包装安全叙事与数据中心品牌。
【观点态度】意图通过立法锁定行业护城河。

items.title:
Humans mostly do not think in words. 
Animals certainly don't think in words, but they do think.

It's just that words a
items.title_en:
Humans mostly do not think in words. 
Animals certainly don't think in words, but they do think.

It's just that words are discrete objects associated with thoughts. 
Their discreteness is what makes them easy to store and remember. 
This gives the illusion that we think in words, but for most things, we don't.

Many people can't speak but can think.
So do animals.

[You might to have a look at my latest talks and/or papers if you think nothing has happened in the last 5 years:
https://t.co/6m0opCsKqP ]
items.title_zh:
人类大多不以言语思考。
动物当然不会用语言思考，但它们确实会思考。

只是词语是与思想相关的离散对象。
它们的离散性使得它们易于存储和记忆。
这给人一种错觉，我们用文字思考，但对于大多数事情，我们并不是这样。

很多人不会说话，但会思考。
